我想做的是旅行。: What I want to do is travel.
名词化：想做的事: Nominalization: what I want to do
-는 것 和 -기 都能名词化，但 -는 것 可以加修饰语（\"제가 좋아하는: Both -는 것 and -기 can nominalize, but -는 것 can take modifiers ("제가 좋아하는 것") and sounds more natural; -기 is often used in fixed expressions (-기 좋다/싫다/시작하다). They're often interchangeable, but -는 것 is more versatile.
🐰 -는 것 是韩语\"万能名词化\"！把任何动词变成\"这件事\"。\"먹는: 🐰 -는 것 is Korean's "all-purpose nominalizer"! Turn any verb into "this thing." "먹는 것" (eating), "자는 것" (sleeping). "제가 좋아하는 것은 음악이에요" (What I like is music) — the perfect pattern for introducing your hobbies.
连接两个动作或状态，表示\"……和……\"、\"……然后……\": Connect two actions or states, meaning "...and..." or "...and then..."
连接动词或形容词，表示并列关系。可以连接两个动作的先后顺序，也可以连接两个并列的: Connect verbs or adjectives to show coordination. Can link two actions in sequence or two parallel states.
吃饭然后去学校。: Eat and then go to school.
这件衣服又漂亮又便宜。: This outfit is both pretty and cheap.
昨天见了朋友然后看了电影。: Yesterday I met a friend and then watched a movie.
先后顺序：见友后看电影: Sequence: meet friend, then watch movie
🐰 -고 是韩语最基本的连接词，相当于\"然后\"或\"和\"。造长句的秘诀就是: 🐰 -고 is Korean's most basic connector, meaning "and then" or "and." The secret to long sentences is -고! "일어나고 씻고 밥 먹고 학교 가요" (wake up → wash up → eat → go to school), say your whole day in one breath!
-고 连接先后动作或并列状态（两个动作不必同时），-(으)면서 强调两个动作同时: -고 connects sequential actions or parallel states (actions don't need to be simultaneous), while -(으)면서 emphasizes two actions happening at the same time with the same subject. "밥을 먹고 TV를 봤어요" (ate and then watched TV, sequential) vs "밥을 먹으면서 TV를 봤어요" (watched TV while eating, simultaneous).
连接前后两个分句，表示后句与前句的逻辑相反。相当于中文的\"虽然……但是……\": Connects two clauses, showing the second clause is logically opposite to the first. Equivalent to "although... but..." in Chinese.
虽然累但必须做作业。: I'm tired but I have to do homework.
-지만 是明确的转折（= 但是），-는데 更柔和，常用于提供背景信息或隐约对比。: -지만 is a clear contrast (= but), while -는데 is softer, often used to provide background info or a subtle contrast.
🐰 想强烈对比时用 -지만：\"비싸지만 맛있어요\"（虽然贵但好吃）。想委婉表: 🐰 Use -지만 for a strong contrast: "비싸지만 맛있어요" (expensive but tasty). Use -는데 for a softer tone or to set up context: "비싼데 맛있어요" (a bit pricey, but pretty tasty). Koreans prefer -는데 because it's gentler.
表示原因（\"因为……所以……\"）或动作先后顺序: Indicates reason ("because... so...") or sequence of actions
接在动词/形容词后，表示因果关系或时间先后。注意：不能用过去时\"았/었서\"，: Attaches to verbs/adjectives to show cause-effect or time sequence. Note: can't use past tense "았/었서" and can't end with commands or suggestions.
词干最后元音 ㅏ/ㅗ → 아서\\n其他元音 → 어서\\n하다 → 해서 (하: Final vowel of stem ㅏ/ㅗ → 아서\nOther vowels → 어서\n하다 → 해서 (하여서)
因为肚子疼所以去了医院。: I went to the hospital because my stomach hurt.
因为天气好所以散了步。: I took a walk because the weather was nice.
原因：天气好散步: Reason: nice weather, took a walk
因为学了韩语所以在韩国公司就业了。: I got a job at a Korean company because I studied Korean.
先后顺序：学了再就业: Sequence: studied, then got a job
-아서/어서 用于客观、一般性原因；-니까 用于主观原因、命令句/请诱句。不能说: -아서/어서 is for objective, general reasons; -니까 is for subjective reasons, commands, or suggestions. You can't say "배 아파서 병원에 가세요" (X), but "배 아프니까 병원에 가세요" (O) is correct.
🐰 最简单的记忆方法：给别人建议/命令时用 -니까，单纯说原因用 -아서/어서。: 🐰 The easiest way to remember: use -니까 for suggestions/commands, and -아서/어서 for just stating a reason. "추우니까 따뜻하게 입으세요" (It's cold, so dress warmly) — since it's a suggestion, use 니까!
表示主观原因，或作为命令/请诱的依据: Indicates a subjective reason or the basis for a command/suggestion
用于表达说话人的主观判断、发现或命令/请诱的原因。前后主语可以不同，可以用过去时: Used to express the speaker's subjective judgment, discovery, or the reason for a command/suggestion. The subjects before and after can differ, and past tense can be used.
词干 + (으)니까\\n无收音/ㄹ收音 + 니까（ㄹ收音示例：알다→아니까）\: Stem + (으)니까\nNo batchim/ㄹ batchim + 니까 (ㄹ batchim example: 알다→아니까)\nOther batchim + 으니까
建议依据：因为冷: Basis for suggestion: because it's cold
饿了，一起去吃饭好吗？: I'm hungry, so shall we go eat together?
想了想，觉得那句话是对的。: After thinking about it, I felt that statement was right.
命令句、请诱句中只能用 -니까，不能用 -아서/어서。: In imperative and propositive sentences, only -니까 can be used, not -아서/어서.
🐰 -니까 是你给建议/命令时的\"王牌连接词\"。\"배 고프니까 같이 먹으: 🐰 -니까 is your "ace connector" for suggestions/commands. "배 고프니까 같이 먹으러 가요" (I'm hungry, so let's go eat together) — since it's a suggestion, use 니까! If just stating a reason: "배 고파서 혼자 먹었어요" (I ate alone because I was hungry).
表示去某处做某事的目的: Indicates the purpose of going somewhere to do something
接在移动动词（가다, 오다, 다니다 等）前面，表示\"为了做……而去/来\"。: Attaches before movement verbs (가다, 오다, 다니다, etc.) to mean "go/come to do..."
词干 + 러 (无收音)、으러 (有收音)\\nㄹ收音 + 러（ㄹ不脱落，如 놀: Stem + 러 (no batchim), 으러 (with batchim)\nㄹ batchim + 러 (ㄹ doesn't drop, e.g., 놀다→놀러)
去餐厅吃饭。: Go to a restaurant to eat.
去弘大见朋友。: Go to Hongdae to meet a friend.
目的移动：去见朋友: Purpose movement: to meet a friend
来图书馆借书。: Come to the library to borrow books.
🐰 -러 只能和移动动词（가다/오다/다니다）搭配！\"看电影\"是\"영화 보: 🐰 -러 only pairs with movement verbs (가다/오다/다니다)! "Watch a movie" is "영화 보러 가요", not "영화 볼러 가요". Remember: before 러 is the purpose, after 러 is the movement.
-러/으러 只能接移动动词（가다/오다/다니다 等），表示\"去/来做某事\"；: -러/으러 only attaches to movement verbs (가다/오다/다니다, etc.), meaning "go/come to do something"; -려고 can attach to all verbs, meaning "intend to/do something for", not limited to movement. "밥 먹으러 가요" (go to eat) = -러 + movement; "밥 먹으려고 준비해요" (preparing to eat) = -려고 + any verb.
提供背景信息，或委婉地表达对比/转折: Provide background info, or softly express contrast/turn
韩语中最重要的连接语尾之一。用于：①提供背景后引出后续内容；②委婉转折；③反期待: One of the most important connective endings in Korean. Used for: ① providing background before leading into the main point; ② soft contrast; ③ unexpectedness ("turns out..."). Very versatile.
动词：词干 + 는데 (现在时)、았/었는데 (过去时)\\n形容词：有收音 +: Verbs: stem + 는데 (present), 았/었는데 (past)\nAdjectives: with batchim + 은데, without batchim + ㄴ데\nNouns + 인데
外面下雨了，有伞吗？（背景+询问）: It's raining outside—do you have an umbrella? (background + question)
背景铺垫：下雨引出问题: Background setup: rain leads to the question
昨天去了，但门关着的。: I went yesterday, but the door was closed.
委婉转折：去了但关门: Soft contrast: went but it was closed
比想象的好啊？（委婉评价）: Better than I thought, huh? (soft evaluation)
-지만 是明确的\"虽然……但是……\"，-는데 更柔和、多功能。: -지만 is a clear "although... but...", while -는데 is softer and more multi-purpose.
🐰 -는데 是韩语的\"万能连接词\"！日常对话无处不在。核心用法：先说背景用: 🐰 -는데 is Korean's "all-purpose connector"! It's everywhere in daily conversation. Core usage: set the background with -는데, then bring up the main point. "배 고픈데 뭐 먹을래요?" (I'm hungry, what should we eat?) — first half is background, second half is the main point.
表示目的（\"以便……\"）或程度（\"到……程度\"）: Indicates purpose ("so that...") or degree ("to the extent of...")
①表示\"为了使……\"的目的；②表示达到某种程度。比 -게 更正式、更强调目的: ① Indicates purpose ("in order to..."); ② indicates reaching a certain degree. More formal and purpose-focused than -게.
请快点，以免迟到。: Please hurry so you won't be late.
请写大一点以便看清楚。: Please write it bigger so it's easy to see.
目的：为了看清楚: Purpose: to make it clear to see
熬夜学习了一整夜。（程度用法：到深夜的程度）: I stayed up studying all night. (degree usage: to the extent of all night)
程度：到整夜的程度: Degree: to the extent of the whole night
-도록 比 -게 更书面、更强调目的性。口语更常用 -게（\"잘 보이게 써 주: -도록 is more written and purpose-focused than -게. In speech, -게 is more common ("잘 보이게 써 주세요"), while -도록 appears more in manuals, announcements, or formal settings. The degree usage (밤새도록) is a fixed expression and can't be replaced with -게.
🐰 日常口语更喜欢用 -게！\"잘 보이게 크게 써 주세요\" 和 \"잘 보: 🐰 In everyday speech, -게 is preferred! "잘 보이게 크게 써 주세요" and "잘 보이도록 크게 써 주세요" are both correct, but the former sounds more natural with friends. -도록 is more common in manuals and announcements.
最常用的条件表达。可用于假设、一般条件、或\"每当……的时候\"。: The most common conditional expression. Used for hypotheses, general conditions, or "whenever..."
有时间的话一起去吧。: If you have time, let's go together.
假设条件：有时间的话: Hypothetical condition: if you have time
一到春天花就开。: Flowers bloom as soon as spring comes.
🐰 -(으)면 是韩语的\"如果\"/\"当……的时候\"，使用频率超高。\"돈: 🐰 -(으)면 is Korean for "if"/"when," and it's super common. "돈 많이 벌면 뭐 할 거예요?" (What would you do if you made a lot of money?) — Master -(으)면 and you can talk about all kinds of hypotheticals and plans.
-(으)면 是中性条件（如果……就……），-아/어도 是让步条件（即使……也……: -(으)면 is a neutral condition (if...then), while -아/어도 is a concessive condition (even if...), with opposite nuance. "비가 오면 안 가요" (If it rains, I won't go) vs "비가 와도 가요" (Even if it rains, I'll go). -거든 is used for conditions followed by explanations/suggestions, and sounds more colloquial.
比 -아/어서 更正式、更强烈的因果关系。可以用于书面语和正式场合。名词 + 때: A more formal and stronger cause-and-effect than -아/어서. Used in writing and formal settings. Noun + 때문에 means "because of...", verb/adjective + 기 때문에 means "because..."
因为下雨不能去郊游。: We can't go on the trip because of the rain.
因为努力学习了所以合格了。: I passed because I studied hard.
因为喜欢韩语所以每天学习。: I study every day because I like Korean.
🐰 때문에 是韩语里的\"因为\"加强版！比 -아/어서 更有强调感。和朋友抱怨: 🐰 때문에 is the "amped-up" version of "because" in Korean! It carries more emphasis than -아/어서. When complaining to friends, "비 때문에" conveys "it's all because of the rain" better than "비가 와서." Use 때문에 directly after nouns, and 기 때문에 after verbs.
-기 때문에 最正式、强调性最强，书面语常用；-아서/어서 最自然、口语常用，但: -기 때문에 is the most formal and emphatic, common in writing; -아서/어서 is the most natural and colloquial, but can't be used with commands/requests; -니까 is colloquial, works with commands/requests, and adds a subjective tone. Same meaning "because I'm tired": 피곤하기 때문에 (written) / 피곤해서 (everyday) / 피곤하니까 (subjective emphasis).
表示两个动作同时进行: Indicates two actions happening at the same time
连接两个由同一主语进行的动作，表示\"一边……一边……\"。前后动作必须是同一主: Connects two actions done by the same subject, meaning "while doing...". Both actions must share the same subject.
同时进行：听音乐+学习: Simultaneous actions: listening to music + studying
🐰 -(으)면서 必须是同一个主语在做两件事！\"我\"一边听音乐一边学习 ✓。: 🐰 -(으)면서 requires the same subject to do both actions! "I" listen to music and study ✓. "I eat, mom talks" can't use -(으)면서 ✗. Note that both actions must be done by the same person.
-(으)면서 要求前后主语相同，强调同时进行；-는 동안 前后主语可以不同，强调: -(으)면서 requires the same subject for both actions, emphasizing simultaneity; -는 동안 allows different subjects, emphasizing that one thing happens during the time another action lasts. "음악을 들으면서 공부해요" (I study while listening to music) vs "내가 공부하는 동안 친구는 게임을 해요" (While I study, my friend plays games—different subjects).
表达说话人对某种结果的推测性原因。带有一点不确定的语气。: Expresses the speaker's conjectural reason for a result. Carries a slightly uncertain tone.
可能是因为昨晚睡得晚，太困了。: Maybe because I slept late last night, I'm so sleepy.
推测因果：可能因为睡晚: Conjectured cause: maybe because of sleeping late
可能是因为下雨，没什么客人。: Maybe because it's raining, there aren't many customers.
推测因果：可能因为下雨: Conjectured cause: maybe because of rain
可能是吃多了，肚子有点不舒服。: Maybe because I ate too much, my stomach feels a bit off.
推测因果：可能吃多了: Conjectured cause: maybe ate too much
-아서 그런지 表示推测性因果（\"可能是因为……\"，有不确定语气），-아서: -아서 그런지 indicates conjectural cause ("might be because...", uncertain tone), while -아서 and -기 때문에 indicate definite cause ("because...", the speaker is sure of the reason).
🐰 그런지 让\"因为\"带上了\"好像是因为……吧\"的不确定语气。韩国人很爱: 🐰 그런지 adds an uncertain "seems like it's because..." tone to "because." Koreans love this euphemistic expression! "감기 걸려서 그런지 머리가 아파요" (Maybe because I caught a cold, my head hurts) — not stating it definitively, leaving room.
表示让步条件，前面情况发生或不发生，后面的结果都不变。: Indicates a concessive condition: whether or not the preceding situation happens, the following result stays the same.
再忙也要吃饭。: Even if you're busy, you should still eat.
让步：再忙也要吃饭: Concession: Even if busy, you must eat
让步：即使下雨也去: Concession: Go even if it rains
再晚也会十点前到。: Even if late, I'll arrive before 10.
🐰 \"아무리 A해도 B\" = 无论多么A也B。\"아무리 바빠도\"（再忙: 🐰 "아무리 A해도 B" = No matter how A, B. "아무리 바빠도" (even if busy), "아무리 어려워도" (even if hard). A common motivational pattern in K-dramas; using it with 아무리 sounds more natural.
-아/어도 是日常让步（\"即使……也\"），-더라도 是强调让步（\"就算……: -아/어도 is everyday concession ("even if..."), -더라도 is emphatic concession ("even if..." with stronger, more formal tone). Use -아/어도 in speech, -더라도 in writing or for extreme hypotheticals.
比 -아/어도 更强的让步表达。用于强调\"即使某个极端情况发生，结果也不会变\: A stronger concession than -아/어도. Used to emphasize that even if an extreme situation occurs, the result won't change. Common in debates and formal writing.
再难也不会放弃。: Even if it's hard, I won't give up.
强让步：再难也不放弃: Strong concession: Won't give up even if hard
结果不好也会尽最大努力。: Even if the result is bad, I'll do my best.
强让步：结果不好也努力: Strong concession: Try even if result is bad
就算撒了谎也请原谅我。: Even if I lied, please forgive me.
强让步：就算撒谎也原谅: Strong concession: Forgive even if lied
🐰 -더라도 是 -아/어도 的强势版本！用在表决心、承诺的场合。日常口语用 -: 🐰 -더라도 is the stronger version of -아/어도! Use it for resolutions and promises. In everyday speech, -아/어도 is enough; use -더라도 in formal settings or for emphasis. "죽더라도 못 해" (can't do even if I die) = I absolutely can't.
-더라도 比 -아/어도 语气更强，强调\"即使极端情况发生也不会变\"，多用于: -더라도 is stronger than -아/어도, emphasizing that even extreme situations won't change the outcome; used in formal settings, writing, or for strong resolve. -아/어도 is everyday concession with a lighter tone. "비가 와도 가요" (go even if it rains, casual) vs "비가 오더라도 반드시 가겠습니다" (will definitely go even if it rains, emphatic).
前句提出一个不太好的选择，后句提出更好的替代。\"与其做A不如做B\"。常与 차: The first clause offers a poor option, the second a better alternative. "Rather than A, better to B." Often used with 차라리 (rather).
与其吃这个，不如饿着。: Rather than eat this, I'd rather starve.
与其在这里等，不如回家。: Rather than wait here, I'd rather go home.
取舍：与其等不如回家: Rather than wait, just go home
与其坐公交，走路更快。: Walking is faster than taking the bus.
🐰 -느니 是表达\"宁可……也不……\"的高级语法。核心结构：A느니 (차라리: 🐰 -느니 is an advanced grammar for expressing "would rather... than...". Core structure: A느니 (차라리) B = rather than A, better to B. Pairing it with 차라리 (just) adds punch. Using it occasionally in everyday complaints is striking.
-느니 强调排斥前项、选择后项的取舍（\"与其A不如B\"，A是不情愿的选项），: -느니 emphasizes rejecting A and choosing B ("rather than A, B"; A is an unwilling option), while -는 것보다 is a neutral comparison ("compared to A, B is better"; no strong rejection). "택시를 타느니 걷겠어" (rather than take a taxi, I'd walk) vs "택시보다 걷는 게 더 좋아요" (compared to a taxi, I prefer walking).
表达两个变化成正比的递进关系。常与 -면 搭配使用形成 -(으)면 -(으)ㄹ수: Expresses a proportional progression between two changes. Often paired with -면 to form the emphatic -(으)면 -(으)ㄹ수록 pattern.
无收音 + ㄹ수록\\n有收音 + 을수록: No final consonant + ㄹ수록\nWith final consonant + 을수록
越往后越难。: The further you go, the harder it gets.
越想越生气。: The more I think about it, the angrier I get.
递进：越想越生气: Progression: the more I think, the angrier
越看越有魅力。: The more you look, the more charming it is.
递进：越看越有魅力: Progression: the more you look, the more charming
🐰 -ㄹ수록 叠加使用才地道！\"-(으)면 -(으)ㄹ수록\" = 越……越…: 🐰 -ㄹ수록 is most natural when stacked! "-(으)면 -(으)ㄹ수록" = the more... the more... "보면 볼수록" (the more you look), "먹으면 먹을수록" (the more you eat), "생각하면 생각할수록" (the more you think) — use this pattern for strong feelings.
-ㄹ수록 单独使用时表示\"随着程度增加……\"（\"갈수록 어려워요\"越往后: -ㄹ수록 alone means "as the degree increases..." ("갈수록 어려워요" the further, the harder), and with -(으)면 as "-(으)면 -(으)ㄹ수록" the progression is stronger ("보면 볼수록" the more you look...). -아/어지다 indicates gradual state change ("좋아져요" got better), -게 되다 emphasizes reaching a result ("알게 됐어요" finally came to know). All three express change but with different focuses.
表示\"因为看到/发现……所以……\"，口语色彩浓: Means "because I saw/found... so...", very colloquial
用于口语中，表达\"因为发现/看到/觉得……所以做了……\"。说话人以自己观察到: Used in speech to express "because I noticed/saw/felt... I did...". The speaker acts based on what they observed. The subject is usually first person.
看着好吃就买了一个。: It looked tasty, so I bought one.
观察因果：看着好吃就买: Observed cause: looked tasty, so bought
朋友看起来很伤心就安慰了一下。: My friend looked sad, so I comforted them a bit.
观察因果：看起来伤心就安慰: Observed cause: looked sad, so comforted
天气好就出来散步了。: The weather was nice, so I went out for a walk.
观察因果：天气好就散步: Observing cause and effect: nice weather → walk
🐰 -길래 是口语中表达\"看到……所以……\"的超自然表达。主语一般是\"我\: 🐰 -길래 is a super natural spoken expression meaning "seeing... so...". The subject is usually "I" because "I saw/felt something, so I did something." Koreans love using it in everyday speech. "배 고파 보이길래 김밥 사줬어" (I saw you looked hungry, so I bought you gimbap).
-길래 是说话人观察到某情况后做出反应（强调亲眼所见/亲身感受，主语通常是第一人: -길래 is used when the speaker reacts after observing a situation (emphasizing what was seen/felt firsthand, usually first-person subject), -아서/어서 is objective cause-and-effect, and -니까 is subjective reasoning. "맛있어 보이길래 샀어요" (It looked delicious, so I bought it — emphasizes visual judgment) vs "맛있어서 샀어요" (It was delicious, so I bought it — objective reason).
强调某种情况达到了相当高的程度。可以用来夸张或强调。: Emphasizes that a situation has reached a fairly high degree. Can be used for exaggeration or emphasis.
无收音 + ㄹ 정도로\\n有收音 + 을 정도로: No batchim + ㄹ 정도로\nBatchim + 을 정도로
走了很多路，腿都疼了。: I walked so much that my legs hurt.
程度：走到腿疼的程度: Degree: to the point of leg pain
感动得眼泪都出来了。: I was so moved that tears came out.
难到无法理解的程度。: It's so hard that it's beyond understanding.
🐰 -ㄹ 정도로 是韩语的\"到了……的程度\"。夸张表达的神器！\"죽을 정도: 🐰 -ㄹ 정도로 is Korean for "to the point of...". The ultimate exaggeration tool! "죽을 정도로 힘들어" (so tired I could die), "말로 표현할 수 없을 정도로 예뻐" (so pretty words can't describe it). Koreans love this dramatic pattern.
-ㄹ 정도로 强调程度极端、接近极限（\"到了……的程度\"，常含夸张），-만큼: -ㄹ 정도로 emphasizes an extreme degree close to the limit ("to the point of...", often with exaggeration), while -만큼 compares equal degrees ("to the same extent as...", no exaggeration). "울 정도로 감동했어요" (moved to the point of crying) vs "그만큼 감동했어요" (moved to that extent).
用于补充说明，连接两个都成立的条件或事实。A不仅成立，B也成立。是书面语中的常用: Used to add supplementary information, connecting two conditions or facts that both hold true. Not only A is true, but B is also true. A common progressive structure in written language.
无收音 + ㄹ 뿐만 아니라\\n有收音 + 을 뿐만 아니라\\n名词 + 일: No batchim + ㄹ 뿐만 아니라\nBatchim + 을 뿐만 아니라\nNoun + 일 뿐만 아니라
那位歌手不仅歌唱得好，舞也跳得好。: That singer not only sings well, but also dances well.
递进：不仅唱好舞也好: Progressive: not only sings well, dances well too
韩语不仅有趣，而且越学越有魅力。: Korean is not only interesting, but the more you learn it, the more charming it becomes.
递进：不仅有趣还越来越好: Progressive: not only interesting, gets better and better
这家酒店不仅设施好，服务也很棒。: This hotel has great facilities, and the service is excellent too.
递进：不仅设施好服务也棒: Progression: Not only are the facilities good, the service is great too.
🐰 -ㄹ 뿐만 아니라 = 不仅……而且……。这个句型特别适合用在写作和正式表达: 🐰 -ㄹ 뿐만 아니라 = not only... but also... This pattern is great for writing and formal expressions. In speech, -고 or -(으)ㄴ데 sounds more natural, but using it in TOPIK writing earns you points!
-(으)ㄹ 뿐만 아니라 是书面/正式的\"不仅A而且B\"，强调递进补充；-고: -(으)ㄹ 뿐만 아니라 is the formal/written "not only A but also B," emphasizing progressive addition; -고도 means "did A and also B," more colloquial, with a slight sense of surprise/concession. "노래를 잘할 뿐만 아니라 춤도 잘 춰요" (written) vs "노래를 잘하고도 춤까지 잘 춰요" (sings well and even dances well too, colloquial).
强调前后两个动作几乎同时发生，间隔极短。: Emphasizes that two actions happen almost simultaneously with very little gap.
一到家就睡了。: I fell asleep as soon as I got home.
即刻：一到家就睡: Immediate: Sleep as soon as you get home
一接电话就出去了。: He went out as soon as he answered the phone.
即刻：一接电话就出去: Immediate: Go out as soon as you answer the phone
一到春天花就开始开了。: Flowers start blooming as soon as spring comes.
即刻：一到春天就开花: Immediate: Bloom as soon as spring arrives
🐰 -자마자 = 一……就马上……。强调几乎没有时间间隔！\"집에 도착하자마자: 🐰 -자마자 = as soon as... immediately... Emphasizes almost no time gap! "집에 도착하자마자 전화해" (call me as soon as you get home) — emphasizes "right away" more than -고 나서. It matches the Chinese "一...就..." structure perfectly, so it's easy to remember.
-자마자 强调前后动作几乎同时发生，间隔极短（\"一……就马上……\"）；-고: -자마자 emphasizes that two actions happen almost simultaneously with a very short gap ("as soon as... immediately..."); -고 나서 only means doing the latter after completing the former, without the "immediately" nuance. "집에 오자마자 잤어요" (I slept as soon as I got home) vs "집에 오고 나서 잤어요" (I slept after coming home, no immediate nuance).
表示\"或者\"，在两个或多个动作/状态中选择: Means "or," choosing between two or more actions/states
用于连接两个动词或形容词，表示\"或\"的意思。可以与名词的\"或\"形式 -(: Used to connect two verbs or adjectives, meaning "or." Can be compared with the noun form -(이)나.
周末通常读书或者运动。: On weekends I usually read or exercise.
无聊或者累的时候听音乐。: I listen to music when I'm bored or tired.
早上吃面包或者喝粥。: In the morning I eat bread or have porridge.
选择：吃面包或喝粥: Choose: eat bread or drink porridge
🐰 -거나 连接动词/形容词表示\"或\"。注意：名词的\"或\"用 -(이)나: 🐰 -거나 connects verbs/adjectives to mean "or." Note: for nouns, use -(이)나 (e.g., 커피나 차 = coffee or tea); for verbs/adjectives, use -거나 (e.g., 먹거나 마시다 = eat or drink).
-거나 连接动词/形容词（\"책을 읽거나 음악을 들어요\"读书或听音乐），-: -거나 connects verbs/adjectives (e.g., "책을 읽거나 음악을 들어요" = read a book or listen to music), while -(이)나 connects nouns (e.g., "커피나 차를 마셔요" = drink coffee or tea). They serve the same function but attach to different parts of speech—don't mix them up.
表示动作进行中转而做另一件事: Indicates switching to another action while one is in progress
表示正在做A的时候停下来转而做B，或持续做A的过程中发生了B的情况。是口语中非常: Indicates stopping action A to do action B, or B happening while A continues. A very common connective ending in spoken Korean.
中途转换：学着睡着了: Mid-action switch: fell asleep while studying
回家路上遇见了朋友。: I ran into a friend on the way home.
中途转换：回家途中遇友: Mid-action switch: met a friend on the way home
吃饭吃到一半接了电话。: I answered the phone in the middle of eating.
中途转换：吃饭时接电话: Mid-action switch: took a call while eating
🐰 -다가 是口语中的高频连接词！表示\"正做A的过程中，转而做B/发生了B\": 🐰 -다가 is a super common connective in spoken Korean! It means "while doing A, switch to B / B happens." Koreans use it all the time in daily conversation. "가다가" (walking along), "보다가" (watching), "먹다가" (eating)—all real-life situations.
-다가 强调\"中途转换/中断\"（做A做到一半，转向B）；-고 나서 强调\": -다가 emphasizes a mid-action switch/interruption (doing A halfway, then turning to B); -고 나서 emphasizes completing A before doing B (finish A, then start B); -는 동안 emphasizes B happening simultaneously during A (two actions in parallel).
将动词名词化后连接 전에（之前），表示在一个动作发生之前做另一个动作。日常使用频: After nominalizing a verb, attach 전에 (before) to express doing one action before another. Very common in everyday speech.
吃饭前请洗手。: Please wash your hands before eating.
来韩国之前学了韩语。: I studied Korean before coming to Korea.
之前：来韩前学语言: Before: studied language before coming to Korea
-기 전에 是\"在……之前\"，-(으)ㄴ 후에 是\"在……之后\"。前者用: -기 전에 means "before..." and -(으)ㄴ 후에 means "after..." The former uses -기 to nominalize, the latter uses the -(으)ㄴ adnominal form—they attach differently.
🐰 记住这组反义词：吃饭前洗手 = \"밥 먹기 전에 손 씻어요\"，吃饭后刷: 🐰 Remember this antonym pair: wash hands before eating = "밥 먹기 전에 손 씻어요", brush teeth after eating = "밥 먹은 후에 양치해요". 기 전에 ← before, 은 후에 ← after.
将动词变为冠形词形式后连接 후에（之后），表示一个动作完成后再做另一个动作。: After changing the verb into an adnominal form, attach 후에 (after) to indicate that one action is completed before another action begins.
动词词干 + (으)ㄴ 후에\\n无收音/ㄹ + ㄴ 후에\\n有收音 + 은: Verb stem + (으)ㄴ 후에\nNo batchim/ㄹ + ㄴ 후에\nWith batchim + 은 후에
大学毕业后去留学。: I'll study abroad after graduating from university.
-(으)ㄴ 후에 是\"在……之后\"，-기 전에 是\"在……之前\"。注意: -(으)ㄴ 후에 means "after", -기 전에 means "before". Note that 후에 takes the adnominal form -(으)ㄴ, while 전에 takes the nominalized form -기 — the connecting patterns are completely different.
🐰 最简单的记忆：후 = 后，전 = 前。밥 먹은 후에 = 吃完饭之后，밥 먹: 🐰 Easiest way to remember: 후 = after, 전 = before. 밥 먹은 후에 = after eating, 밥 먹기 전에 = before eating. Once you remember these two Sino-Korean words, you'll never mix them up!
表示某个动作或状态持续的时间段内，发生了另一件事。前后动作的主语可以不同。: Indicates that another event occurs during the time period when an action or state continues. The subjects of the two actions can be different.
我不在的时候过得好吗？: Did you do well while I was away?
期间：我不在的那段时间: During: the time I was away
等飞机的时候读了书。: I read a book while waiting for the plane.
期间：等飞机时读书: During: read while waiting for the plane
放假期间学了韩语。: I studied Korean during the vacation.
🐰 -는 동안 = \"在……的期间\"。前面主语和后面主语可以不同，这点和 -: 🐰 -는 동안 = "during". The subject before and after can be different, unlike -(으)면서! "내가 자는 동안 엄마가 청소했어" (Mom cleaned while I was sleeping) — two people doing different things is fine with 동안.
-는 동안 前后主语可以不同（A做某事的期间，B做另一件事）；-(으)면서 要求: -는 동안 allows different subjects before and after (while A does something, B does another); -(으)면서 requires the same subject (one person doing two things simultaneously). "내가 자는 동안 엄마가 청소했어" (동안✓) but 면서 is not possible (because the subjects differ).
用于比喻或类比，表示某一行为或状态与另一情况相似。可以搭配 마치（好像）使用。: Used for metaphors or comparisons, indicating that an action or state is similar to another situation. Can be used with 마치 (as if).
动词词干 + 는 듯이\\n形容词词干 + (으)ㄴ 듯이\\n过去 + 았/었: Verb stem + 는 듯이\nAdjective stem + (으)ㄴ 듯이\nPast + 았/었듯이
不要装作知道的样子说话。: Don't talk as if you know.
雨像泼水一样下着。: It's raining as if pouring water.
他表现得好像什么都知道似的。: He acts as if he knows everything.
🐰 -듯이 描绘\"好像……一样\"的画面感。搭配 마치（仿佛/好像）使用更完整: 🐰 -듯이 paints the picture of "as if...". Pair it with 마치 (as if) for a fuller effect. "마치 꿈인 듯이" (like a dream) — a high-frequency expression in K-dramas and Korean lyrics.
-듯이 多用于动词性比喻（\"물이 쏟아지듯이\"像水泼出来一样），-(으)ㄴ/: -듯이 is mostly used for verb-based metaphors ("물이 쏟아지듯이" like water pouring out), while -(으)ㄴ/는 것처럼 is more general and can attach to nouns, verbs, and adjectives ("어린아이처럼" like a child). In speech, -처럼 is more common; -듯이 feels more literary.
对已经发生且无法改变的事情做反事实假设。\"如果那时……的话……\"的遗憾或假设: A counterfactual assumption about something that already happened and can't be changed. Conveys regret or hypothetical "if only... then..." tone. Often paired with "았/었/였을 거예요" or "았/었/였을 텐데".
要是再早一点出发的话就不会迟到了。: If I had left a bit earlier, I wouldn't have been late.
当时要是没说过那句话就好了……: I wish I hadn't said that back then...
反事实：没说那话就好了: Counterfactual: not saying that would've been better
要是当时努力学习了的话就会合格的。: If I had studied hard back then, I would have passed.
🐰 -았/었더라면 是韩语的\"如果当初……就好了\"。表达后悔、遗憾的神器。常: 🐰 -았/었더라면 is Korean for "if only I had...". The go-to grammar for regret and remorse. Often paired with -았/었을 거예요 (would have...) or -았/었을 텐데 (would have... too bad). Standard grammar for regret scenes in K-dramas.
-았/었더라면 是反事实假设（对已发生的事做假设，现实中没成真，常含遗憾），-(: -았/었더라면 is a counterfactual (hypothesizing about what already happened, not true in reality, often with regret), while -(으)면 is a general conditional (about future or uncertain situations, neutral). "열심히 공부했더라면 합격했을 거예요" (If I had studied hard, I would have passed — but I didn't) vs "열심히 공부하면 합격할 거예요" (If I study hard, I'll pass — future-oriented).
表示过去发生的动作或状态: Indicates a past action or state
韩语的过去时由词干 + 았/었/였 构成。这是韩语最基本的时态表达之一。: Korean past tense is formed with stem + 았/었/였. This is one of the most basic tense expressions in Korean.
词干元音 ㅏ/ㅗ → 았어요\\n其他 → 었어요\\n하 → 했어요 (하였어: Stem vowel ㅏ/ㅗ → 았어요\nOthers → 었어요\n하 → 했어요 (하였어요)
疑问：问昨天做什么: Question: asking what was done yesterday
周末见了朋友。: I met a friend over the weekend.
🐰 判断 았/었 的秘诀：看词干最后一个元音！ㅏ/ㅗ → 았다 (갔다, 좋았다: 🐰 The trick to choosing 았/었: look at the last vowel of the stem! ㅏ/ㅗ → 았다 (갔다, 좋았다), others → 었다 (먹었다, 읽었다). 하다 always becomes 했다! Memorize these three rules and you'll never mess up the past tense.
-았/었 是单纯的完成过去（强调动作已结束），-던 是带回想色彩的过去（强调\": -았/었 is a simple completed past (emphasizing the action is finished), while -던 is a past with a nostalgic feel (emphasizing the memory of "used to often/once..."). "먹었어요" (ate, action completed) vs "자주 먹던 음식" (food I used to eat often, with a wistful tone).
表示将来的计划或推测: Indicates a future plan or speculation
用于表达说话人打算做的事情或对未来情况的推测。在日常口语中非常常用。: Used to express what the speaker intends to do or to speculate about a future situation. Very common in everyday speech.
无收音 + ㄹ 거예요\\n有收音 + 을 거예요\\nㄹ结尾词干 + 거예요: No final consonant + ㄹ 거예요\nFinal consonant + 을 거예요\nStem ending in ㄹ + 거예요 (e.g., 살다 → 살 거예요)
明天打算做什么？: What do you plan to do tomorrow?
打算去韩国。: I plan to go to Korea.
将来：打算去韩国: Future: planning to go to Korea
-ㄹ 거예요 是有计划的\"打算做\"（事先决定），-겠어요 是当场决定的\"会: -ㄹ 거예요 is a planned "intend to do" (decided in advance), while -겠어요 is an on-the-spot "will do" (immediate commitment).\nExample: "한국에 갈 거예요" (already planned to go to Korea) vs "제가 하겠습니다" (immediately saying "I'll do it").
🐰 韩国人说\"我会做\"时，-ㄹ 거예요 和 -겠어요 都能用，但有微妙区别！: 🐰 When Koreans say "I'll do it," both -ㄹ 거예요 and -겠어요 work, but there's a subtle difference! Use -ㄹ 거예요 for planned things, and -겠어요 for on-the-spot commitments. Saying "열심히 하겠습니다!" (I'll work hard!) in an interview is an immediate commitment.
相当于中文的\"正在……\"，接在动词后表示动作正在进行中。: Equivalent to "currently doing..." in Chinese; attached to a verb to show an action is in progress.
🐰 \"지금 뭐 하고 있어요?\" 是你在韩剧里听到最多的句子之一！等于英文的: 🐰 "지금 뭐 하고 있어요?" is one of the most common lines you'll hear in K-dramas! It's like saying "What are you doing now?" in English. To answer, just use verb + 고 있어요: "밥 먹고 있어요" (eating), "공부하고 있어요" (studying).
-고 있다 强调动作正在进行（\"지금 밥을 먹고 있어요\"正在吃饭，动作过程: -고 있다 emphasizes an action in progress ("지금 밥을 먹고 있어요" eating now, the process), while -아/어 있다 emphasizes the ongoing state after an action ("의자에 앉아 있어요" sitting, the state continues). "문이 열고 있다"❌ You should say "문이 열려 있다" (the door is open).
表示过去持续或反复的动作，带有回想意味: Indicates a past ongoing or repeated action, with a sense of recollection
用于回忆过去经常做或持续进行的事情。与单纯过去时 -았/었 不同，-던 带有\": Used to recall things you often did or that continued in the past. Unlike the simple past -았/었, -던 carries a nostalgic, reflective feel.
以前常去的咖啡馆关门了。: The café I used to go to closed down.
回想：以前常去的地方: Recollection: A place I used to visit often
去了小时候住过的街区。: I went to the neighborhood where I lived as a kid.
回想：小时候住过的地方: Recollection: Where I lived as a child
刚才在看的书去哪了？: Where's the book I was just reading?
回想：刚才在看的书: Recollection: The book I was just reading
🐰 -던 带有温暖的\"回忆滤镜\"。和单纯过去时 -았/었 不同，-던 让你说: 🐰 -던 adds a warm "nostalgia filter." Unlike the simple past -았/었, -던 gives your words a reflective tone. "자주 먹던 음식" (food I used to eat often) feels more like "missing that taste" than "자주 먹은 음식."
-던 强调过去持续或反复的动作，带有回想语气（\"以前经常……的\"）；-(으): -던 emphasizes a past ongoing or repeated action with a nostalgic tone ("used to..."); -(으)ㄴ is the simple past adnominal form ("did..."). "자주 가던 카페" (a café I used to go to often) vs "어제 간 카페" (the café I went to yesterday).
表示说话人的意志（\"会/要\"）或推测（\"应该/会\"）: Indicates the speaker's intention ("will") or conjecture ("probably")
-겠- 有两大用法：①意志/承诺（第一人称为主：\"我会……\"）；②推测（基于: -겠- has two main uses: ① intention/commitment (mainly first person: "I will..."); ② conjecture (immediate guess based on what you see/hear: "it should..."). It's more formal than -ㄹ 거예요; the intention use is stronger, and the conjecture use is more intuitive than reasoned.
意志：当场表态我来做: Intention: Deciding on the spot to do it
明天天气应该会好。: The weather should be nice tomorrow.
推测：看着好吃的感叹: Guess: exclamation about how good it looks

接在动词后，表达说话人的愿望。第三人称使用时需要改为 -고 싶어하다。: Attached to a verb stem to express the speaker's wish. When used for a third person, it changes to -고 싶어하다.
愿望：想去韩国: Wish: want to go to Korea
愿望：询问对方想吃: Wish: asking what the other person wants to eat
朋友想学韩语。（第三人称用 싶어하다）: My friend wants to learn Korean. (Third person uses 싶어하다)
🐰 只有自己才知道自己\"想\"什么！所以说\"我想\"用 -고 싶다，\"他想: 🐰 Only you know what you "want"! So "I want" uses -고 싶다, "he wants" uses -고 싶어하다. "친구가 가고 싶어해요" (my friend wants to go) — because you can't say "he wants" for someone else.
-고 싶다 是明确的愿望（\"想做……\"，情感直接），-(으)ㄹ까 하다 是犹: -고 싶다 is a clear wish ("want to do...", direct emotion), while -(으)ㄹ까 하다 is a hesitant/considering intention ("thinking about whether to...", uncertain tone). "한국에 가고 싶어요" (want to go to Korea, clear wish) vs "한국에 갈까 해요" (considering whether to go to Korea, not decided yet).
既可以表示人的能力（会做某事），也可以表示客观可能性。其否定形式表示\"不会/不: Can indicate a person's ability (know how to do something) or objective possibility. Its negative form means "can't / not able / impossible."
无收音 + ㄹ 수 있다 → 할 수 있다\\n有收音 + 을 수 있다 → 먹: No final consonant + ㄹ 수 있다 → 할 수 있다\nWith final consonant + 을 수 있다 → 먹을 수 있다
🐰 -ㄹ 수 있다 的两种含义靠语境区分：\"저는 한국어를 할 수 있어요\": 🐰 The two meanings of -ㄹ 수 있다 are distinguished by context: "저는 한국어를 할 수 있어요" = I can speak Korean (ability); "비가 올 수 있어요" = it might rain (possibility). Note: "don't know how to do" is -ㄹ 줄 모르다, "can't do" is -ㄹ 수 없다.
-ㄹ 수 있다 表示能力或可能性（条件具备就能做），-ㄹ 줄 알다 专指技能性能: -ㄹ 수 있다 indicates ability or possibility (can do if conditions are met), while -ㄹ 줄 알다 specifically refers to skill-based ability (a skill learned through study). "수영할 수 있어요" (can swim, maybe the water temperature is right today) vs "수영할 줄 알아요" (know how to swim, learned this skill).
许可形：아/어도 되다（可以做……）。禁止形：(으)면 안 되다（不可以做……）: Permission form: 아/어도 되다 (may do...). Prohibition form: (으)면 안 되다 (must not do...). Note that the prohibition form shouldn't be confused with Chinese thinking — it's "if you do it, it's not okay."
许可：词干 + 아/어도 되다\\n禁止：词干 + (으)면 안 되다: Permission: stem + 아/어도 되다\nProhibition: stem + (으)면 안 되다
🐰 \"……해도 돼요?\"（可以做……吗？）是生活中最实用的句型之一。问许可的: 🐰 "...해도 돼요?" (Can I do...?) is one of the most useful sentence patterns in daily life. The golden pattern for asking permission: "들어가도 돼요?" (Can I go in?), "먹어도 돼요?" (Can I eat?). For prohibition, use "-(으)면 안 돼요".
-아/어도 되다 表示许可（\"可以做\"），-아/어야 하다 表示义务（\"必: -아/어도 되다 indicates permission ("can do"), -아/어야 하다 indicates obligation ("must do"), and -(으)면 안 되다 indicates prohibition ("can't do"). "먹어도 돼요" (can eat) vs "먹어야 해요" (must eat) vs "먹으면 안 돼요" (can't eat).
用于表达说话人基于某种根据的推测。比 -겠- 的语气更柔和、更不确定。口语中使用: Used to express the speaker's conjecture based on some evidence. It's softer and more uncertain than -겠-. Extremely common in spoken language.
动词/形容词 + ㄹ/을 것 같다\\n过去推测：았/었을 것 같다: Verb/Adjective + ㄹ/을 것 같다\nPast conjecture: 았/었을 것 같다
这部电影看起来应该好看。: This movie looks like it should be good.
推测：电影应该好看: Conjecture: The movie should be good
那个人好像已经知道了。: That person seems to already know.
推测：对方可能已知: Conjecture: The other person might already know
🐰 韩国人说话爱留余地，所以 -ㄹ 것 같다 比 -ㄹ 거예요 更常用！\"맛있: 🐰 Koreans like to leave room when speaking, so -ㄹ 것 같다 is more common than -ㄹ 거예요! "맛있을 것 같아요" (seems delicious) is more natural and humble than "맛있을 거예요" (it will be delicious). When unsure, use -ㄹ 것 같다!
-ㄹ 것 같다 是基于思考/推断的推测（\"感觉好像……\"，语气柔和），-겠-: -ㄹ 것 같다 is conjecture based on thought/inference ("feels like...", soft tone), while -겠- is a direct judgment based on immediate senses ("맛있겠다!" looks delicious, more direct). "비가 올 것 같아요" (feels like it might rain, inference after thinking) vs "비가 오겠어요" (looks like it'll rain, based on observation).
表达做某事的必要性或义务。-아/어야 하다 更强调主观义务，-아/어야 되다 是: Expresses the necessity or obligation to do something. -아/어야 하다 emphasizes subjective obligation, while -아/어야 되다 is objective necessity. But in spoken language, they're often used interchangeably.
明天之前必须做作业。: I have to do my homework by tomorrow.
现在不走会迟到的，必须走了！: If I don't leave now, I'll be late—I have to go!
🐰 -아/어야 해요 和 -아/어야 돼요 在日常对话中可以互换！但有个小差别：: 🐰 -아/어야 해요 and -아/어야 돼요 are interchangeable in everyday conversation! But there's a small difference: 해야 해요 leans more toward "I have an obligation to do it," while 해야 돼요 leans more toward "the situation requires me to do it." Don't overthink it—Koreans understand either one.
-아/어야 하다 表示义务/必要（\"必须做\"），-지 않아도 되다 是其否定: -아/어야 하다 expresses obligation/necessity ("must do"), and -지 않아도 되다 is its negative form ("don't have to do"). Note: -지 않아야 하다 ("must not do") ≠ -지 않아도 되다 ("don't have to do")—they mean completely different things.
用于表达某种普遍真理或必然规律。相当于中文的\"自然就会……\"、\"总是会……: Used to express a universal truth or inevitable pattern. Equivalent to "naturally..." or "always ends up..." in English.
努力就必然会成功。: If you work hard, success is inevitable.
必然规律：努力必成功: Inevitable pattern: effort leads to success
时间过去自然就会忘记的。: As time passes, you naturally forget.
必然规律：时间过会忘: Inevitable pattern: time makes you forget
经常见面自然就会变亲近。: If you meet often, you naturally grow close.
必然规律：常见必亲近: Inevitable pattern: frequent meetings breed closeness
🐰 -기 마련이다 = \"自然会……\"。表达人生哲理的标配语法。\"자주 안: 🐰 -기 마련이다 = "naturally..." It's the go-to grammar for expressing life wisdom. "자주 안 만나면 멀어지기 마련이에요" (If you don't meet often, you naturally drift apart)—sounds very philosophical.
-기 마련이다 强调必然性、客观规律（\"本来就会……\"），-는 법이다 强调: -기 마련이다 emphasizes inevitability and objective laws ("it's bound to..."), while -는 법이다 emphasizes principle/ought ("it stands to reason that..."). "노력하면 성공하기 마련이에요" (If you work hard, success is inevitable—a law) vs "노력하면 성공하는 법이에요" (If you work hard, success should follow—a principle). They're often interchangeable, but -기 마련이다 stresses unavoidability more.
委婉地表达某种倾向或归类。不是绝对的判断，而是\"相对来说属于……\"的语感。非: Euphemistically expresses a tendency or categorization. It's not an absolute judgment but a sense of "relatively speaking, it falls into..." This fits Koreans' habit of indirect communication perfectly.
动词：词干 + 는 편이다\\n形容词：有收音 + 은 편、无收音 + ㄴ 편: Verbs: stem + 는 편이다\nAdjectives: with batchim + 은 편, without batchim + ㄴ 편
韩语发音算是不错的。: My Korean pronunciation is pretty good, I'd say.
我算是能吃辣的。: I can handle spicy food, relatively speaking.
这个小区算是安静的。: This neighborhood is on the quiet side.
🐰 -는 편이다 让你说话留有分寸。\"잘하는 편이에요\"（算是不错的）比\": 🐰 -는 편이다 helps you speak with tact. "잘하는 편이에요" (pretty good) is more modest and natural than "잘해요" (very good). It fits the Korean communication style of avoiding absolutes. It's especially appropriate for interviews and self-introductions.
-는 편이다 是客观归类（\"算是属于……这类\"，有比较基准），-ㄹ 것 같다: -는 편이다 is objective categorization ("kind of falls into this category," with a comparative basis), while -ㄹ 것 같다 is subjective speculation ("seems like..." — the speaker isn't sure). "매운 음식을 잘 먹는 편이에요" (I'm pretty good at eating spicy food — objective self-assessment) vs "매운 걸 잘 먹을 것 같아요" (I think I can eat spicy food — speculation).
表示某种变化的结果或自然的演变过程。语气上弱化了动作的主动性，带有\"自然而然地: Indicates the result of a change or a natural progression. It softens the sense of deliberate action, carrying a subtle nuance of "naturally..." or "due to external reasons..."
（各种原因导致）来到了韩国。: (Due to various reasons) ended up coming to Korea.
变化结果：自然来到韩国: Result of change: naturally came to Korea
（不知不觉）喜欢上了那个人。: (Before I knew it) ended up liking that person.
变化结果：渐渐喜欢上: Result of change: gradually fell for them
努力学习后韩语变好了。: After studying hard, my Korean ended up improving.
-게 되다 强调结果的达成（\"最终……了\"），-아/어지다 强调状态的自然变: -게 되다 emphasizes the achievement of a result ("ended up..."), while -아/어지다 emphasizes a natural change in state ("became...").
🐰 -게 되다 是韩国人的万能\"甩锅\"句型！不用强调主观意志，而是\"各种原: 🐰 -게 되다 is Koreans' go-to "pass the buck" pattern! Instead of emphasizing personal will, it's "various reasons led to..." "한국에 오게 됐어요" (ended up coming to Korea) — sounds more humble and natural than "한국에 왔어요" (I came to Korea).
表示\"决定做……\"、\"约定做……\": indicates "decide to do..." or "promise to do..."
表达自己或团体的决定、约定、计划。通常用于陈述已经做出的决定，语气比 -(으)ㄹ: Expresses a decision, promise, or plan made by oneself or a group. Usually states a decision already made, with a more definite tone than -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
决定从明天开始运动。: Decided to start exercising from tomorrow.
和朋友约好周末见面。: Promised to meet a friend on the weekend.
约定：约好周末见面: Promise: agreed to meet on the weekend
🐰 -기로 하다 = \"决定/约定做……\"。比 -(으)ㄹ 거예요 更有确定: 🐰 -기로 하다 = "decide/promise to do..." It carries more certainty than -(으)ㄹ 거예요. "운동하기로 했어요" (I've decided to exercise) vs "운동할 거예요" (I plan to exercise) — the former is a firm decision, the latter is still just a plan.
-기로 하다 表示已经做出的决定（\"决定了……\"，确定），-(으)ㄹ까 하다: -기로 하다 indicates a decision already made ("decided to...", certain), while -(으)ㄹ까 하다 indicates still considering, undecided ("thinking about whether to...", uncertain). "부산에 가기로 했어요" (decided to go to Busan) vs "부산에 갈까 해요" (considering whether to go to Busan).
表示\"会/不会做……\"（技能）或\"知道/不知道将……\"（预知）: Indicates "know how to / don't know how to do..." (skill) or "know / don't know that... will happen" (anticipation).
有两种含义：①表示是否掌握某种技能（\"会不会做……\"）；②表示是否预知某结果: Has two meanings: ① whether one has a skill ("know how to do..."); ② whether one anticipates an outcome ("know/don't know that... will"). Context determines the meaning.
无收音 + ㄹ 줄 알다\\n有收音 + 을 줄 알다\\n过去: 았/었을 줄: No batchim + ㄹ 줄 알다\nWith batchim + 을 줄 알다\nPast: 았/었을 줄 알다
不会做泡菜锅。（技能）: I don't know how to make kimchi stew. (skill)
技能否定：不会做: Skill negation: don't know how to
没想到会下雨。（未预知）: I didn't expect it to rain. (not anticipated)
🐰 -ㄹ 줄 알다 有两种完全不同的意思：①\"会做某事\"（技能）→\"수영할: 🐰 -ㄹ 줄 알다 has two completely different meanings: ① "know how to do something" (skill) → "수영할 줄 알아요" (can swim); ② "thought that... would" (anticipation) → "비가 올 줄 알았어요" (I thought it would rain). Judge by context!
-(으)ㄹ 줄 알다 强调掌握方法/技能（\"知道怎么做\"），-ㄹ/을 수 있: -(으)ㄹ 줄 알다 emphasizes knowing the method/skill ("know how to"), while -ㄹ/을 수 있다 emphasizes ability/possibility ("can do"). "수영할 줄 알아요" (can swim, have the skill) vs "수영할 수 있어요" (can swim, able/allowed). For not knowing a skill, use -ㄹ 줄 모르다; for lack of ability/condition, use -ㄹ 수 없다.
表示正在考虑做某事，还没有完全决定: Indicates considering doing something, not fully decided yet.
表达说话人正在犹豫、考虑做某事的状态。\"我在想是不是要……\"的语感。比 -기: Expresses the speaker's state of hesitating or considering doing something. Feels like "I'm thinking about whether to...". More uncertain than -기로 하다, softer than -고 싶다.
无收音 + ㄹ까 하다\\n有收音 + 을까 하다: No batchim + ㄹ까 하다\nWith batchim + 을까 하다
我考虑周末去釜山。: I'm thinking about going to Busan this weekend.
我在想要不要买这个包，怎么办？: I'm wondering whether to buy this bag, what should I do?
犹豫：要不要买包: Hesitation: whether to buy the bag
我在考虑要不要申请那个公司。: I'm considering whether to apply to that company.
🐰 -(으)ㄹ까 하다 表达\"我在犹豫要不要……\"。韩国人委婉表达计划的最佳: 🐰 -(으)ㄹ까 하다 expresses "I'm hesitating about whether to...". It's Koreans' best choice for expressing plans politely. Softer than "할 거예요" (will do), leaving room to change your mind. "갈까 해요" = I'm thinking of going (but not fully decided).
-(으)ㄹ까 하다 表示还在考虑、未决定（\"我在想是不是要……\"），-기로: -(으)ㄹ까 하다 indicates still considering, undecided ("I'm thinking about whether to..."), while -기로 하다 indicates already decided ("I decided to..."). "부산에 갈까 해요" (considering going to Busan) vs "부산에 가기로 했어요" (decided to go to Busan).
途中/顺便: on the way / by the way
表示\"正在去/来的路上\"，或\"顺便做……\": Indicates being on the way to/from somewhere, or doing something along the way.
表示正在前往某处的途中。常用表达：가는 길이다（正在去的路上）、오는 길이다（正: Indicates being on the way to somewhere. Common expressions: 가는 길이다 (on the way there), 오는 길이다 (on the way back). Can also mean 'doing something along the way.'
动词词干 + 는 길이다\\n가는 길이다 / 오는 길이다 / 돌아가는 길이: Verb stem + 는 길이다\n가는 길이다 / 오는 길이다 / 돌아가는 길이다\n(Not limited to movement verbs; can also be used with 퇴근하는 길에, etc.)
现在正在回家的路上。: I'm on my way home right now.
下班路上顺便去了超市。: I stopped by the supermarket on my way home from work.
顺便：下班顺路买东西: By the way: running errands on the way home from work
正好在来的路上，一起走吧。: I'm on my way here anyway, let's go together.
途中：正好在来路上: On the way: already on the way here
-는 길이다 强调\"路途中\"的场景（正在去/来的途中），-는 중이다 强调\: -는 길이다 emphasizes the 'on the way' scenario (in the middle of going/coming), while -는 중이다 emphasizes an action in progress (not limited to movement). '가는 길이에요' (on the way) vs '가는 중이에요' (in the middle of going, more emphasis on the action in progress).
🐰 -는 길이다 专用于\"路上\"场景。\"가는 길이에요\"（在去的路上）、: 🐰 -는 길이다 is specifically for 'on the way' scenarios. '가는 길이에요' (on the way there), '오는 길이에요' (on the way back). When answering the phone, say '지금 가는 길이에요!' (I'm on my way!) — the standard expression Koreans use when friends are rushing them.
转述他人的话或自己的想法: Reporting someone else's words or one's own thoughts
用于引述陈述、疑问、命令、请求等。口语中常缩写为 -대요/-래요/-냬요/-재요: Used to quote statements, questions, commands, requests, etc. In spoken language, often abbreviated to -대요/-래요/-냬요/-재요.
陈述：动词 + ㄴ/는다고、形容词 + 다고、名词 + (이)라고\\n疑问：-:
Statements: verb + ㄴ/는다고, adjective + 다고, noun + (이)라고
Questions: -냐고/느냐고
Commands: -(으)라고
Suggestions: -자고
朋友说明天来。: My friend said they're coming tomorrow.
妈妈问我吃了什么。: Mom asked me what I ate.
老师让我们做作业。: The teacher told us to do our homework.
命令引语：老师让做作业: Command quote: teacher told to do homework
🐰 间接引语是韩语里的\"转述神器\"。四种类型记住：陈述 = -다고、疑问 =: 🐰 Indirect speech is Korean's 'quoting tool.' Remember the four types: statements = -다고, questions = -냐고, commands = -라고, suggestions = -자고. In spoken Korean, these are often shortened to -대요/-냬요/-래요/-재요, and the shortened versions are more common.
-다고/라고/냐고/자고 해요 是完整形式（书面、正式或强调时用），-대요/-래: -다고/라고/냐고/자고 해요 is the full form (used in writing, formal speech, or for emphasis), while -대요/-래요/-냬요/-재요 is the spoken abbreviated form (more common in everyday conversation). The meaning is identical, just a difference in register. '온다고 해요' = '온대요', '오라고 해요' = '오래요'.
口语中常用的间接引语缩写形式: Common abbreviated forms of indirect quotation in spoken language
在口语中 -다고 해요 缩略为 -대요，-라고 해요 缩略为 -래요，-냐고 해: In spoken Korean, -다고 해요 is shortened to -대요, -라고 해요 to -래요, -냐고 해요 to -냬요, and -자고 해요 to -재요. These shortened forms are extremely common in everyday conversation.
听说明天要下雨。: I heard it's going to rain tomorrow.
缩略陈述引语：听说下雨: Abbreviated statement quote: heard it's raining
朋友说一起吃饭吧。: My friend said let's eat together.
缩略提议引语：说一起吃: Abbreviated suggestion quote: said to eat together
妈妈问我在干嘛。: Mom asked what I was doing.
缩略疑问引语：问干嘛: Abbreviated question quote: asked what doing
老师说要安静。: The teacher said to be quiet.
缩略命令引语：让安静: Abbreviated command quote: told to be quiet
🐰 日常口语中，韩国人几乎不用 -다고 해요 全称，直接说缩略版！\"비 온대\: 🐰 In everyday speech, Koreans almost never use the full -다고 해요 form—they just say the shortened version! "비 온대" (heard it's raining), "밥 먹재" (said let's eat), "뭐 하냬" (asked what doing). Learn the shortened forms and your listening comprehension will instantly level up.
-대요/-래요/-냬요/-재요 是口语缩略形式（日常对话首选），-다고/라고/냐: -대요/-래요/-냬요/-재요 are spoken shortened forms (preferred in daily conversation), while -다고/라고/냐고/자고 해요 are the full forms (used in writing or formal settings). They mean the same thing, just differ in register. You'll hear the shortened versions constantly when listening to Koreans, but use the full forms in writing.
表示疑问内容的间接引用或不确定: Indirect quotation of a question or expression of uncertainty
用于间接引用疑问句，或表达\"不知道/不确定……\"的内容。常与 알다/모르다（: Used to indirectly quote a question, or to express "not knowing/being unsure about..." Often paired with 알다/모르다 (know/don't know), 기억나다 (remember), etc.
不知道那个人是谁。: I don't know who that person is.
不知道明天天气好不好。: I don't know if the weather will be good tomorrow.
不知道是不是这泡菜锅太辣了，嘴像着了火。: I don't know if this kimchi stew is too spicy—my mouth is on fire.
不确定原因：不知是否太辣: Uncertain cause: not sure if too spicy
🐰 -는지 最常和 모르다（不知道）搭配。\"언제 끝날지 몰라요\"（不知道什: 🐰 -는지 is most often paired with 모르다 (don't know). "언제 끝날지 몰라요" (don't know when it'll end), "누가 올지 몰라요" (don't know who'll come). It's your go-to for expressing "not sure" in daily life.
-(으)ㄴ/는지 引用疑问内容或表达不确定（\"不知道……\"，常搭配 모르다/: -(으)ㄴ/는지 quotes question content or expresses uncertainty ("don't know...", often with 모르다/알다), while -냐고 relays someone else's question ("someone asked..."). "언제 오는지 몰라요" (don't know when coming—my own uncertainty) vs "언제 오냐고 물어봤어요" (asked when coming—relaying a question).
接在动词/形容词后，表示使别人做某事或使某物处于某种状态。是非直接使动（-이/히: Attaches after verbs/adjectives to indicate making someone do something or causing something to be in a certain state. This is the indirect causative (-이/히/리/기/우 are direct causatives).
间接使动：让孩子吃饭: Indirect causative: make the child eat
间接使动：使我感到幸福: Indirect causative: make me feel happy
🐰 -게 하다 = \"让……做……\"。和形容词搭配也很常用：\"행복하게 해: 🐰 -게 하다 = "make/let someone do something." It's also commonly used with adjectives: "행복하게 해요" (make me happy), "슬프게 해요" (make me sad). This usage is super common in K-drama OST lyrics.
-게 하다 是间接使动（任何动词/形容词都能用，结构灵活），-이/히/리/기 是: -게 하다 is the indirect causative (works with any verb/adjective, flexible structure), while -이/히/리/기 is the direct causative (only specific verbs have corresponding forms, more concise). "밥을 먹게 했어요" (made someone eat, indirect) = "밥을 먹였어요" (fed someone, direct). Verbs without a direct causative form can only use -게 하다.
韩语的被动/使动由词干 + 이/히/리/기 构成。不是所有动词都能变被动/使动。: Korean passive/causative is formed with stem + 이/히/리/기. Not all verbs can become passive/causative. Passive: subject passively receives the action; Causative: subject makes someone else do something.
【被动】词干 + 이/히/리/기（主语被动接受）\\n이: 보다→보이다, 쓰다:
【Passive】Stem + 이/히/리/기 (subject passively receives action)
이: 보다→보이다, 쓰다→쓰이다
히: 읽다→읽히다, 먹다→먹히다
리: 열다→열리다, 듣다→들리다
기: 끊다→끊기다, 안다→안기다
【Causative】Stem + 이/히/리/기 (subject makes someone else do)
이: 먹다→먹이다 (feed), 보다→보이다 (show)
히: 앉다→앉히다 (make sit), 읽다→읽히다 (make read)
리: 울다→울리다 (make cry), 날다→날리다 (make fly)
기: 웃다→웃기다 (make laugh), 벗다→벗기다 (make take off)
从远处传来音乐声。（被动）: Music can be heard from afar. (Passive)
老师让学生们读书。（使动）: The teacher made the students read. (Causative)
那个喜剧演员总是逗大家笑。（使动）: That comedian always makes everyone laugh. (Causative)
🐰 韩语被动和使动用的是同一套后缀，区分靠语境！\"먹이다\"——妈妈喂孩子是使: 🐰 In Korean, passive and causative use the same suffixes—context tells them apart! "먹이다"—mom feeding a child is causative, "먹히다"—food being eaten is passive. High-frequency passive verbs are worth memorizing separately: 보이다/들리다/열리다/팔리다/잡히다.
-이/히/리/기 使动 是直接使动（主语直接让某人做，动词形式固定），-게 하다: -이/히/리/기 causative is direct (subject directly makes someone do something, fixed verb form), -게 하다 is indirect (universal, works with any verb); -이/히/리/기 passive is direct passive, -아/어지다 is natural-change passive (emphasizes gradual state change). "문을 열었어요" (opened the door, active) → "문이 열렸어요" (the door was opened, direct passive) vs "문이 열려졌어요" (❌ double passive, forbidden).
表示\"变得……\"或自然被动的结果: Indicates "becomes..." or a natural passive result
-아/어지다 有两个核心用法：①与形容词结合表示\"变得……\"（状态变化）；②: -아/어지다 has two core uses: ① with adjectives, it means "becomes..." (state change); ② with some verbs, it indicates a natural passive result.
韩国生活变得很习惯了。: Life in Korea has become familiar.
这本书不容易读。: This book isn't easy to read.
🐰 -아/어지다 和形容词搭配表示\"变得……\"：좋다→좋아지다（变好）、예쁘: 🐰 -아/어지다 with adjectives means "becomes...": 좋다→좋아지다 (gets better), 예쁘다→예뻐지다 (gets prettier). It's the go-to grammar for describing change! "한국어가 점점 재미있어져요" (Korean is getting more and more fun)—you'll definitely use this sentence as a Korean learner.
共动句终结语尾，用于提议大家一起做某事，相当于中文的\"（我们）……吧\"。属于: A cohortative ending used to propose doing something together, equivalent to "let's..." in English. It's in the formal polite style (합쇼체), more solemn than -아/어요. In everyday speech, -아/어요 (like "같이 가요") or -(으)ㄹ까요 is more common for suggestions; -ㅂ시다 is a bit formal, so use it cautiously with elders.
无收音词干 + ㅂ시다 (가다→갑시다)\\n有收音词干 + 읍시다 (먹다→먹: Stem without batchim + ㅂ시다 (가다→갑시다)\nStem with batchim + 읍시다 (먹다→먹읍시다)\nㄹ batchim drops + ㅂ시다 (놀다→놉시다)
-ㅂ시다 是较正式的共动句（\"我们……吧\"，直接提议），-(으)ㄹ까요 更柔: -ㅂ시다 is a more formal cohortative ("let's...", direct suggestion), while -(으)ㄹ까요 is softer ("shall we...?", asking for input). For elders or when being polite, -(으)ㄹ까요 or -(으)시겠어요 is more appropriate; -ㅂ시다 has a slightly rallying/commanding tone, used mostly with peers or those below you.
🐰 -ㅂ시다 是\"一起……吧\"，但语气比想象中正式，别对长辈用。和朋友说\": 🐰 -ㅂ시다 means "let's...", but it's more formal than you'd think—don't use it with elders. With friends, "같이 가요" is more natural; use "갑시다" in formal settings or when leading a call to action.
만 接在名词后，表示\"只有、仅仅\"，把范围限定在这一项。可以替代或叠加在其他: 만 attaches to nouns to mean "only, just," limiting the scope to that one thing. It can replace or stack with other particles (like 만을, 만이, 에만, 만 하다). It emphasizes "nothing else besides this."
名词 + 만 (直接加，不受收音影响)\\n可与其他助词叠加：에만、만을、만이: Noun + 만 (attached directly, regardless of final consonant)\nCan stack with other particles: 에만, 만을, 만이
만 表示\"只\"（肯定语气，\"只有这个\"），밖에 也表示\"只\"但必须接: 만 means "only" (affirmative, "just this"), while 밖에 also means "only" but requires a negative predicate ("물밖에 없어요" = only water / nothing but water). 도, on the other hand, means "also, too" (additive). "커피만 마셔요" (only drink coffee) vs "커피도 마셔요" (also drink coffee).
🐰 만 = \"只\"，超好用。\"이것만 주세요\"（只要这个）、\"조금만요: 🐰 만 = "only," super handy. "이것만 주세요" (just this), "조금만요" (just a little). To say "nothing but...", switch to 밖에 + negative: "시간이 조금밖에 없어요" (only a little time).
있다（有/在）和 없다（没有/不在）是韩语最基础的存在动词。表示事物的存在或所有: 있다 (have/be) and 없다 (not have/not be) are Korean's most basic existential verbs. They express existence or possession: subject + 이/가 + 있다/없다. They can mean "have or not" (possession) or "be here or not" (location, often with 에).
有收音名词 + 이 있다/없다 (시간이 있어요)\\n无收音名词 + 가 있다: Noun with final consonant + 이 있다/없다 (시간이 있어요)\nNoun without final consonant + 가 있다/없다 (차가 없어요)\nLocation: place + 에 + 있다/없다
있다/없다 用于事物或平辈（\"친구가 있어요\"有朋友）；主语是需要尊敬的人时: 있다/없다 is used for things or peers ("친구가 있어요" I have a friend); when the subject is someone to be respected, "be here" uses the honorific verb 계시다 ("할머니께서 계세요" Grandma is here). For possession, the honorific is 있으시다 ("시간이 있으세요?" Do you have time?).
🐰 있다/없다 是你最早学会的两个动词！\"있어요\"＝有/在，\"없어요\"＝: 🐰 있다/없다 are the first two verbs you'll learn! "있어요" = have/be here, "없어요" = don't have/not here. Asking directions, time, or finding things all rely on it. Note: for someone respected, "be here" uses 계시다, not "할머니가 있어요".
在过去时 -았/었 后再加 -었-，构成\"大过去时\"，强调某事发生在过去且与: Adding -었- after the past tense -았/었 forms the "pluperfect," emphasizing that something happened in the past and contrasts with the present state ("it used to be that way, but now it's different"). It carries the nuance of "that's in the past, things have changed."
词干元音 ㅏ/ㅗ → 았었 (살다→살았었다)\\n其他元音 → 었었 (먹다→: Stem vowel ㅏ/ㅗ → 았었 (살다→살았었다)\nOther vowels → 었었 (먹다→먹었었다)\n하다 → 했었 (공부하다→공부했었다)
大过去：曾住首尔（现已搬走）: Pluperfect: used to live in Seoul (moved away)
-았었 强调\"过去发生且如今已改变\"的断裂感（\"살았었어요\"以前住过、现: -았었 emphasizes the break of "happened in the past and has since changed" ("살았었어요" used to live there, not anymore); -았/었 is simply completed past ("살았어요" lived there, no contrast implied); -던 has a nostalgic tone ("살던 집" the house I used to live in). Use -았었 to highlight "things are different now."
🐰 -았었 = 过去时再加一层\"但现在不一样了\"。\"서울에 살았어요\"只: 🐰 -았었 = past tense plus an extra layer of "but now it's different." "서울에 살았어요" just says you lived there, "서울에 살았었어요" implies "I don't live there now." To emphasize how things have changed, stack this layer.
表示\"要想……的话，就得……\": Means 'if you want to... you have to...'
由 -(으)려고 하면 缩略而来，表示\"如果打算/想要做某事的话\"，后句通常: Shortened from -(으)려고 하면, meaning 'if you intend/want to do something.' The following clause usually gives the condition, method, or advice needed to achieve that goal. The first clause is the intention, the second is the necessary condition.
无收音/ㄹ词干 + 려면 (가다→가려면)\\n有收音词干 + 으려면 (먹다→: No batchim/ㄹ stem + 려면 (가다→가려면)\nBatchim stem + 으려면 (먹다→먹으려면)
意图条件：想学好就得练: Intentional condition: To learn well, you have to practice
意图条件：想唱就先看词: Intentional condition: To sing, first look at the lyrics
意图条件：想合格就用功: Intentional condition: To pass, you have to study hard
-(으)려면 专指\"为了实现某意图的条件\"（\"합격하려면 공부해야 해요\: -(으)려면 specifically means 'the condition to achieve an intention' (e.g., '합격하려면 공부해야 해요' to pass, you must study—the first clause is the goal), while -(으)면 is a general condition (e.g., '시간이 있으면' if there's time, no intention involved). The second clause often pairs with -아/어야 하다 (must) to give the method.
🐰 -(으)려면 后面几乎总跟\"该怎么做\"。\"살을 빼려면 운동해야 돼요: 🐰 -(으)려면 is almost always followed by 'what to do.' E.g., '살을 빼려면 운동해야 돼요' (to lose weight, you have to exercise). Want to say 'if you want to... you have to...'? This pattern nails it.
接在动词后，表示说话人的意图或计划（\"打算做……\"），也可表示某事即将发生的: Attached to verbs, it expresses the speaker's intention or plan ('intend to do...'), and can also indicate something is about to happen ('on the verge of...'). It emphasizes 'intention/inner plan' more than -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
无收音/ㄹ词干 + 려고 하다 (가다→가려고 하다)\\n有收音词干 + 으려: No batchim/ㄹ stem + 려고 하다 (가다→가려고 하다)\nBatchim stem + 으려고 하다 (먹다→먹으려고 하다)
打算：因考试打算复习: Plan: Planning to study for the exam
-(으)려고 하다 强调\"心里的意图/打算\"（可能还没最终定，也可表示即将发: -(으)려고 하다 emphasizes 'inner intention/plan' (may not be final, can also indicate imminent action); -(으)ㄹ 거예요 is a more definite plan or guess; -기로 하다 is a firm decision/commitment. '가려고 해요' (planning to go, want to go) vs '가기로 했어요' (decided to go).
🐰 -(으)려고 하다 = \"打算…\"。还有个隐藏用法：表示\"眼看要…\": 🐰 -(으)려고 하다 = 'plan to...' It also has a hidden use: indicating 'about to...' like '비가 오려고 해요' (it's about to rain). Perfect when you see dark clouds.
表示\"（请）为我做……\"、\"帮……做……\": Means '(please) do... for me' or 'help do...'
动词 + 아/어 주다，表示为对方或替对方做某事。命令形 -아/어 주세요 是最: Verb + 아/어 주다 means doing something for or on behalf of someone. The imperative form -아/어 주세요 is the most common polite request ('please... for me'). For elders or superiors, replace 주다 with the honorific 드리다 (see '-아/어 드리다').
词干元音 ㅏ/ㅗ → 아 주다 (사다→사 주다)\\n其他元音 → 어 주다:
Stem vowel ㅏ/ㅗ → 아 주다 (사다→사 주다)
Other vowels → 어 주다 (읽다→읽어 주다)
하다 → 해 주다
Polite request: -아/어 주세요
请求：请帮忙保存: Request: Please save it for me
-아/어 주다 是\"为对方做\"（接受者是平辈/晚辈，或请对方为自己做）；-아: -아/어 주다 means "doing for someone" (the recipient is a peer or junior, or asking someone to do for you); -아/어 드리다 is its honorific form, used for elders or superiors ("도와 드릴게요" I'll help you). Plain -(으)세요 is a command ("앉으세요" please sit), while -아/어 주세요 emphasizes "do me this favor."
🐰 \"-아/어 주세요\"是韩国生活求助万能句！\"도와주세요\"（请帮帮我）: 🐰 "-아/어 주세요" is the all-purpose request phrase in Korean daily life! "도와주세요" (please help me), "사진 찍어 주세요" (please take a photo for me). For elders, upgrade 주세요 to 드리다: "제가 해 드릴게요" (I'll do it for you).
-지요（口语缩略为 -죠）用于向对方确认自己已知或猜测的事，寻求认同，相当于\": -지요 (colloquially shortened to -죠) is used to confirm something you already know or guess with the other person, seeking agreement—equivalent to "...right?" or "...isn't it?" It can also be used for statements, gentle commands, or suggestions, with a friendly and soft tone.
-지요? 向对方求证共识（\"맛있지요?\"好吃吧？期待认同），-잖아요 是提醒: -지요? seeks consensus from the other person ("맛있지요?" It's delicious, right? expecting agreement), -잖아요 reminds the other person of something they should already know ("맛있잖아요" It's delicious, you know), and -네요 is an exclamation of a new discovery on the spot ("맛있네요" Oh, it's delicious!). -지요 is asking, -잖아요 is reminding, -네요 is exclaiming.
🐰 -죠 是韩国人聊天的黏合剂！\"그렇죠\"（对吧）、\"좋죠\"（好啊）、\: 🐰 -죠 is the glue of Korean conversation! "그렇죠" (right), "좋죠" (sounds good), "맞죠?" (that's right, isn't it?). Add 죠 when you want to confirm with someone or get closer, and the tone instantly softens.
用动词/形容词修饰名词，\"……的+名词\": Using verbs/adjectives to modify nouns, "...'s + noun"
把动词或形容词变成定语来修饰后面的名词，相当于中文\"……的\"。时态不同用不同: Turn verbs or adjectives into attributive forms to modify the following noun, equivalent to Chinese "...的." Different tenses use different forms: present tense verbs use -는, past uses -(으)ㄴ, future/supposition uses -(으)ㄹ; adjectives use -(으)ㄴ. This is the core structure for building complex sentences.
动词现在 + 는 (먹는 사람)\\n动词过去 + (으)ㄴ (먹은 사람)\\:
Verb present + 는 (먹는 사람)
Verb past + (으)ㄴ (먹은 사람)
Verb future + (으)ㄹ (먹을 사람)
Adjective + (으)ㄴ (예쁜 사람)
Adjectives can also take present + 는 (있다/없다 type: 맛있는)
现在冠形：在听的歌: Present attributive: the song listening to
将来冠形：要学的语法: Future attributive: the grammar to learn
冠形词形直接修饰名词（\"먹는 사람\"吃的人）；接 것 就名词化成\"……的事: The attributive form directly modifies a noun ("먹는 사람" the person eating); attached to 것 it nominalizes into "...thing/matter" ("먹는 것" the act of eating). For past tense, -(으)ㄴ indicates simple completion ("먹은 빵" bread that was eaten), while -던 carries recollection ("먹던 빵" bread you used to eat / half-eaten bread).
🐰 冠形词形是韩语造长句的关键！记住时态三件套：현재-는、과거-(으)ㄴ、미래-: 🐰 The attributive form is key to making long Korean sentences! Remember the tense trio: present -는, past -(으)ㄴ, future -(으)ㄹ. "내가 좋아하는 사람" (the person I like), "어제 산 옷" (the clothes I bought yesterday), "내일 만날 친구" (the friend I'll meet tomorrow).
아니다 是 이다（是）的否定形，表示\"不是……\"。名词 + 이/가 + 아니: 아니다 is the negative form of 이다 (to be), meaning "is not..." Noun + 이/가 + 아니다. A common pattern is "A가 아니라 B" meaning "not A but B," used for correction or contrast.
有收音名词 + 이 아니다 (학생이 아니에요)\\n无收音名词 + 가 아니다: Noun with final consonant + 이 아니다 (학생이 아니에요)\nNoun without final consonant + 가 아니다 (의사가 아니에요)\nContrast: A이/가 아니라 B
이/가 아니다 是名词谓语\"是\"的否定（\"학생이 아니에요\"不是学生）；: 이/가 아니다 is the negative of the noun predicate "to be" ("학생이 아니에요" = not a student); 안/-지 않다 is the negative of verbs/adjectives ("안 가요" = don't go, "예쁘지 않아요" = not pretty). Use 아니다 to negate noun identity, and 안 for actions/states.
🐰 이다（是）的反义就是 아니다（不是）。\"학생이에요\"（是学生）↔\"학생: 🐰 The opposite of 이다 (to be) is 아니다 (to not be). "학생이에요" (is a student) ↔ "학생이 아니에요" (is not a student). To correct someone, use "A가 아니라 B": "제 게 아니라 친구 거예요" (It's not mine, it's my friend's).
表示\"我会……的\"（对听者的承诺）: Indicates "I will..." (a promise to the listener)
表示说话人对听者做出的承诺或意志表态，\"我（会为你）……\"。主语只能是第一人: Indicates a promise or expression of intention made by the speaker to the listener, "I (will) ... for you." The subject can only be first person, and it carries a nuance of considering and responding to the other person. Unlike -(으)ㄹ 거예요, which simply states a plan, -(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise spoken to the listener.
无收音/ㄹ词干 + ㄹ게요 (가다→갈게요)\\n有收音词干 + 을게요 (먹다: No batchim/ㄹ stem + ㄹ게요 (가다→갈게요)\nWith batchim stem + 을게요 (먹다→먹을게요)
承诺：到了就联系: Promise: I'll contact you when I arrive

嘴巴自然张开，发音时舌面后部稍微抬起，唇形略扁。: Open your mouth naturally, slightly raise the back of your tongue, and keep your lips somewhat flat.
想象「a」=「啊」最响亮的元音，竖线像人，旁边一横像伸出的手臂。: Imagine 'a' = 'ah', the most resonant vowel. The vertical line is like a person, and the horizontal line beside it is like an outstretched arm.
ㅏ 嘴大开、舌位靠前；ㅓ 嘴开度小、舌位靠后。形状上 ㅏ 短横在右、ㅓ 短横在左: ㅏ: mouth wide open, tongue forward; ㅓ: smaller mouth opening, tongue back. In shape, ㅏ has the short stroke on the right, ㅓ on the left.
短横 左→右: Short horizontal stroke: left to right
由 y 滑音快速过渡到 ㅏ，发音时先发 y 音然后迅速过渡到「啊」，整体读作「呀: Glide quickly from a 'y' sound into ㅏ. Say 'y' first, then transition rapidly to 'ah', making it 'ya'.
ㅏ 右边多一道短横 = 给「啊」加上 y 起音，写作「ya」=「呀」。: An extra short stroke on the right of ㅏ = adding a 'y' onset to 'ah', written as 'ya' = 'ya'.
ㅑ 收尾是 ㅏ（大开口、舌位靠前）；ㅕ 收尾是 ㅓ（开度小、舌位靠后）。形状上: ㅑ ends with ㅏ (wide open, tongue forward); ㅕ ends with ㅓ (smaller opening, tongue back). In shape, ㅑ has double strokes on the right, ㅕ on the left.
上短横 左→右: Upper short stroke: left to right
下短横 左→右: Lower short stroke: left to right
发音时口型比 ㅏ 稍小，舌位更低，双唇放松，不要撅圆嘴。: When pronouncing, the mouth shape is slightly smaller than ㅏ, tongue lower, lips relaxed—don't round them.
ㅏ 的「啊」翻转 → 短横移到左边，发音也从张开变成往后收，听感介于「哦」和「呃: Flip the 'ah' of ㅏ → the short stroke moves to the left, and the sound shifts from open to pulled back, between 'oh' and 'uh'.
ㅓ 不要撅圆嘴，舌位往后；ㅏ 嘴大开、舌位靠前。形状上短横方向相反。: ㅓ: don't round your lips, tongue back; ㅏ: mouth wide open, tongue forward. The short strokes face opposite directions.
哟（扁嘴，非圆嘴 ㅛ）: Yo (flat lips, not rounded like ㅛ)
由 y 滑音快速过渡到 ㅓ，发音类似「哟」，注意嘴不要撅圆。: Glide quickly from a 'y' sound into ㅓ, similar to 'yo', but keep your lips flat, not rounded.
ㅓ 左边多一道短横 = 给 ㅓ 加上 y 起音，写作「yeo」。: An extra short stroke on the left of ㅓ = adding a 'y' onset to ㅓ, written as 'yeo'.
ㅕ 收尾是 ㅓ（嘴小、舌位靠后）；ㅑ 收尾是 ㅏ（嘴大开、舌位靠前）。形状上双横: ㅕ ends in ㅓ (small mouth, tongue back); ㅑ ends in ㅏ (mouth wide open, tongue front). The two horizontal lines point in opposite directions.
嘴巴略微收圆，舌面后部抬起，发音较饱满。: Round your lips slightly, raise the back of your tongue, and pronounce it fully.
一横上面加一短竖 = 太阳从地平线升起，发圆唇的「o」。: A horizontal line with a short vertical above = the sun rising over the horizon, pronounced with rounded lips as 'o'.
ㅗ 短竖在横线上方、嘴唇圆但不嘟；ㅜ 短竖在下方、嘴唇向前嘟起更明显。: ㅗ has the short vertical above the horizontal line, lips rounded but not pouted; ㅜ has it below, lips pouted forward more clearly.
由 y 滑音快速过渡到 ㅗ，发音时嘴唇收圆并突出。: Glide quickly from a y sound to ㅗ, rounding and protruding your lips.
ㅗ 上方加双竖 = 给「o」加上 y 起音，写作「yo」=「哟」。: Adding double verticals above ㅗ = adding a y onset to 'o', written as 'yo' = 'yo'.
ㅛ 双竖在横线上方（圆嘴 yo）；ㅠ 双竖在横线下方（嘟嘴 yu）。: ㅛ has double verticals above the horizontal line (rounded-lip yo); ㅠ has them below (pouted-lip yu).
左短竖 上→下: left short vertical: top to bottom
右短竖 上→下: right short vertical: top to bottom
发音时嘴唇收得很圆很小，舌面后部高高抬起。: Pronounce with lips very rounded and small, tongue back raised high.
一横下面加一短竖 = 水滴往下掉，发嘟嘴的「u」。: A horizontal line with a short vertical below = a water drop falling, pronounced with pouted lips as 'u'.
ㅜ 嘴唇嘟起更明显（接近「乌」）；ㅗ 嘴唇圆但不嘟（接近「哦」）。形状上短竖位置: ㅜ has lips pouted more clearly (close to 'u'); ㅗ has lips rounded but not pouted (close to 'o'). The short vertical is positioned opposite vertically.
由 y 滑音快速过渡到 ㅜ，发音时嘴唇收得很圆很小。: Glide quickly from a y sound to ㅜ, keeping lips very rounded and small.
ㅜ 下方加双竖 = 给「u」加上 y 起音，写作「yu」=「由」。: Adding double verticals below ㅜ = adding a y onset to 'u', written as 'yu' = 'yu'.
ㅠ 双竖在横线下方（嘟嘴 yu）；ㅛ 双竖在横线上方（圆嘴 yo）。: ㅠ has two vertical lines below the horizontal line (pouty lips, yu); ㅛ has two vertical lines above the horizontal line (rounded lips, yo).
发音时嘴唇稍微扁平，舌面中部抬起，气流从舌面和硬腭之间通过。中文里没有完全对应的: When pronouncing, the lips are slightly flattened, the middle of the tongue rises, and air passes between the tongue surface and the hard palate. There's no exact equivalent in Chinese.
形状就是一条横线 = 嘴唇也压扁成一条线。: The shape is a horizontal line = lips also pressed flat into a line.
ㅡ 嘴角横向拉平、几乎不张嘴；ㅣ 嘴角横向拉开但比 ㅡ 更开，发清晰的「一」。: ㅡ Pull the corners of your mouth horizontally flat, barely opening your mouth; ㅣ Pull the corners wider than ㅡ, making a clear 'ee' sound.
舌尖抵住下齿龈，舌面前部高高抬起，接近硬腭前部形成缝隙，发清晰的「一」。: Press the tip of your tongue against the lower gum, raise the front of the tongue high, forming a gap near the front of the hard palate, and make a clear 'ee' sound.
一根竖线 = 一个人站立的形状，正好对应中文「一」的发音。: A vertical line = the shape of a person standing, which matches the Chinese 'one' sound.
ㅣ 嘴向两边拉开发「一」；ㅡ 嘴几乎不张、发压扁的「呃」。形状上一竖一横。: ㅣ Pull lips to both sides for 'ee'; ㅡ Barely open mouth for a flattened 'uh'. Shape-wise, one vertical and one horizontal.
发音时口型介于 ㅏ 和 ㅔ 之间（比 ㅏ 略小、比 ㅔ 略大），舌面位置较低；是: When pronouncing, the mouth shape is between ㅏ and ㅔ (slightly smaller than ㅏ, slightly larger than ㅔ), with the tongue lower; it's a monophthong [ɛ], don't read it as the diphthong 'ai'.
ㅏ + ㅣ → ae，嘴张得比 ㅏ 小一些: ㅏ + ㅣ → ae, mouth opens slightly smaller than ㅏ
现代口语 ㅐ 和 ㅔ 几乎同音，传统上 ㅐ 嘴更张开。: In modern speech, ㅐ and ㅔ sound almost identical; traditionally, ㅐ has a more open mouth.
先发 y 滑音再过渡到 ㅐ，与 ㅖ 在口语中同音。: Start with a y glide then transition to ㅐ, same sound as ㅖ in speech.
ㅑ + ㅣ → yae（口语缩略词 얘 = 这孩子）: ㅑ + ㅣ → yae (colloquial abbreviation 얘 = this kid)
现代口语 ㅒ 和 ㅖ 同音，靠词来分辨。: In modern speech, ㅒ and ㅖ sound the same; distinguish by the word.
发音时口型比 ㅐ 更小更扁，舌面位置更高，发短促清晰的「诶」。: When pronouncing, the mouth shape is smaller and flatter than ㅐ, the tongue position is higher, producing a short, clear "eh."
ㅓ + ㅣ → e，与 ㅐ 现代口语同音: ㅓ + ㅣ → e, same sound as ㅐ in modern speech
现代发音几乎相同，按词记忆即可。: Modern pronunciation is nearly identical; just memorize by word.
发音时口型介于 ㅕ 和 ㅣ 之间，舌面位置较高。: When pronouncing, the mouth shape is between ㅕ and ㅣ, with a higher tongue position.
ㅕ + ㅣ → ye，出现在 예/계/시계 等词: ㅕ + ㅣ → ye, appears in words like 예/계/시계
由 ㅗ 和 ㅏ 结合而成，发音时先发 ㅗ 的音然后迅速过渡到 ㅏ。: Formed by combining ㅗ and ㅏ; when pronouncing, first make the ㅗ sound then quickly transition to ㅏ.
ㅘ 收尾是 ㅏ；ㅙ 收尾是 ㅐ。: ㅘ ends with ㅏ; ㅙ ends with ㅐ.
右短横 左→右: short horizontal stroke, left to right
发音时口型介于 ㅘ 和 ㅐ 之间，口语与 ㅚ/ㅞ 同音。: The mouth shape is between ㅘ and ㅐ; in speech, it sounds the same as ㅚ/ㅞ.
ㅙ/ㅚ/ㅞ 现代口语全部同音 we。: ㅙ/ㅚ/ㅞ are all pronounced as 'we' in modern speech.
中短横 左→右: Short horizontal stroke, left to right
现代口语读 we，标准音为圆唇单元音 [ø]。: In modern speech it's 'we', but the standard sound is the rounded vowel [ø].
ㅚ/ㅙ/ㅞ 现代口语全部同音。: ㅚ/ㅙ/ㅞ are all pronounced the same in modern speech.
由 ㅜ（现代口语中滑至 ㅗ 类似）和 ㅓ 结合而成，发音时嘴唇稍微收圆。: Formed by combining ㅜ (which in modern speech glides toward ㅗ) and ㅓ; round your lips slightly when pronouncing.
ㅝ 收尾是 ㅓ；ㅞ 收尾是 ㅔ。: ㅝ ends with ㅓ; ㅞ ends with ㅔ.
发音时口型介于 ㅝ 和 ㅔ 之间，与 ㅚ/ㅙ 同音。: The mouth shape is between ㅝ and ㅔ, and it sounds the same as ㅚ/ㅙ.
ㅞ/ㅚ/ㅙ 现代口语全部同音。: ㅞ/ㅚ/ㅙ are all pronounced the same in modern speech.
先嘟起嘴唇发 ㅜ，再快速滑到 ㅣ，整体接近中文「威」。: Pucker your lips for ㅜ, then quickly glide to ㅣ — overall it sounds like Chinese 'wēi'.
ㅟ 收尾是 ㅣ（清亮 i）；ㅚ 收尾偏 e。: ㅟ ends with ㅣ (a clear i); ㅚ ends closer to e.
先发 ㅡ 扁嘴再快速滑到 ㅣ，词中位置常省略。: Start with ㅡ with flat lips, then quickly glide to ㅣ; it's often dropped in the middle of words.
ㅡ + ㅣ → ui（助词 의 表示\"的\"）: ㅡ + ㅣ → ui (the particle 의 means "of")
助词位置常读成 ㅔ（如 우리의 → 우리에）。: The particle is often pronounced as ㅔ (e.g., 우리의 → 우리에).
发音时舌根紧贴软腭阻塞气流，然后突然放开使气流爆破而出，类似中文「哥」的声母。: When pronouncing, the back of the tongue blocks airflow at the soft palate, then releases suddenly to create a burst, similar to the initial consonant of Chinese "gē."
ㄱ 不送气；ㅋ 强烈送气。: ㄱ is unaspirated; ㅋ is strongly aspirated.
一笔勾 顶横→右竖: one stroke: top horizontal → right vertical
发音时舌尖抵住上齿龈阻碍气流并通过鼻腔发出声音，类似中文「呢」的声母。: When pronouncing, the tip of the tongue touches the upper gum to block airflow and sound comes through the nose, similar to the initial consonant of Chinese "ne."
像一个角，舌头抵上颚的形状: shaped like a horn, with the tongue touching the palate
ㄴ 鼻音从鼻腔出；ㄷ 口腔短促爆破。: ㄴ is a nasal sound from the nose; ㄷ is a short burst from the mouth.
一笔勾 左竖→底横: one stroke: left vertical → bottom horizontal
发音时舌尖抵住上齿龈阻塞气流然后突然放开使气流爆破而出，类似中文「的」的声母。: When pronouncing, the tip of the tongue blocks airflow at the upper gum, then releases suddenly to create a burst, similar to the initial consonant of Chinese "de."
ㄷ 不送气；ㅌ 强烈送气。: ㄷ is unaspirated; ㅌ is strongly aspirated.
发音时舌尖卷起接触或接近硬腭后部发出颤音或边音。元音间为弹舌音 [ɾ]，收音位置: When pronouncing, the tip of the tongue curls up to touch or approach the back of the hard palate to produce a trill or lateral sound. Between vowels it's a flap [ɾ], and in final position it's a lateral [l]. Chinese has no exact equivalent; "la" is closest but not precise.
像蜿蜒的小路 → 舌尖像路一样弹过去: Like a winding path → the tongue flicks across like a road
ㄹ 弹舌或侧音；ㄴ 鼻音从鼻腔出。: ㄹ is a flap or lateral sound; ㄴ is a nasal sound from the nasal cavity.
发音时双唇紧闭阻塞气流然后通过鼻腔发出声音，类似中文「妈」的声母。: Close both lips to block airflow, then release through the nose, similar to the initial consonant of Chinese 'ma' (妈).
像一个口字的形状: like the shape of the character 口
ㅁ 鼻音持续；ㅂ 双唇短促爆破。: ㅁ is a sustained nasal; ㅂ is a short bilabial burst.
发音时双唇紧闭阻塞气流然后突然放开使气流爆破而出，类似中文「波」的声母。: Close both lips to block airflow, then release suddenly for a burst, similar to the initial consonant of Chinese 'bo' (波).
像一个水桶的形状: like the shape of a bucket
ㅂ 不送气；ㅍ 强烈送气。: ㅂ is unaspirated; ㅍ is strongly aspirated.
发音时舌尖抵住下齿背靠近齿龈阻碍气流并从舌尖和齿龈间空隙中流出；遇 ㅣ 和 y: Place the tongue tip against the lower teeth near the gums to block airflow, then let it escape through the gap; before ㅣ and y-series semivowels (ㅑ/ㅕ/ㅛ/ㅠ), it palatalizes to [ɕ] (like 'sh').
像一座山的形状: like the shape of a mountain
ㅅ 是摩擦音；ㅈ 是爆破+摩擦的塞擦音。: ㅅ is a fricative; ㅈ is an affricate (stop + fricative).
作初声时不发音，只是占位；作终声时发 ng。: Silent as an initial, just a placeholder; pronounced as 'ng' as a final.
哥哥（妹称）: Older brother (said by a younger sister)
ㅇ 初声不发音；ㅎ 喉部送气。: ㅇ is silent as an initial; ㅎ is aspirated from the throat.
舌面贴硬腭爆破+摩擦，类似英语 jeep 的 j。: Tongue against hard palate, plosive + fricative, similar to 'j' in English 'jeep'.
像一个人伸出手臂: Like a person extending an arm
ㅈ 不送气；ㅊ 强烈送气。: ㅈ is unaspirated; ㅊ is strongly aspirated.
舌面贴硬腭爆破+强送气，不卷舌，类似中文\"七\"的声母 [tɕʰ]。: Tongue against hard palate, plosive with strong aspiration, not retroflex, similar to the initial [tɕʰ] in Chinese 'qi'.
ㅈ 加一短横 → 送气版: ㅈ plus a short stroke → aspirated version
ㅊ 强送气；ㅈ 不送气。: ㅊ is strongly aspirated; ㅈ is unaspirated.
发音时舌根贴紧软腭阻塞气流然后突然放开并送气发出声音，类似英语 key 的 k。: The tongue root presses against the soft palate to block airflow, then releases with aspiration, similar to 'k' in English 'key'.
ㄱ 加一中横 → 送气版: Add a horizontal stroke to ㄱ → aspirated version
ㅋ 强送气；ㄱ 不送气。: ㅋ is strongly aspirated; ㄱ is not aspirated.
发音时舌尖抵住上齿龈阻塞气流然后突然放开并送气发出声音，类似中文「他」的声母。: When pronouncing, the tip of the tongue blocks airflow at the upper gum, then releases suddenly with aspiration, similar to the initial consonant of Chinese 'ta' (他).
ㄷ 加一中横 → 送气版: Add a horizontal stroke to ㄷ → aspirated version
ㅌ 强送气；ㄷ 不送气。: ㅌ is strongly aspirated; ㄷ is not aspirated.
发音方法与 ㅂ 相同但力度更强，为送气音，类似英语 pin 的 p。: Pronounced like ㅂ but with more force, aspirated, similar to the 'p' in English 'pin'.
ㅍ 强送气；ㅂ 不送气。: ㅍ is strongly aspirated; ㅂ is not aspirated.
发音时舌根和软腭放松让气流从口腔自由呼出产生摩擦声，类似中文「哈」的声母。: When pronouncing, relax the back of the tongue and soft palate to let air flow freely out of the mouth, creating friction, similar to the initial consonant of Chinese 'ha' (哈).
上方一点+一横+下方圆圈: a dot on top + a horizontal stroke + a circle below
ㅎ 喉部明显送气；ㅇ 初声完全不发音。: ㅎ has clear aspiration from the throat; ㅇ is silent as an initial consonant.
声带紧绷，不送气，比 ㄱ 更用力的\"嘎\"。: Vocal cords are tense, not aspirated, a stronger 'ga' than ㄱ.
ㄲ 紧不送气；ㅋ 强送气。: ㄲ is tense and not aspirated; ㅋ is strongly aspirated.
声带紧绷，不送气，比 ㄷ 更用力的\"哒\"。: Vocal cords tense, unaspirated, a stronger 'da' than ㄷ.
ㄸ 紧不送气；ㅌ 强送气。: ㄸ is tense and unaspirated; ㅌ is strongly aspirated.
声带紧绷，不送气，比 ㅂ 更用力的\"吧\"。: Vocal cords tense, unaspirated, a stronger 'ba' than ㅂ.
ㅃ 紧不送气；ㅍ 强送气。: ㅃ is tense and unaspirated; ㅍ is strongly aspirated.
声带紧绷的摩擦音，比 ㅅ 更短促有力。: A tense fricative with a tight vocal cord, shorter and more forceful than ㅅ.
ㅅ 轻而短；ㅆ 紧而长（声门收紧，时长更长）。: ㅅ is light and short; ㅆ is tense and longer (glottis tightened, longer duration).
声带紧绷的塞擦音，比 ㅈ 更用力。: A tense affricate with a tight vocal cord, more forceful than ㅈ.
ㅉ 紧不送气；ㅊ 强送气。: ㅉ is tense and unaspirated; ㅊ is strongly aspirated.
10个基础元音，是韩语的发音基石。每个元音都由天、地、人三个元素演化而来。: The 10 basic vowels are the foundation of Korean pronunciation. Each vowel evolved from the three elements: heaven, earth, and human.
ㅓ嘴型扁平不圆唇，ㅗ嘴型圆拢像在吹小口哨: ㅓ: flat lips, not rounded. ㅗ: rounded lips, like blowing a soft whistle.
嘴型扁平，类似英语 but 中的 u: Flat lips, similar to the 'u' in English 'but'.
嘴不圆，像惊讶时微微张嘴: Lips not rounded, slightly open like in surprise.
嘴型圆拢，类似中文\"哦\": Rounded lips, similar to the Chinese '哦' (oh).
嘴巴嘟圆，像在吹蜡烛: Pucker lips round, like blowing out a candle.
ㅡ嘴角向两边拉，ㅜ嘴唇向前嘟起: ㅡ: pull corners of mouth to the sides. ㅜ: push lips forward.
嘴角向两边拉，类似拼音\"e\": Pull mouth corners to the sides, similar to the pinyin 'e'.
嘴唇向前嘟起，类似中文\"乌\": Push lips forward, similar to the Chinese '乌' (wu).
11个合成元音，由基础元音组合而成。掌握基础元音后，合成元音就是简单的拼合。: The 11 compound vowels are formed by combining basic vowels. Once you master the basic vowels, compound vowels are simple combinations.
两者在现代韩语中发音几乎相同。ㅐ嘴张得稍大一点，但日常会话中基本不分: The two sound almost identical in modern Korean. ㅐ is pronounced with a slightly wider mouth, but in daily conversation they're basically indistinguishable.
类似英语\"apple\"的a，嘴稍大: Similar to the 'a' in English 'apple', mouth slightly wider.
ㅏ+ㅣ=ae，嘴比ㅔ稍大: ㅏ+ㅣ=ae, mouth slightly wider than ㅔ.
类似英语\"bed\"的e，嘴稍小: Similar to the 'e' in English 'bed', mouth slightly smaller.
ㅓ+ㅣ=e，嘴比ㅐ稍小: ㅓ+ㅣ=e, mouth slightly smaller than ㅐ.
三者发音非常接近，现代口语几乎相同。ㅚ=ㅗ+ㅣ，ㅙ=ㅗ+ㅐ，ㅞ=ㅜ+ㅔ（类似英语: These three sound very similar, almost identical in modern speech. ㅚ=ㅗ+ㅣ, ㅙ=ㅗ+ㅐ, ㅞ=ㅜ+ㅔ (similar to 'we' in English 'wet').
现代口语读 [we]，与 ㅙ/ㅞ 几乎同音: In modern speech, pronounced [we], almost the same as ㅙ/ㅞ.
现代口语读 [we]，与 ㅚ/ㅞ 几乎同音: In modern speech, pronounced [we], almost identical to ㅚ/ㅞ
现代口语读 [we]，与 ㅚ/ㅙ 几乎同音: In modern speech, pronounced [we], almost identical to ㅚ/ㅙ
14个基础辅音（含5个送气音），模仿发音器官的形状创造。韩语辅音的关键是\"松紧: 14 basic consonants (including 5 aspirated ones), created by imitating the shape of the speech organs. The key to Korean consonants is "tenseness" and "aspiration."
ㄱ=轻声g(松音)，ㅋ=强送气k，ㄲ=喉部用力不送气(紧音): ㄱ = soft g (lax), ㅋ = strongly aspirated k, ㄲ = tense, no aspiration (fortis)
ㅂ=轻声b(松音)，ㅍ=强送气p，ㅃ=喉部用力不送气(紧音): ㅂ = soft b (lax), ㅍ = strongly aspirated p, ㅃ = tense, no aspiration (fortis)
ㅈ=轻声j(松音)，ㅊ=强送气ch，ㅉ=喉部用力不送气(紧音): ㅈ = soft j (lax), ㅊ = strongly aspirated ch, ㅉ = tense, no aspiration (fortis)
ㄷ=轻声d(松音)，ㅌ=强送气t，ㄸ=喉部用力不送气(紧音): ㄷ = soft d (lax), ㅌ = strongly aspirated t, ㄸ = tense, no aspiration (fortis)
5个紧音（双写辅音），发音时喉部肌肉紧张、声带紧闭。想象你在用力搬重物时的感觉。: 5 tense consonants (doubled consonants). When pronouncing, the throat muscles tighten and the vocal cords close. Imagine the feeling of straining to lift something heavy.
松音=放松、送气；紧音=用力、不送气。把手指放在喉结上感受震动差异: Lax = relaxed, aspirated; tense = forced, unaspirated. Put your fingers on your Adam's apple to feel the difference in vibration.
7种收音发音，是韩语区别于中文的重要特征。一个音节末尾的辅音不发全、只做口型。: 7 batchim sounds — a key feature that sets Korean apart from Chinese. A consonant at the end of a syllable isn't fully pronounced; you just form the mouth shape.
ㄱ系收音=舌根堵住，ㄷ系收音=舌尖堵住，ㅂ系收音=双唇堵住。都是只做口型不爆破: ㄱ-series batchim = blocked at the back of the tongue, ㄷ-series = blocked at the tip of the tongue, ㅂ-series = blocked at the lips. All are just mouth shapes with no release.
把前面学的字母拼起来，读真正的韩文单词。看到词 → 试着读 → 听发音验证。读完: Put the letters you've learned together and read real Korean words. See the word → try to read it → listen to verify. Finish these and you'll really be able to use Korean!
一个人站立，两臂展开: A person standing with arms outstretched
嘴张开比 ㅏ 小一些，舌位往后，发不圆唇的\"呃\"（类似英语 but 中的 u: Open your mouth slightly less than for ㅏ, pull your tongue back, and make an unrounded 'uh' (like the 'u' in English 'but'). Don't round your lips.
一竖左边一短横，与 ㅏ 镜像: A vertical line with a short horizontal stroke on the left, mirroring ㅏ

ㅓ 左边再加一短横，加 y 滑音: Add another short stroke to the left of ㅓ, plus a 'y' glide
一横上方加一短竖，像太阳冒出地平线；嘴型圆: A horizontal line with a short vertical stroke above it, like the sun rising over the horizon; round your lips
一横下方加一短竖，像滴下的水滴；嘴型嘟起: A horizontal line with a short vertical stroke below it, like a dripping drop of water; pucker your lips
由 y 滑音过渡到嘟嘴的 ㅜ，类似中文\"由\"。: Glide from a 'y' sound into a puckered ㅜ, similar to Chinese 'you'.
嘴角向两侧拉平发\"呃\"的短促音，无鼻音: Pull the corners of your mouth flat and make a short 'uh' sound, no nasal tone
像一条横线，嘴型扁平: Like a horizontal line, with flat lips
像一根竖线，嘴唇向两边拉: Like a vertical line, stretch your lips to both sides
嘴角向两侧拉开，比 ㅏ 开口略小，发短促的\"哎\"。现代口语与 ㅔ 同音: Pull the corners of your mouth apart, open slightly less than for ㅏ, and make a short 'eh'. In modern speech, it sounds the same as ㅔ.
ㅏ+ㅣ→ae，嘴张得比ㅏ小: ㅏ + ㅣ → ae, open your mouth less than for ㅏ
现代口语与 ㅖ 几乎同音，类似中文\"耶\"；多用于口语缩略（얘/걔/쟤）: In modern speech, it's almost the same as ㅖ, similar to Chinese 'ye'; often used in colloquial contractions (얘/걔/쟤)
嘴角向两侧适度拉开，发短促清晰的\"诶\"；现代口语与 ㅐ 同音: Pull the corners of your mouth apart moderately and make a short, clear 'eh'; in modern speech, it sounds the same as ㅐ.
ㅓ+ㅣ→e；现代口语与 ㅐ 同音: ㅓ + ㅣ → e; in modern speech, it sounds the same as ㅐ
类似中文\"耶\"；高频元音，出现在 예/계/시계/예의 等词: Similar to Chinese 'ye'; a high-frequency vowel found in words like 예/계/시계/예의
