韩国烘焙 · 面包被玩成本土艺术: Korean Baking · Bread Turned into a Local Art Form
韩国烘焙店不是西方复制版——단팥빵、메론빵、소보로 都是韩国原创，你在巴黎找不到: Korean bakeries aren't Western copies—단팥빵, 메론빵, and 소보로 are all Korean originals you won't find in Paris. Koreans have made bread their own.
巴黎贝甜韩国首店，此后面包文化爆发: Paris Baguette opened its first store in Korea, and bread culture exploded from there.
蛋糕按「号」算尺寸，1号约 15cm: Cakes are sized by "number," with No. 1 being about 15cm.
大部分烘焙店支持外卖，面包也送: Most bakeries offer delivery, and they'll even deliver bread.
韩国面包比日本还甜: Korean bread is even sweeter than Japanese bread.
甜度普遍高于日式——단팥빵 的红豆馅甜到齁，크림빵 的奶油挤到满出来。如果你不爱: It's generally sweeter than Japanese bread—단팥빵's red bean filling is cloyingly sweet, and 크림빵's cream is stuffed to overflowing. If you don't like sweet, go for 식빵 (toast) or 바게트 (baguette); those aren't sweet. Everything else is.
韩国人生日必吃蛋糕——不是自己买，是朋友订好送过来。用巧克力酱写「생일 축하합니: Koreans always have cake on birthdays—not bought for themselves, but ordered and delivered by friends. Writing "생일 축하합니다" in chocolate sauce is standard. "24시 케이크 배달" (24-hour cake delivery) is a legit industry in Korea.
面包店都帮你切: Bakeries will slice it for you
买吐司或法棍，店员会问「썰어드릴까요?」（要切吗？）。韩国人默认要切片——不切回: When you buy toast or a baguette, the staff will ask "썰어드릴까요?" (Want it sliced?). Koreans default to having it sliced—if not, you'd have to cut it at home, but home knives aren't great. It's free, so always say 네.
每家烘焙店有「굽는 시간」（出炉时间），通常早 7 点和下午 3 点。那时间去买: Every bakery has a "굽는 시간" (baking time), usually 7 AM and 3 PM. Go then, and the bread is still warm; if the staff are in a good mood, they'll throw in a free sample. With luck, you might even get fresh corner scraps.
韩国 파리바게뜨/뚜레쥬르 都嵌 카페 区——买面包配一杯 4,500 원美式，: Korean chains like Paris Baguette and Tous les Jours all have café sections—grab a pastry with a 4,500 won Americano and sit for two hours. That's the 'bbang-café' (bread café) culture: cheaper than indie cafés and the bread fills you up.
为什么韩国「菠萝包」叫「蜜瓜面包」？: Why is Korea's 'pineapple bun' called 'melon bread'?
外形像哈密瓜网纹。日语原名「メロンパン」直译，韩语沿用外来语「메론빵」。里面其实: It looks like a cantaloupe's netted skin. The Japanese name 'melon pan' was translated directly, and Korean borrowed it as 'melon-ppang.' There's actually no melon inside—it's cream or red bean filling. Pronounced: me-ron-ppang.
一种表面撒糖粒面粉粒的酥皮面包，源自日语「そぼろ」（松散）。韩国人下课人手一个，: A crumbly bread topped with sugar and flour granules, from the Japanese 'soboro' (crumbled). Korean students grab one after class—1,500 won and you're full. Unlike melon bread, soboro is coarser but flakier.
韩国面包店为什么都有咖啡机？: Why do Korean bakeries all have coffee machines?
韩国人认为「面包 = 早餐 = 咖啡」，缺了咖啡不完整。连锁品牌 파바 / 뚜쥬: Koreans see bread as breakfast and breakfast as coffee—it's incomplete without it. Chains like Pava and Tjou have long bundled bread + coffee into sets (8,000–12,000 won), cheaper than Starbucks and more filling.
想预订生日蛋糕。: I'd like to order a birthday cake.
「갓 나온 빵」= 刚出炉: 'Gat naon ppang' = fresh out of the oven
店员会主动推销「갓 나온 빵이에요」（刚出炉的）。这个词的余温能到 30 分钟后: Staff will push 'gat naon ppang-ieyo' (fresh out of the oven). That word's warmth lasts up to 30 minutes—the sooner you buy, the better it tastes.
在连锁店买 20,000 원 以上，问「선물 포장해 주세요」大部分免费提供缎带: At chains, spend over 20,000 won and ask 'seonmul pojanghae juseyo'—most give ribbon boxes for free. Indie shops may charge 500–1,000 won.
当日不卖完的面包晚 8 点后打对折。想省钱又不介意品质稍降的话，20:00 之后: Unsold bread gets 50% off after 8 PM. If you want to save money and don't mind slightly older bread, walk in after 20:00.
식(食·汉字)+빵(面包，源自葡语 pão)，一袋 6-8 片。: Sik (食, Sino-Korean) + ppang (bread, from Portuguese pão)—a loaf has 6–8 slices.
식(食)＝汉字「食」+ 빵(源自葡萄牙语 pão)＝「食用面包」，汉字+外来语组: Sik (食) = the Chinese character for 'food' + ppang (from Portuguese pão) = 'eating bread'—a Sino-Korean + loanword combo.
法语 croissant 音译，念时把 c 弱化：크루아상。记「牛角」形状。: Transliteration of French 'croissant'; soften the 'c' when pronouncing: 크루아상. Think of the 'horn' shape.
有红豆面包吗？: Do you have red bean bread?
国民面包，几乎每家烘焙都有。: A national bread, available at almost every bakery.
단(甜)+팥(红豆)+빵(面包)＝甜红豆面包，三个词拼一起，字面直译。: 단(sweet)+팥(red bean)+빵(bread)=sweet red bean bread; three words combined, literally translated.
日语そぼろ(松散)音译，表面撒着松散糖粒＝酥皮。: Transliteration of Japanese 'soboro' (loose); surface sprinkled with loose sugar granules = crumbly topping.
菠萝包还有吗？: Do you still have pineapple buns?
메론(melon)+빵(面包)，外形像哈密瓜网纹但没蜜瓜味。: 메론(melon)+빵(bread); looks like melon's netted pattern but has no melon flavor.
cake 音译成 케이크，三个音节拆开念：케-이-크。: 'Cake' transliterated as 케이크, broken into three syllables: 케-이-크.
预订 24 小时前更稳。: Ordering 24 hours in advance is safer.
생일(生日，汉字词)+케이크(蛋糕，外来语)，汉字+英文直接拼。: 생일(birthday, Sino-Korean)+케이크(cake, loanword); Sino-Korean + English directly combined.
法语 macaron 音译，念时鼻音消失：마-카-롱。: It's a transliteration of the French macaron; the nasal sound drops when pronounced: 마-카-롱.
타르트=tart（挞）；派另有其词 파이（pie），两者不同。: Tart = tart (挞); pie is a different word, 파이 (pie). They're different.
tart 音译，t 结尾在韩语里加 -르트 三音节：타-르-트。: Tart transliterated: the final 't' becomes -르트 in Korean, making three syllables: 타-르-트.
cookie 音译，念快就是쿠-키两音节，比中文「曲奇」还接近英文。: Cookie transliterated: said quickly it's two syllables, 쿠-키, even closer to English than the Chinese '曲奇'.
生日蛋糕/特殊尺寸需要。: Needed for birthday cakes or special sizes.
예약(豫约)＝汉字词，中文的「预约」！同源词，一次记住。: 예약 (豫约) is a Sino-Korean word, same as Chinese '预约'! Cognate—remember it once.
문구(文句)＝汉字词「文句」，即写在蛋糕上的字。: 문구 (文句) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'phrase'—the text written on a cake.
문구＝短句/贺词/标语；문장＝完整句子。蛋糕上写的一般是문구。: 문구 = short phrase/message/slogan; 문장 = full sentence. What's written on cakes is usually 문구.
外来语 pickup。也说「가지러 올게요」。: Loanword: pickup. You can also say '가지러 올게요'.
pickup 音译，念快跟英文几乎一样：픽-업。: Pickup transliterated: said quickly it sounds almost like English: 픽-업.
픽업＝你去店里取；배달＝店家送到家。蛋糕两种都可以。: 픽업 means you pick it up at the store; 배달 means the shop delivers it to your home. Either works for the cake.
「선물 포장」= 礼品包装，通常免费。: 「선물 포장」 means gift wrapping, usually free.
포장(包装)＝汉字词「包装」，同源直接记。: 포장 (包装) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'wrapping'—same origin, so just remember it directly.
面包店有微波炉，可以加热。: The bakery has a microwave, so you can heat it up.
데우다＝加热的动作。「데워 주세요」是最常听到的活用形。: 데우다 means the action of heating. '데워 주세요' is the most common conjugated form you'll hear.
달다的달和「달콤（甜蜜）」同根，甜字都从달来。: The 달 in 달다 shares a root with '달콤 (sweet),' so all sweetness comes from 달.
달다是基本形；단是修饰形，前置修饰名词：단 빵＝甜面包。: 달다 is the basic form; 단 is the modifying form placed before nouns: 단 빵 means 'sweet bread.'
有咸口面包吗？: Do you have any savory bread?
形容词，多修饰含奶酪/培根的面包。: An adjective, often used to describe bread with cheese or bacon.
짭짤＝拟态词，两个「짭」的重复暗示咸味在舌头上跳跃感。: 짭짤 is an onomatopoeic word—the repetition of '짭' suggests a salty sensation bouncing on the tongue.
形容外皮酥脆的口感。: Describes a crispy, crunchy texture on the outside.
바삭＝拟声词，模仿咬到脆物「咔嚓」的声音，바-사-크 三拍。: 바삭 is an onomatopoeia mimicking the 'crunch' sound of biting into something crispy—three beats: 바-사-크.
面包身软绵的常用词。: A common word for bread that's soft and fluffy.

인기(人氣)＝汉字词「人气」，+ 있는(有)＝有人气的。汉字+韩语组合。: 인기 (人氣) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'popularity,' + 있는 (have) = popular. A Sino-Korean + native Korean combination.
数字「둘」在量词前变成「두」（두 개）；「하나」变成「한」（한 개）。单独说时保: The number '둘' becomes '두' before a counter (두 개); '하나' becomes '한' (한 개). When said alone, they keep their original forms.
（更正式）请给两个可颂。: (More formal) Please give me two croissants.
这里是双主语句：「이거」是主题（这个东西），「맛이」才是真正的主语（味道）——「: This is a double-subject sentence: '이거' is the topic (this thing), while '맛이' is the actual subject (flavor)—the possessive -의 in '이거의 맛이' is omitted, as '이거의 맛' sounds awkward.

「-고 싶다」只能对第一人称用。第三人称要用「-고 싶어하다」：동생이 예약하고: '-고 싶다' is only for first person. For third person, use '-고 싶어하다': 동생이 예약하고 싶어해요.

烤肉店 · 韩国的社交仪式: Korean BBQ · A Social Ritual in Korea
韩国烤肉不是「餐厅吃饭」——是一种社交仪式。围着烤盘、喝烧酒、剪刀剪肉、生菜包肉: Korean BBQ isn't just 'eating out'—it's a social ritual. Gathering around the grill, drinking soju, cutting meat with scissors, wrapping it in lettuce, and chatting while you cook and drink—this is the soul of a Korean get-together.
五花肉——国民烤肉，人均 1-2 人份: Samgyeopsal—the national BBQ, 1-2 servings per person
韩国烤肉按 인분（人份）点——最少 1 인분起，通常 150-200 克。两个人: Korean BBQ is ordered by in-bun (servings)—minimum 1 in-bun, usually 150-200 grams. Two people ordering 2-3 in-bun is just right. **You can't order just 1 serving for two people**—the staff will remind you '최소 1인분씩' (at least 1 serving per person).
店员帮你烤 + 剪: Staff grills and cuts for you
韩式烤肉不是「自己烤」——大部分店店员帮你烤，烤好用剪刀（가위）剪成小块，夹到盘: Korean BBQ isn't 'DIY grilling'—at most places, the staff grills for you, then cuts the meat into bite-sized pieces with scissors (가위) and puts them on your plate. All you do is eat. High-end places offer full service; budget spots might have you flip the meat yourself.
상추 包肉 · 正确吃法: Sangchu (lettuce) wraps · How to eat properly
拿一片生菜 → 放一块肉 → 一点饭 → 蒜 → 包饭酱（쌈장）→ 辣椒 → 包: Take a lettuce leaf → add a piece of meat → some rice → garlic → ssamjang (쌈장) → chili → wrap it up and eat it in one bite. This is called '싸서 먹다' (eating wrapped). **One whole wrap per bite, never half**—a Korean table taboo.
烤肉配 소주 是标配——360ml 一瓶，16-20 度，1,700 원。规矩：: BBQ with soju is a must—360ml per bottle, 16-20% ABV, 1,700 won. Rules: when an elder or senior pours your drink, receive it with both hands; pouring your own drink is called 'jajak' (self-pour) and is considered rude when drinking with others. For toasts, say 'geonbae,' and turn your head to cover your mouth when drinking.
跟长辈喝，酒杯要低于对方；单手拿酒杯是失礼，双手拿最保险。第一杯必须一口干（원샷: When drinking with elders, keep your glass lower than theirs; holding it with one hand is rude, two hands is safest. The first shot must be downed in one go (원샷). If you're not familiar with these rules, just follow along—Korean drinking tables are a social exam.
为什么韩国烤肉用剪刀不用刀？: Why does Korean BBQ use scissors instead of a knife?
朝鲜时代宫廷用银筷（试毒），刀被视为「武器」不宜上餐桌。加上剪刀更能精准控制肉片: In the Joseon Dynasty, the royal court used silver chopsticks (to test for poison), and knives were seen as 'weapons' unfit for the dining table. Scissors also allow precise control of meat size without needing a cutting board. Today, scissors are a must for BBQ—a uniquely Korean tableware culture.
삼겹살 和 목살 到底选哪个？: Which to pick: 삼겹살 or 목살?
삼겹살 = 五花肉（有肥肉，香但腻）；목살 = 猪颈肉（瘦肉多，嚼劲）。年轻人选: 삼겹살 = pork belly (fatty, fragrant but greasy); 목살 = pork neck (leaner, chewy). Young people pick 삼겹살 (flavor), middle-aged pick 목살 (healthier). First time at a BBQ place, order 2 삼겹살 + 1 목살 to try both.
상추 包肉怎么包才不会漏？: How to wrap meat in 상추 without it leaking?
生菜内侧朝上摊平，肉/饭/蒜/酱按顺序叠，**从下往上折**——不是像卷饼那样卷: Lay the lettuce inner side up, stack meat/rice/garlic/sauce in order, **fold from bottom up**—not like rolling a wrap. Just fold 3 times and eat it in one bite. The first time sauce will leak, but by the 5th time you'll be a pro.
倒酒双手接: Receive the pour with both hands
喝소주或啤酒，长辈/上级倒酒要双手接杯。年轻人之间可单手，但双手更礼貌。: When drinking 소주 or beer, if an elder or superior pours, receive the glass with both hands. Between young people one hand is fine, but two hands is more polite.
喝소주时对着长辈/上级要侧身转脸再喝，别正面直视对方喝。这是韩国酒桌礼仪的核心。: When drinking 소주, turn your body and face away from elders/superiors—don't drink facing them directly. This is the core of Korean drinking etiquette.
AA 或轮流请: Split the bill or take turns paying
「N 빵」= AA 制。或者「제가 낼게요」（我请）+ 下次别人请。学生党/朋友: 'N 빵' = going Dutch. Or '제가 낼게요' (I'll pay) + someone else pays next time. Common among students and friends.
삼겹(三겹)+살(肉)=三层肉，肥瘦相间的猪腹肉。拆字对应中文「五花」。: 삼겹 (three layers) + 살 (meat) = three-layer meat, the fatty-and-lean pork belly. The characters correspond to Chinese '五花'.
삼겹살肥瘦相间(五花肉)；목살瘦肉多(猪颈肉)。第一次点 삼겹살 2 + 목살: 삼겹살 is fatty and lean (pork belly); 목살 is leaner (pork neck). First time, order 2 삼겹살 + 1 목살 to taste both.
목(脖子)+살(肉)=猪颈部的肉。跟삼겹살同构词法（部位+살），瘦肉多有嚼劲。: 목 (neck) + 살 (meat) = meat from the pig's neck. Same word structure as 삼겹살 (part + 살), leaner and chewy.
소(牛,固有词)+고기(肉)=牛肉。同套构词还有 돼지고기(猪)/닭고기(鸡)。: 소 (native word for cow) + 고기 (meat) = beef. Similar compounds include 돼지고기 (pork) and 닭고기 (chicken). Grilled beef is pricier, starting at 40,000–60,000 won.
닭(鸡)+고기(肉)=鸡肉。烤肉店主打猪牛，鸡一般去 치킨집(炸鸡店)。: 닭 (chicken) + 고기 (meat) = chicken. BBQ places focus on pork and beef; for chicken, you'd go to a 치킨집 (fried chicken place).
굽다联想「烤面包/烤鱼」都用同一动词。ㅂ→우 不规则：굽+어→구워。: 굽다 is used for grilling bread or fish alike. ㅂ→우 irregular: 굽+어→구워.
굽다=你/店员主动去烤(动作)；익다=肉在烤盘上变熟(状态)。「구워주세요」是请: 굽다 means you or the staff actively grill (action); 익다 means the meat cooks on the grill (state). '구워주세요' is a request, '익었어요' is a judgment.
익다=自然变熟。想成「熟」的过去时「익었어요」最常听——店员端上桌就说这句。: 익다 means to cook naturally. Think of it as the past tense '익었어요'—you'll hear it most when staff bring it to the table.
固有词。朝鲜宫廷视刀为武器不上桌，剪刀替代——韩国烤肉必用가위，文化独有。: Native word. In the Joseon court, knives were seen as weapons and not placed on the table; scissors replaced them—Korean BBQ always uses 가위, a unique cultural trait.
불(火)+판(板)=烧焦时喊「불판 갈아 주세요」（换烤盘），店员会免费换新的。: 불(火)+판(板)=When it burns, shout '불판 갈아 주세요' (change the grill plate), and the staff will replace it for free.
집다(夹)+게(工具后缀)=夹子。烤肉店翻面工具，跟가위配套用。: 집다(to pick up)+게(tool suffix)=Tongs. The flipping tool at BBQ restaurants, used together with scissors.
상추=包肉专用生菜，比中式沙拉生菜更厚更脆。免费续，尽管开口要。: 상추=Lettuce for wrapping meat, thicker and crunchier than Chinese salad lettuce. Free refills, just ask.
상추=绿色圆叶生菜；깻잎=带薄荷香的锯齿叶，两者常搭配一起端上。: 상추=Green round-leaf lettuce; 깻잎=Serrated leaves with a minty aroma, often served together.
大酱 + 辣椒酱混合。: A mix of soybean paste and gochujang.
쌈(包)+장(酱)=包肉专用酱。쌈싸다=包饭，酱按用途命名，一秒记住。: 쌈(wrap)+장(sauce)=Sauce for wrapping meat. 쌈싸다=to wrap food, the sauce is named by its use, easy to remember.
공기(小碗)+밥(饭)=一碗饭。공기专指不锈钢小碗（跟「空气」同音但不同源），一: 공기(small bowl)+밥(rice)=A bowl of rice. 공기 specifically refers to the stainless steel small bowl (homophone with 'air' but different origin), about 1,500-2,000 won per bowl.
김치=韩国国民配菜，烤肉店免费无限续。烤过的김치더 香，值得尝试。: 김치=Korea's national side dish, free unlimited refills at BBQ restaurants. Grilled kimchi is even more fragrant, worth trying.
烤肉配汤最佳。: Best paired with soup at a BBQ.
된장(大酱)+찌개(炖汤)=浓稠版味噌汤。吃完油腻烤肉喝一口最解腻。: 된장(soybean paste)+찌개(stew)=A thicker version of miso soup. A sip after greasy BBQ is the best palate cleanser.
싸다=用叶子包起来。쌈장/쌈밥都由这个动词衍生。: 싸다 = to wrap with leaves. 쌈장 and 쌈밥 both come from this verb.
同形异义：싸다①=包(动词)；싸다②=便宜(形容词)。餐桌上永远是①，价格牌上才: Homonym: 싸다① = to wrap (verb); 싸다② = cheap (adjective). At the table it's always ①, on the price tag it's ②.
계산서(计算书)=汉字词，中文的「计算书/账单」。结账三连：계산서→카드로요→잘: 계산서 (bill) is a Sino-Korean word, like Chinese '计算书/账单'. The three-step checkout: 계산서 → 카드로요 → 잘 먹었습니다.
자르다=切/剪。르 不规则：자르+아→잘라。搭配「가위로 잘라주세요」是烤肉店高: 자르다 = to cut/slice. '르' irregular: 자르 + 아 → 잘라. '가위로 잘라주세요' is a common phrase at BBQ places.
包完一口吞。: Wrap it up and eat it in one bite.
한(一)+입(嘴/口)=一口。쌈必须一口吃，咬半口是餐桌禁忌。: 한 (one) + 입 (mouth/bite) = one bite. Ssam must be eaten in one bite; biting it in half is a table taboo.
더(更/再)+시키다(点菜)=加点。同伴间问「더 시킬까?」半语更自然。: 더 (more/again) + 시키다 (to order) = to order more. Asking '더 시킬까?' in banmal is more natural among friends.
시키다=口语加点(店内)；주문하다=正式下单(菜单/网上)。桌边加菜用시키다更地: 시키다 = casual ordering (in-store); 주문하다 = formal ordering (menu/online). For adding dishes at the table, 시키다 is more natural.
请给我两人份五花肉。: Please give me two servings of pork belly.
烤肉份数用「인분」（人份），不是「그릇」（碗）或「접시」（盘）——「삼겹살 2그: For grilled meat portions, use '인분' (servings), not '그릇' (bowl) or '접시' (plate) — '삼겹살 2그릇' is wrong; only soups/rice dishes use 그릇. Attach numbers directly: 1인분/2인분/3인분.
（更正式）请给两人份五花肉。: (More formal) Please give me two servings of pork belly.
굽다 ㅂ 不规则：굽+아→구워，不能写成「굽아 주세요」。同类还有 돕다→도와、: 굽다 is ㅂ irregular: 굽+아→구워, not '굽아 주세요'. Similar: 돕다→도와, 줍다→주워.
（极度礼貌）能帮我烤好吗？: (Very polite) Could you grill it for me?
想让店员帮剪肉时: When asking staff to cut meat
자르다 르 不规则：자르+아→잘라(ㄹ 复写脱ㅡ)，不能写成「자르아 주세요」。: 자르다 is 르 irregular: 자르+아→잘라 (ㄹ doubles, ㅡ drops), not '자르아 주세요'. Similar: 모르다→몰라, 다르다→달라.
（极度礼貌）能帮我用剪刀剪吗？: (Very polite) Could you cut it with scissors for me?
（半语，对同伴）用剪刀剪一下。: (Banmal, to friend) Cut it with scissors.
想续配菜时: When you want more side dishes
「더」放名词后而不是前——「상추 더 주세요」✓，「더 상추 주세요」✗。汉语「: '더' goes after the noun, not before — '상추 더 주세요' ✓, '더 상추 주세요' ✗. Chinese '多给' has the opposite structure from Korean.
（极度礼貌）能再多给一点生菜吗？: (Very polite) Could I have a bit more lettuce?
这个没熟。再烤一下。: This isn't cooked. Grill it a bit more.
发现肉没熟时: When you find the meat isn't cooked
判断肉熟用「익다」不用「굽다」——「안 구웠어요」是「（我）没烤」，意思完全不同: To say meat is cooked, use '익다' not '굽다' — '안 구웠어요' means 'I didn't grill it,' which is totally different. Say '안 익었어요' (not cooked yet).
（更礼貌）这个好像还没熟，能再烤一下吗？: (More polite) This doesn't seem cooked yet. Could you grill it a bit more?
（半语，对同伴）这个还没熟，再烤下。: (Banmal, to a friend) This isn't cooked yet. Grill it more.
和同伴商量要不要加菜时: When discussing with friends whether to order more
「-(으)ㄹ까요?」是征询同伴意见，主语是「我们」；「-(으)실래요?」才是问对: '-(으)ㄹ까요?' asks for your companion's opinion, with 'we' as the subject; '-(으)실래요?' asks if the other person wants something, with them as the subject. When deciding to order more at a BBQ table, the former is more natural.
（对长辈更礼貌）您还要加点吗？: (More polite to elders) Would you like a bit more?
（半语，对朋友）再点点？: (Banmal, to a friend) Order a bit more?
吃完想买单时: When you want to pay after eating
「계산서」是账单，「영수증」是收据（发票）——刷卡后才拿到영수증，别混用。也可省: '계산서' is the bill, '영수증' is the receipt—you get 영수증 only after paying by card, so don't mix them up. You can also shorten it to '계산할게요' to just settle the bill.
（更正式）麻烦给我账单。: (More formal) Could I have the bill, please?
「数字 + 명이요」是人数最简答法。: 'Number + 명이요' is the simplest way to state the number of people.
「数字 + 인분이요」是烤肉店专用回答。: 'Number + 인분이요' is the standard answer at a BBQ restaurant.
「N + 数量요」是加菜最简答法。: 'N + quantity + 요' is the simplest way to order more.
服务员告知可以吃时的礼貌回应。: A polite response when the server says it's ready to eat.
「충분해요」= 「够了」是委婉拒绝。: '충분해요' = 'I've had enough' is a polite way to decline.

两碗米饭一份大酱汤。: Two bowls of rice and one soybean paste stew.
谢谢。哇，真好吃！: Thanks. Wow, this is really good!

韩国是全世界极少数有 24 小时书店的国家——真的有店员、有咖啡、有座位、凌晨: Korea is one of the few countries in the world with 24-hour bookstores—real ones with staff, coffee, seats, and lights on at 3 AM. Koreans have turned bookstores into 'late-night sanctuaries.'
韩国最大连锁书店，光化门总店 24h 营业: Korea's largest bookstore chain, Gwanghwamun flagship open 24h
书咖啡——买书可以坐着喝: Book café—buy a book and sit with a drink
韩国畅销书均价，比中国贵 3-4 倍: Average bestseller price, 3-4x more expensive than China
不是噱头——真的有人在凌晨 2 点买书。考试复习的学生、失眠的上班族、分手后散心: Not a gimmick—people really buy books at 2 AM. Students cramming for exams, insomniac office workers, young people clearing their heads after a breakup. Two major brands: **영풍문고** (Youngpoong) and **교보문고** (Kyobo). The Gwanghwamun Kyobo flagship has been open 24 hours since 1981.
韩国书店不是「买完就走」——里面有 북카페，从书架上拿一本书，坐下点一杯咖啡，读: Korean bookstores aren't 'grab and go' — they have book cafés inside. Take a book off the shelf, sit down, order a coffee, read it, and put it back. **You don't have to buy it.** Some people treat bookstores like libraries — one Americano and you can sit all day, no one kicks you out.
书价贵，翻 30 分钟再买: Books are pricey — flip through for 30 minutes before buying
韩国一本书 13,000-18,000 원（70-100 元人民币），比中国贵: A Korean book costs 13,000–18,000 won (70–100 RMB), 3–4 times pricier than in China. So Koreans stand and flip through a book for 30 minutes before buying, to make sure it's worth it. Used bookstores (헌책방) are common near universities, with old books at 50–70% off.
韩语学习书在「한국어」区: Korean learning books are in the '한국어' section
书店外语学习区叫「외국어」（外语），韩语学习书**不在那里**——在「한국어」区: The foreign language section is called '외국어' (foreign languages), but Korean learning books are **not there** — they're in the '한국어' section, alongside Korean-as-a-foreign-language textbooks. TOPIK prep, language institute materials, and Korean grammar books are all here. Look for the '한국어교재' label.
买书想送礼说「선물 포장해 주세요」，店员用漂亮纸+丝带包好。不加钱。买书送人在: To gift a book, say '선물 포장해 주세요' and the staff will wrap it in pretty paper with a ribbon — no extra charge. Giving books as gifts is a classy move in Korea — it shows more thought than cosmetics or chocolate.
为什么韩国书店 24 小时营业？: Why are Korean bookstores open 24 hours?
1981 年 교보문고 开业时创始人 신용호 的理念——「知识不该有营业时间」。: When Kyobo Bookstore opened in 1981, founder Shin Yong-ho's philosophy was — 'knowledge shouldn't have business hours.' The Gwanghwamun flagship has never closed in over 40 years, except for a brief adjustment during COVID. It's become part of Korean culture, more symbolic than commercial.
교보문고 和 영풍문고 哪个大？: Which is bigger: Kyobo or Youngpoong?
교보 更大——全国 20+ 家店，藏书 230 万+；영풍 有 15+ 家店，藏: Kyobo is bigger—20+ stores nationwide, 2.3M+ books; Youngpoong has 15+ stores, 1M books. Kyobo is more commercial (café/stationery sections), Youngpoong feels more like a pure bookstore. Both are in central Seoul.
韩国电子书普及率只有 10%——远低于欧美。原因：韩国人重视「读书仪式感」，翻纸: E-book adoption in Korea is only 10% — far lower than in the West. The reason: Koreans value the 'ritual of reading' — flipping paper pages with coffee is part of the culture. Plus, Korean e-book content is limited (low digitization rate of Korean-language books), and e-readers are far less popular than in Japan.
在找韩语学习书。: I'm looking for Korean learning books.
韩国书店允许在店里读书，甚至读完不买也 OK。想坐着读几十页都行。找喜欢再决定买: Korean bookstores let you read in the store, and it's fine to read without buying. You can sit and read dozens of pages. Decide to buy only if you like it.
买书想送礼说「선물 포장해 주세요」，店员用漂亮纸+丝带包好。不加钱。: To gift a book, say '선물 포장해 주세요' and the staff will wrap it in pretty paper with a ribbon — no extra charge.
大书店有「외국어」（外语）专区。英/日/中书都有。韩语初学者可看「어린이 책」（: Large bookstores have a '외국어' (foreign language) section with English, Japanese, and Chinese books. Korean beginners can use '어린이 책' (children's books) for reading practice.
固有词一音节「chaek」，收音 ㄱ 轻含在喉咙里，联想中文「册」的册页感。: Native one-syllable word 'chaek' — the final ㄱ is lightly held in the throat. Think of the Chinese character '册' (book) and its page-like feel.
Bestseller 音译，念时把 st 拆开：베-스-트-셀-러，五音节一个都: Bestseller transliterated — when pronouncing, split the 'st': 베-스-트-셀-러, all five syllables, don't skip any.
신(新)+간(刊)=汉字词「新刊」，跟中文完全同源，一眼认出。: 신(新) + 간(刊) = Sino-Korean '신간' (new publication), completely cognate with Chinese — you'll recognize it at a glance.
신간=刚出版的新书；중고책=用过的旧书，两个反义词一起记。: 신간 = newly published book; 중고책 = used book. Memorize these two antonyms together.
추(推)+천(薦)=汉字词「推薦」，跟中文「推荐」同字同序。: 추(推) + 천(薦) = Sino-Korean '추천' (recommendation), same characters and order as Chinese '推荐'.
중고(中古)+책(书)=旧书。「中古」跟日语同源，指用过的东西。: 중고(中古) + 책(book) = used book. '중고' shares its origin with Japanese, meaning something secondhand.
중고책偏汉字词书面感；헌책更口语，大学附近「헌책방」（二手书店）招牌多用헌책。: 중고책 has a more formal Sino-Korean feel; 헌책 is more colloquial. Near universities, signs for '헌책방' (used bookstore) mostly use 헌책.
소설(小説)=汉字词，소→小，설→説，一次拿下两字。: 소설(小説) is a Sino-Korean word: 소→小, 설→説. Two characters, one go.
Essay 音译，念快就是에-세-이三音节，跟英文几乎一致。: Essay is transliterated—say it fast and it's 에-세-이, three syllables, almost identical to English.
汉字词「自己啓発」，韩国书店年度畅销榜必有一半是这类。: The Sino-Korean word is 자기계발 (自己啓発). Half of Korea's annual bestseller list is always this genre.
자기(自己)+계발(啓発)=「开发自己」，四字汉字词，跟励志书完美对应。: 자기(自己)+계발(啓発)= 'develop yourself'—a four-character Sino-Korean word that maps perfectly to self-help books.
한국(韩国)+어(语)=汉字词「韩国语」，学韩语的你必背第一词。: 한국(韩国)+어(语)= Sino-Korean 'Korean language'—the first word you must memorize as a Korean learner.
요리(料理)=汉字词，跟日语「料理」同源同意，一词记两语。: 요리(料理) is Sino-Korean, same origin and meaning as Japanese '料理'—one word, two languages.
좌석(座席)=汉字词「座席」，中文也说「座席」！同源同意。: 좌석(座席) is Sino-Korean—Chinese also says '座席'! Same origin, same meaning.
좌석是汉字词偏书面；자리是固有词更口语，问店员「자리 있어요?」比「좌석 있어요: 좌석 is Sino-Korean and more formal; 자리 is native Korean and more colloquial. Asking a staff member '자리 있어요?' sounds more natural than '좌석 있어요?'
外来语 cafe。书店里的 카페 区通常在角落。: Loanword: cafe. The 카페 area in a bookstore is usually tucked in a corner.
Cafe 外来语，音译两音节：카-페，跟英文一样。: Cafe is a loanword, transliterated as two syllables: 카-페, same as English.
독서(読书)=汉字词，독→读，서→书，跟中文的「读书」意思一样。: 독서(読书) is a Sino-Korean word: 독 means 'read', 서 means 'book', same meaning as Chinese '读书'.
汉字词「包装」。买书送礼的「선물 포장」通常免费。: Sino-Korean word for 'wrapping'. Gift wrapping (선물 포장) for books is usually free.
포장(包装)=汉字词「包装」，同源直接记。: 포장(包装) is a Sino-Korean word, same origin as Chinese '包装', just memorize it directly.
汉字词「交换」。书店买错版本或有印刷问题都可以换。: Sino-Korean word for 'exchange'. You can exchange at bookstores if you bought the wrong edition or there's a printing issue.
교환(交换)=汉字词「交换」，跟中文完全同源。: 교환(交换) is a Sino-Korean word, completely same origin as Chinese '交换'.
교환=换成别的东西继续买；환불=退钱走人。书店多数只接受교환，不接受환불。: 교환 means exchanging for something else; 환불 means getting a refund and leaving. Most bookstores only accept 교환, not 환불.
「24 + 시간」，教保文库光化门店的招牌。: '24 + 시간' is the sign at Kyobo Bookstore's Gwanghwamun branch.
数字 24 + 시간(时间)=汉字词「时间」，24 小时书店的招牌词。: Number 24 + 시간(时间) is a Sino-Korean word for 'time', the sign word for a 24-hour bookstore.
固有词。指 0-4 时。: Native Korean word. Refers to 0-4 AM.
固有词，专指凌晨 0-4 点那段黑到发蓝的时刻，比밤更深一层。: Native Korean word, specifically the dark blue-black hours of 0-4 AM, deeper than 밤.
밤=晚上 9-12 点还有人活动；새벽=凌晨 0-4 点最深夜。24 小时书店的: 밤 is 9 PM-midnight when people are still active; 새벽 is the deepest night of 0-4 AM. For a 24-hour bookstore's late night, use 새벽.
늦다(晚)+ -게(副词化)=「晚地」，末尾 -게 就是副词的招牌尾巴。: 늦다 (late) + -게 (adverbializer) = 'lately,' and the ending -게 is the signature tail of adverbs.
항상(恒常)=汉字词「恒常」，「常」字就是总是，一次拿下。: 항상 (恒常) = Sino-Korean '항상' — the character '常' means always, so you've got it in one go.
「문 + 닫다」。24 小时书店最爱说的一句。: '문 + 닫다' — the favorite phrase of 24-hour bookstores.
문(门)+닫다(关)=关门，动作动词。광화문 교보문고的宣传语就是「문 안 닫아: 문 (door) + 닫다 (close) = to close the door, an action verb. Gwanghwamun Kyobo Bookstore's slogan is '문 안 닫아요' (we don't close the door).
手指某本书或递手机截图问店员时: When pointing at a book or showing a phone screenshot to the staff
「없어요」是完全没卖；「품절이에요」是暂时缺货可预约——店员回「품절」别以为是拒: '없어요' means it's not sold at all; '품절이에요' means temporarily out of stock but orderable — if the staff says '품절,' don't take it as a rejection; you can ask '언제 들어와요?' (when will it come in?).
（更委婉）请问有这本书吗？: (More polite) Do you have this book?

书店分区用「코너」（区/角），别用「구역」（区域，公务/管制场合词）——「자기계: Bookstores use '코너' (corner/section), not '구역' (zone, a word for official/regulated contexts) — '자기계발 구역' sounds like a designated administrative area, while '자기계발 코너' is the natural way to say a category section.
（更完整）畅销书区在哪里？: (More complete) Where is the bestseller section?

「추천하다」不能省成「추천 주세요」——动词必须带 -해 주세요 完整活用。名词: '추천하다' can't be shortened to '추천 주세요' — the verb must be fully conjugated with -해 주세요. If using the noun '추천' alone, add 좀: '추천 좀 해 주세요'.
（极度礼貌）能帮我推荐吗？: (Very polite) Could you recommend something for me?
进店告诉店员自己在找什么时: When entering a store and telling the staff what you're looking for
「찾고 있어요」是「正在找」，比「찾아요」（找）更强调进行中。跟店员说「在找」用: '찾고 있어요' means 'am looking for' and emphasizes the ongoing action more than '찾아요' (look for). When telling a store clerk you're looking for something, the former sounds more natural.
（更委婉）在找韩语学习书……（-는데요留话尾等回应）: (More polite) I'm looking for Korean learning books... (-는데요 leaves the sentence open for a response)
这个可以试读吗？: Can I read a bit of this?
在架子上抽了一本想坐下翻时: When you've pulled a book off the shelf and want to sit down and flip through it

（更委婉）这个可以看一下吗？: (More polite) Could I take a look at this?
（更随意）这个能看吗？: (More casual) Can I look at this?

「몇 시」是「几点」，「얼마나」是「多久」。想问营业时长用前者，别问「얼마나 열: '몇 시' means 'what time,' and '얼마나' means 'how long.' To ask about business hours, use the former; don't ask '얼마나 열어요?'—it sounds odd.

（更委婉）凌晨也开门吗？: (More polite) Do you open even at dawn?
书类 + 水平一次说清。: State the book type and level all at once.
被让座后的礼貌回应。: A polite response after someone gives up their seat.

语言区在 2 层。初级吗？: The language section is on the 2nd floor. Beginner level?
这本怎样？畅销书。: How about this one? It's a bestseller.
可以，坐这读吧。: Sure, have a seat and read here.

韩国高速巴士比你想象的先进——프리미엄 座椅接近平躺，USB 充电口，还有 Wi: Korean express buses are more advanced than you'd think—premium seats recline nearly flat, with USB charging ports and Wi-Fi. From Seoul to Busan takes 4.5 hours, and the fare is only half of KTX.
车上 Wi-Fi 免费，够看视频: Free Wi-Fi on board, enough for streaming videos
고속 vs 시외 · 别买错: Express vs Intercity · Don't Buy the Wrong One
고속버스（高速巴士）走高速直达，停站少；시외버스（市外巴士）走国道，停站多，慢: Express buses (고속버스) take the highway directly with few stops; intercity buses (시외버스) use national roads with more stops—30% slower but 30% cheaper. Check carefully when buying—choose express for speed, intercity to save.
一般座 4 排 27 座；우등 3 排 21 座 + 电动腿托；프리미엄 3 排: Regular seats have 4 rows with 27 seats; premium has 3 rows with 21 seats plus electric leg rests; premium+ has 3 rows with full recline, privacy dividers, and individual screens. For overnight long trips, choose premium or premium+—more comfortable than first class.
首尔→釜山等热门线有深夜班次（심야버스）—— 23:00-01:00 发车，凌晨: Popular routes like Seoul→Busan have late-night services (심야버스)—departing 23:00-01:00, arriving at dawn. Fares are 20% higher, but you save a night's accommodation. A favorite among Korean college students on business trips.
강남터미널（江南）走岭南/釜山；센트럴시티 走湖南/光州；동서울종합터미널 走江: Gangnam Terminal (강남터미널) serves Yeongnam/Busan; Central City serves Honam/Gwangju; Dong Seoul Terminal serves Gangwon/Gyeongsang. Confirm which terminal your bus departs from before buying—running to Gangnam on Line 1 only to find your bus at Central City is a wasted trip.
长途每 2 小时在服务区停 15-20 分钟。可上厕所、买零食、伸腿。韩国服务区: Every 2 hours, the bus stops at a rest area for 15-20 minutes. You can use the restroom, grab snacks, and stretch your legs. Korean rest areas have 국밥 / 호두과자 / 라면, almost like a mini food court. Don't get too carried away and miss the bus—the driver won't wait.
为什么韩国巴士司机开得那么猛？: Why do Korean bus drivers drive so aggressively?
韩国高速巴士司机按班次计工资，晚点扣钱。加上韩国高速限速 110km/h（车速表: Korean express bus drivers are paid per shift and get fined for delays. Plus, the highway speed limit is 110km/h (though the speedometer can hit 130+), so drivers often push the limit. First-timers might get weak knees, but the on-time rate is among the top three globally.
프리미엄 和 일반 到底差什么？: What's the real difference between 프리미엄 and 일반?
票价差 60-80%（首尔→釜山：一般 27,000 / 프리미엄 47,000: The fare difference is 60-80% (Seoul→Busan: 일반 27,000 / 프리미엄 47,000). It's not just the seats—프리미엄 comes with UV-sanitized armrests, privacy curtains, and individual reading lights. It's the choice for business travelers.
巴士上有厕所吗？: Is there a restroom on the bus?
一般巴士没厕所——每 2 小时停服务区。프리미엄巴士部分线路有小卫生间但不常用（: Regular buses don't have restrooms—they stop at rest areas every 2 hours. Some 프리미엄 buses have small restrooms on certain routes, but they're rarely used (it's considered 'impolite'). Going before you board is the unspoken rule for Korean long-distance buses.
请给我去釜山的票。: Please give me a ticket to Busan.
请给靠窗的位子。: Please give me a window seat.
售票机很多不认外国 Visa/Master，柜台可以刷。现金也行，但准备好整钱最: Many ticket machines don't accept foreign Visa/Master, but the counter does. Cash works too, but having exact change is easiest.
发车前 10 分钟到月台: Arrive at the platform 10 minutes before departure
巴士司机准点发车，晚到 1 分钟车就走了。提前进闸口候车，票需要打印或亮出手机: The bus departs on time—if you're even 1 minute late, it's gone. Get to the gate early, and have your ticket printed or your phone QR ready.
登车前把大箱子交给司机放行李舱，随身包上车。下车时凭票再取，别忘拿。: Hand your big suitcase to the driver to store in the luggage compartment before boarding, and take your carry-on with you. When you get off, retrieve it with your ticket—don't forget it.
请给我一张去釜山的票。: Please give me a ticket to Busan.
「승차권」是正式说法，日常用「표」。: '승차권' is the formal term, but '표' is used in everyday speech.
汉字词「票」，字面就是中文的「票」，pyo 短促一音节，一秒记住。: The Sino-Korean word '표' literally means 'ticket' in Chinese—just one short syllable, 'pyo,' easy to remember in a second.
往返= 왕복。价格差异大约 5% 折扣。: Round-trip = 왕복. There's about a 5% discount.
편도(片道)＝汉字词「片道」，日韩通用，片(单)+道(路)＝单程一趟。: 편도(片道) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'one-way,' used in both Korean and Japanese—편(片, single) + 도(道, road) = one trip.
편도＝只去不回；왕복＝去+回来。往返票通常有 5-10% 折扣。: One-way means only going; round trip means going and coming back. Round-trip tickets usually have a 5-10% discount.
返程日期一般 15 天内有效，具体看车站。: The return date is usually valid within 15 days, depending on the station.
왕복(往复)＝汉字词「往复」，中文说往返，韩汉同源直接对应。: 왕복 (往复) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'back and forth'; in Chinese it's 往返, directly corresponding as cognates.
왕복＝去+回来一起买；편도＝只买单向。返程改日期看车站规定。: 왕복 means buying both going and return together; 편도 means buying only one way. Changing the return date depends on station rules.
请给靠窗的。: Please give me a window seat.
走道 = 통로. 长途推荐창가看风景。: Aisle = 통로. For long trips, window seats (창가) are recommended for the view.
창(窗)+가(边)＝窗边，자리＝纯韩语位子，合起来窗边座。: 창 (window) + 가 (side) = window side; 자리 is pure Korean for 'seat', so together it's a window seat.
창가＝靠窗看风景；통로＝走道方便起身上厕所。长途窗，短途走道。: 창가 means window side for views; 통로 is the aisle for easy bathroom access. Window for long trips, aisle for short ones.
「우등고속」一排 3 座，比一般贵 50%。: '우등고속' has 3 seats per row and costs about 50% more than regular.
우등(优等)＝汉字词「优等」，中文的「优等生」就是这个词，巴士座椅分级用。: 우등 (优等) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'excellent'; it's the same word as in Chinese '优等生' (top student), used for bus seat classes.
우등＝一排 3 座+腿托；일반＝一排 4 座普通。长途选 우등 舒服很多。: 우등 has 3 seats per row with leg rests; 일반 is a regular 4-seat row. For long trips, 우등 is much more comfortable.
问班次路线时: when asking about routes and schedules
汉字后缀，跟着目的地城市：대구행 / 광주행。: A Sino-Korean suffix attached to the destination city: 대구행 / 광주행.
행(行)＝汉字词「行」，跟日语「东京行き」的行是同一个用法，接城市名。: 행 (行) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'bound for', same usage as Japanese 'Tokyo-yuki', attached to city names.
출발(出发)＝汉字词「出发」，出+发，中文同源直接记。: 출발 (departure) = Sino-Korean word '出发', 出+发, directly related to Chinese, easy to remember.
巴士晚点常见，看实时显示屏更靠谱。: Buses are often late; checking the real-time display is more reliable.
도착(到着)＝汉字词「到着」，跟日语「到着」一模一样，都表示到达。: 도착 (arrival) = Sino-Korean word '到着', identical to Japanese '到着', both mean arrival.
相对「경유」（经停）。长途直达更省时间。: Compared to '경유' (stopover). Long-distance direct routes save more time.
직행(直行)＝汉字词「直行」，直＋行＝直达不停，跟中文完全同源。: 직행 (direct) = Sino-Korean word '直行', 直+行 = direct without stops, fully cognate with Chinese.
직행＝中途不停一路开到；경유＝会在中途城市停站上下客，慢 30%。: 직행 = non-stop all the way; 경유 = stops at intermediate cities for passengers, 30% slower.
也可以说「몇 시간 걸려요?」，更口语。: You can also say '몇 시간 걸려요?' which is more colloquial.
소요(所要)+시간(时间)＝所需时间，两个汉字词拼在一起，跟中文完全对应。: 소요 (required) + 시간 (time) = required time, two Sino-Korean words combined, fully corresponding to Chinese.
编号从 1 开始，票上会印。: Numbering starts from 1 and is printed on the ticket.
승강(乘降)+장(场)＝汉字词「乘降场」，乘(上车)+降(下车)+장(地方)，跟: 승강 (boarding/alighting) + 장 (place) = Sino-Korean word '乘降场', 乘 (board) + 降 (alight) + 장 (place), cognate with Japanese '乗降场'.
候车厅有座位/自动贩卖机/充电口。: The waiting hall has seats, vending machines, and charging ports.
대합실(待合室)＝汉字词「待合室」，跟日语一模一样，等人聚集的房间＝候车厅。: 대합실 (waiting room) = Sino-Korean word '待合室', identical to Japanese, a room where people gather to wait = waiting hall.
在小卖部买紫菜包饭。: Buy gimbap at the convenience store.
巴士站三明治/紫菜包饭/热咖啡最全。: Bus stops have the best selection of sandwiches, gimbap, and hot coffee.
매점(卖店)＝汉字词「卖店」，卖东西的小店，跟日语「売店」同源。: 매점 (shop) = Sino-Korean word '卖店', a small shop selling things, cognate with Japanese '売店'.
按小时收费，出行前寄存行李最方便。: Charged by the hour, storing luggage before travel is most convenient.
물품(物品)+보관(保管)+함(函)＝物品保管的柜子，三个汉字词叠加直译。: 물품(物品)+보관(保管)+함(函)＝A cabinet for storing items, a direct translation of three Sino-Korean words combined.
售票处在那边。: The ticket office is over there.
柜台 + 自助机并存，柜台可用现金。: Both counter and self-service machines are available; the counter accepts cash.
매(卖)+표(票)+소(所)＝卖票的地方，三个汉字词直译成售票处。: 매(卖)+표(票)+소(所)＝A place selling tickets, three Sino-Korean words directly translated as ticket office.
「카드로요」口语最常用。: 「카드로요」 is the most common in spoken language.
card 音译，念快跟英文完全一样：카-드。加 로 = 用卡。: Card transliteration, pronounced fast exactly like English: 카-드. Adding 로 = with card.
大额需要提前取现，售票机接受纸币。: For large amounts, withdraw cash in advance; ticket machines accept banknotes.
현금(现金)＝汉字词「现金」，中文完全同源，读音也接近「贤金」。: 현금(现金)＝Sino-Korean word 'cash', fully cognate with Chinese, pronunciation also close to '贤金'.

취소(取消)＝汉字词「取消」，中文完全同源，一字不改。: 취소(取消)＝Sino-Korean word 'cancel', fully cognate with Chinese, unchanged.

걸리다 是自动词，接主格助词 이/가 或直接省略，不能用宾格助词 을/를。「시간: 걸리다 is intransitive, takes the subject particle 이/가 or is omitted — never the object particle 을/를. '시간을 걸려요' ✗.

韩国年轻人约会/聚会首选不是咖啡厅——是野餐。带一块 돗자리（野餐垫）、买 김밥: For young Koreans, the go-to for dates or hangouts isn't a café — it's a picnic. Bring a 돗자리 (picnic mat), grab some 김밥 and 컵라면, and sit on the park lawn for the whole afternoon. Photos, chatting, snacking — all for under 1 만원.
樱花季 · 全民社交盛事: Cherry Blossom Season · A Nationwide Social Event
韩国 4 月赏樱叫「벚꽃 구경」——不是「看花」，是「拍照」。汝矣岛轮中路、石村: In Korea, April cherry blossom viewing is called '벚꽃 구경' — it's not about 'seeing flowers,' it's about 'taking photos.' Yeouido's Wheel Road, Seokchon Lake, and Namsan Park are packed with people. Essentials: picnic mat + triangle kimbap + camera. Wear pink or white to match the blossoms.
韩国人在公园拍照追求「人生中最好的一张」。为了一张完美照片，摆 20 个 pos: Koreans aim for 'the best photo of your life' when shooting in parks. For one perfect shot, they'll strike 20 poses, take 100 photos, and edit for 2 hours. Korean social media has made 'taking photos' the core of park activities.
韩国宠物文化 2020 年后爆发——公园里遛狗的比遛孩子的多。看到可爱的狗会问「: Korea's pet culture exploded after 2020 — there are more people walking dogs in parks than kids. When you see a cute dog, you ask '만져도 돼요?' (Can I pet it?) instead of just reaching out. Dog walking is a way for young Koreans to break the ice.
汉江公园所有区域都能叫外卖。App 上选「한강 배달」区块，指定坐标炸鸡/披萨: You can order delivery to any area of Hangang Park. Pick the '한강 배달' section in the app, set your coordinates, and fried chicken or pizza arrives in 30 minutes. The delivery driver waits in the parking area for you to pick it up — this is Korea's unique park delivery culture.
为什么韩国公园没有「广场舞」？: Why are there no 'square dances' in Korean parks?
韩国大妈跳舞更多在 노래방 / 콜라텍（Colatec，老人 KTV 舞厅）——: Korean ajummas dance more at norebang / Colatec (senior KTV dance halls) — paying for a private room is more mainstream than dancing free in parks. Plus, Korean parks have rules against loud volume, so square dancing has no room to survive.
벚꽃 和 개나리 有什么区别？: What's the difference between 벚꽃 and 개나리?
벚꽃 = 樱花（4 月初、粉白色、大朵）；개나리 = 迎春花（3 月末、明黄色、: 벚꽃 = cherry blossoms (early April, pinkish-white, large petals); 개나리 = forsythia (late March, bright yellow, shrub-like). In Korea's spring, 개나리 blooms first (March), then 벚꽃 (April), followed by 진달래 (azaleas).
한강공원 为什么那么火？: Why is Hangang Park so popular?
免费 + 大 + 交通方便（多个地铁站直达）+ 允许外卖。首尔 12 个汉江公园: Free + huge + easy to reach (direct subway access from multiple stations) + delivery allowed. Seoul has 12 Hangang parks, with Banpo being the most famous (Moonlight Rainbow Fountain). There are music festivals on summer nights and fireworks shows in autumn.
可以帮忙拍照吗？: Could you take a photo for us?
公园垃圾桶少且分类严格。带垃圾袋（쓰레기봉투），走时全部装走扔到便利店门口分类桶: Parks have few trash bins and strict sorting rules. Bring a trash bag (쓰레기봉투), pack everything up when you leave, and toss it in the sorting bins outside convenience stores.
汉江夜景比白天好: The Hangang night view is better than daytime

大公园每 500 米一个卫生间，免费。夜间可能上锁到早上 6 点。: Big parks have a restroom every 500 meters, free of charge. At night, they may be locked until 6 AM.
picnic 直接音译，念时把 c 弱化：피-크-닉，跟英文几乎一样。: Picnic is directly transliterated; soften the 'c' when pronouncing: 피-크-닉, almost identical to English.

자전거(自转车)＝汉字词，中文的「自转车」＝自行车，一次记住。: 자전거 (自转车) = Sino-Korean; Chinese '自转车' means bicycle—remember it in one go.
固有词，一个字就是花；后面接名词组词也常用（벚꽃/국화꽃）。: Native word; one syllable means flower; commonly used before nouns (벚꽃/국화꽃).

벚（樱）+꽃（花）＝樱花；꽃是花的通用后缀，记一次全套受益。: 벚 (cherry) + 꽃 (flower) = cherry blossom; 꽃 is a common suffix for flowers, learn it once and benefit across the board.

正式演讲第一句：「존경하는 여러분, 안녕하십니까」。第二句：「오늘 이 자리에: First line of a formal speech: '존경하는 여러분, 안녕하십니까'. Second: '오늘 이 자리에 참석하게 되어 영광입니다' (It's an honor to be here today). Third: self-introduction.
发表结束后主持人说「질문 받겠습니다」（接受提问）。听众举手说「한 가지 질문: After the presentation, the host says '질문 받겠습니다' (I'll take questions). Audience raises hand and says '한 가지 질문 있습니다'. Replies use '답변 드리겠습니다'.
演讲结束的固定收尾：「이상으로 제 발표를 마치겠습니다. 감사합니다」= 「以: The standard closing: '이상으로 제 발표를 마치겠습니다. 감사합니다' = 'I'll end my presentation here. Thank you.' Followed by a bow and applause.
演讲者对听众说话时不用「말해요」，而是「말씀드리겠습니다」（我来说）——把自己的: When a speaker addresses the audience, they don't use '말해요' but '말씀드리겠습니다' (I will speak) — lowering their own 'speaking'. The audience's words are called '말씀' (honorific). One verb, two directions — the core politeness logic of 하십시오체.
말 = 「话」通用；말씀 = 「话」尊敬 + 谦让。「선생님 말씀」= 「老师的: 말 = 'words' general; 말씀 = 'words' honorific + humble. '선생님 말씀' = 'teacher's words' (honorific); '제가 말씀드리겠습니다' = 'I will speak' (humble). Both directions are essential in speeches.

존경(尊敬)＝汉字词「尊敬」，+하는(做…的)＝尊敬着的。修饰名词的形式，别用「: 존경(尊敬) = Sino-Korean 'respect' + 하는 (doing) = respecting. Used to modify nouns; don't use '존경' alone.
对多人的尊称。: A respectful term for a group of people.
여러(多种)+분(位，敬称)＝各位。「분」是「사람」的敬称形，一次记住。: 여러 (various) + 분 (honorific for people) = everyone. '분' is the honorific form of '사람'; remember it once.
여러분＝直接称呼听众(各位)；여러 사람＝第三人称说「许多人」。演讲用여러분。: 여러분 = directly addressing the audience (everyone); 여러 사람 = third-person 'many people'. Use 여러분 in speeches.
감사(感谢)＋드리다(给…的谦让形)＋습니다＝把感谢「呈上」给听众，比「감사합니: 감사 (thanks) + 드리다 (humble form of 'give') + 습니다 = presenting thanks to the audience, one level above '감사합니다'.
감사드립니다＝把谢意「呈上」，演讲/公函最高级；감사합니다＝日常道谢。: 감사드립니다 = presenting gratitude, highest level for speeches/formal letters; 감사합니다 = everyday thanks.
말씀(话，尊/谦双向)+드리다(给的谦让形)＝把话「呈上」，说话者压低自己。: 말씀 (speech, honorific/humble) + 드리다 (humble 'give') = presenting words, lowering oneself.
말씀드리다＝我自谦(我说)；말씀하시다＝抬对方(您说)。同一「말씀」两个方向。: 말씀드리다 = humble self (I say); 말씀하시다 = honor the other (you say). Same '말씀', two directions.
演讲收尾固定。: A fixed phrase for ending a speech.
마치다(结束，主动)+겠(意愿)+습니다(하십시오체)＝「我来结束」，比「끝났어: 마치다 (to end, active) + 겠 (intention) + 습니다 (하십시오체) = "I will end it," 5 times more formal than 끝났어요.
마치다＝主动结束(演讲者宣告)；끝나다＝自动结束(时间到了)。发表收尾用主动的마: 마치다 = to actively end (the speaker declares); 끝나다 = to end on its own (time is up). Use the active 마치다 to conclude a presentation.
의(意)+견(见)＝汉字词「意见」，跟中文同字同义。: 의(意)+견(见) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'opinion,' identical in characters and meaning to Chinese.
의견＝正式立场(辩论/会议)；생각＝个人想法(日常)。市政厅用의견。: 의견 means a formal stance (debate/meeting); 생각 means a personal thought (everyday). Use 의견 at city hall.
찬(赞)+성(成)＝汉字词「赞成」，跟中文同字同义。: 찬(赞)+성(成) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'approve,' identical to Chinese.
반(反)+대(对)＝汉字词「反对」，跟中文同字同义。: 반(反)+대(对) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'oppose,' identical to Chinese.
반대＝表明反对立场(整体)；반박＝反驳具体论点(局部)。表态用반대。: 반대 means stating an opposing stance (overall); 반박 means refuting a specific point (partial). Use 반대 for statements.
토(讨)+론(论)＝汉字词「讨论」，跟中文同字同义。: 토(讨)+론(论) = Hanja word 'discussion' (토론), same characters and meaning as Chinese.
토론＝有立场对立(辩论)；논의＝无立场讨论(商讨)。市政厅两者都用。: 토론 = opposing positions (debate); 논의 = neutral discussion (deliberation). City Hall uses both.
타(妥)+협(协)＝汉字词「妥协」，跟中文同字同义。: 타(妥) + 협(协) = Sino-Korean word 'compromise' (타협), same characters and meaning as Chinese.
「안녕하십니까」是最正式的问候，日常绝对不用；日常只用「안녕하세요」。二者场合不: '안녕하십니까' is the most formal greeting, never used in daily life; only '안녕하세요' is used daily. The two cannot be mixed in context.
（更完整）尊敬的各位好。很高兴见到大家。: (More complete) Respected everyone, hello. Glad to see you all.
今天很荣幸能出席。: It's an honor to attend today.
得以同席: to have the honor of being present
得以发言: to have the opportunity to speak
得以出席这场（-게 되어 得以）: to be able to attend this (via -게 되어, meaning 'to have the honor of')
是荣幸（영광 + 이다 하십시오체）: is an honor (영광 + 이다 in 하십시오체)
「-게 되어」不能替换成「-아서/-어서」——「참석해서 영광입니다」语法可通但: '-게 되어' cannot be replaced with '-아서/-어서' — '참석해서 영광입니다' is grammatically fine but lacks the humble nuance of 'having the honor to'; in formal settings, '-게 되어' is a must.
（更庄重）今天能出席这场意义深远的活动我深感荣幸。: (More formal) It is a great honor to attend this meaningful event today.
演讲人不能对听众说「제가 말씀하시겠습니다」——「말씀하시다」是抬对方的尊敬形，: A speaker cannot say '제가 말씀하시겠습니다' to the audience — '말씀하시다' is an honorific that elevates the other person; for yourself, use the humble form '말씀드리다'. Getting the direction wrong is rude.
（更正式）借此机会，我想说说我的意见。: (More formal) Taking this opportunity, I would like to share my opinion.
辩论表态时: when taking a stance in a debate
关于那点（+ 主题助词 는）: about that point (+ topic particle 는)
「~에 대해」是「关于~」，跟宾语助词「~을/를」不能混——「그 점을 찬성합니: '~에 대해' means 'about' and cannot be mixed with the object particle '~을/를' — '그 점을 찬성합니다' is grammatically incorrect. In formal debate, use '그 점에 대해서 찬성합니다' or simply '그 점에 찬성합니다'.
（更正式）关于那点我也完全表示赞成。: (More formal) I fully agree on that point as well.
我的想法有点不同。: My thoughts are a bit different.
「다르다」（不同）不是「틀리다」（错的）——韩国人常把两者混用，但正式辩论必须用: '다르다' (different) is not '틀리다' (wrong)—Koreans often mix them up, but in formal debate you must use '다릅니다'; saying '틀립니다' implies the other person is wrong, and the atmosphere immediately turns tense.
（极度委婉）关于这部分我想说明我的看法略有不同。: (extremely polite) Regarding this part, I'd like to note that my view is slightly different.
（半正式）我的想法有点不同。: (semi-formal) My thoughts are a bit different.
能给我说明吗（설명하다 + -아 주시다 + -겠어요 委婉）: Could you explain it to me? (설명하다 + -아 주시다 + -겠어요, polite)
「-주시겠어요?」的「-겠-」是推测性委婉，不是意愿——直译「您愿意…吗」而非「: The '-겠-' in '-주시겠어요?' is a speculative softening, not a volition—it translates as 'would you be willing to...' rather than 'will you...'. Ignoring this nuance makes it sound blunt.
（极度礼貌）关于那部分能否再详细说明一下？: (very polite) Could you elaborate a bit more on that part?
「마치다」是主动结束（我来结束），「끝나다」是自动结束（时间到了自然结束）——演: '마치다' is an active ending (I end it), while '끝나다' is a passive ending (it ends naturally when time is up)—a speaker announcing the conclusion must use the active '마치겠습니다'; saying '끝났습니다' sounds like surrendering.
（更完整）以上是我发表的全部内容，衷心感谢各位聆听。: (more complete) That concludes my presentation; I sincerely thank you all for listening.
「시작하겠습니다」= 「开始」的正式意愿表达。: '시작하겠습니다' = a formal expression of intention to begin.
「한 가지 있어요」= 「有一个」是提问前的标准开场。: '한 가지 있어요' = 'There's one thing' is the standard opening before asking a question.
那部分能再说明一下吗？: Could you explain that part again?
「설명해 드리다」= 「说明给对方」的谦让形。: '설명해 드리다' = the humble form of 'explain to someone.'
「저는 + 입장 + 합니다」是表明立场的正式说法。: '저는 + 입장 + 합니다' is a formal way to state your position.
「마무리하다」= 「收尾/结束」，时间压力时用。: '마무리하다' = 'to wrap up/finish,' used when under time pressure.
「수고하셨습니다 → 감사합니다」是最常见对答。: '수고하셨습니다 → 감사합니다' is the most common exchange.
介绍下一位发表者。请开始。: Introducing the next presenter. Please begin.
今天很荣幸出席。: I'm honored to be here today.
今天我想说的主题是「多元文化社会的未来」。: Today, I'd like to talk about 'The Future of a Multicultural Society.'
以上结束我的发表。谢谢。: That concludes my presentation. Thank you.
发表听完了。有问题的朋友？: The presentation is over. Any questions?
我赞成。那法案对市民有帮助。: I agree. That bill helps the citizens.
我的想法不同。费用花得太多。: I see it differently. It costs too much.
但长期收益大。能说明吗？: But the long-term benefits are big. Can you explain?
好，初期费用 100 亿。税收要涨。: Okay, the initial cost is 10 billion. Taxes will go up.
那点对，但 10 年后会有收益。: That's true, but there will be returns after 10 years.
好意见谢谢。再讨论吧。: Good points, thanks. Let's discuss more.
每隔 50 米就一家，24 小时亮灯，凌晨 3 点也能买到热饭团——CU/GS2: One every 50 meters, lit 24/7, hot rice balls at 3 AM—CU/GS25/7-Eleven aren't just convenience stores; they're the backbone of Korean life.
全韩便利店总数，平均每 950 人一家: Total convenience stores nationwide, one per 950 people on average
年三角饭团销量估计，全民早餐首选: Estimated annual triangle rice ball sales, the nation's top breakfast choice
三角饭团起源于日本，在韩国被玩出花。CU 每年上新 100+ 种口味——金枪鱼蛋: Triangle rice balls originated in Japan but Korea took them to the next level. CU releases 100+ new flavors a year—tuna mayo, tteokbokki, pork cutlet—with seasonal limiteds more frequent than Starbucks. Korean breakfast = samgak gimbap + banana milk.
便利店 = 快递柜 + ATM + 充值站: Convenience store = parcel locker + ATM + top-up station
不只是买东西。这里可以收快递、取现金、充交通卡、买彩票、打印文件、交水电费。有些: It's not just for shopping. You can receive packages, withdraw cash, top up transit cards, buy lottery tickets, print documents, and pay utility bills. Some CU stores even have microwaves and seating, turning into 'mini study rooms' for international students.
冰杯自助 · 夏天的仪式: Self-serve Ice Cups · A Summer Ritual
夏天冰柜旁有透明冰杯自取。买一瓶可乐或啤酒，自己装杯加冰——店员不会帮你。韩国人: In summer, there are self-serve clear ice cups by the freezer. Buy a Coke or beer, fill your cup with ice yourself—the staff won't do it for you. Koreans standing outside convenience stores drinking ice-cold beer in summer is a perfectly normal sight.
CU 常跟男团女团出联名商品——BTS 保温杯、Blackpink 便当、New: CU frequently collaborates with boy and girl groups—BTS tumblers, Blackpink lunch boxes, NewJeans banana milk. Fans travel across Seoul's CU stores to collect full sets of photocards. Convenience stores have become fan maps.
2024 年起年轻人出门只带手机。Kakao Pay 扫码覆盖 95% 便利店，: Since 2024, young people only carry their phones when going out. Kakao Pay QR codes cover 95% of convenience stores, even street stalls have QR codes. If you pull out cash at CU, people in line ahead and behind will silently give you a look.
为什么便利店店员几乎不说「欢迎光临」？: Why do convenience store clerks almost never say "Welcome"?
客流量太大——一小时进出 50-100 人，逐个招呼会喊哑嗓子。「어서 오세요」: Foot traffic is too heavy—50-100 people come and go per hour, greeting each one would wear out your voice. "어서 오세요" is usually only heard when you approach the counter, a completely different world from the enthusiasm of cosmetics stores or restaurants.
CU 和 GS25 到底哪个便宜？: Which is actually cheaper, CU or GS25?
价格基本一样，供应链几乎相同。但 CU 的 1+1 集中在饭团/零食，GS25: Prices are basically the same, with nearly identical supply chains. But CU's 1+1 deals focus on rice balls/snacks, while GS25's 2+1 deals focus on drinks/alcohol. If you like KPOP collabs, go to CU; if you like private-label snacks, go to GS25.
为什么香蕉牛奶是胖乎乎的圆瓶？: Why is banana milk in a chubby round bottle?
「바나나맛 우유」的圆瓶是 1974 年 빙그레 公司设计的——模仿韩国传统陶罐: The round bottle of "바나나맛 우유" was designed by Binggrae in 1974—modeled after the traditional Korean earthenware jar "단지," symbolizing the warmth of home. The design hasn't changed in 50 years, making it one of Korea's most iconic packages.
买了饭团/杯面结账时说「젓가락 주세요」（要筷子）。免费。也可要「포크」（叉子）: When buying a rice ball or cup noodles, say "젓가락 주세요" (asking for chopsticks) at checkout. It's free. You can also ask for "포크" (fork).
便利店 100% 收卡（含外国信用卡）。也可 Kakao Pay/T-money: Convenience stores accept cards 100% (including foreign credit cards). Kakao Pay/T-money also work. If paying cash, have small bills ready, as change comes with lots of coins.
24 小时店凌晨全都在。深夜可以进去暖一下、买热咖啡、用洗手间。首尔安全区。: 24-hour stores are fully staffed at dawn. You can go in late at night to warm up, buy hot coffee, or use the restroom. Seoul is a safe area.
삼각(三角)+김밥(紫菜饭)＝三角形紫菜包饭。汉字+固有词组合。: 삼각 (triangle) + 김밥 (seaweed rice) = triangular gimbap. A combination of a Sino-Korean word and a native Korean word.
삼각김밥＝三角形便携装；김밥＝海苔卷（切片圆卷）。便利店大多是前者。: 삼각김밥 = triangular portable pack; 김밥 = seaweed roll (sliced round roll). Convenience stores mostly have the former.
컵(cup)+라면(拉面)＝杯装泡面，热水一冲就能吃。外来语拼接。: 컵 (cup) + 라면 (ramen) = cup noodles, ready to eat with hot water. A loanword combination.
컵라면＝杯装即食（加热水即可）；라면＝袋装（需自煮）。便利店大多卖前者。: Cup ramen = instant (just add hot water); bagged ramen = needs cooking. Convenience stores mostly sell the former.
음료수(饮料水)＝汉字词，字面「饮的水」，中韩同源。: Eumnyosu (drink water) = Sino-Korean, literally 'water to drink', same origin in Chinese and Korean.
ice cream 音译，念时五音节拆开：아-이-스-크-림。: Transliteration of 'ice cream', pronounced in five syllables: a-i-seu-keu-rim.
데우다＝加热的动作。「데워 주세요」是便利店最常听到的活用形。: Deuda = the action of heating. 'Deowo juseyo' is the most common form heard in convenience stores.
데우다＝加热保温（微波炉/温水）；끓이다＝烧到沸腾（锅里）。便利店只说데우다。: Deuda = heat/warm (microwave/warm water); kkeulida = boil (in a pot). Convenience stores only use deuda.
전자(电子汉字词)+레인지(range外来语)＝电子range，混合词造微波炉。: Jeonja (electronic, Sino-Korean) + reinji (range, loanword) = electronic range, a hybrid word for microwave.
가락＝细长条状（손가락手指/한 가락一段）；젓가락＝夹东西的细长两根。: Garak = long thin shape (songarak finger/han garak a strand); jeotgarak = two long thin sticks for picking up food.
fork 音译，两音节：포-크，跟英文发音几乎相同。: Transliteration of 'fork', two syllables: po-keu, almost identical to the English pronunciation.
빨다(吸)+대(棍)＝吸东西的棍子。固有词字面直译。: Ppada (suck) + dae (stick) = stick for sucking. Literal native Korean compound.
card 音译，一模一样两音节：카-드。: Card, transliterated with identical two syllables: 카-드.
현금(现金)＝汉字词「现金」，中韩同源直接记。: 현금 (现金) = Sino-Korean word for 'cash'; same origin as Chinese, just memorize it directly.
거스르다(退回)+돈(钱)＝退回来的钱。固有词字面直译。: 거스르다 (to return) + 돈 (money) = money returned. Native Korean word, literal translation.
봉투(封套)＝汉字词，跟中文「封套」同源。: 봉투 (封套) = Sino-Korean word, same origin as Chinese '封套'.
봉투＝店家塑料袋（收 100-200원）；에코백＝自带布袋（免费）。: 봉투 = store plastic bag (costs 100-200 won); 에코백 = your own cloth bag (free).
영수증(领收证)＝汉字词，「领收证」＝收到的证明。: 영수증 (领收证) = Sino-Korean word; '领收证' means proof of receipt.
T(Traffic)+money，韩语拼「티머니」ti-meo-ni，公交地铁都: T (Traffic) + money, spelled '티머니' (ti-meo-ni) in Korean; use it for buses and subways.
T-money 和 캐시비 都是交通卡；T-money 更普及，全国通用。: T-money and 캐시비 are both transportation cards; T-money is more common and works nationwide.
충전(充填)＝汉字词，字面「填满」——把钱填进卡里。: 충전 (充填) = Sino-Korean word, literally 'fill up' — filling money into the card.
接在金额后＝值这么多钱的量。천 원어치（一千元的量）/ 만 원어치。: Attached after an amount = the quantity worth that much. 천 원어치 (worth 1,000 won) / 만 원어치.
来一包烟。: Give me a pack of cigarettes.
固有词。买烟需成年证明。: Native Korean word. Buying cigarettes requires proof of adulthood.
복권(福券)＝汉字词，字面「福气券」——中奖就是福。: 복권 (福券) = Sino-Korean, literally 'fortune ticket' — winning is fortune.
选好商品结账时: When checking out with selected items
「이거 주세요」不能省成「이 주세요」——이 是修饰形，必须接名词（如 이 커피: '이거 주세요' can't be shortened to '이 주세요' — 이 is a modifier and must attach to a noun (e.g., 이 커피, 이 라면); for pointing alone, use '이거' (=이것).
（更正式）请给一个这个。: (More formal) Please give me one of these.
结账时店员问加热: When the clerk asks about heating at checkout
请加热得温一点: Please heat it up a bit warm.
「데워」是「데우다」的아/어形，不能说成「데어 주세요」——데우다活用是데워，不: '데워' is the 아/어 form of '데우다'; you can't say '데어 주세요' — 데우다 conjugates to 데워, not 데어.
（更礼貌）能帮我加热吗？: (More polite) Could you heat it for me?
买热食需要工具时: When you need utensils for hot food
筷子的数量词用「벌」（一双筷子＝젓가락 한 벌），但便利店口语直接说「젓가락 주: The counter for chopsticks is '벌' (a pair = 젓가락 한 벌), but in convenience store speech, just saying '젓가락 주세요' without a number is easiest. When adding a number, don't use '한 개' (that's one stick, not a pair).
（更礼貌）想要一双筷子。: (More polite) I'd like a pair of chopsticks.
结账时被问要不要袋子: Asked if you need a bag at checkout
「필요」是名词，否定最自然用「필요 없어요」（有/无搭配）；别说「필요 안 해요: '필요' is a noun, so the most natural negative is '필요 없어요' (have/don't have pairing); don't say '필요 안 해요' — the noun '필요' can't be directly negated with '안' (though the adjective 필요하다 can be 필요하지 않다, it's far less natural than 필요 없어요 in daily speech).

在韩国，偶像是真的会在公园被遇到的。汉江公园、汝矣岛、弘大——偶像下班后跑步、遛: In Korea, idols really do get spotted at parks. Han River Park, Yeouido, Hongdae—idols go running, walk their dogs, and take photos after work. Korean fans don't rush over for autographs; they snap a photo from afar and post it on social media.
韩国演唱会和签售的标配。每组合有自己的应援棒——BTS 的 ARMY Bomb（: A must-have for Korean concerts and fan signs. Each group has its own light stick—BTS's ARMY Bomb (purple), Blackpink's lightstick (pink), LUMI PAW's paw print light (in member colors). There are YouTube tutorials before concerts.

韩国 4 月赏樱叫 「벚꽃 구경」——不是「去看花」，是「去拍照」。汝矣岛轮中路: Cherry blossom viewing in Korea in April is called 벚꽃 구경—it's not about 'seeing flowers,' it's about 'taking photos.' Yeouido's Yunjung-ro, Seokchon Lake, Namsan Park—packed with people. Essentials: picnic mat + triangle rice balls + camera.

If you win, you get 30 seconds face-to-face with the idol, plus a signature and photo. Japanese fans fly to Korea just for this—it's the priciest ritual in KPOP culture.
韩国樱花和日本樱花有区别吗？: Is there a difference between Korean and Japanese cherry blossoms?
品种不同。日本樱花以 소메이요시노 为主（白粉色，花期一周）；韩国主要是 왕벚나: The varieties differ. Japan's are mainly 소메이요시노 (white-pink, blooming for a week); Korea's are mostly 왕벚나무 (king cherry, deep pink, blooming for 10 days). The cherry blossoms on Yeouido were said to be planted during Japanese colonial rule, but post-2000 Korean research proved they're a native Korean species.

想送小礼物选便宜实用款（唇膏/口罩/贴纸）。太贵的爱豆有原则不能收，会婉拒还给你: If you want to give a small gift, pick something cheap and practical (lip balm/mask/stickers). Idols have principles and can't accept anything too expensive—they'll politely decline and return it.

ticketing 音译成티켓팅—BTS 演唱会 30 万张票 200 万人抢，: Ticketing transliterated as 티켓팅—BTS concert: 300K tickets, 2M people fighting, sold out in 5 minutes. Fans call it a 'bloodbath'.

ㅂ 不规则活用为자랑스러워요，为偶像成就骄傲用它。: ㅂ irregular conjugation becomes 자랑스러워요; use it when proud of your idol's achievements.

문제(问题)+지(纸)＝问题纸，印着题目的那张。: 문제 (question) + 지 (paper) = question paper, the one with questions printed.
정(正)+답(答)＝正+答＝正确答案，跟中文思路一致。: 정 (correct) + 답 (answer) = correct answer, same logic as Chinese.
정답＝正答(对的)；오답＝误答(错的)。前缀 정 vs 오。: 정답 = correct answer; 오답 = wrong answer. The prefixes are 정 vs 오.
시작(始作)＝汉字词「始作」，就是\"开始\"。: 시작 (始作) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'start'.
끝的音「kkeut」短促收尾，像切断的声音，联想「戛然而止」。: The sound of 끝 is 'kkeut', ending abruptly like a cut-off sound—think of a sudden stop.
进场前收进袋。: Put your phone in the bag before entering.
휴대(携带)+폰(phone)＝携带电话。汉字+外来语组合词。: 휴대 (carry) + 폰 (phone) = mobile phone. A combination of a Sino-Korean word and a loanword.
两个都指手机。휴대폰是正式词；핸드폰(hand phone)日常口语更常见。: Both mean cell phone. 휴대폰 is formal; 핸드폰 (hand phone) is more common in everyday speech.
汉字词「不正行为」，抓到取消成绩。: Sino-Korean word for 'improper act'; if caught, your score is canceled.
부정(不正)+행위(行为)＝不正行为，考场专用书面词。: 부정 (improper) + 행위 (act) = improper act, a formal term used in exam settings.
부정행위是书面/正式；커닝(from cunning)是学生间口语。考场通告用부: 부정행위 is formal/written; 커닝 (from cunning) is slang among students. Exam notices use 부정행위.
감독(监督)+관(官)＝监督+官员，中文「监考」的对应词。: 감독 (supervise) + 관 (official) = supervisor, the Korean equivalent of Chinese '监考.'
감독관＝监考(临时角色)；선생님＝老师(职业身份)。考场里通常喊감독관님。: 감독관 = proctor (temporary role); 선생님 = teacher (professional identity). In exam rooms, you usually call them 감독관님.
心理状态时: When referring to a mental state
발표(发表)＝汉字词「发表」，指演讲、公开陈述。: 발표 (presentation) = Sino-Korean word meaning 'to present' or 'public statement.'
주제(主题)＝汉字词「主题」，跟中文同义同用法。: 주제 (topic) = Sino-Korean word, same meaning and usage as Chinese '主题.'
준비(准备)＝汉字词「准备」，同源直接记。: 준비 (preparation) = Sino-Korean word, same origin, easy to remember.
긴장(紧张)＝汉字词「紧张」，跟中文完全同义。: 긴장 (tension) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'tension,' exactly the same as Chinese.
긴장＝一时的紧张(考前 · 上台前)；걱정＝持续的担心(未来 · 结果)。: 긴장 = momentary nervousness (before a test or on stage); 걱정 = ongoing worry (about the future or results).
자신(自信)+감(感)＝自信+感觉，比中文「自信」多一个감字。: 자신 (confidence) + 감 (feeling) = confidence + feeling, adding '감' compared to Chinese '自信.'
어렵다(难)去 -다，加 -웠어요＝어려웠어요，形容词过去式变位规则。: Remove -다 from 어렵다 (hard), add -웠어요 to get 어려웠어요 — the past tense conjugation rule for adjectives.
어려워요＝(现在)难；어려웠어요＝(考完回想)当时难。考后回顾用过去时。: 어려워요 = hard (now); 어려웠어요 = was hard (looking back after the test). Use past tense when reflecting afterward.
쉽다(容易)去 -다，加 -웠어요＝쉬웠어요，跟어려웠어요同变位规则。: Remove -다 from 쉽다 (easy), add -웠어요 to get 쉬웠어요 — same conjugation rule as 어려웠어요.
这次考得好。: I did well on this test.
「시험을 잘 보다」= 考好。: '시험을 잘 보다' = to do well on a test.
잘(好好地)+봤어요(看了)＝考好了。韩语说\"考试用「보다(看)」\"。: 잘 (well) + 봤어요 (saw) = did well. Korean uses '보다 (to see)' for taking a test.
못(不能)+봤어요(考了)＝没考好。跟「잘 봤어요」互为反义对。: 못 (can't) + 봤어요 (took) = didn't do well. It's the opposite of '잘 봤어요'.
못 봤어요＝没考好(客气)；망쳤어요＝彻底搞砸(更强烈情绪)。: 못 봤어요 = didn't do well (polite); 망쳤어요 = totally messed up (stronger emotion).
합격(合格)＝汉字词「合格」，通过考试的正式说法。: 합격 (合格) = Sino-Korean for 'pass', the formal way to say you passed an exam.
합격＝通过；불합격＝不通过。前缀「불(不)」表否定。: 합격 = pass; 불합격 = fail. The prefix '불(不)' indicates negation.
入场时问考场位置: Asking for the exam room location upon entry
「어디예요?」不能省成「어디?」——那是半语，对监考老师失礼；正式场合务必保留「: '어디예요?' can't be shortened to '어디?' — that's casual speech, rude to the proctor; in formal settings, keep '예요'.
（更正式）请问考场在哪里？: (More formal) Where is the exam room, please?
（半语，只对熟朋友）考场在哪？: (Casual, only to close friends) Where's the exam room?
时间点必须加「에」（9시에 시작해요）——问句/答句都要，省略「에」在书面上不成: Time points must include '에' (9시에 시작해요) — in both questions and answers; omitting '에' isn't valid in writing.
（更正式）几点开始？（对监考老师）: (More formal) What time does it start? (to the proctor)
（半语，只对同学）几点开始？: (Casual, only to classmates) What time does it start?
考试中想知道剩余时间: Want to know the remaining time during an exam
「남다」（剩）表示结果状态，说「现在还剩多少」要用过去式「남았어요」——「시간: '남다' (to remain) indicates a resulting state; to say 'how much is left now,' use the past tense '남았어요' — '시간 남아요?' sounds like asking about a general situation, while '시간 남았어요?' specifically asks how much is left at this moment.
（更正式）还剩多少时间？（对监考老师）: (More formal) How much time is left? (to the proctor)
考前跟同学互相打气: Cheering each other up before an exam
「긴장돼요」（自动词，感到紧张）和「긴장해요」（他动词，让紧张）不同——描述自己: '긴장돼요' (intransitive, to feel nervous) and '긴장해요' (transitive, to make nervous) are different — use 돼요 to describe your own feelings.
（正式）非常紧张。（发表前对听众可用）: (Formal) I'm very nervous. (can be said to the audience before a presentation)
发表开场对听众说: Opening a presentation to the audience
「-겠습니다」只用于正式发表/宣告；日常跟朋友说话用「-ㄹ게요」，用错级别会显得: '-겠습니다' is only used for formal presentations/announcements; in everyday speech with friends, use '-ㄹ게요' — using the wrong level sounds stiff.
（更完整开场）现在开始发表。: (More complete opening) I will now begin the presentation.
考后问同学感受: Asking classmates how they felt after the exam
韩语\"考试\"搭配「보다(看)」而不是「하다(做)」——「시험 했어요?」是错: In Korean, 'exam' pairs with '보다' (to take/look) not '하다' (to do) — '시험 했어요?' is wrong; only '시험 봤어요?' is correct.
（对长辈/尊敬）您考得好吗？: (To elders/respectful) Did you do well on the exam?
「합격하다」的过去式是「합격했어요」，不是「합격어요」——하 + 았 缩合成했，: The past tense of '합격하다' is '합격했어요', not '합격어요' — 하 + 았 contracts to 했, a fixed conjugation for 하다 verbs in Korean.
进考场必答，递证件时最标准。: A must-answer when entering the exam room; most standard when handing over your ID.
考试开始，请关手机。: The exam is starting, please turn off your phone.
被告知剩余时间时的标准应答。: Standard response when told the remaining time.
肯定回答直接说「됐어요」；不好答「조금 더 필요해요」。: For a positive answer, just say '됐어요'; if not, say '조금 더 필요해요'.
感受评价用「어렵/쉽 + 았어요」是最直观答法。: For expressing feelings, '어렵/쉽 + 았어요' is the most direct way to answer.
「할 수 있어요」= 「能做」是最简明确认。: '할 수 있어요' = 'can do' is the simplest confirmation.
几点开始考试？: What time does the exam start?
太紧张。语法有点难。: So nervous. Grammar is a bit hard.
没关系。你能行。要有自信。: It's okay. You can do it. Be confident.
有点难。第 3 题不太确定。: It was a bit hard. Not sure about question 3.
啊，我也选②。好像不错！: Oh, I picked ② too. Looks good!
太好了。下次得考更好。: Great. I need to do better next time.
一起学吧。图书馆见。: Let's study together. See you at the library.
생일카페 · 粉丝为爱豆包场: Birthday Cafe · Fans renting out a place for their idol
粉丝租一家咖啡厅，布置偶像生日主题，免费请路过粉丝喝咖啡——韩国的「생일카페」文: Fans rent a cafe, decorate it with an idol's birthday theme, and offer free coffee to passing fans—Korea's 'birthday cafe' culture is one of a kind. Even ordinary college students can pull it off.
生日应援咖啡厅简称，通常持续 2-3 天: Short for birthday support cafe, usually lasts 2-3 days
免费喝咖啡——粉丝自掏腰包办: Free coffee—fans pay for it out of their own pockets
周边袋——参加就送小礼包: Goodie bag—free gift set for participating
路过看到咖啡厅门口有偶像海报，推门进去。给工作人员看你的社交媒体关注（证明是粉丝: If you pass by and see an idol poster at the cafe entrance, just walk in. Show the staff your social media follows (to prove you're a fan), and you can get free coffee, take photos, and grab merch. You don't need to buy an album—but bringing one makes you more welcome.
不是随便贴几张海报——是有主题的。粉色系、复古风、太空主题、电影海报风……有些生: It's not just slapping up a few posters—there's a theme. Pink vibes, retro, space, movie-poster style... Some birthday cafes have setups that rival professional curation. Fans start prepping materials a month in advance, and decorating costs 50-200만원.
为什么咖啡厅愿意租？: Why would a café agree to host it?
因为생카能带来流量。生카期间粉丝排队来拍照、发社交媒体，咖啡厅曝光暴增。咖啡厅不: Because a birthday café brings foot traffic. During the event, fans line up to take photos and post on social media, giving the café a huge exposure boost. The café doesn't charge a venue fee but requires "each person orders at least one drink"—fans pay, everyone wins.
韩国追星有个独特环节——手写信给偶像，签售时递过去。偶像会读，有些还在直播里读出: Korean fan culture has a unique ritual—writing a handwritten letter to your idol and handing it over at a fan sign. Idols actually read them, and some even read them aloud on livestreams. Koreans see a "handwritten letter" as more sincere than "monetary support"—it's the heart of fan culture.
팬싸 · 抽签见偶像: Fan sign · Lottery to meet your idol
팬사인회 = 粉丝签售会。买专辑 10-30 张参加抽签，中签率 1-2%。中了: A fan sign is a fan signing event. You buy 10-30 albums to enter the lottery, with a 1-2% chance of winning. If you win, you get 30 seconds face-to-face with your idol, plus a signature and photo. Japanese fans fly to Korea just for this—it's the priciest ritual in K-pop.
생카 和 팬싸 有什么区别？: What's the difference between a birthday café and a fan sign?
생카 = 粉丝办的生日咖啡厅（爱豆不到场，粉丝间交流）；팬싸 = 娱乐公司办的粉: A birthday café is fan-organized (the idol doesn't show up; it's for fans to connect), while a fan sign is company-run (the idol is there, but you need to win the lottery to get in). The former is free and open to all; the latter is a lottery battle.
粉丝为什么愿意花这么多钱办 생카？: Why are fans willing to spend so much on a birthday café?
既是对偶像的爱表达，也是粉丝圈内地位——办过 생카 = 「大粉」（core fa: It's both a way to show love for the idol and a status symbol in the fandom—hosting a birthday café makes you a "core fan." It's also an offline meetup for the fan community, where you trade photocards and meet like-minded people, turning fandom into a social scene.
偶像知道自己的 생카 吗？: Do idols know about their own birthday cafés?
知道。粉丝会在社交媒体标签「@偶像账号 생일 축하해요 💜」，偶像团队看得到。有: Yes. Fans tag "@idol's account 생일 축하해요 💜" on social media, and the idol's team sees it. Some idols even drop by their own birthday café—when they walk in, fans scream on the spot. That's called a "깜짝 방문" (surprise visit).
买了专辑来的。: I came after buying the album.
面对偶像脑袋会空白。提前写下想说的 3-5 句：「좋아하는 곡 뭐예요?」/「건: Your mind goes blank in front of your idol. Write down 3-5 things you want to say beforehand: "좋아하는 곡 뭐예요?" / "건강 조심하세요" / "다음 앨범 기대해요." Memorize them cold.
录音录像绝对禁止: Recording and filming are strictly forbidden
팬싸会现场监督员严格禁止拍照录像。想留纪念只能用官方拍的立拍得（폴라로이드）或者: At fan signs, on-site supervisors strictly ban photos and videos. To keep a memento, you can only use the official Polaroid (폴라로이드) or write a blog post afterward to remember it.
信不要太长: Don't make the letter too long
A4 一面手写足够。开头「OO 오빠/언니에게」，内容 3-5 段谢意 + 期待: One side of A4 handwritten is enough. Start with "OO 오빠/언니에게," write 3-5 paragraphs of thanks and anticipation. Sign it "사랑하는 팬 토리." Idols sometimes read a bit on the spot.
简称「팬싸」，是娱乐公司办的官方粉丝签售。: Short for "팬싸," it's an official fan signing event hosted by the entertainment company.
팬(fan)+사인(sign)+회(会)=粉丝签名会，三段拼接直接理解。: Fan + sign + 会 (meeting) = fan signing event — just combine the three parts.
今天去了生日应援。: Went to a birthday support event today.
简称「생카」，粉丝办的生日主题咖啡厅。: Short for '생카' — a birthday-themed cafe run by fans.
생일(生日 汉字词)+카페(café 外来语)=生日+咖啡厅，中韩英混合词。: 생일 (birthday, Sino-Korean) + 카페 (café, loanword) = birthday + cafe — a mixed Korean-Chinese-English word.
생카=粉丝办、爱豆不到场；팬사인회=公司办、爱豆本人到场。: 생카 = fan-organized, idol doesn't attend; 팬사인회 = company-organized, idol is present.
外来语 album。팬싸抽签必须买专辑；생카入场也常要出示。: Loanword 'album.' For 팬싸 (fan signing) draws, you must buy an album; 생카 entry often requires showing one too.
album 音译，念时 l 弱化：앨-범。: 'Album' is transliterated, with the 'l' softened: 앨-범.
汉字词「应募」，买专辑→报名→随机抽。: Sino-Korean '응모' (apply) — buy album → sign up → random draw.
응모(应募)=汉字词「应募」，中文的「报名」，同源。: 응모 (应募) = Sino-Korean for 'apply,' same as Chinese '报名' — cognates.
응모=报名参加（掏钱买专辑那步）；당첨=中签的结果。: 응모 = signing up (the step where you pay for the album); 당첨 = the result of winning.
中签所以来了。: Came because I won the draw.
汉字词「当籤」，팬싸中签率 1-2%。: Sino-Korean '당첨' (当籤) — the win rate for 팬싸 is 1-2%.
당첨(当籤)=汉字词「当签」，跟中文「中签」语义完全一致。: 당첨 (当籤) = Sino-Korean for 'winning the draw,' exactly matching Chinese '中签.'
外来语 slogan。粉丝举的横幅，写爱豆名或应援语。: Loanword 'slogan.' A banner fans hold up with the idol's name or a support message.
slogan 音译，中文「口号/标语」，粉丝场景特指手举横幅。: 'Slogan' is transliterated — Chinese '口号/标语' — but in fan contexts, it specifically means a handheld banner.
简称「포카」。专辑内附赠的爱豆照片卡，随机款。: Short for '포카.' A random photocard of the idol included in the album.
photo(포토)+card(카드)=照片卡，K-POP专辑核心收藏品。: Photo (포토) + card (카드) = photocard, a core K-pop album collectible.
准备了花束。: I prepared a bouquet of flowers.
팬싸能带花束，但娱乐公司常有大小限制。: You can bring flowers to fansigns, but agencies often have size restrictions.
꽃(花)+다발(束)=花的束，字面直译。다발是量词兼名词。: 꽃(flower)+다발(bundle) = a bundle of flowers, literal translation. 다발 is both a counter and a noun.
手写信是韩国追星的核心仪式，比礼物更受重视。: Handwritten letters are a core ritual in Korean fan culture, valued more than gifts.
편지(便紙)=汉字词「便纸」，现代中文没这词，只保留在韩语里指「信」。: 편지(便紙) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'letter'; modern Chinese doesn't use this term, it only survives in Korean.
편지=纸质手写信；문자=手机短信。팬싸只递편지。: 편지 = handwritten letter; 문자 = text message. At fansigns, only 편지 is given.
汉字词「膳物」。递礼物时习惯说「작은 선물이에요」表谦虚。: Sino-Korean word '膳物'. When giving a gift, it's customary to say '작은 선물이에요' to be humble.
선물(膳物)=汉字词，本义供奉的食物，现在泛指礼物。: 선물(膳物) is a Sino-Korean word, originally meaning food offered in sacrifice, now generally meaning gift.
外来语 sign。팬싸场景专用词，不用正式的「서명」。: Loanword from 'sign'. Used specifically in fansign contexts, not the formal '서명'.
sign 音译，粉圈通用词，不用汉字词「서명」。: Transliteration of 'sign', common in fan circles, not the Sino-Korean '서명'.
사인=팬싸/明星签名；서명=合同/文件签字。: 사인 = fansign/celebrity signature; 서명 = contract/document signing.
昵称写什么？: What should I write for the nickname?
汉字词「爱称」。爱豆问「애칭 뭐라고 할까요」是팬싸标配。: Sino-Korean word '爱称'. Idols asking '애칭 뭐라고 할까요' is a fansign staple.
애칭(爱稱)=汉字词「爱称」，被爱豆亲切叫的名字。: 애칭(爱稱) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'nickname', a name affectionately called by idols.
要爱豆对镜头说一句话，用于粉丝录音留念。: Ask the idol to say something to the camera for fans to record as a keepsake.
한(一)+마디(句/节)=一句/一段话，마디本义是「节」。: 한(one)+마디(word/measure)=one phrase/utterance; 마디 originally means 'segment' or 'node'.
外来语 heart。K-POP场景专指「比心手势」，不是心脏。: Loanword from 'heart.' In K-POP contexts, it specifically means the finger heart gesture, not the organ.
heart 音译，粉丝文化里=手指比心动作，不指器官。: Transliteration of 'heart'; in fan culture, it means the finger heart gesture, not the organ.
「셀프 + 카메라」缩写。爱豆举手机自拍是팬싸经典画面。: Abbreviation of 'self + camera.' An idol holding up their phone for a selfie is a classic fansign moment.
셀프(self)+카메라(camera)缩写，念快就是「셀카」两拍。: Abbreviation of self + camera; said quickly, it becomes two beats: 'sel-ka.'
셀카=自拍（自己举手机）；사진=一般照片。: 셀카 = selfie (holding the phone yourself); 사진 = a regular photo.
汉字词 응원(应援)+해요，粉丝表态最基础的一句。: Sino-Korean word 응원 (support) + 해요; the most basic phrase for fans to show their support.

课上用手机不太礼貌但大多数教授不管。低头看手机只要不出声，不会被打扰。但如果教授: Using your phone in class is a bit rude, but most professors don't care. As long as you're quiet while looking down at your phone, you won't be bothered. But if a professor asks you a question and you can't answer—your participation grade drops immediately.

교수님 = 教授（大学正式教师，有 PhD 学位）；선생님 = 老师（通用尊称，: 교수님 = professor (a full-time university instructor with a PhD); 선생님 = teacher (a general honorific used in elementary/middle/high schools, language institutes, and cram schools). Even though language institutes are affiliated with universities, they use 선생님 because instructors don't necessarily have doctorates.

有——「반장」/「과대」（과 = 系，과 대표 = 系代表）。作用跟中国「班长」: Yes—'반장'/'과대' (과 = department, 과 대표 = department representative). Its role differs from China's 'class president': it mainly handles relaying messages, organizing group meals, and coordinating presentation groups—not discipline.

想说「问题」用「질문」，不能用「문제」——「문제 있어요」在课堂里会被误听成「我: To say 'question,' use '질문,' not '문제' — '문제 있어요' in class would be misheard as 'I have a problem/issue,' not a question.
