韩国宿舍文化：第一次见室友，带一碗 떡볶이 或一盒 치킨 当见面礼。这不夸张——: Korean dorm culture: When meeting your roommate for the first time, bring a bowl of tteokbokki or a box of chicken as a gift. It's not an exaggeration—for Koreans, 'eating together = bonding' is the basic logic. You don't need to say a word; a box of chicken is enough.
大部分韩国大学宿舍有门禁（통금），23:00-24:00。晚归要提前申请，超过: Most Korean university dorms have a curfew (tonggeum), from 23:00 to 24:00. Late returns need prior approval; more than 3 times may get you kicked out. On weekends, some dorms extend it to 01:00, but not all—check before heading back.
严格到变态：一般垃圾、厨余、可回收（再分纸类/塑料/玻璃/金属），每种用不同颜色: Strict to the point of insanity: general waste, food waste, recyclables (further split into paper/plastic/glass/metal), each with different colored paid bags. If you're caught on camera tossing it wrong in the sorting area downstairs, it's a 100,000 won fine.
韩国宿舍隔音差，晚上 11 点后被投诉噪音，宿管直接敲门。3 次投诉 = 退宿。: Korean dorms have poor soundproofing; after 11 PM, a noise complaint means the RA knocks on your door directly. 3 complaints = eviction. Koreans have extremely low tolerance for noise—even footsteps or hairdryer sounds can get you reported. Walk around in socks at night.
WiFi 密码在公告栏: The WiFi password is on the bulletin board.
每层楼一张公告，密码通常是宿舍名 + 年份（如 hanbit2024）。房间信号: There's a notice on each floor; the password is usually the dorm name + year (e.g., hanbit2024). If the signal is weak in your room, you can ask to swap the router. 'What's the WiFi password?' is the must-ask question on a freshman's first day.
为什么韩国大学生大多不住宿舍？: Why do most Korean college students not live in dorms?
宿舍名额比学生少 3 倍——首尔大学宿舍覆盖率只有 25%。大部分学生租学校周边: Dorm spots are 3 times fewer than students—Seoul National University's dorm coverage is only 25%. Most students rent a one-room or gosiwon near campus, with monthly rent of 400,000–600,000 won. Dorms are actually the 'lucky ones' choice, but with lots of rules.
기숙사 和 하숙 有什么区别？: What's the difference between gisuk-sa and hasuk?
기숙사 = 学校宿舍（有门禁、规矩多、便宜）；하숙 = 寄宿家庭（住阿姨家、包饭: Gisuk-sa = school dorm (curfew, many rules, cheap); hasuk = homestay (live with an auntie, meals included, twice the price). Most international students stay in a gisuk-sa their first semester, then rent a one-room starting the second.
为什么宿舍 WiFi 密码那么长？: Why is the dorm WiFi password so long?
韩国大学 WiFi 常用「학교名 + 년도 + 특별문자」组合（如 SNU202: Korean university WiFi often uses a combo like 'school name + year + special character' (e.g., SNU2024!), to prevent outsiders from leeching while meeting the IT department's security policy. Save it on your phone after registering on day one—don't ask every time.
来办宿舍入住。: Come to check in for the dorm.
进门要脱鞋: Take off your shoes when entering.
韩国宿舍/民宿一律在玄关脱鞋。踩着鞋进房间是严重失礼，室友第一天就会提醒。: Korean dorms and guesthouses always require taking off shoes at the entryway. Walking in with shoes on is a serious faux pas; your roommate will remind you on day one.
一般垃圾/纸类/塑料/厨余，各自袋子。厨余用专用「음식물쓰레기봉투」（可回收袋）: General waste/paper/plastic/food waste, each with its own bag. Food waste uses the dedicated 'food waste bag' (recyclable bag); improper disposal gets fined.
晚上 10 点后压低声音: Keep your voice down after 10 PM
大部分宿舍晚 10 点后要求安静。看剧戴耳机，视频通话去公共休息室。这是韩国宿舍: Most dorms require quiet after 10 PM. Wear headphones for shows, and take video calls in the common lounge. It's an unwritten rule in Korean dorms.
기숙사(寄宿舍)＝汉字词三连：寄+宿+舍，中文的「寄宿舍」，同源直接记。: 기숙사(寄宿舍) = three Sino-Korean characters: 寄+宿+舍, same as Chinese '寄宿舍', remember it directly from the same origin.
기숙사＝学校宿舍（便宜、规矩多）；하숙＝住阿姨家（包饭、贵）。留学生首学期一般住: 기숙사 = school dorm (cheap, many rules); 하숙 = staying at an auntie's house (meals included, expensive). International students usually live in 기숙사 their first semester.
相反是「퇴사」（退宿）。「입사」不是「入职」哦。: The opposite is '퇴사' (check-out). '입사' doesn't mean 'starting a job' here.
입사(入舍)＝入+舍，宿舍语境专用。别跟公司「입사(入社)」搞混，同音不同字。: 입사(入舍) = 入+舍, used specifically in dorm contexts. Don't confuse it with company '입사(入社)'—same sound, different characters.
입사＝入住；퇴사＝退宿。宿舍语境两词是一对。公司语境퇴사＝辞职。: 입사 = check-in; 퇴사 = check-out. The two are a pair in dorm contexts. In company contexts, 퇴사 means resignation.
汉字词「房」。房号更正式的说法是「호실」。: Sino-Korean word '房'. A more formal term for room number is '호실'.
방(房)＝汉字词，跟中文「房」同一个字，念 bang 短促一音节。: 방(房) = Sino-Korean word, same character as Chinese '房', pronounced 'bang' as a short syllable.
常简说「203호」，去掉「실」也懂。: Often shortened to '203호'; dropping '실' is still understood.
호실(号室)＝号+室，汉字词。日常口语常省成「호」，如203호。: 호실(号室) = 号+室, Sino-Korean. In casual speech, often shortened to '호', like 203호.
外来语 roommate，年轻人常用。: A loanword from 'roommate,' commonly used by young people.
roommate 音译，四音节拆开：룸-메-이-트。也可缩说「룸메」更亲切。: Roommate is transliterated into four syllables: 룸-메-이-트. It can also be shortened to '룸메' for a friendlier tone.
可以领房间钥匙吗？: Can I get the room key?
有些宿舍已改电子锁，说「비밀번호」（密码）。: Some dorms have switched to electronic locks, so say '비밀번호' (password).
방(房)+열쇠(钥匙)＝房+钥匙。열쇠是固有词，字面「打开的东西」。: 방 (room) + 열쇠 (key) = room + key. 열쇠 is a native word, literally meaning 'something that opens.'
楼门/宿舍入口刷卡，丢了要罚款补办。: You swipe it at the building/dorm entrance; if lost, you'll have to pay a fine for a replacement.
출입(出入)＝汉字词「出入」+ 카드(card 音译)。「出入卡」直译。: 출입 (entry/exit) is a Sino-Korean word meaning '出入' + 카드 (card transliteration). It's a direct translation of '出入卡.'
通常 1 楼或地下 1 楼，投币或用 App。: Usually on the 1st floor or basement level 1, coin-operated or via an app.
세탁(洗涤)+실(室)＝汉字词「洗涤室」。세탁기＝洗衣机同源。: 세탁 (washing) + 실 (room) = Sino-Korean for '洗涤室.' 세탁기 (washing machine) shares the same root.
房间一般禁止用电磁炉，做饭必须去公用厨房。: Induction cooktops are usually banned in rooms, so cooking must be done in the shared kitchen.
공용(共用)+주방(厨房)＝两个汉字词拼合，「共用厨房」直译。: 공용 (shared) + 주방 (kitchen) = two Sino-Korean words combined, a direct translation of '共用厨房.'
公告栏或宿管会告诉，全楼共用。: The bulletin board or dorm manager will tell you; it's shared by the whole building.
WiFi 音译，四音节：와-이-파-이。念时把 F 变成韩语的 ㅍ。: WiFi is transliterated into four syllables: 와-이-파-이. When pronouncing, the F becomes a Korean ㅍ.
委婉说法。想请对方小声：「조금만 줄여 주실 수 있어요?」: A polite way to put it. To ask someone to be quieter: '조금만 줄여 주실 수 있어요?'
소음(骚音)＝汉字词「骚音」，骚(骚)=喧闹，跟中文「噪音」同义。: 소음 (骚音) = Sino-Korean word '骚音', 骚 (骚) = noisy, same meaning as Chinese '噪音' (noise).
今晚申请了外宿。: I applied for staying out overnight tonight.
不在宿舍过夜要提前报备。: You need to report in advance if you're not sleeping in the dorm.
외박(外泊)＝外+泊，字面「在外面过夜」。中文「外宿」意思一样。: 외박 (外泊) = 外 + 泊, literally 'staying overnight outside'. Same meaning as Chinese '外宿'.
외박＝在外过夜；외출＝白天出门（不过夜）。宿舍只需报备외박。: 외박 = staying out overnight; 외출 = going out during the day (not overnight). For the dorm, you only need to report 외박.
「청소 당번」= 值日。跟室友分工。: '청소 당번' = duty roster. Divide tasks with your roommate.
청소(清扫)＝汉字词「清扫」，中文同义直接记。: 청소 (清扫) = Sino-Korean word '清扫', same meaning as Chinese, just memorize it.
哪里分类垃圾？: Where do you sort the trash?
发音注意：「분리」实际念「불리」，是流音化。: Pronunciation note: '분리' is actually pronounced '불리' due to liquidization.
분리(分离)+수거(收去)＝汉字词「分离收取」，即把垃圾分类回收。: 분리 (分离) + 수거 (收去) = Sino-Korean words 'separate collection', i.e., sorting trash for recycling.
用专用袋，扔错会有社区通知。: Use the designated bags; if you sort wrong, the community will notify you.
음식물(饮食物)＝汉字词「饮食物」+ 쓰레기(垃圾，固有词)。汉字+固有词组合。: 음식물 (饮食物) = Sino-Korean word '饮食物' + 쓰레기 (trash, native word). A Sino-Korean + native word combination.
暗含「会归还」的意思，比 가져가다 安全。: It implies 'will return it', safer than 가져가다.
빌리다＝我这边「借入」。别跟빌려주다（借出）搞反——주다结尾就是「给出去」。: 빌리다 = 'borrow' on my side. Don't mix it up with 빌려주다 (lend) — the 주다 ending means 'giving out'.
빌리다＝我借入（主语是我）；빌려주다＝我借出（对方拿走）。方向相反。: 빌리다 = I borrow (subject is me); 빌려주다 = I lend (the other person takes it). The direction is opposite.
主动加时间承诺更礼貌。: Adding a time commitment proactively is more polite.
돌리다(转/回)+주다(给)＝「转回来给你」，就是归还。: 돌리다 (turn/return) + 주다 (give) = 'turn it back to you,' meaning to return.
能借吹风机吗？: Can I borrow a hair dryer?
英语 dryer 简化，宿舍室友最常借。: Shortened from English 'dryer,' most commonly borrowed among dorm roommates.
dryer 音译 + 韩语后缀 -기(器)＝드라이+器＝吹干+器。: Transliteration of 'dryer' + Korean suffix -기 (device) = 드라이 + 기 = blow-dry + device.
室友之间借充电器/耳机是社交起点。: Borrowing chargers/earphones between roommates is a social starting point.
충전(充电)＝汉字词「充电」+ 기(机/器)＝充电+器。汉字直译。: 충전 (charging) = Sino-Korean 'charge' + 기 (machine/device) = charge + device. Direct Sino-Korean translation.
到宿管前台报到时: When checking in at the dorm front desk
「-러」后必须接来去类动词（오다/가다/다니다）；不能说「입사하러 해요」——这: After '-러,' you must use a come/go verb (오다/가다/다니다); you can't say '입사하러 해요' — that's wrong.
（更正式）我来办宿舍入住。: (More formal) I'm here to check into the dorm.
问被分到哪间房: Asking which room you've been assigned
「몇」和量词之间要空一格：몇 호 ✓ / 몇호 ✗；也不加助词直接接：몇 호예요: Leave a space between 몇 and the counter: 몇 호 ✓ / 몇호 ✗; also attach directly without a particle: 몇 호예요 ✓ / 몇 호가 예요 ✗.
（更委婉）能告诉我房间是几号吗？: (More polite) Could you tell me what room number it is?
想要领取物品时: When you want to pick up an item
「받다」是「收」不是「领」。想强调「主动去取」时用「가지러 갈 수 있어요?」更: 받다 means 'receive,' not 'pick up.' To emphasize actively going to get it, 가지러 갈 수 있어요? is more fitting.
（更委婉）不知道能不能领钥匙？: (More polite) I wonder if I could get the key?
（更直接）请给钥匙。: (More direct) Please give me the key.
入住第一天问信息时: When asking for info on the first day of moving in
「뭐예요」问「是什么」，问「多少钱」要用「얼마예요」。密码属于「是什么」范畴，用: 뭐예요 asks 'what is it,' while 'how much' uses 얼마예요. A password falls under 'what is it,' so use 뭐예요.
（更委婉）WiFi 密码是怎么样的？: (More polite) What's the WiFi password like?
想向室友借东西时: When you want to borrow something from a roommate
「빌리다」是「借入」(我借来)，「빌려주다」是「借出」(借给别人)。方向别搞反—: 빌리다 means 'to borrow' (I take), while 빌려주다 means 'to lend' (give to someone else). Don't mix up the direction—use 빌리다 when you want to borrow from someone.
（极度礼貌）能借给我这个吗？: (extremely polite) Could you lend me this?
明天早上还你。: I'll return it to you tomorrow morning.
借完东西承诺归还时: when promising to return something borrowed
「-ㄹ게요」表承诺，「-ㄹ 거예요」只表推测。答应还东西必须用「돌려줄게요」，用: -ㄹ게요 expresses a promise, while -ㄹ 거예요 only indicates speculation. When promising to return something, you must use 돌려줄게요; using 돌려줄 거예요 sounds like you're guessing about yourself.
（更礼貌）明早一定还给您。: (more polite) I'll definitely return it to you tomorrow morning.
外宿怎么报备？: How do I report an overnight stay outside?
「어떻게」问「怎么做」（方法），「왜」问「为什么」（原因）。别搞混——「왜 해요: 어떻게 asks 'how' (method), while 왜 asks 'why' (reason). Don't mix them up—'왜 해요?' turns into an accusation.
（更委婉）外宿报备该怎么办呢？: (more polite) How should I go about reporting an overnight stay?
（更简短）外宿怎么报？: (shorter) How do I report an overnight stay?
请告诉我姓名和学号。: Please tell me your name and student ID.
「A이고, B예요」是把两项信息串起来的连接方式。: 'A이고, B예요' is a way to connect two pieces of information.
带入住申请表了吗？: Did you bring the check-in application form?
有→「네, 여기 있습니다」+ 递出物品最标准。: For 'yes,' '네, 여기 있습니다' + handing over the item is the most standard.
不知情/未见面用「아직 못 + V-았어요」= 「还没能…」。: For not knowing/not having met, use '아직 못 + V-았어요' = 'haven't been able to...'
吃饭了吗？一起吃吗？: Have you eaten? Want to eat together?
先答问题「아직 안 먹었어요」，再表达乐意「좋아요」，社交自然。: First answer with '아직 안 먹었어요,' then express willingness with '좋아요'—natural social flow.
被指出问题第一反应先致歉+答应，是最基本礼貌。: When called out, the first reaction should be to apologize and agree—basic politeness.
外宿请提前报备。: Please report overnight stays in advance.
「알겠습니다」是最正式的应答，比「알겠어요」尊敬。: '알겠습니다' is the most formal response, more respectful than '알겠어요.'
告诉宿管来意 + 姓名 + 学号: Tell the dorm manager your purpose + name + student ID
问房号 / 拿房间钥匙 + 门禁卡: Ask for room number / get room key + access card
洗衣房 / 厨房 / WiFi 位置和密码: Laundry room / kitchen / WiFi location and password
互相打招呼 / 吃饭邀请 / 保持安静: Greet each other / invite to eat / keep quiet
你好，我来办宿舍入住。: Hi, I'm here to check in to the dormitory.
好的，在这。门禁卡也一起给你。: Alright, here it is. Here's your access card too.
在 1 楼。公用厨房也在旁边。: It's on the 1st floor. The shared kitchen is right next to it.
hanbit1234。有不懂的随时问。: hanbit1234. Feel free to ask anytime if you have questions.
对话 B · 和室友的日常: Dialogue B · Daily Life with a Roommate
你好！我叫金敏秀。我们是室友了。: Hi! I'm Kim Min-su. We're roommates now.
吃饭了吗？一起去吃吗？: Have you eaten? Want to grab something together?
食堂吧。我还不熟。: Let's go to the cafeteria. I'm still not familiar with the area.
那我带你去。这边走。: Then I'll take you there. This way.
首尔咖啡文化 · 全世界都在惊叹: Seoul's Coffee Culture · The World Is Amazed
每 30 米一家咖啡馆，年人均 300+ 杯，2 元一杯的美式和 8 元一杯的手: A café every 30 meters, 300+ cups per person per year, and $2 Americanos coexisting with $8 pour-overs—Seoul has turned coffee into a lifestyle.
首尔咖啡馆数量，比全球任何城市都多: Seoul has more cafés than any other city in the world
韩国年人均咖啡消费量，全球第 2: Korea's annual coffee consumption per person, 2nd in the world
首尔咖啡馆冰美式全年销量占比: Share of iced Americano sales in Seoul cafés year-round
平均步行到最近咖啡馆的时间: Average walking time to the nearest café
「얼죽아」冬天也喝冰美式: 'Eoljuga' Drinking Iced Americanos Even in Winter
「얼어 죽어도 아이스 아메리카노」（冻死也要冰美式）。零下 10 度，你还是能: 'Eoreo jugeodo aiseu amerikano' (I'd rather freeze to death than give up iced Americano). At minus 10 degrees, you'll still see Koreans holding an iced Americano in one hand and their other hand in their pocket—this isn't a joke, it's a typical Seoul winter day.
咖啡馆 = 城市共享客厅: Cafés = The City's Shared Living Room
首尔人不在家会客——租金贵，房子小。咖啡馆变成了工作、约会、学习、独处的公共起居: Seoulites don't host guests at home—rent is expensive and apartments are small. Cafés have become public living rooms for work, dates, studying, and alone time. 'Kagongjok' (people who study at cafés) can camp out for an entire day.
别掏钱包。首尔 95% 咖啡馆只刷卡或 Kakao Pay，甚至有店挂「현금 사: Don't pull out your wallet. 95% of cafes in Seoul only take cards or Kakao Pay, some even have signs saying '현금 사절' (no cash). Learning '카드로요' is more useful than memorizing money amounts.
很多首尔咖啡馆开在小巷、地下室、没有招牌——但它们的 Instagram 有几万: Many Seoul cafés are tucked away in alleys, basements, or have no sign at all—yet they have tens of thousands of Instagram followers. The competition isn't about the coffee; it's about space design and photo angles.
为什么星巴克在韩国叫「스타벅스」？: Why is Starbucks called '스타벅스' in Korea?
按英语 Starbucks 的发音转写，实际念「seu-ta-beok-sseu: It's a transliteration of the English pronunciation, actually read as 'seu-ta-beok-sseu.' Koreans love to shorten it to '스벅,' and young people almost only use the abbreviation in everyday speech.
为什么点单要说「걸로」而不是「것을」？: Why do you say '걸로' instead of '것을' when ordering?
「걸로」= 것으로 的口语缩写，表达「就选这个」的选择感。日常几乎听不到「것을」: '걸로' is the colloquial abbreviation of 것으로, conveying a sense of 'I'll go with this.' You rarely hear the full form '것을' in daily conversation.
1902 年首尔 손탁호텔（Sontag Hotel）——韩国第一家商业售咖啡的: In 1902, at the Sontag Hotel in Seoul—Korea's first hotel to commercially serve coffee. Emperor Gojong had already drunk coffee earlier (1896) at the Russian legation, but the officially operating café started here.
얼어 죽어도 아이스 아메리카노（冻死也要冰美式）—— 韩国人真的一年四季喝冰美: 'Iced Americano even if I freeze to death'—Koreans really drink iced Americanos all year round, even in winter.
首尔咖啡馆基本只刷卡或手机支付。「카드로요（刷卡）」是最保险的答复。: Seoul cafés basically only accept card or mobile payments. '카드로요' (by card) is the safest answer.

韩国最热销咖啡，默认冰的居多。: Korea's best-selling coffee, usually iced by default.

바닐라=Vanilla，发音和英文高度接近，跟着读几遍就记住。: Vanilla = Vanilla, the pronunciation is very close to English, read it a few times and you'll remember it.
不是所有店都有，问一下再点。: Not every shop has it, ask before ordering.
Cold Brew 直接音译，念时把每个音节拆开：콜-드-브-루。: Cold Brew is directly transliterated, break it into syllables: kol-deu-beu-ru.
想调整饮品配方时: When you want to adjust a drink recipe

추가(追加)是汉字词，中文也用\"追加\"，意思完全一样！: Chuga (add) is a Sino-Korean word, Chinese also uses 'add', meaning exactly the same!
晚上想喝咖啡又怕失眠时点这个。: Order this when you want coffee at night but are afraid of insomnia.

뜨겁다的词根发音「tteu」带点紧张感，和热气腾腾的感觉很像。: The root 'tteu' in 뜨겁다 has a tense feel, like steam rising.

星巴克有톨/그란데/벤티专属叫法；一般咖啡店直接说작은/큰。: Starbucks has its own terms 톨/그란데/벤티; regular cafés just say 작은/큰.

크다(大)→큰(修饰形)，크다的크발音就像\"克\"，联想\"大克拉\"。: 크다 (big) → 큰 (modifier form). The 크 in 크다 sounds like 'keu', think 'big carat'.

口语更常说「포장이요」，短又快。테이크아웃요 显得更像外国人。: In casual speech, '포장이요' is more common—short and quick. Saying '테이크아웃요' sounds more like a foreigner.

포장(包装)=汉字词，中文的「包装」！同源词，直接记住。: 포장 (packaging) = Sino-Korean word, same as Chinese '包装'! Cognate, just memorize it.

현금(现金)＝汉字词「现金」，中韩同源，读音「hyeon-geum」轻松记。: 현금(现金) is a Sino-Korean word for 'cash,' shared with Chinese; pronounce it 'hyeon-geum' for easy recall.

美式一杯。（超简短，对熟悉的店员）: One Americano. (Very short, for familiar staff)

（极度礼貌）能帮我加一份浓缩吗？: (Very polite) Could I get an extra shot of espresso?
「빼고 주세요」中的「고」表并列连接（去掉 X 再给我），别写成「빼서」——「빼: In '빼고 주세요', '고' indicates a parallel connection (remove X and give it to me). Don't use '빼서'—that's a sequential connection meaning 'after removing X first,' which sounds unnatural when ordering.

工具助词 -로/-으로 看收音：无收音或ㄹ收音用「로」（카드로／서울로），其他辅: The instrumental particle -로/-으로 depends on the final consonant: use '로' after no final consonant or 'ㄹ' (카드로/서울로), and '으로' after other consonants (현금으로/손으로). Don't mix them up.

「괜찮아요」是委婉拒绝的万能句，比「싫어요」礼貌得多。: '괜찮아요' is a versatile polite refusal, much more courteous than '싫어요'.
否认后加「포장이요」告诉店员要外带，一步到位。: After declining, add '포장이요' to tell the staff you want it to go—all in one step.
有积分卡吗？: Do you have a rewards card?

弘大街头文化兴起，弘益大周边艺术社区: Hongdae's street culture thrives in the artsy neighborhood around Hongik University
弘大周末凌晨 3 点比白天还热闹: On weekends, Hongdae at 3 AM is livelier than in the daytime
韩国年轻人追星不叫「追星」，叫「덕질」。这个词不贬义——是身份认同。你在弘大看到: Young Koreans don't call it 'star-chasing'—they call it '덕질'. It's not a put-down; it's an identity. Those people lining up 3 hours for photocards in Hongdae aren't 'crazy fans'—it's a social activity. Korea's fan culture is unmatched worldwide.
路边摊是弘大的灵魂: Street Food Stalls Are the Soul of Hongdae
弘大路边摊不是「给游客的」——韩国人自己也吃。떡볶이 3,000 원、순대 3,: Hongdae's street stalls aren't 'for tourists'—Koreans eat there too. Tteokbokki is 3,000 won, sundae 3,000 won, and eomuk 1,500 won a skewer. You can eat standing or squatting. Tanghulu was the hottest street snack of 2023; a 1-hour wait is normal.
粉丝租一家咖啡厅，布置偶像生日主题——照片墙、应援棒、定制杯套。路过粉丝可以进来: Fans rent out a café and decorate it for their idol's birthday—photo walls, light sticks, custom cup sleeves. Passing fans can drop in for free coffee, photos, and merch. Nowhere else in the world does this.
弘大街头表演不是随便谁都能上——需要向区政府申请「街头表演许可证」，审核通过后分: Hongdae street performances aren't open to just anyone—you need to apply for a 'street performance permit' from the district office, which assigns time slots and spots after review. Weekend prime time is competitive; some apply 2 months in advance.
2 号线 / 6 号线 / 京义中央线 三线交汇——首尔最重要的换乘站之一。末班: Lines 2 / 6 / Gyeongui-Jungang meet here—one of Seoul's most important transfer stations. Last trains: Line 6 at 24:00 / Line 2 at 24:30. If late, take a taxi or the 심야버스 (night bus).
「홍익대학교」（弘益大学）的缩写。以设计/艺术专业闻名。学校周围形成的商圈就叫「: It's short for Hongik University, famous for design and art. The shopping district around it is called Hongdae sanggwon—but 90% of people here aren't here for the school.
爱豆专辑内附的照片小卡，每张成本 100 원但二级市场炒到 5-50 만원。稀有: Photocards included in idol albums cost about 100 won each to make, but resell for 50,000–500,000 won. Rarity tiers: regular → fansign exclusive → first-press limited → photobook. Fans trade, sell, and rent them—it's a uniquely Korean economy.

2023 年被韩国 YouTuber 带火，改良版：草莓/葡萄/柑橘等水果串起裹: Popularized by Korean YouTubers in 2023, this version uses strawberries, grapes, or citrus on sticks with a sugar coating—sweeter than the Chinese hawthorn original. 3,000–5,000 won per stick. Tanghulu shops are everywhere in Hongdae, and lines are common.
来一份炒年糕。: I'll have a serving of tteokbokki.

街头表演鼓掌不打赏也 OK: Clapping for street performers is enough—no tip needed.
弘大街头有大量 busking（街头表演）。听完鼓掌是最好回报，如果有帽子/箱子: Hongdae streets are full of busking. Clapping after a performance is the best reward; if there's a hat or box, dropping a few thousand won is fine.
生카拍照要问清楚: Ask before taking photos of saengka.

弘大最经典。辣味可选「덜 매운 걸로」。: Hongdae's classic. For spice level, ask for 'deol maeun geollo' (less spicy).

생일카페（生日+咖啡）的缩写，粉丝租店给偶像庆生。: Short for 'birthday cafe' (birthday + cafe), where fans rent a shop to celebrate an idol's birthday.
album 音译，念时三音节：앨-범。: Album is transliterated, pronounced in three syllables: 앨-범.
发音注意：「잃」念「일」（收音 ㅎ 脱落）。: Pronunciation note: '잃' is read as '일' (the final consonant ㅎ is dropped).
길(路)+잃다(丢)＝字面「丢了路」＝迷路。: 길 (road) + 잃다 (to lose) = literally 'lost the road' = to be lost.
附近有便利店吗？: Is there a convenience store nearby?
근(近)+처(处)＝汉字词「近处」，中文说「附近」，字不同但意思一致。: 근 (near) + 처 (place) = Sino-Korean word 'nearby place'; in Chinese we say '附近', different characters but same meaning.
근처＝很近的范围（几百米内）；주변＝更广的周边区域，都可用于问路。: 근처 = a very close range (within a few hundred meters); 주변 = a broader surrounding area. Both can be used when asking for directions.
弘大骨干路少，走小巷是常态。: Hongdae has few main roads, so taking alleys is the norm.
길＝所有道路的统称；골목＝狭窄的小巷/胡同，宽敞大道不叫골목。: 길 = general term for all roads; 골목 = narrow alley/lane; a wide avenue is not called 골목.
汉字词。相反：돌아가다（回转）。: Sino-Korean word. Opposite: 돌아가다 (to turn back).
직진(直进)＝汉字词，跟中文「直进」同源，加하다就是「直走」。: 직진 (直进) = Sino-Korean word, same origin as Chinese '直进'; add 하다 and it means 'go straight'.
拒绝推销/搭讪时常用。: Commonly used when refusing sales pitches or approaches.
지나다(经过)+가다(去)＝经过着走＝路过。: 지나다 (to pass) + 가다 (to go) = passing by while going = to pass through.
有些店门口禁止拍照，先问一句。: Some shops prohibit photos at the entrance, so ask first.
사진(写真)＝汉字词「照片」+ 찍다(拍/按)＝拍照片。: 사진 (写真) = Sino-Korean word for 'photo' + 찍다 (to take/press) = to take a photo.
请求帮拍: Ask someone to take a photo
店员搭话时的礼貌回避。: A polite way to brush off a salesperson.
구경하다＝只看不一定买；쇼핑하다＝以买为目的的购物。店员问时用구경하다更委婉。: 구경하다 means just looking without necessarily buying; 쇼핑하다 means shopping with the intent to buy. When a salesperson asks, using 구경하다 is more polite.
弘大街边店/服装店可试砍，专柜别砍。: You can try haggling at Hongdae street shops/clothing stores, but not at department store counters.
깎다＝顾客主动请求便宜；할인＝店家给出的折扣/优惠。砍价场景用깎다。: 깎다 means the customer actively asks for a lower price; 할인 means the store's discount/offer. Use 깎다 when haggling.
夜宵吃什么？: What should we eat for late-night snacks?
弘大凌晨都有店开着。: Stores in Hongdae stay open late into the night.
야식(夜食)＝汉字词，字面「夜里吃的东西」。: 야식 (夜食) is a Sino-Korean word, literally meaning 'food eaten at night.'
路边摊点单时: When ordering at a street stall
串状食物（어묵/닭꼬치）习惯用「꼬치」量词，说「어묵 하나」摊主也懂，但「한 꼬: For skewered foods (어묵/닭꼬치), the counter '꼬치' is commonly used. Saying '어묵 하나' works, but '한 꼬치' sounds more natural.
（更正式）请给我一份炒年糕。: (More formal) Please give me one serving of tteokbokki.
在街上求助时: When asking for help on the street
「잃다」和「잊다」易混：잃다＝丢东西/迷路（实体丢失）；잊다＝忘记（记忆丢失）。: '잃다' and '잊다' are easily confused: 잃다 = losing things/getting lost (physical loss); 잊다 = forgetting (memory loss). For getting lost, you must use 잃다.
（更礼貌）不好意思，我迷路了，能帮个忙吗？: (More polite) Excuse me, I'm lost. Could you help me?
问附近有无某处: Asking if a place is nearby
「이 근처에」的 에 是「有/在」的位置助词，不能换成 에서（에서 用于动作发生: The 에 in '이 근처에' is the location particle for 'there is/being,' not to be replaced with 에서 (which marks where an action happens); saying '이 근처에서 편의점 있어요?' is unnatural.
（更委婉）附近可能有便利店吗？: (More polite) Is there a convenience store around here?
（半语，朋友间）附近有便利店吗？: (Casual, between friends) Is there a convenience store nearby?
「-아/어도 돼요?」求许可，别混成「-아/어야 돼요」（必须做）——差一个字意: '-아/어도 돼요?' asks permission; don't confuse it with '-아/어야 돼요' (must do) — one letter changes the meaning completely: '찍어야 돼요?' becomes 'Do I have to take a photo?'
（更委婉）这里拍照会不会有问题？: (More polite) Would it be a problem to take photos here?
（半语，朋友间）这里能拍照吗？: (Casual, between friends) Can I take photos here?
被店员搭话时: When a store clerk talks to you
「V-는 거예요」表示当下持续动作；「V-ㄴ 거예요」（过去修饰）意思是「（之前: 'V-는 거예요' indicates an ongoing action; 'V-ㄴ 거예요' (past modifier) means 'something done (before),' so getting the tense wrong turns it into 'just finished looking.'
能给便宜（깎다 + -아 주시다 尊敬 + -ㄹ 수 있다）: Can you give a discount (깎다 + -아 주시다 honorific + -ㄹ 수 있다)
「-아 주실 수 있어요?」= 주다(给) + -시-(尊敬) + -ㄹ 수 있: '-아 주실 수 있어요?' = 주다 (give) + -시- (honorific) + -ㄹ 수 있다 (can) — three layers stacked; dropping '시' changes '주실→줄', which is less polite to shopkeepers/elders.
（极度礼貌）请问能便宜一点吗？: (Very polite) Could you please make it a bit cheaper?
（半语，熟客/朋友间）便宜点嘛。: (Banmal, between regulars/friends) Make it cheaper, yeah?
和同伴提议合照: Suggesting a group photo with companions
「-(으)ㄹ래요?」比较随意，对陌生长辈/正式场合不合适；对朋友或同龄人最自然。: '-(으)ㄹ래요?' is casual — not suitable for unfamiliar elders/formal settings; most natural with friends or peers.
（更礼貌）方便的话一起拍照吗？: (More polite) Would you like to take a photo together if you don't mind?
（半语，朋友间）一起拍照吗？: (Banmal, between friends) Wanna take a photo together?
要炒年糕吗？还有血肠。: Want some tteokbokki? There's also sundae.
「A랑 B 주세요」是并列两个食物的口语说法。: 'A랑 B 주세요' is a colloquial way to list two foods together.
肯定 + 괜찮아요 表达「没问题」，最省事。: Affirmative + 괜찮아요 to say 'no problem' — the easiest way.
在找路吗？: Are you looking for a way?
是的，弘大入口站在哪？: Yes, where is Hongik Univ. Station?
肯定 + 具体问题，一步到位。: Affirmative + specific question — gets it done in one step.
要帮您拍照吗？: Would you like me to take a photo for you?
被善意帮助时先答谢意，最自然。: When helped kindly, thanking first is most natural.
「포장이요 / 여기서 먹을게요」二选一最快。: Pick 'pohjang-iyo' (to go) or 'yeogiseo meogeulgeyo' (eat here)—fastest that way.
今天有生日应援。感兴趣吗？: There's a birthday event today. Interested?
在哪？到几点？: Where is it? Until what time?
感兴趣时直接问细节 = 表达明确意愿。: Ask details when interested = show clear intent.
一份多少 / 能砍价吗: How much per serving / Can I bargain?
问能不能拍 / 一起拍: Ask to take photos / take one together
炒年糕和鱼糕。多少钱？: Tteokbokki and fish cake. How much?
炒年糕 3,000，鱼糕一串 1,500。: Tteokbokki is 3,000, fish cake is 1,500 per skewer.
可以。再来一根糖葫芦。: Sure. I'll also have a tanghulu.
对话 B · 问路 + 追星: Dialogue B · Asking directions + fan activities
不好意思，我迷路了。弘大入口站在哪？: Excuse me, I'm lost. Where is Hongik Univ. Station?
沿这条小巷直走，右手边。5 分钟。: Go straight down this alley, it's on your right. About 5 minutes.
谢谢！还有，知道哪卖小卡吗？: Thanks! Also, do you know where I can buy photocards?
知道，那边有周边店。听说今天还有生日应援。: Yes, there's a merch shop over there. I heard there's also a birthday event today.
「星尘」咖啡厅。从那直走在左边。: Stardust Café. Go straight from there, it's on the left.
韩国医院 · 挂号 5,000 元看病: Korean Hospital · Registration 5,000 won per visit
韩国医疗体系在全球排得上号——全民健康保险、看病便宜、预约制高效。但外国人第一次: Korea's healthcare system ranks among the best globally—national health insurance, affordable care, and an efficient appointment system. But first-timers from abroad often find the process a bit confusing.
有保险普通门诊挂号费: Registration fee for a regular outpatient visit with insurance
平均候诊时间，比中国三甲快很多: Average wait time—much faster than top-tier hospitals in China
① 접수（挂号，交保险证）→ ② 진료（就诊，医生看诊）→ ③ 약 처방（开处方: ① 접수 (registration, submit insurance card) → ② 진료 (consultation, see the doctor) → ③ 약 처방 (prescription, pick up meds at the pharmacy). Hospitals don't sell medicine—Korea separates prescribing and dispensing, so you take your prescription to an outside pharmacy.
韩国医院打针（주사）很常见——感冒发烧 38 度以上，医生可能直接打退烧针。中国: Injections (주사) are common at Korean hospitals—if you have a cold or fever above 38°C, the doctor may give you a fever-reducing shot. Chinese people find it 'over the top,' but Koreans think 'it works faster.' Injection costs 3,000-5,000 won.
韩国医院预约用 Naver 或医院官网。搜索医院名 → 选科室时间 → 填个人信: Book at Korean hospitals via Naver or the hospital's website. Search the hospital name → pick a department and time → fill in your info → confirm. No phone calls needed. Foreigners without a Korean number can book in person.
医生给你「처방전」（处方单），拿去医院附近的 약국 买。药剂师配药 10-15: The doctor gives you a 처방전 (prescription), which you take to a nearby 약국 (pharmacy). The pharmacist fills it in 10-15 minutes. **The prescription is valid for 3 days—after that, it's void—** so head to the pharmacy right away.
认清科室别挂错: Know your department, don't pick the wrong one
내과（内科）= 感冒发烧肠胃；이비인후과（耳鼻喉）= 咽喉/耳朵/鼻炎；정형외과: 내과 (internal medicine) = colds, fevers, stomach issues; 이비인후과 (ENT) = throat, ears, rhinitis; 정형외과 (orthopedics) = fractures, joints; 피부과 (dermatology) = skin; 안과 (ophthalmology) = eyes. Pick the wrong one and you'll have to re-register, wasting half a day.
为什么韩国看病这么便宜？: Why is seeing a doctor in Korea so cheap?
国民健康保险（NHIS）政府补贴 70%，个人自付 30%。挂号 5,000 원: National Health Insurance (NHIS) covers 70% of costs, with individuals paying 30%. The 5,000 won registration fee is just your share—the actual cost is 15,000-20,000 won. This system ranks in the global top 10 and is Korea's biggest public welfare program.
한의원 和 병원 有什么区别？: What's the difference between 한의원 and 병원?
한의원（韓医院）= 传统韩医（针灸/艾灸/草药）；병원 = 西医院（现代医学）。: 한의원 (Korean medicine clinic) = traditional Korean medicine (acupuncture, moxibustion, herbal remedies); 병원 = Western medicine hospital (modern medicine). Go to 병원 for colds and fevers, and 한의원 for chronic conditions or back/neck care. 한의원 costs 2-3 times more.
外国人没保险看病多少钱？: How much does it cost for a foreigner without insurance?
普通感冒无保险 30,000-50,000 원（含挂号+诊金+药费），有保险 1: A common cold without insurance costs 30,000-50,000 won (registration + consultation + meds), but with insurance it's 10,000-15,000 won. **There's a 3-month gap before NHIS kicks in**, so you'll pay full price for urgent care—get travel insurance before applying for your alien registration card.
3 天前开始不舒服。: I've been feeling unwell for 3 days.
第一次去医院必带외국인등록증 或 护照 + 健康保险卡。忘带的话只能自费全价，比: First time at the hospital, bring your Alien Registration Card or passport + health insurance card. Forget it and you'll pay full price out of pocket — 3x more than with insurance.
穿方便脱衣的: Wear something easy to take off
医生检查可能要脱外套/挽袖测血压/量心跳。穿松身、易脱、无金属饰品的衣服最省事。: The doctor may need you to take off your coat or roll up your sleeve to check blood pressure and pulse. Loose, easy-to-remove clothes without metal accessories are your best bet.
大部分小诊所午休时间关门，别白跑。急诊看「응급실」（急诊室），大医院 24 小时: Most small clinics close for lunch, so don't waste a trip. For emergencies, look for "응급실" (ER); big hospitals are open 24/7.
挂号就诊时: When checking in for a visit
汉字词「接受」。中文的「接受」在韩语里变成「挂号/登记」。: The Hanja word is "接受." In Chinese it means "accept," but in Korean it means "check-in/registration."
접수(接受)＝汉字词，但意思不同：中文=接收，韩语=登记挂号。: 접수 (接受) is a Hanja word, but the meaning differs: in Chinese it's "receive," in Korean it's "register/check in."
想预约就诊。: I'd like to schedule a visit.
汉字词「诊疗」，涵盖挂号+看病全过程。: The Hanja word is "诊疗," covering the whole process from check-in to consultation.
진료(诊疗)＝诊断+治疗，两个汉字拼在一起就是「看诊」。: 진료 (诊疗) = diagnosis + treatment; the two characters together mean "seeing a doctor."
진료＝诊断+简单治疗（一次就诊）；치료＝长期治疗（可能多次）。: 진료 = diagnosis + simple treatment (one visit); 치료 = long-term treatment (possibly multiple sessions).
大医院要预约，小诊所可现场排队。: Big hospitals require appointments; small clinics allow walk-ins.
예약(豫约)＝汉字词「预约」，同源词，一次记住。: 예약 (豫约) is the Hanja word for "appointment"—a cognate, so you'll remember it in one go.
汉字词「医师」。当面称呼要加 선생님（老师）＝「医生您」。: The Hanja word is "医师." When addressing them directly, add 선생님 (teacher) = "Doctor."
의사(医师)＝汉字词，念快就是\"医师\"。: 의사 (医师) is a Hanja word; said quickly, it sounds just like "医师."
의사是身份词；当面对医生说话必须加 선생님＝의사 선생님，否则失礼。: 의사 is a status word; when speaking directly to a doctor, you must add 선생님 = 의사 선생님, otherwise it's rude.
汉字词「看护师」。也称 선생님 更礼貌。: Sino-Korean word '看护师'. Also, adding 선생님 is more polite.
간호사(看护师)＝汉字词，看护+师＝护士。: 간호사 (看护师) = Sino-Korean word, 看护 + 师 = nurse.
基本形。指部位时配「-가/이 아파요」，主语助词不能省。: Basic form. When referring to a body part, use '-가/이 아파요'; the subject particle can't be omitted.
아프다的아联想「哎」的呻吟声，疼到叫出来的感觉。: The '아' in 아프다 reminds you of the groan '哎'—the feeling of hurting so much you cry out.
「열이 나다」= 发烧；「열이 높다」= 高烧；「열이 있다」= 有烧感。: '열이 나다' = to have a fever; '열이 높다' = high fever; '열이 있다' = to feel feverish.
열(热)＝汉字词「热」，열이 나다＝热出来了＝发烧。: 열 (热) = Sino-Korean word '热'; 열이 나다 = heat comes out = to have a fever.
ㅂ 不规则变化：어지럽다 → 어지러워요。指旋转感，站起来眼前发黑常用。: ㅂ irregular: 어지럽다 → 어지러워요. Refers to a spinning sensation, often used when you stand up and your vision goes dark.
어지럽다的어지→联想「晕呼呼」的旋转感，词尾럽다是形容词标志。: The '어지' in 어지럽다 reminds you of the spinning feeling of '晕呼呼'; the ending -럽다 marks it as an adjective.
汉字词「疲困」。日常口语高频，跟中文的\"疲倦\"完全同义。: Sino-Korean word '疲困'. Very common in everyday speech; exactly the same meaning as Chinese '疲倦'.
피곤(疲困)＝汉字词「疲困」，同源词，直接记。: 피곤 (疲困) = Sino-Korean word '疲困', a cognate—just memorize it.
ㅅ 不规则动词，过去时 ㅅ 脱落：붓다 → 부었어요。: ㅅ irregular verb, ㅅ drops in past tense: 붓다 → 부었어요.
붓다的붓联想「肿包」鼓起来的感觉，词尾다是动词标志。: Think of 붓 in 붓다 as a swelling bump; the ending 다 marks it as a verb.
붓다＝肿（动作/状态变化，动词）；아프다＝疼（感觉，形容词）。可以同时说：부었고: 붓다 = to swell (action/state change, verb); 아프다 = to hurt (feeling, adjective). You can say both: 부었고 아파요.
汉字词「血压」。搭配「재다」＝测量。: Sino-Korean word for 'blood pressure.' Pairs with '재다' = to measure.
혈압(血压)＝汉字词「血压」，同源词，一次记住。: 혈압 (blood pressure) = Sino-Korean '혈압,' cognate, remember it once.
汉字词「体温」。正常值 36.5도，超 37.5도就是热。: Sino-Korean for 'body temperature.' Normal is 36.5도, above 37.5도 is a fever.
체온(体温)＝汉字词「体温」，念快就是\"体温\"。: 체온 (body temperature) = Sino-Korean '체온,' say it fast and it's '体温.'
체온＝客观温度数值；열＝主观发热感/发烧状态。医生问「체온」是要度数。: 체온 = objective temperature reading; 열 = subjective feverish feeling/state. When a doctor asks '체온,' they want the number.
外来语 X-ray。搭配「찍다」＝拍摄。: Loanword X-ray. Pairs with '찍다' = to take (a picture).
X-ray 音译，念时把每个字母拆开：엑-스-레-이。: X-ray transliteration, say each letter separately: 엑-스-레-이.
汉字词「注射」。「주사를 맞다」＝挨针（被动），不是「주사를 하다」。: Sino-Korean for 'injection.' '주사를 맞다' = to receive a shot (passive), not '주사를 하다.'
주사(注射)＝汉字词「注射」，同源直接记。: 주사 (injection) = Sino-Korean '주사,' cognate, just memorize it.
医院开，药店买药用。有效期 3 天，超时作废。: The hospital issues it, the pharmacy fills it. Valid for 3 days, expires after that.
처방(处方)+전(笺)＝处方笺，三个汉字拼一起，医院给的药方纸。: 처방(处方)+전(笺)＝처방전, three Chinese characters combined, the prescription paper from the hospital.
처방전＝纸质处方单（医院开）；약＝实际药品（药店买）。医院不卖药，只给처방전。: 처방전＝paper prescription (from hospital); 약＝actual medicine (from pharmacy). Hospitals don't sell meds, they only give 처방전.
医生结尾万能话，几乎每次就诊都会听到。: The doctor's go-to closing line, heard at almost every visit.
푹＝拟态副词，形容深深地/彻底地。쉬다(休息)+세요(敬语)＝请好好休息。: 푹＝mimetic adverb meaning deeply/thoroughly. 쉬다(rest)+세요(polite)＝please rest well.
드시다＝喝/吃的敬语，医生对患者的标准说法。: 드시다＝polite form of drink/eat, standard for doctors addressing patients.
물(水)+많이(多)+드세요(请喝)，三个词按顺序拼，跟中文语序一样。: 물(water)+많이(much)+드세요(please drink), three words in order, same word order as Chinese.
汉字词「禁酒」。感冒/胃病/服药期间常见嘱咐。: Sino-Korean word 「禁酒」. Common advice for colds, stomach issues, or while on medication.
금(禁)+주(酒)＝汉字词「禁酒」，两个字都是汉字来源。: 금(禁)+주(酒)＝Sino-Korean 「禁酒」, both characters of Chinese origin.
금주=戒酒；금연=戒烟。两个词都是「禁+X」结构，只换后一个字。: 금주=abstain from alcohol; 금연=quit smoking. Both follow the 「禁+X」 pattern, only the last character changes.
汉字词「禁烟」。呼吸道/心血管相关最常听到。: Sino-Korean word 「禁烟」. Most common for respiratory or cardiovascular issues.
금(禁)+연(烟)＝汉字词「禁烟」，跟금주同结构，好记。: 금(禁)+연(smoke)＝Sino-Korean 「禁烟」, same structure as 금주, easy to remember.
一周后复诊。: Come back in a week for a follow-up.
다시(再)+오세요(请来)，两个词拼在一起就是「请再来」。: 다시 (again) + 오세요 (please come) — put together, it means 'Please come again.'
第一次进医院到前台时: When you first enter the hospital and go to the front desk
来做（-러 表目的 + 왔어요 过去）: Came to do (-러 for purpose + 왔어요 past)
「-(으)러」的选择：动词词干有收音用 -으러（받으러），无收音用 -러（하러）: Choosing -(으)러: if the verb stem ends in a consonant, use -으러 (받으러); if it ends in a vowel, use -러 (하러). Don't mix them up.
想预约。: I want to make an appointment.
前台预约就诊时: When making an appointment at the front desk
想预约（예약하다 + -고 싶다）: Want to make an appointment (예약하다 + -고 싶다)
「-고 싶다」只能对第一人称用。说他人时用「-고 싶어하다」：동생이 예약하고: -고 싶다 is only for the first person. For others, use -고 싶어하다: 동생이 예약하고 싶어해요.
（更正式）我是来预约的。: (More formal) I'm here to make an appointment.
从昨天开始不舒服。: I've been feeling unwell since yesterday.
医生问何时起症状时: When the doctor asks when symptoms started
从昨天（+ 起点助词 부터）: From yesterday (+ starting point particle 부터)
「부터」表起点，「까지」表终点，别用反。「어제까지 아파요」= 疼到昨天为止（已: 부터 marks the starting point, 까지 the ending point — don't mix them up. '어제까지 아파요' means it hurt until yesterday (now better), which is totally different.
（更正式）从昨天开始一直不舒服。: (More formal) I've been feeling unwell since yesterday.
不知道部位名指着说时: When pointing without knowing the body part name
主语助词 이/가 不能省。「여기 아파요」听得懂但语法不完整；「여기가 아파요」: The subject particle 이/가 can't be omitted. '여기 아파요' is understandable but grammatically incomplete; '여기가 아파요' is natural.
「열이 높다」是固定搭配，形容烧得厉害。别用「열이 크다」——「크다」用于尺寸不: '열이 높다' is a fixed phrase meaning a high fever. Don't use '열이 크다' — '크다' is for size, not degree.
（更正式）烧得很高，39 度。: (More formal) The fever is high, 39 degrees.
担心/询问治疗方式时: When worried or asking about treatment
「주사」的搭配动词是「맞다」（挨/接受），不是「하다」。「주사 해요」是错的，「: The verb that goes with '주사' is '맞다' (to get/receive), not '하다'. '주사 해요' is wrong; '주사 맞아요' is correct.
（更委婉）一定要打针吗？: (More polite) Do I really have to get a shot?
就诊结束问康复时间时: When asking about recovery time after a visit
「낫다」（康复）跟「낳다」（生孩子）发音相近但意思完全不同，写错很尴尬。医院场景: '낫다' (to recover) and '낳다' (to give birth) sound similar but mean completely different things—mixing them up is awkward. In a hospital context, it's '낫다'.
（更委婉）大概什么时候能好呢？: (More polite) About when might I get better?
（半语，只对朋友）什么时候好？: (Banmal, only to friends) When will you get better?
并列症状用「-고」，跟药店回答一样。: Use '-고' to list symptoms, same as the pharmacy response.
「时间 + 부터요」是最短起始点回答。: 'Time + 부터요' is the shortest way to answer when it started.
「없어요」是最简否定。有过敏答「네, XX 알레르기요」。: '없어요' is the simplest negation. If you have allergies, say '네, XX 알레르기요'.
肯定+「괜찮아요」是能接受最自然表达。害怕说「무서워요」。: Affirmative + '괜찮아요' is the most natural way to accept. If scared, say '무서워요'.
量一下血压。: Let me check your blood pressure.
医生的检查指令，简短应答即可。: A doctor's examination instruction—a brief response is fine.
接受医嘱的标准应答。: Standard response to accepting medical advice.
哪里痛 + 何时起 + 度数: Where it hurts + When it started + Severity
过敏/服药/能不能打针: Allergies / Medication / Can I get a shot?
打针吗 / 处方 / 何时好: Shot? / Prescription / When will I get better?
来挂号。第一次来。: I'm here to register. First time.
请填这张表。写姓名和联系方式。: Please fill out this form. Write your name and contact info.
3 天前嗓子痛、发烧。也咳嗽。: Sore throat and fever since 3 days ago. Also coughing.
张嘴。嗓子肿了不少。: Open up. Your throat is quite swollen.
不用，吃药够了。开感冒药和消炎药。: No need. Pills are enough. I'll prescribe cold and anti-inflammatory meds.
3-4 天会好。好好休息。一周后复诊。: You'll be better in 3-4 days. Rest well. Come back in a week for a follow-up.
量血压。伸胳膊。: Let me check your blood pressure. Extend your arm.
有点高，135/90。最近压力大吗？: A bit high, 135/90. Been stressed lately?
是的，因为考试。经常头晕。: Yes, because of exams. I get dizzy often.
太累了。咖啡喝得多吗？: You're too tired. Do you drink a lot of coffee?
减少。多喝水好好休息。: Cut back. Drink more water and rest well.
仁川机场 · 12 年蝉联全球最佳: Incheon Airport · Best in the World 12 Years Running
从落地到出关平均 22 分钟，免税店比商场还大，还有室内花园和韩国文化体验区——: From landing to customs in 22 minutes on average, duty-free shops bigger than malls, plus indoor gardens and a Korean culture zone—this is the first glimpse of Korea for foreigners.
入境通关平均耗时，人多可能翻倍: Average immigration clearance time; can double when crowded
免税店品牌数，规模亚洲前列: Number of duty-free brands; among the largest in Asia
AREX 直达车到首尔站用时: AREX express train time to Seoul Station
免税店 · 曾经的代购天堂: Duty-free shops: a former daigou paradise
仁川免税店 70% 营业额来自中国游客。乐天、新罗、新世界三大免税店曾靠代购养活: 70% of Incheon duty-free revenue came from Chinese tourists. Lotte, Shilla, and Shinsegae once relied on daigou to sustain half the industry. After 2020, the daigou model shifted, turning duty-free shops into 'live-stream warehouses'—still bustling.
别在机场买 SIM 卡: Don't buy a SIM card at the airport
机场 SIM 卡柜台价格是市价 2 倍。聪明做法：提前在 Klook/KKday: Airport SIM counters charge double the market price. Smart move: book an eSIM on Klook/KKday in advance and activate on arrival, or grab an LG U+ prepaid card at a convenience store—16,500 won for 5 days. The savings cover three meals.
仁川出租车两种：白色/银色普通车，去首尔市区 6-7 万韩元；黑色模范出租（모범: Incheon has two taxi types: white/silver regular ones cost 60,000–70,000 won to central Seoul; black deluxe taxis (모범택시) are 30% pricier but offer better service. Students do fine with regular—black is for business travelers.
行李寄存柜可以放 5 天: Luggage lockers can hold bags for 5 days
수하물 보관 按天收费，最多存 5 天。中途要去济州/釜山不用拖着行李——寄机场: 수하물 보관 is charged by the day, up to 5 days. Heading to Jeju or Busan in between? No need to drag your bags—store them at the airport and pick them up on your return. A backpacker favorite.
入境大厅便利店直接卖。3,000 원空卡 + 充值。地铁/公交/便利店通用，每次: Convenience stores in the arrivals hall sell them. 3,000 won for the card + top-up. Works on subways, buses, and at convenience stores, saving 100 won per ride. Don't bother replacing it downtown—the airport is the easiest spot.
为什么仁川机场没有 4 号航站楼？: Why does Incheon Airport have no Terminal 4?
不是没建，是数字禁忌——汉字词「사」（四）跟「사」（死）同音，跟日本、中国一样忌: It's not that it wasn't built—it's a number taboo. The Sino-Korean word '사' (four) sounds like '사' (death), just like in Japan and China. Incheon currently has T1 and T2, and future plans skip 4 as well.
为什么护照说「여권」不说「패스포트」？: Why is a passport called '여권' instead of '패스포트'?
여권 是汉字词（旅券），机场/银行/政府全用这个。패스포트（外来语 passpo: 여권 is a Sino-Korean word (旅券), used everywhere from airports to banks and government offices. Koreans rarely say 패스포트 (the loanword for passport)—if you do, staff will pause. Learn 여권 as your first word.
AREX 直达车和普通车差多少？: How much difference between the AREX express and regular train?
直达约 43 分钟直到首尔站；普通车约 60 分钟站站停。直达票贵约一倍，行李多: The express takes about 43 minutes straight to Seoul Station; the regular stops at every station, about 60 minutes. Express tickets cost roughly double—go express with lots of luggage, or regular on a budget. The regular is just the airport subway line, so tap T-money like any metro.
机场铁路在哪坐？: Where do I catch the airport railroad?
K-ETA 提前 72 小时办: Apply for K-ETA 72 hours in advance
免签国旅客入境韩国前须在 k-eta.go.kr 网上申请，10,000 원，2: Visa-free travelers must apply online at k-eta.go.kr before entering Korea—10,000 won, with temporary exemptions for some countries since 2024.
机场换汇汇率通常差 30-50 원/美元。少换点够坐车即可，市区明洞/东大门的换: Airport exchange rates are usually 30-50 won per dollar worse. Just exchange enough for transportation — money changers in Myeongdong/Dongdaemun downtown offer better rates.
免税品出关时才拿: Duty-free items are picked up when leaving customs.
在市内免税店买的东西，要在机场登机前的「인도장」（引渡处）凭护照+登机牌领取，不: Items bought at downtown duty-free shops must be picked up at the '인도장' (delivery counter) before boarding, with passport + boarding pass — you can't take them directly.
递护照时说这句最标准，「여기 있어요」也可以。: Handing over your passport, this phrase is the most standard; '여기 있어요' also works.
여권(旅券)＝汉字词「旅+券」＝旅行证件。正式用语，比外来语 패스포트 更常用。: 여권 (旅券) = Sino-Korean 'travel + certificate' = travel document. It's the formal term, more common than the loanword 패스포트.
여권 是官方/正式用语，机场/银行/政府全用这个；패스포트 是外来语，韩国人几乎: 여권 is the official/formal term — airports, banks, and government all use it; 패스포트 is a loanword Koreans rarely use.
入境卡写完了。: The arrival card is filled out.
飞机上空乘会发，落地前用英文填好。: The flight attendant hands it out on the plane; fill it out in English before landing.
입국(入国)＋신고(申告)＋서(书)＝入境+申报+纸，三个汉字词拼一起。: 입국 (入国) + 신고 (申告) + 서 (书) = entry + declaration + paper — three Sino-Korean words combined.
目的最常用回答。学业「학업」/ 出差「출장」也常见。: The most common answer for purpose. '학업' (study) / '출장' (business trip) are also common.
관광(观光)＝汉字词「观+光」，中文同源，看一眼就懂。: 관광 (观光) = Sino-Korean 'see + light', same roots as Chinese — easy to recognize at a glance.
海关必问。回答直接说数字+期间：일주일/한 달。: Customs always asks this. Just answer with number + period: 일주일/한 달.
체류(滞留)＋기간(期间)＝停留+时段，两个汉字词组合，官方用语。: 체류 (滞留) + 기간 (期间) = stay + period — two Sino-Korean words combined, formal usage.
세관(税关)＋신고(申告)＝海关+申报，全是汉字词，念一次记一辈子。: 세관 (税关) + 신고 (申告) = customs + declaration — all Sino-Korean, once you say it you'll remember it forever.
外来语 carrier，年轻人常用。: Loanword from 'carrier,' commonly used by young people.
carrier 音译，念时省略 -r 音：캐-리-어。: Transliteration of 'carrier,' pronounced without the -r sound: 캐-리-어.
캐리어 是行李箱本身（物品）；수하물 是需要托运的所有件数（正式词）。海关问件数: 캐리어 refers to the suitcase itself (the item); 수하물 is the formal term for all pieces to be checked. Customs asks about the number of pieces using 수하물.
正式词，海关问「몇 개예요?」时用。: Formal term, used when customs asks '몇 개예요?'
수하물(手荷物)＝日语汉字词「手+荷+物」，直译\"手上带的行李\"。: 수하물 (手荷物) is a Sino-Japanese word meaning 'hand + carry + goods,' literally 'luggage carried by hand.'
口语常说「잃어버렸어요」，意思相同更亲切。: In speech, '잃어버렸어요' is common and friendlier with the same meaning.
분실(纷失)＝汉字词，正式书面语；申报单/柜台标识用这个。: 분실 (纷失) is a Sino-Korean word, formal written language; used on declaration forms and counter signs.
분실하다 是官方用语（填报案单用它）；잃어버리다 是日常口语。: 분실하다 is official (used on report forms); 잃어버리다 is everyday speech.
行李丢失找到后免费送到你填写的住址。: Once lost luggage is found, it's delivered free to the address you provided.
배송(配送)＝汉字词，跟中文「配送」一模一样。: 배송 (配送) is a Sino-Korean word, identical to Chinese '配送.'
机场标识很清楚，跟着 Exit 走即可。: Airport signs are clear; just follow the Exit signs.
출구(出口)＝汉字词，跟中文一样。반대말：입구(入口)。: 출구 (出口) is a Sino-Korean word, same as Chinese. Opposite: 입구 (入口).
Transit 也标了英文，找 Transfer Desk。: It's also marked in English as 'Transit' — look for the Transfer Desk.
환승(换乘)＝汉字词，中日韩共通，一次记住三国通用。: 환승 (换乘) is a Sino-Korean word shared across Chinese, Japanese, and Korean — learn it once, use it in all three.
免税店在几层？: What floor is the duty-free shop on?
出发大厅一般在 4 层，抵达后不能逛。: The departure hall is usually on the 4th floor; you can't browse after arriving.
면세(免税)＋점(店)＝汉字词「免税+店」，字面直译。: 면세 (免税) + 점 (店) = Sino-Korean for 'duty-free + store,' a literal translation.
机场汇率比市区差，只换够坐车的钱。: Airport rates are worse than downtown — only exchange enough for the ride.
환(换)＋전(钱)＋소(所)＝换+钱+地方，三个汉字拼成\"换钱处\"。: 환 (换) + 전 (钱) + 소 (所) = exchange + money + place — three characters forming 'money exchange spot.'
去问询处问问。: Go ask at the information desk.
有中文/英文/日文服务员，别怕问。: They have Chinese, English, and Japanese staff — don't be afraid to ask.
안내(案内)＋소(所)＝告知/引导+地方，日语汉字词。: 안내 (案内) + 소 (所) = guidance + place, a Japanese Sino-Korean term.
AREX。地下 1 层，跟着 Airport Railroad 走。: AREX. It's on basement level 1 — follow the Airport Railroad signs.
공항(空港)＋철도(铁道)＝汉字词「空港+铁道」，字面直译。: 공항 (空港) + 철도 (铁道) = Sino-Korean for 'airport + railway,' a literal translation.
票价 15,000-17,000 원，直达各主要区域。: Fares are 15,000–17,000 won and go directly to major areas.
limousine bus 音译，韩国把机场大巴统称 리무진。: It's a transliteration of 'limousine bus' — Korea calls all airport buses 리무진.
模范/国际（黑）出租更贵但可英语沟通。: Deluxe/international (black) taxis cost more but drivers speak English.
taxi 音译，念快就是\"塔可\"，全世界都能懂。: It's a transliteration of 'taxi' — said fast it sounds like 'taco,' and it's understood worldwide.
坐地铁去首尔站。: Take the subway to Seoul Station.
AREX 一般列车即为地铁 인천공항선 直达首尔站。: The AREX all-stop train is the subway—the Incheon Airport Line goes directly to Seoul Station.
지하(地下)＋철(铁)＝汉字词「地下+铁」＝地铁。中日韩通用概念。: 지하 (underground) + 철 (iron) = the Sino-Korean word for 'subway.' A concept shared across Chinese, Japanese, and Korean.
推车在哪租？: Where can I rent a cart?
仁川机场推车免费，随处可取。: Carts at Incheon Airport are free and available everywhere.
cart 音译，两个音节：카-트。: A transliteration of 'cart,' two syllables: 카-트.
「-러 왔어요」和「-으로 왔어요」都能表目的，但前者动词后（공부하러），后者名: Both '-러 왔어요' and '-으로 왔어요' express purpose, but the former follows a verb (공부하러), the latter a noun (관광으로).
海关问停留时间: When customs asks how long you're staying
「-ㄹ 거예요」是推测/计划；口语更常说「일주일이에요」= 就是一周，语感更肯定: '-ㄹ 거예요' expresses a guess/plan; in speech, '일주일이에요' = it's one week, sounds more certain.
（正式书面）停留期为一周。: (Formal, written) The stay is one week.
「잃어버리다」（丢东西）和「잊어버리다」（忘事情）拼写只差一个字，意思完全不同。: '잃어버리다' (to lose something) and '잊어버리다' (to forget something) differ by only one letter but have completely different meanings. Use '잃어버렸어요' for losing a wallet, and '잊어버렸어요' for forgetting a password—don't mix them up.
「어디」= 哪；「어디서」= 在哪（+ 起点助词 서）。问动作发生地必须加 서。: '어디' means 'where'; '어디서' means 'where' (with the starting point particle 서). You must add 서 when asking where an action takes place.
（更委婉）请问机场铁路在哪里可以乘坐？: (More polite) Excuse me, where can I take the airport railroad?
换汇要说金额+币种：100달러 환전해 주세요；单说 환전해 주세요 店员会追问: When exchanging money, state the amount and currency: '100달러 환전해 주세요'; if you just say '환전해 주세요', the clerk will ask '얼마 바꾸시겠어요?'
（正式）麻烦帮我换汇。: (Formal) Could you please exchange money for me?
在几层（몇 = 几，층 = 层）: On which floor (몇 = how many, 층 = floor)
楼层用汉字数字（일/이/삼）不用固有数字（하나/둘/셋）。: Floor numbers use Sino-Korean numbers (일/이/삼), not native Korean numbers (하나/둘/셋).
（更委婉）请问免税店在几层？: (More polite) Excuse me, which floor is the duty-free shop on?

「잘 못해요」（做得不好，谦虚）和「잘못해요」（做错了，写在一起）意思完全不同—: '잘 못해요' (not good at it, humble) and '잘못해요' (made a mistake, written together) mean completely different things — the space matters.

韩国 노래방 跟中国 KTV 完全不同——不是「大包厢 + 派对」，而是「小房间: Korea's noraebang is completely different from China's KTV — it's not about 'big rooms + parties,' but a daily activity of 'small rooms + friends + singing.' You can even go alone; it's called 'coin noraebang' (coin-operated KTV).
投币 KTV——1,000 원唱 3 首: Coin KTV — sing 3 songs for 1,000 won
两大点歌系统——歌曲库不同: Two major song-selection systems — different song libraries
「爱唱歌」——每人都有必唱曲: "Love to Sing" — Everyone Has a Go-To Song
코인노래방 · 一个人唱歌的天堂: Coin Noraebang · A Solo Singer's Paradise
韩国街头到处是投币 KTV——1-2 人隔音小隔间，1,000 원唱 3 首。不: Coin KTVs are everywhere on Korean streets—soundproof booths for 1-2 people, 1,000 won for 3 songs. No friends needed, no reservations, just walk in, close the door, and sing. Koreans feeling down on the way home from work pop in for 3 songs to decompress.
点歌用遥控器: Use the Remote to Pick Songs
搜歌名或歌手名。支持中文搜索（部分机器），但大部分是韩文界面。输入曲编号（곡 번: Search by song title or artist. Some machines support Chinese search, but most interfaces are in Korean. Entering the song number (곡 번호) is faster—Koreans make a habit of memorizing the numbers of their 애창곡.
每个韩国人有 2-3 首「爱唱歌」——KTV 必唱的拿手歌。常见：아이유的「너의: Every Korean has 2-3 "love-to-sing" songs—their go-to KTV anthems. Common picks: IU's "너의 의미", Buzz's "가시", Kim Gun-mo's "잘못된 만남". Koreans love it when foreigners sing K-pop.
韩国 KTV 唱完显示 0-100 分。韩国人认真对待——80 以上算「唱得好」: Korean KTVs show a score from 0-100 after each song. Koreans take it seriously—80+ means "good singing," below 60 gets teased. Foreigners with imperfect Korean pronunciation usually score low, but everyone finds it fun.
韩国 KTV 包间不卖酒——法律规定。想喝酒的话自带（部分店允许）或旁边喝完再来: Korean KTV rooms don't sell alcohol—it's the law. If you want to drink, bring your own (some places allow it) or drink at a nearby bar first. Some "노래방 술집" (singing bars) are specially licensed, but cost 3x more.
为什么韩国 노래방 不卖酒？: Why Don't Korean Noraebangs Sell Alcohol?
韩国「음악산업진흥에 관한 법률」把 노래방 归为「娱乐场所」不属「酒馆」——不: Korea's "Music Industry Promotion Act" classifies noraebangs as "entertainment venues," not "taverns"—so they can't get liquor licenses. It also prevents minors from drinking. If you want to drink and sing, go to a "단란주점" (hostess bar) or "감성주점" (music bar).
코인노래방 的隔音效果好吗？: Is Coin Noraebang Soundproofing Any Good?
出乎意料的好——真空玻璃 + 吸音棉墙。虽然只有 1-2 人的隔间，但隔壁人再嘶: Surprisingly good—vacuum glass and sound-absorbing foam walls. Even in a 1-2 person booth, you can't hear the person next door screaming. It's a triumph of Korean industrial design. Belt out those notes without worry.
TJ 和 금영 到底选哪个？: TJ or Geumyoung—Which One to Pick?
TJ 미디어 歌曲库更新快，KPOP 新歌 3 天内上线；금영 主打老歌，韩国: TJ Media updates its song library fast—new K-pop hits within 3 days; Geumyoung focuses on oldies, with all the Korean classics from the 90s. Young people pick TJ, singing with elders pick Geumyoung.
进包间后门通常反锁避免打扰。想加饮料/结账用房间电话拨 0。别自己乱开门。: The door usually auto-locks after you enter to prevent interruptions. To order drinks or pay, use the room phone and dial 0. Don't open the door yourself.
금영/TJ 都出了手机 App 蓝牙连接点歌台，比遥控器输文字快 5 倍。装了后: Both Geumyoung and TJ have mobile apps that connect to the song machine via Bluetooth—5x faster than typing on the remote. Once installed, just connect using the room number (방 번호).
生日请客买时间: Buying Time to Treat Someone on Their Birthday
朋友生日在노래방庆生是韩国习惯。请客只需说「내가 낼게」（我付），加一小时+饮料: Celebrating a friend's birthday at a norebang is a Korean custom. To treat, just say '내가 낼게' (I'll pay). Adding an hour plus drinks costs around 40,000 won.
노래(歌)+방(房)=歌房。字面直译中国的\"歌厅\"，一目了然。: 노래 (song) + 방 (room) = song room. Literally like China's 'song hall'—clear at a glance.
英文 room 音译成一个音节：룸。노래방场合几乎都说룸，比\"방\"更常见。: The English 'room' is transliterated as one syllable: 룸. In norebang settings, almost everyone says 룸—more common than '방'.
룸=外来语，KTV/酒店专用；방=固有词，泛指所有房间。노래방里说룸更自然。: 룸 is a loanword, used for KTV/hotels; 방 is a native word for any room. In a norebang, saying 룸 sounds more natural.
英文 mic 音译成三音节：마-이-크。念时不要念全 microphone。: The English 'mic' is transliterated as three syllables: 마-이-크. Don't say the full 'microphone'.
英文 remote control 缩成三音节리모컨，跟日语リモコン同源，都是英: The English 'remote control' is shortened to three syllables: 리모컨, same origin as Japanese リモコン—both are clipped English.
음(音)+량(量)=音量。跟中文完全同源，一次记住不用死背。: 음 (sound) + 량 (amount) = volume. Fully cognate with Chinese—learn it once, no need to memorize.
汉字\"曲\"的韩语音读=곡。中文\"歌曲\"里的\"曲\"就是它。: The Korean reading of the Chinese character '曲' is 곡. It's the same 'song' in Chinese '歌曲'.
곡=一首具体曲子/曲编号，正式；노래=歌本身，日常。点歌用\"이 곡\"，聊喜好: 곡=one specific song/song number, formal; 노래=the song itself, everyday. Use "이 곡" to request a song, "이 노래" to talk about preferences.
번(番)+호(号)=番号。日本\"番号\"、中文\"编号\"三边同源，一次记住。: 번(番)+호(号)=番号. Japanese "番号" and Chinese "编号" share the same origin—learn once, remember all three.
검(检)+색(索)=检索。跟\"检索\"完全同源，比\"搜索\"更接近韩语原词。: 검(检)+색(索)=检索. Same origin as Chinese "检索", closer to the Korean original than "搜索".
此处指点歌加入队列。: Here it means adding a song to the queue.
예(预)+약(约)=预约。跟中文完全同源。노래방里\"예약\"专指\"排队等唱\: 예(预)+약(约)=预约. Same origin as Chinese. In noraebang, "예약" specifically means "waiting in line to sing", not reserving a seat.
「건너뛰다」的名词化，遥控器按键名。: Nominalization of 「건너뛰다」, the remote control button name.
건너(跨过)+뛰기(跳)=跨过去跳。固有词组合，画面感十足。: 건너(cross over)+뛰기(jump)=jump across. Native word combination, very vivid.
잘(好好地)+부르다(唱)=唱得好。부르다本义\"叫/唤\"，唱歌也是\"叫出来: 잘(well)+부르다(sing)=sing well. 부르다 originally means "call/summon", singing is also "calling out".
음(音)+정(程)=音程。乐理里的\"音程\"指音与音的距离，韩语引申为唱得准不: 음(音)+정(程)=음정. In music theory, 'interval' means the distance between notes; in Korean, it's extended to mean how accurately you sing.
음정=音高准不准；박자=节拍对不对。夸别人时两个词一起用最专业。: 음정 = pitch accuracy; 박자 = rhythm accuracy. Using both together when complimenting someone sounds most professional.
박(拍)+자(子)=拍子。日语\"拍子\"同源，就是打拍子的\"拍\"。: 박(拍)+자(子)=박자. Japanese '拍子' shares the same origin—it's the 'beat' in keeping time.
고(高)+음(音)=高音，跟中文完全同源。对应词有저음(低音)。: 고(高)+음(音)=고음, completely cognate with Chinese. The counterpart is 저음 (low note).
外来语 duet，两人一唱一和。: Loanword from 'duet'—two people singing back and forth.
英文 duet 音译成两音节：듀-엣。두엣是错的，듀엣才对。: The English 'duet' is transliterated into two syllables: 듀-엣. 두엣 is wrong; 듀엣 is correct.
음(饮)+료(料)=饮料，跟中文完全同源。念时ㄹ受前面ㅁ影响变成ㄴ音：eum-n: 음(饮)+료(料)=음료, completely cognate with Chinese. When pronounced, ㄹ becomes ㄴ due to the preceding ㅁ: eum-nyo.
맥(麦)+주(酒)=麦酒，跟日语ビール不同，韩语走汉字词路线。: 맥(麦)+주(酒)=맥주. Unlike Japanese 'ビール', Korean uses a Sino-Korean word.

固有词얼음来自动词얼다(结冰)+名词化-음=冻起来的东西。跟\"冰\"字面同义。: The native word 얼음 comes from the verb 얼다 (to freeze) + nominalizer -음 = something frozen. It's literally synonymous with 'ice.'
英文 chicken 音译成치킨，但在韩国只指\"炸鸡\"，白煮鸡叫닭。炸鸡+啤: The English 'chicken' is transliterated as 치킨, but in Korea it only means 'fried chicken'; boiled chicken is 닭. Fried chicken + beer = 치맥.
시간(时间)+연장(延长)=延长时间。两个汉字词拼起来，跟中文完全同源。: 시간 (time) + 연장 (extension) = extended time. Two Sino-Korean words combined, fully cognate with Chinese.
请给一个包间。: Please give us a private room.
进店要包间时: When entering and asking for a private room.
数字「하나」在量词前变成「한」（한 개），单独说时才保持하나。这里「룸 하나」是: The number '하나' becomes '한' before a counter (한 개), but stays '하나' when said alone. Here, '룸 하나' is the object said alone, so '하나' is correct.
（更正式）麻烦给一个包间。: (More formal) Could we have a private room, please?

是（有收音 用 이요）: Yes (use 이요 after a final consonant)
数「시간」（小时时长）用固有数词（한/두/세/네 시간）；「시」（几点钟）也用固: For counting 시간 (duration in hours), use native Korean numbers (한/두/세/네 시간); for 시 (o'clock), also use native numbers. But for 분 (minutes) and 초 (seconds), use Sino-Korean numbers instead. This mixed rule is the easiest to trip over.
这首歌怎么找？: How do I find this song?

「어떻게」是问方法(how)，「무엇을」是问对象(what)。别搞混——问方法用: 어떻게 asks about method (how), 무엇을 asks about object (what). Don't mix them up—use 어떻게 for how, and 무슨 곡 for what song.
（更委婉）请问这首歌该怎么找呢？: (More polite) How should I go about finding this song?
（对朋友半语）这首歌咋找？: (To a friend, casual) How do I find this song?

往下一首（곡有ㄱ收音 + 으로）: To the next song (곡 ends in ㄱ + 으로)
「곡」以ㄱ收音结尾，方向助词用「으로」不用「로」——「곡으로」✓／「곡로」✗。ㄹ: 곡 ends with the ㄱ final consonant, so the direction particle is 으로, not 로—곡으로 ✓ / 곡로 ✗. The exception is ㄹ, which takes 로 (e.g., 서울로); all other consonants take 으로.
（更委婉）跳到下一首怎么样？: (More polite) How about skipping to the next song?
邀请朋友合唱时: When inviting a friend to sing together
「부르다」是「르」不规则动词，遇到 -아/어 时 으 脱落 + ㄹ 加倍：부르: '부르다' is a '르' irregular verb. When followed by -아/어, the 으 drops and ㄹ doubles: 부르 + 어 → 불러. '부르어요' is wrong; '불러요' is correct. Similar: 흐르다→흘러요 / 모르다→몰라요.
要求店员调设备时: When asking staff to adjust equipment
「좀」不是数量副词\"一点点\"，而是缓和请求的语气词。省掉也语法对，但显得生硬: '좀' isn't the quantity adverb 'a little'; it's a particle that softens requests. Omitting it is grammatically fine but sounds blunt. Adding it is more polite.
（极度礼貌）能麻烦帮忙调大音量吗？: (Very polite) Could you please help turn up the volume?
（对朋友半语）音量调大点。: (To a friend, casual) Turn the volume up.
结束前问朋友要不要再唱: Asking a friend if they want to sing more before ending
「-(으)ㄹ래요?」只用于问对方意愿，不用第三人称。想说\"他要不要唱\"要用「: '-(으)ㄹ래요?' is only used to ask about the listener's intention, not third person. To say 'Does he want to sing?' use '-고 싶어할까요?'.
（更礼貌）再唱一首好吗？: (More polite) Could you sing one more?
「数字 + 시간이요」是最简时长回答。: 'Number + 시간이요' is the simplest way to answer duration.
「数字 + 명이요」是回答人数最简答法。: 'Number + 명이요' is the simplest way to answer the number of people.
要小包间还是大包间？: Would you like a small room or a large room?
「크기 + 걸로요」是选大小最简答法。: 'Size + 걸로요' is the simplest way to choose a size.
直接说饮料名 + 数量，一步到位。: Just say the drink name + quantity, done in one step.
积极响应邀请，氛围最重要。: Respond enthusiastically to invitations—the vibe matters most.
「감사합니다 + 谦虚」是韩国接受赞美的标准。: '감사합니다 + humility' is the standard way to accept compliments in Korea.

在房间里。去 5 号房。: It's in the room. Go to room 5.
你要唱什么？: What are you going to sing?
OO 的歌。一起唱！: An OO song. Let's sing together!

(노래 끝) 怎么样？唱得好吗？: (Song ends) How was it? Did I sing well?
哇唱得好！音准好。: Wow, you sang well! Great pitch.
谢谢！再唱一首吗？: Thanks! Want to sing another one?
好！这次轮到我了。: Okay! This time it's my turn.
韩国图书馆 · 考试战争的战壕: Korean Library · The Trenches of the Exam War
韩国图书馆不是「安静看书的地方」——它是「考试战争的战壕」。韩国人去图书馆不是为: Korean libraries aren't 'quiet places to read'—they're 'trenches in the exam war.' Koreans go to the library not to read, but to **study for exams**.
规则第一条：安静。手机振动都不行: Rule number one: Quiet. Not even phone vibrations.
小组讨论室——韩国图书馆特色: Group discussion rooms—a Korean library specialty.
카공족 · 在咖啡馆学习的人: 카공족 · People who study at cafés
韩国人不在图书馆学习——他们在咖啡馆学。这叫「카공」（카페 + 공부）。一杯 4: Koreans don't study at the library—they study at cafés. This is called '카공' (café + studying). One 4,000 won Americano buys you a whole day. Korean café Wi-Fi is faster than the library's.
韩国公共图书馆的畅销书排队等 6 个月是常态。热门小说只能去书店买。图书馆主要是: At Korean public libraries, waiting 6 months for a bestseller is normal. For popular novels, you'll have to buy them at a bookstore. Libraries are mainly for students studying and prepping for exams—참고도서 (reference books) can't be borrowed, only read in the library.
韩国大学图书馆座位预约制。考试季（期中/期末）早上 7 点开馆，6:50 已排队: Korean university libraries use a seat reservation system. During exam season (midterms/finals), the library opens at 7 AM, but people are already queuing at 6:50. Some libraries even have "seat time limits"—after 4 hours, you must get up and rest for 30 minutes.
打印比复印贵: Printing is more expensive than copying
打印（출력）100 원/张，复印（복사）50 원/张。U 盘插打印机直接打，不需: Printing (출력) is 100 won per page, copying (복사) is 50 won per page. You can plug a USB drive into the printer and print directly—no computer needed. But some libraries only take coins, so bring change.
水杯 OK，热食禁止: Water bottles OK, hot food not allowed

割引(할인)＝汉字词，日语来的。10% 할인=九折，20% 할인=八折。: 할인 (discount) is a Sino-Korean word borrowed from Japanese. 10% 할인 = 10% off, 20% 할인 = 20% off.

세일=促销活动（一段期间）；할인=具体折扣数字。促销期内商品会打折。: 세일 means a sale event (a period); 할인 is the specific discount. Items are discounted during the sale.

membership 音译，商场会员卡结账前会被问。: Loanword 'membership,' you'll be asked about your store membership card before checkout.
换尺寸/颜色/款式都用这词。: Use this word for size, color, or style changes.
交换(교환)＝汉字词，跟中文「交换」同源。: 교환 is a Sino-Korean word, same origin as Chinese '交换' (exchange).
還拂(환불)＝汉字词「还拂」，即退钱。规则通常 7 天内可选。: 환불 is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'refund.' Usually you can choose within 7 days.
환불=退钱；교환=换成别的商品。买贵了想省钱选환불，尺码不对选교환。: Refund = get your money back; exchange = swap for a different item. If you overpaid and want to save money, choose refund; if the size is wrong, choose exchange.

领收证(영수증)＝汉字词「领收证」。退换/报销都靠它。: Receipt (영수증) = Sino-Korean word for 'receipt.' You need it for returns, exchanges, or reimbursements.
售后在哪办？: Where do I go for after-sales service?
After Service 缩写，念英文字母「에이에스」。삼성/LG 服务点都写: Abbreviation for After Service, pronounced as English letters 'A/S.' Samsung/LG service centers all use 'A/S 센터.'
汉字词「无偿」。保修期内不收费。: Sino-Korean word for 'free of charge.' No fee during the warranty period.
無償(무상)＝汉字词「无偿」，保修期内维修/换货不收费。: 무상 = Sino-Korean for 'free of charge'; repairs or exchanges are free within the warranty period.
무상=服务/维修免费（보증기간 내 무상 A/S）；무료=商品/入场免费（무료: 무상 = free for services/repairs (e.g., free A/S within warranty); 무료 = free for goods/admission (e.g., free shipping).

衣服用입다，鞋用신다，帽/眼镜/口罩用쓰다，包用메다/들다——不能一律用입다。: Use 입다 for clothes, 신다 for shoes, 쓰다 for hats/glasses/masks, and 메다/들다 for bags—you can't use 입다 for everything.

大一号的（크다 + -ㄴ + 것 + 助词 로）: One size bigger (크다 + -ㄴ + 것 + particle 로).
「하나 큰」不是「큰 하나」——修饰形容词在名词化「걸로」前，「하나」表示\"一: It's '하나 큰,' not '큰 하나'—the modifying adjective comes before the nominalized '걸로,' and '하나' means 'one size/step.'
（更礼貌）能麻烦给大一号吗？: (More polite) Could I get one size bigger, please?
「다른」是修饰形，必须直接接名词；不能说「다르는 색」——다르다是形容词，修饰形: '다른' is a modifier and must directly precede a noun; you can't say '다르는 색'—다르다 is an adjective, and its modifier form is 다른.
（更委婉）不知道还有别的颜色吗？: (More polite) I don't suppose there's another color?
动词接「-는 거」，形容词接「-ㄴ/은 거」——할인되다是动词所以是「할인되는: Verbs take '-는 거', adjectives take '-ㄴ/은 거'—할인되다 is a verb, so it's '할인되는 거', not '할인된 거'.
（更正式）这是打折商品吗？: (More formal) Is this a discounted item?
出示商品要换退: Showing the item to exchange or return
「-ㄹ 수 있어요?」问的是「有没有可能/店规允许」；如果想问「我可不可以（求许: '-ㄹ 수 있어요?' asks if it's possible/store policy allows; if you want to ask 'may I (ask permission)', use '-아/어도 돼요?'—'교환해도 돼요?' leans more toward a personal request.

적립하다是\"你自己去累积\"，店员帮你时应该说「적립해 주세요」；只说「적립하: 적립하다 means 'you accumulate it yourself'; when the staff does it for you, you should say '적립해 주세요'; just saying '적립하세요' sounds a bit like a command.

「비싼데」不是「비싸는데」——形容词接「-ㄴ데」，动词才接「-는데」。: '비싼데' isn't '비싸는데' — adjectives take '-ㄴ데', only verbs take '-는데'.

不确定时坦白说不清楚，店员会主动建议起点尺码。: If you're unsure, just say so — the staff will suggest a starting size.

肯定「네, 카드로요」是最短答法。现金说「현금으로요」。: '네, 카드로요' is the shortest way to confirm. For cash, say '현금으로요'.
要，请给我。: Yes, please give it to me.
想收据说「네, 주세요」；不要说「아니요, 괜찮아요」。: To get a receipt, say '네, 주세요'; don't say '아니요, 괜찮아요'.

可以，试衣间在那边。尺寸多少？: Sure, the fitting room is over there. What size?

来换昨天买的衣服。: I'm here to exchange clothes I bought yesterday.
请出示收据。有什么问题吗？: Please show your receipt. Is there a problem?
尺码不合适。想换大一号。: The size doesn't fit. I'd like to exchange for a bigger one.
好，换成同款 L 码吗？: Okay, exchange for the same style in L?

韩国药店 · 没处方买不到抗生素: Korean Pharmacies · No Antibiotics Without a Prescription
韩国药店跟中国最大的区别：没有处方买不到抗生素。感冒了去药店，药剂师只会给你缓解: The biggest difference between Korean and Chinese pharmacies: you can't get antibiotics without a prescription. If you have a cold, the pharmacist will only give you symptom-relief medication—you'll need to go to the hospital for a prescription.
药店标志是绿十字，不是「药」字: The pharmacy sign is a green cross, not the character '약'
抗生素需要处方，普通感冒药不需要: Antibiotics require a prescription, but regular cold medicine doesn't
有健康保险药费打 3 折: With health insurance, medication costs 30% of the full price
感冒药 = 一包多种: Cold medicine = one packet with multiple pills
韩国感冒药不是一盒药片——药剂师会给你配好「약 봉투」（药袋），每个时间点一包，: Korean cold medicine isn't a box of pills—the pharmacist prepares '약 봉투' (medicine packets), one for each time of day, containing 3-5 different pills: fever reducer, cough suppressant, anti-inflammatory, and vitamins. Just take 3 packets a day; no need to figure it out yourself.
약은 물로 · 药必须用水: 약은 물로 · Medicine must be taken with water
韩国人吃药必须用凉水，不用热茶或饮料。药剂师会特别叮嘱「물로 드세요」（用水服用: Koreans must take medicine with cold water, not hot tea or drinks. Pharmacists will specifically advise '물로 드세요' (take with water). Taking medicine with tea is believed to reduce its effectiveness—this is a Korean obsession.
韩国大部分药店支持外送——打电话给药店，说症状，药剂师配好药，30 分钟内骑手送: Most Korean pharmacies offer delivery—call the pharmacy, describe your symptoms, the pharmacist prepares the medicine, and a rider delivers it to your door within 30 minutes. Delivery fee: 2,000-3,000 won. Fever of 39°C and don't want to go out? One phone call and it's done.
韩国普通药店 9 点关门。深夜生病搜「24시 약국」——每个区有 1-2 家通宵: Regular Korean pharmacies close at 9 PM. If you get sick late at night, search for '24시 약국'—each district has 1-2 all-night pharmacies. In Seoul, Gangnam has one near Yeoksam Station, and Hongdae has one near Hapjeong Station.
结账时药剂师必问。持외국인등록증 6 个月以上可申请国民健康保险（NHIS）。有: The pharmacist always asks this at checkout. If you've held an 외국인등록증 (alien registration card) for over 6 months, you can apply for National Health Insurance (NHIS). With insurance, medication is 30-70% cheaper—students must get it.
为什么韩国药店不卖「999 感冒灵」？: Why don't Korean pharmacies sell '999 Cold Medicine'?
中韩药品品牌不通——韩国感冒药本土品牌有「판피린」（Panpyrin）、「테라플: Chinese and Korean medicine brands don't overlap—Korean cold medicine brands include '판피린' (Panpyrin), '테라플루' (Theraflu), etc. To buy Chinese medicine, you'd need to go to a Chinese store (Central District/Yanbian Street). Most Korean medicines are sweeter and come in smaller pills.
한약 和 양약 有什么区别？: What's the difference between 한약 and 양약?
한약（韓薬）= 传统草药，需去 한의원（韩医院）开方；양약（洋薬）= 西药，普通: 한약 (Korean medicine) = traditional herbal medicine, requires a prescription from a 한의원 (Korean medicine clinic); 양약 (Western medicine) = sold at regular 약국 (pharmacies). For colds and fevers, buy 양약; for chronic conditions, visit a 한의원. Prices differ by 5-10 times.
不是问「有没有保险公司」——是问你是否加入韩国国民健康保险（NHIS）。有的话药: It's not asking 'do you have an insurance company'—it's asking if you're enrolled in Korea's National Health Insurance (NHIS). If yes, you pay 30% of the medication cost; if no, you pay full price. Answer '네, 건강보험이요' or '아니요, 없어요'.
请给感冒药。: Please give me some cold medicine.
嗓子痛，还有点发烧。: I have a sore throat and a slight fever.
一天吃几次？: How many times a day should I take it?
药袋写清剂量: The pill bag clearly states the dosage
药剂师用药袋分装并写明「1일 3회 식후」（一日 3 次饭后）。药袋不要扔——上: The pharmacist packs the medicine in a pill bag and writes '1일 3회 식후' (3 times a day after meals). Don't throw away the pill bag—it has the name, usage, and side effects, and customs may check it when you return home.
许多韩国感冒药和消炎药含 아세트아미노펜（对乙酰氨基酚），酒精一起吃伤肝。买药时: Many Korean cold and anti-inflammatory medicines contain 아세트아미노펜 (acetaminophen). Taking it with alcohol can damage your liver. When buying medicine, the pharmacist will ask, '음주 안 하시죠? (You don't drink, right?)'.
儿童/孕妇 明确说: Clearly state if it's for children or pregnant women
有小孩用药或自己孕妇，一定要说「아이 거예요（是给小孩的）」/「임신 중이에요（: If you're getting medicine for a child or you're pregnant, be sure to say '아이 거예요' (It's for a child) or '임신 중이에요' (I'm pregnant). The pharmacist will switch to a safer formulation.
向药剂师描述症状时: When describing symptoms to the pharmacist
「열이 나다」=发烧出现，나다是固定搭配。: '열이 나다' means a fever appears; 나다 is a fixed collocation.
기침＝固有词。跟열一样搭配「나다」（自然出现）：기침이 나요 = 咳嗽出来了。: 기침 is a native Korean word. Like 열, it pairs with '나다' (naturally appearing): 기침이 나요 = a cough came out.
기침＝咳嗽（喉咙）；재채기＝打喷嚏（鼻子）。两个都用「나다」。: 기침 means cough (throat); 재채기 means sneeze (nose). Both use '나다'.
코(鼻子)+ㅅ+물(水)＝鼻子的水，两个固有词拼合。中间的ㅅ叫사이시옷（连接音）: 코 (nose) + ㅅ + 물 (water) = nasal water, combining two native words. The ㅅ in the middle is called 사이시옷 (linking sound).
汉字词「头痛」。也说「머리가 아파요」。: The Sino-Korean word for headache. You can also say '머리가 아파요'.
두통(头痛)＝汉字词「头痛」，与中文同源直接搬。口语「머리가 아파요」更常用。: 두통 (headache) is a Sino-Korean word, directly borrowed from Chinese. In speech, '머리가 아파요' is more common.
두통＝名词（较书面/写药袋）；머리가 아파요＝句子（口语）。药剂师听两个都懂。: 두통 is a noun (more formal/used on pill bags); 머리가 아파요 is a sentence (colloquial). The pharmacist understands both.
汉字词「腹痛」。日常说「배가 아파요」。: The Sino-Korean word for abdominal pain. In daily speech, say '배가 아파요'.
복통(腹痛)＝汉字词「腹痛」，中文同源。药袋写복통，日常口语说「배가 아파요」。: 복통 (腹痛) is a Sino-Korean word meaning 'abdominal pain,' sharing the same origin as Chinese. The medicine bag says 복통, but in everyday speech you'd say '배가 아파요.'
복통＝名词（书面/正式）；배가 아파요＝句子（口语）。跟药剂师说哪个都行。: 복통 is a noun (written/formal); 배가 아파요 is a sentence (colloquial). Either works when talking to a pharmacist.
直接购买特定药品时: When buying a specific medicine directly
综合款，含退烧+止咳+抗组胺。: All-in-one, containing fever reducer + cough suppressant + antihistamine.
감기(感气，汉字词「感气」意受寒)+약(药)＝药，拼起来就是感冒药。中文现在说「: 감기 (感气, Sino-Korean for 'catching cold') + 약 (medicine) = cold medicine. In Chinese, '感冒' is used now, not '感气.'
해열제(解热剂)＝해(解)+열(热)+제(剂)＝解+热+剂＝退烧的药剂，汉字拼合: 해열제 (解热剂) = 해 (解) + 열 (热) + 제 (剂) = antipyretic medicine, a Sino-Korean compound.
해열제专降烧；진통제专止痛。发烧+头痛可以问药剂师推荐综合款。: 해열제 lowers fever; 진통제 relieves pain. For fever + headache, ask the pharmacist for a combined option.
진통제(镇痛剂)＝진(镇)+통(痛)+제(剂)＝镇+痛+剂，与中文「镇痛剂」同源: 진통제 (镇痛剂) = 진 (镇) + 통 (痛) + 제 (剂), sharing the same origin as Chinese '镇痛剂.'
汉字词「消化剂」，饭后吃。: Sino-Korean word '消化剂' (digestive), taken after meals.
소화제(消化剂)＝소화(消化)+제(剂)，同中文「消化剂」。吃撑或胃胀常用。: 소화제 (消化剂) = 소화 (消化) + 제 (剂), same as Chinese '消化剂.' Commonly used for overeating or bloating.
汉字词「软膏」。外用。: Sino-Korean word '软膏' (ointment). For external use.
연고(软膏)＝汉字词「软膏」，연(软)+고(膏)。外用涂抹的药，动词搭配「바르다: 연고 (软膏) is a Sino-Korean word, 연 (软) + 고 (膏). It's a topical medicine; use the verb '바르다' (apply), not '먹다' (eat).
询问用法用量时: When asking about dosage and usage
하루＝固有词，一整天的概念。加助词에变「하루에」＝在一天里，用来表频率范围。: 하루 is a native Korean word meaning 'a whole day.' Adding the particle 에 makes it 하루에, meaning 'in a day,' used to express frequency range.
搭配「번」= 次数量词。: Paired with 번, a counter for times.
몇(几，固有词疑问)+번(番，汉字词量词「次」)，两词拼起来问频率。: 몇 (how many, native interrogative) + 번 (番, Sino-Korean counter for 'times') combine to ask about frequency.
汉字词「食后」。相反「식전」（饭前）。: Sino-Korean for 'after meals.' The opposite is 식전 (before meals).
식후(食后)＝汉字词，식(食)+후(后)＝饭+后＝吃完饭之后。药袋常印这两个字。: 식후 (食后) is Sino-Korean: 식 (食, food) + 후 (后, after) = after eating. These characters are often printed on medicine packets.
식후＝饭后（吃饭之后）；식전＝饭前（吃饭之前）。药袋会明确写哪个时段。: 식후 means after meals; 식전 means before meals. The medicine packet clearly indicates which time.
알(颗粒/珠子)+약(药)＝颗粒状的药＝药片。数它用固有量词「알」，一片就是「한: 알 (grain/bead) + 약 (medicine) = granular medicine = tablet. Count it with the native counter 알; one tablet is 한 알.
알약＝硬药片（片剂）；캡슐＝胶囊。物形不同，服法基本一样。: 알약 is a hard tablet; 캡슐 is a capsule. Different forms, but the dosage is basically the same.
부작용(副作用)＝汉字词，跟中文「副作用」完全同源，一次搞定不用背。: 부작용 (副作用) is Sino-Korean, sharing the same origin as the Chinese '副作用,' so you don't need to memorize it separately.
