「-당하다」= 被动后缀，多用于负面：거절당하다（被拒绝）/ 무시당하다（被无视: "-당하다" = passive suffix, often used negatively: 거절당하다 (to be rejected) / 무시당하다 (to be ignored) / 차별당하다 (to be discriminated against). It emphasizes the sense of victimization more than "~을/를 받다".
억울하다 = 「委屈」（觉得不公平/无处申诉）；슬프다 = 「难过」（心情低落）: 억울하다 = feeling wronged (unfair, no one to appeal to); 슬프다 = sad (feeling down). Use 억울하다 for discrimination/injustice, 슬프다 for heartbreak/loss of a loved one.
汉字词「異議提起」。念 i-ui-je-gi。「이의제기하다」= 「提出异议」是: It's a Sino-Korean word "異議提起". Pronounced i-ui-je-gi. "이의제기하다" = "to raise an objection" is a legal term — using it here immediately shows you know the rules.
我想提出异议。: I want to raise an objection.
被歧视对话可以录音（韩国允许单方录音）。截图招聘广告、保存工资协议。事后投诉时都: You can record conversations where you're discriminated against (Korea allows one-party recording). Screenshot job postings and save wage agreements. These all serve as evidence when filing a complaint later.
找韩国朋友陪同: Have a Korean friend accompany you
重要维权场合有韩国朋友/学校国际处老师陪同，对方会更谨慎。你说韩语受挫也有人接话: In important rights-protection situations, having a Korean friend or a school international office teacher accompany you makes the other party more cautious. If you struggle with Korean, someone can step in.
韩国雇佣歧视投诉从事件发生日起 90 天内有效。超过就无法立案。发现问题要及时。: Complaints about employment discrimination in Korea are valid within 90 days from the date of the incident. After that, they cannot be filed. Address issues promptly.
면접(面接)＝汉字词「面接」，跟日语同源。看面试用「면접 보다」（看面试）。: 면접(面接) = Sino-Korean word '面接', same origin as Japanese. To 'take an interview' use '면접 보다' (literally 'watch an interview').
汉字词「不合格」。相反 합격。: Sino-Korean word '不合格'. The opposite is 합격.
불(不)+합격(合格)＝汉字词「不合格」，去掉「불」就是「合格」。: 불(不) + 합격(合格) = Sino-Korean word '不合格'. Remove '불' and you get '合格'.
불합격＝没通过；합격＝通过。前缀「불」= 「不」。: 불합격 = fail; 합격 = pass. The prefix '불' = 'not'.
거절(拒絶)＝汉字词「拒绝」，加「-당하다」变被动：거절당하다＝被拒绝。: 거절(拒絶) = Sino-Korean word 'reject'. Add '-당하다' to make it passive: 거절당하다 = to be rejected.
사유(事由)＝汉字词「事由」，比「이유」更书面正式。: 사유(事由) = Sino-Korean word 'reason', more formal/written than '이유'.
사유＝正式/书面（多用于表格、法律）；이유＝口语通用。问原因两者都行，投诉时用사: 사유 = formal/written (used in forms, legal contexts); 이유 = common in speech. Both work for asking reasons, but using 사유 in complaints sounds firmer.
固有词，ㅂ 不规则：아쉽다 → 아쉬워요。语气比 슬프다 轻，多用「差一点」的场: Native Korean word, ㅂ irregular: 아쉽다 → 아쉬워요. Lighter in tone than 슬프다, often used for 'so close' situations.
무시(無视)＝汉字词「无视」+ 하다。加「-당하다」变被动：무시당하다＝被无视。: 무시(無视) = Sino-Korean 'ignore' + 하다. Add '-당하다' to make it passive: 무시당하다 = to be ignored.
차별(差別)＝汉字词「差别/歧视」。加「-당하다」＝被歧视；加「하다」＝歧视人。: 차별(差別) = Sino-Korean 'discrimination'. Add '-당하다' = to be discriminated against; add '하다' = to discriminate.
불(不)+공정(公正)＝汉字词「不公正」。前缀「불」= 否定，跟불합격同套逻辑。: 불(不)+공정(公正) = Sino-Korean 'unfairness'. The prefix '불' = negation, same logic as 불합격.
불공정＝不公平（有加害感）；공정＝公正、平等（中性）。抗议时用불공정更强。: 불공정 = unfair (with a sense of harm); 공정 = fair, impartial (neutral). Use 불공정 for stronger protest.
외면(外面)＝汉字词「转开脸/回避」。比무시多一层「明知却装看不见」的意思。: 외면(外面) = Sino-Korean 'turn away/avoid'. It adds a layer of 'pretending not to see' compared to 무시.
못(不能)+본(看过的)+척(假装)＝装作没看到。「V-ㄴ 척하다」＝ 「装 V: Pretending not to see. 'V-ㄴ 척하다' = 'pretend to V' pattern.
항의(抗議)＝汉字词「抗议」+ 하다。语气比이의제기口语，比不满强烈。: 항의(抗議) = Sino-Korean 'protest' + 하다. More colloquial than 이의제기, stronger than dissatisfaction.
항의＝口语抗议、发牢骚；이의제기＝法律术语，走正式流程时用。: 항의 = colloquial protest/complaint; 이의제기 = legal term, used in formal procedures.
想提出异议。: I want to raise an objection.
汉字词「異議提起」。: Sino-Korean word '異議提起' (raising an objection).
이의(異議)+제기(提起)＝汉字词「提出异议」，法律/行政用语，说出来立刻显得懂: 이의(異議)+제기(提起) = Sino-Korean 'raise an objection', legal/administrative term that makes you sound rule-savvy.
想提异议: I want to raise an objection.
정당(正當)＝汉字词「正当」+ 하다（形容词化）。表示「合法/有正当理由」。: 정당(正當) = Sino-Korean 'justified' + 하다 (adjectivized). Means 'legal/has valid reason'.
정당하다＝有正当理由/合法（针对行为）；공정하다＝公平（针对过程）。: 정당하다 = has valid reason/legal (for actions); 공정하다 = fair (for processes).
권리(权利)＝汉字词「权利」。写作两字念作 궐-리（连音变化）。: 권리(权利) = Sino-Korean 'right'. Written as two characters, pronounced 궐-리 (liaison change).
권리＝可以主张（权利）；의무＝必须履行（义务）。维权时说제 권리。: Rights = what you can claim; duties = what you must fulfill. When asserting rights, say 제 권리.
공정(公正)+하다 → 副词形 공정하게。「A-게 + V」＝ 「按 A 的方式: 공정(公正)+하다 → adverb form 공정하게. 'A-게 + V' = standard structure for 'do V in the way of A.'
화(火)+나다(冒出)＝火气冒出来＝生气。跟中文「上火」的比喻同源。: 화(火)+나다(冒出) = fire flares up = to be angry. Same metaphor as Chinese '上火' (getting heated).
억울(抑鬱)＝汉字词「抑郁」，但含义是「觉得不公无处申诉」——被冤枉的那种委屈。: 억울(抑鬱) = Sino-Korean 'depression,' but means 'feeling wronged with no outlet' — the frustration of being falsely accused.
억울하다＝觉得不公平的委屈（要有加害方）；슬프다＝纯粹心情低落。被歧视时用억울하: 억울하다 = feeling unfairly wronged (requires a perpetrator); 슬프다 = just feeling down. When discriminated against, 억울하다 is more precise.
실망(失望)＝汉字词「失望」+ 하다。多用过去式实际感受：실망했어요。: 실망(失望) = Sino-Korean 'disappointment' + 하다. Often used in past tense for actual feelings: 실망했어요.
분노(憤怒)＝汉字词「愤怒」。比화更书面/严重，多用于新闻标题。: 분노(憤怒) = Sino-Korean 'fury.' More formal/severe than 화, often in news headlines.
固有词「忍/憋」。「못 참겠어요」＝ 忍不下去了，是委屈爆发前的常用句。: Native word for 'endure/hold in.' '못 참겠어요' = can't hold it in anymore, a common phrase before emotions burst out.
成了（되다 过去时敬语）: It turned out (되다 past tense honorific)
「어떻게 됐어요?」用过去时됐어요，因为结果已经出来。用现在时「어떻게 돼요?」: '어떻게 됐어요?' uses past tense 됐어요 because the result is already out. Using present tense '어떻게 돼요?' would ask 'how is it going,' a different meaning.
（更委婉）面试结果出来了吗？: (More polite) Has the interview result come out?
（半语，朋友之间）面试怎么样？: (Casual, between friends) How was the interview?
没通过。理由是什么？: It didn't pass. What's the reason?
「이유가 뭐예요?」用主语助词「가」而非「는」——追问单一具体原因用가；泛泛谈话: '이유가 뭐예요?' uses subject particle '가' not '는'—use 가 for a single specific reason; use 는 for general topics.
（更委婉）如果不合格，能告知事由吗？: (More polite) If it's a fail, could you tell me the reason?
被拒绝了。很委屈。: I got rejected. It's so unfair.
「-당하다」只接负面动词（거절/무시/차별/폭행）。「선물당하다」不成立，正面动: '-당하다' only attaches to negative verbs (거절/무시/차별/폭행). '선물당하다' doesn't work; for positive actions use '-받다' (선물받다 = receive a gift).
（正式书面）被拒绝了，非常委屈。: (Formal written) I was rejected and feel deeply wronged.
想提异议（이의제기하다 + -고 싶다）: Want to raise an objection (이의제기하다 + -고 싶다)
「-고 싶다」只能用于第一人称。对第三人称要用「-고 싶어하다」：동료가 이의제: '-고 싶다' is only for first person. For third person use '-고 싶어하다': 동료가 이의제기하고 싶어해요 (My colleague wants to raise an objection).
（正式书面）我要提出异议，请告知正式流程。: (Formal written) I'd like to raise an objection; please inform me of the official procedure.
修饰动词必须用「-게」副词化，不能用修饰形「-ㄴ」。「공정한 해 주세요」错误，: To modify a verb, you must use the adverbial '-게', not the attributive '-ㄴ'. '공정한 해 주세요' is wrong; '공정한 사람' is correct for modifying a noun.
（极度礼貌）能公平处理吗？: (Very polite) Could you handle this fairly?
能给我考虑（생각하다 + -아 주시다 + -ㄹ 수 있다）: Could you consider it for me (생각하다 + -아 주시다 + -ㄹ 수 있다)
「다시 생각해 주실 수 있어요?」= 다시（再）+ 생각하다 + -아 주다: 「다시 생각해 주실 수 있어요?」= 다시 (again) + 생각하다 + -아 주다 + -시- (honorific) + -ㄹ 수 있다 (can) — four layers stacked; missing one layer lowers the respect.
（极度礼貌）不知能否再考虑一次？: (Extremely polite) Would it be possible to reconsider once more?
「-지 마세요」= 请不要 V（禁止敬语），只用于动词；形容词/名词不能直接接，: 「-지 마세요」= Please don't V (polite prohibition), only used with verbs; adjectives/nouns can't directly attach, so 「차별적이지 마세요」 is wrong. For nouns, add 「하다」: 차별하다→차별하지 마세요.
（半语，只对熟人）别歧视。: (Banmal, only to close friends) Don't discriminate.
没通过。不知道理由。: I didn't pass. I don't know the reason.
结果 + 疑惑感 = 引出朋友帮你分析。: Result + sense of confusion = prompts friend to help you analyze.
简洁陈述被拒绝的关键疑点。: Briefly state the key suspicious point of being rejected.
肯定 + 具体证据（不回答）说明歧视性质。: Affirmation + specific evidence (no response) shows the discriminatory nature.
要提出异议。: I'm going to raise an objection.
面试被歧视了。: I was discriminated against in the interview.
直接说被歧视，让对方知道严重性。: Directly say you were discriminated against to make the other person aware of the seriousness.
接受帮助 + 邀请陪同，多一人更安全。: Accepting help + inviting accompaniment, safer with more people.
被无视/歧视的具体行为: Specific acts of being ignored/discriminated against
没通过。没告诉理由。: I didn't pass. They didn't give a reason.
不知道。只说「招了别人」。: I don't know. They just said 'we hired someone else.'
面试时说了什么？: What did they ask during the interview?
也没怎么问。回答也不给。: They didn't ask much. They didn't even respond to my answers.
被无视？不抗议吗？: Ignored? Aren't you going to protest?
要提异议。要求公平对待。: I'll raise an objection. Demand fair treatment.
对。加油！一起去。: Right. You can do it! Let's go together.
我是上次面试没通过的人。: I'm the one who didn't pass the last interview.
是的，什么事？: Yes, what can I do for you?
我想提异议。请告诉理由。: I'd like to raise an objection. Please tell me the reason.
理由？就是不是合适的人。: Reason? Just that they're not the right person.
面试时也没怎么问。: They didn't ask much during the interview either.
不要无视。这不公平。: Don't ignore me. This isn't fair.
(한숨) 好了。下次联系。: (Sigh) Fine. I'll contact you next time.
사냥꾼거리 · 紧张对话训练场: Hunter Street · High-Pressure Conversation Training Ground
「길을 잃었어요」（我迷路了）—— 在不安全的场景快速用韩语求助/婉拒/撤离。这: '길을 잃었어요' (I'm lost) — Quickly ask for help, politely decline, or retreat in Korean in unsafe situations. This is the high-pressure conversation skill required at TOPIK intermediate level.
「도와주세요!」（帮帮我！）是所有紧急场景通用的呼救。跟着说位置：「여기 어디예: '도와주세요!' (Help me!) is the universal cry for help in all emergencies. Follow up with your location: '여기 어디예요?' / '길을 잃었어요'. A passerby will come over.
112 是韩国警察号码。App「Safe 112」外国人友好，可发定位。地铁站/: 112 is the Korean police number. The 'Safe 112' app is foreigner-friendly and can send your location. There are '비상벨' (emergency bells) at subway stations and convenience store entrances.
突发状况找 GS25/CU 便利店（24 小时有人）或地铁站员工室。夜间避开小巷: In an emergency, find a GS25/CU convenience store (staffed 24/7) or the subway station staff office. At night, avoid alleys (골목) and stick to main roads (큰길).
韩国出入境管理局的 24 小时多语言热线（中/英/日/越/俄），迷路/受骗/被抢: The Korea Immigration Service's 24-hour multilingual hotline (Chinese/English/Japanese/Vietnamese/Russian). You can call for help if you're lost, scammed, or robbed. Free.
被警告「돌아가세요」（请回去）不是普通「再见」，是「原路撤退、别再往前」。听到就: When warned '돌아가세요' (go back), it's not a casual 'goodbye' — it means 'retreat the way you came, don't go further'. Turn around and leave immediately. Don't argue, don't pull out your phone to take photos.
위험해요 = 「危险」（客观状态）；무서워요 = 「害怕」（主观感受）。「이 곳: 위험해요 = 'dangerous' (objective state); 무서워요 = 'scared' (subjective feeling). '이 곳은 위험해요' = the place is dangerous; '저는 무서워요' = I am scared.
「-니까」= 「因为…（提示原因让对方判断）」，多用于命令/建议前：「위험하니까: '-니까' = 'because... (giving a reason for the other person to judge)', often used before commands/suggestions: '위험하니까 가지 마세요'. '-아/어서' = 'because... so', objective statement.
가세요 = 「请走」（去某处）；돌아가세요 = 「请回去」（返回来路）。警告场景: '가세요' = 'please go' (to somewhere); '돌아가세요' = 'please go back' (return the way you came). In warning situations, '돌아가세요' means 'go back the way you came, don't go further'.
怎么去安全的地方？: How do I get to a safe place?
找便利店求助: Find a convenience store for help
不熟环境时优先进 GS25/CU/7-Eleven（24 小时明亮有店员）。说「: When unfamiliar with the area, prioritize GS25/CU/7-Eleven (open 24 hours, bright, with staff). Say '여기서 잠깐 있어도 돼요?' (Can I stay here for a bit?), and staff will usually help contact the police.
夜间坚决走「큰길」（大路）而非「골목」（小巷）。大路有摄像头、路灯、便利店。骨干: At night, firmly take '큰길' (main road) rather than '골목' (alley). Main roads have cameras, streetlights, and convenience stores. You won't lose contact on main roads.
包/手机戴身前，钱包分散放。不要因为担心引起注意就走得慌张——沉着大方走。: Carry your bag/phone in front, spread out your wallet. Don't walk nervously out of fear of drawing attention—walk calmly and confidently.
위험하다描述客观状态（地方危险）；무섭다描述主观感受（我害怕）。: '위험하다' describes an objective state (the place is dangerous); '무섭다' describes a subjective feeling (I'm scared).
조심(操心) = 汉字词「操心」+ 하다，字面「操心留意」。: '조심' (care) = Sino-Korean 'care/worry' + 하다, literally 'be careful and attentive'.
请对方小心: Ask the other person to be careful
ㅂ 不规则：무섭 + 어요 → ㅂ 变 우 → 무서워요。: ㅂ irregular: 무섭 + 어요 → ㅂ changes to 우 → 무서워요.
경고(警告) = 汉字词「警告」，同源直接记。: Warning (경고) = Sino-Korean word '警告', same origin, memorize directly.
금지(禁止) = 汉字词「禁止」，同源直接记。街上标志常见。: Prohibition (금지) = Sino-Korean word '禁止', same origin, memorize directly. Common on street signs.
길(路)을 잃다(丢失) = 固定搭配「丢了路」，不能拆用。: 길(road)을 잃다(lose) = fixed phrase 'lost the road', can't be split.
疑问词「哪里」，可搭 예요/로/에서 造问句。: Interrogative 'where', can combine with 예요/로/에서 to form questions.
크다(大)的修饰形 큰 + 길(路) = 큰길，一体化词。: 크다(big)'s modifier form 큰 + 길(road) = 큰길, a fused word.
큰길有路灯摄像头人多；골목窄暗，夜间韩国人建议避开。: 큰길 has streetlights, cameras, and people; 골목 is narrow and dark, Koreans advise avoiding it at night.
固有词，夜间避开的窄巷；与「큰길」相对。: Native word, narrow alley to avoid at night; opposite of '큰길'.
돌다(转) + 가다(去) = 原路返回。听到就转身走。: 돌다(turn) + 가다(go) = return the way you came. If you hear this, turn and leave.
请对方回去: Ask the other person to go back
들다(进入) + 가다(去) = 走进去。「들어가지 마세요」= 不要进去。: 들다 (enter) + 가다 (go) = go in. 「들어가지 마세요」 = Don't go in.
들어가다=进去；나가다=出去。方向相反。: 들어가다 = go in; 나가다 = go out. Opposite directions.
늦다(晚) + -었어요 敬语过去时，表「已经晚了」的状态。: 늦다 (late) + -었어요 polite past tense, indicating the state of 'already late'.
副词「快」，置于动词前：빨리 가세요 / 빨리 도와주세요。: Adverb 'quickly', placed before the verb: 빨리 가세요 / 빨리 도와주세요.
独自一人，置于动词前作副词：혼자 왔어요（一个人来的）。: Alone, used as an adverb before the verb: 혼자 왔어요 (came alone).
돕다(帮) + -아 주세요，ㅂ 不规则：돕 → 도와。声音要大要清晰。: 돕다 (help) + -아 주세요, ㅂ irregular: 돕 → 도와. Speak loudly and clearly.
경찰(警察) = 汉字词「警察」，同源直接记。报警拨 112。: 경찰 (police) = Sino-Korean 'police', same origin, easy to remember. Call 112 for police.

ATMs are interconnected, but there's a fee for using other banks' machines, so Koreans only use their own bank's ATMs. Before opening an account, ask a friend '어느 은행이 좋아요?', and once you pick, you stick with it.

One app manages all your bank cards, free transfers, plus credit card payments, fund investments, and insurance. In 2024, users surpassed 30 million—half of Korea's population uses it.

韩国汇率最好的地方不是银行，是南大门市场的「환전소」（换汇所）。汇率比银行高 2: The best exchange rates in Korea aren't at banks, but at the '환전소' (exchange shops) in Namdaemun Market. Rates are 2-3% better than banks, and no waiting. Myeongdong has plenty of exchange shops too, but rates are slightly lower. Budget-conscious students go to Namdaemun.
外国人从韩国往外汇款有年度限额 5000 만원（约 27 万人民币），且需要收入: Foreigners sending money out of Korea have an annual limit of 50 million won (about 270,000 RMB), and need proof of income or tax payment. For large transfers, you need to prepare documents in advance—you can't just send whatever amount you want.

외국인등록증（外国人登录证）= 韩国生活通行证。没有它，银行不给开户、手机不给办: The 외국인등록증 (Alien Registration Card) = your passport to life in Korea. Without it, banks won't open accounts, phone companies won't sign you up, and landlords won't rent to you. You must get it at the immigration office within 90 days of arriving—it costs 30,000 won.
ATM 有中文界面为什么还是看不懂？: Why is the ATM still confusing even with a Chinese interface?
中文选项通常只翻译菜单，具体操作说明还是韩文。而且「입금 / 출금 / 이체」这: The Chinese options usually only translate the menus—the actual instructions are still in Korean. Even if words like 입금/출금/이체 are translated as deposit/withdrawal/transfer, you still need to understand the difference between 계좌번호 (account number) and 비밀번호 (PIN). Bringing a Korean friend along the first time is your safest bet.
체크카드 和 신용카드 到底差什么？: What's the real difference between a check card and a credit card?
체크카드 = 借记卡（刷卡即扣款，不透支）；신용카드 = 信用卡（月底还款）。韩: A check card is a debit card—money is deducted immediately, no overdrafts. A credit card lets you pay at the end of the month. Young Koreans prefer check cards—no debt, no bills, and it keeps spending in check. Credit cards are mostly for big purchases paid in installments.
为什么韩国人不爱用现金？: Why don't Koreans like using cash?
2010 年代政府推「무현금 사회」（无现金社会）政策——所有商家必须能刷卡，连: In the 2010s, the government pushed a cashless society policy—every business had to accept cards, even street vendors use Kakao Pay. These days, paying with cash makes young cashiers see you as an oddball. The older generation still sticks to cash and passbooks.

银行只做工作日: Banks are only open on weekdays
韩国银行工作时间 09:00-16:00，周末不开门。周六急事只能去 ATM 或: Korean banks are open 09:00–16:00 on weekdays only. If something urgent comes up on Saturday, you're stuck with the ATM or an app. If you need the counter, taking a half day off is your safest bet.
登录证 + 手机号办完后立刻注册「토스」。免费转账 + 查全部账户 + 交话费水: Once you have your alien registration card and phone number, sign up for Toss right away. Free transfers, a view of all your accounts, and bill payments for phone and utilities—it triples your efficiency living in Korea. A must-have app for students.

ATM 上多显示「출금」（口语常用）；「인출」是更书面的说法，两者意思相同。: ATMs usually show '출금' (common in speech); '인출' is more formal, both mean the same.
송(送)+금(金)＝送出去的钱＝汇款，跟日语「送金」同源。: 송(送)+금(金) = money sent out = remittance, same origin as Japanese '送金'.
송금＝汇款（含跨国、异行）；이체＝同行账户间转账。银行 App 按钮通常分开。: 송금 = remittance (including international, interbank); 이체 = transfer between accounts at the same bank. Bank app buttons are usually separate.
환전(换錢)＝환(换)+전(钱)＝换钱，跟中文\"换钱\"完全同构，一次记住。: 환전(换錢) = 환(换)+전(钱) = exchange money, exactly parallel to Chinese '换钱', remember it in one go.
여권(旅券)＝汉字词，\"旅行券\"就是护照，日语也叫 旅券。: 여권(旅券) = Sino-Korean, 'travel voucher' means passport, Japanese also calls it 旅券.
也有外国人登录证。: I also have an Alien Registration Card.
외국인(外国人)+등록(登录)+증(证)＝汉字词全同源，长但每个字都认识。: 외국인(外国人)+등록(登录)+증(证) = all Sino-Korean, long but you know every character.
여권＝本国签发的护照；외국인등록증＝韩国政府发给在韩外国人的居留证。银行两个都要: 여권 = passport issued by your country; 외국인등록증 = residence card given by the Korean government to foreigners. Banks need both.
신분(身分)+증(证)＝汉字词，\"身份+证\"直接同源。韩国人的 신분증＝주민: 신분(身分)+증(证) = Sino-Korean, directly parallel to 'identity + card'. Koreans' 신분증 = 주민등록증.
주소(住所)＝汉字词\"住所\"，跟日语 住所 完全一样。: 주소(住所) is a Sino-Korean word meaning "address," identical to the Japanese 住所.
서명(署名)＝汉字词\"署名\"，即\"签自己的名字\"。: 서명(署名) is a Sino-Korean word meaning "signature," i.e., signing your own name.
汉字词「圓」，韩国货币单位。: Sino-Korean word "원" (圓), the Korean currency unit.
원(圓)＝汉字词\"圆\"，跟人民币\"元\"同源—东亚货币都从\"圆\"字来。: 원(圓) is a Sino-Korean word meaning "round," sharing the same origin as the Chinese yuan—East Asian currencies all derive from the character 圓.
dollar 音译，念时 r 弱化：달-러 两个音节。: Transliteration of "dollar," with the r softened: two syllables, 달-러.
위안＝中文\"元\"的普通话发音音译，加\"화(貨)\"＝人民币货币（위안화）。: 위안 is a transliteration of the Mandarin pronunciation of "yuan," plus 화(貨) = Chinese yuan currency (위안화).
환율(换率)＝汉字词，换算比率＝汇率。发音有 ㄴ 添加，念[환뉼]（hwan-n: 환율(换率) is a Sino-Korean word meaning conversion rate = exchange rate. It has an ㄴ insertion, pronounced [환뉼] (hwan-nyul).
수수료(手數料)＝手+数+料，日语也叫\"手数料\"，韩中日通用的金融词汇，零学: 수수료(手數料) = hand + number + fee; Japanese also calls it 手数料. It's a common financial term across Korea, China, and Japan—zero learning cost.

창구(窓口)＝日式汉字词，对应中文\"窗口\"，跟日语 窓口 完全一样。: 창구(窓口) = Japanese-style Sino-Korean, matching Chinese 'window', identical to Japanese 窓口.

「-고 싶다」只能对第一人称用；说别人想做什么要用 「-고 싶어 하다」。「친구: '-고 싶다' is only used for the first person; to say someone else wants to do something, use '-고 싶어 하다'. '친구가 계좌 개설하고 싶어요' is wrong; you should say '친구가 계좌 개설하고 싶어 해요'.

（습니다 体）请问汇率是多少？: (습니다 form) May I ask what the exchange rate is?

手续费用「수수료」，别说「봉사료」——봉사료是餐厅/酒店服务费，银行/换汇场景说: The fee is '수수료', not '봉사료'—'봉사료' is a service charge at restaurants/hotels. Say it wrong at a bank or currency exchange, and the teller will pause. The correct word is only '수수료'.
「-(으)ㄹ 수 있어요?」问的是\"能不能做\"的可能性/许可，不是\"想不想: '-(으)ㄹ 수 있어요?' asks about possibility/permission ('can you do it?'), not desire. '하고 싶어요?' asks about willingness. The two can't be swapped.

「며칠」（几天）和 「몇일」是常见拼写错误，正确写法只有 「며칠」。发音相近但拼: '며칠' (a few days) and '몇일' are commonly misspelled—only '며칠' is correct. They sound similar, but watch the spelling.

韩国银行 서명 通常要求跟护照/登录证上一致，中间随意签一个可能被要求重签。签之: At Korean banks, your signature usually needs to match your passport or alien registration card. Signing casually might get you asked to redo it. Check the spot before signing.

韩国餐厅 · 小菜无限续的国度: Korean Restaurants · The Land of Unlimited Banchan Refills
点一份 8,000 원的泡菜汤，老板端来 5 盘小菜，吃完可以再要，不收一分钱—: Order an 8,000 won kimchi stew, and the owner brings out 5 side dishes. When you finish them, you can ask for more—free of charge. This is a dining rule unique to Korean tables worldwide.
一碗拌饭最低价: The lowest price for a bowl of bibimbap
韩国菜含辣，不吃辣要提前说: Korean food is spicy—say it in advance if you can't handle it.
반찬 无限续，吃完再要不收钱: Banchan refills are unlimited—ask for more after finishing, no charge.
吃饭不端碗: Don't lift your bowl while eating
韩国人吃饭，碗放桌上，勺子吃米饭，筷子只夹菜。端碗吃在日本/中国是常态，在韩国是: Koreans keep their bowl on the table, use a spoon for rice, and chopsticks only for side dishes. Eating with the bowl in hand is normal in Japan/China, but in Korea it's seen as a 'begging posture'—elders will scold you. This is the easiest Korean table manner to get wrong.
勺子夹米饭，筷子夹菜: Spoon for rice, chopsticks for side dishes
「숟가락」（勺子）和「젓가락」（筷子）分工明确。米饭用勺子舀，泡菜用筷子夹——用: The '숟가락' (spoon) and '젓가락' (chopsticks) have clear roles. Scoop rice with the spoon, pick up kimchi with chopsticks—using the wrong tool looks ill-mannered. Mixing them up is the most common mistake on a student's first day.
一瓶 소주（烧酒）+ 一杯 맥주（啤酒）混着喝，叫「소맥」。度数不高，后劲大。是: A bottle of 소주 (soju) + a glass of 맥주 (beer) mixed together is called "소맥". Not too strong but packs a delayed kick. It's the soul of Korean gatherings — don't even think about talking work until you finish this glass. When mixing, letting the beer foam rise to the rim is part of the 소맥 ritual.
大部分韩国餐厅没有服务员倒水——门口有饮水机或水壶，自己拿杯子倒。有些店甚至用不: Most Korean restaurants don't have servers pouring water — there's a water dispenser or pitcher by the entrance, grab a cup and pour it yourself. Some places even use stainless steel bowls for drinking (the kind that's a bit too hot to hold). Don't wait at your table; you'll be waiting all day.
吃饭前说「잘 먹겠습니다」（我要开动了），吃完说「잘 먹었습니다」（吃好了）。对: Say '잘 먹겠습니다' (I will eat well) before eating and '잘 먹었습니다' (I ate well) after. Say it to the restaurant, your companions, and the cook—it marks the start and end of a Korean meal. Forgetting it comes off as rude.
为什么韩国餐厅不给小费？: Why don't Korean restaurants get tips?
韩国服务业默认不收小费——账单已含服务费，多给反而让服务员困扰（觉得你在同情）。: Korean service industry doesn't expect tips by default—the bill already includes service fees, and tipping extra actually makes staff uncomfortable (they think you're pitying them). This is the opposite of US/European culture. To truly show thanks, say '잘 먹었습니다' + a bow.
반찬 到底有多少种？: How many kinds of banchan are there?
韩国泡菜类小菜有 200+ 种，家常餐厅一般配 3-5 种：김치（泡菜）/ 콩나: There are 200+ types of Korean pickled side dishes. Home-style restaurants usually serve 3-5: kimchi, bean sprouts, spinach, radish strips, and steamed egg. The owner switches them up by season.
为什么点烤肉一定要 1 인분起？: Why must you order at least 1 serving of grilled meat?
韩国烤肉按重量计（1 인분 ≈ 150g），设最低起卖是为了保证厨房翻台效率。两: Korean BBQ is sold by weight (1 serving ≈ 150g). The minimum order is to keep kitchen turnover efficient. If two people insist on sharing one serving, staff will refuse—saying '죄송하지만 1인당 1인분씩 주문해 주세요'.
肉/汤够但饭不够时说「공기밥 추가해 주세요」。1,000-2,000 원一碗。: When the meat/stew is enough but rice isn't, say '공기밥 추가해 주세요'. It's 1,000-2,000 won per bowl. Some places offer free refills for students.
大部分食堂进门旁有水机 / 自助水台。自己拿杯倒水。别在桌上等服务员送。: Most eateries have a water dispenser/self-serve station by the entrance. Grab a cup and pour your own. Don't wait at the table for staff to bring it.
「수저」= 숟가락(勺) + 젓가락(筷)的合称，勺筷一套。桌上有个铁盒装。别搞: '수저' is a combo of 숟가락 (spoon) + 젓가락 (chopsticks), a set. They're in a metal box on the table. Don't mix them up.
国民汤，餐餐有。: The national soup, served at every meal.

They're more hygienic, durable, and reusable than wood or plastic. The downside: heavy and slippery—most international students can't pick up kimchi on their first try.

「감성문구」产业的胜利——2010 年后韩国文具品牌把日用品当潮玩设计。猫头/兔: A win for the 'sensibility stationery' industry—since 2010, Korean stationery brands have designed everyday items like trendy toys. 채소和야채几乎同义。채소更正式（超市标牌用），야채更口语（家里说）。: 채소 and 야채 are nearly synonyms. 채소 is more formal (used on supermarket signs), while 야채 is more colloquial (used at home).

고기＝固有词，前面加动物名就是那种肉：소고기(牛肉)/돼지고기(猪肉)/닭고기(: 고기 is a native word; add an animal name before it to specify the meat: 소고기 (beef), 돼지고기 (pork), 닭고기 (chicken).
고기＝食用的肉；살＝身上的肉/皮肉。买肉说고기。: 고기 means meat for eating; 살 means flesh on the body. Use 고기 when buying meat.
汉字词「鶏卵」。一盘 30 个。: Sino-Korean word '鶏卵' (chicken egg). A tray has 30 eggs.
계란(鶏卵)＝汉字词，「鸡卵」的音译。판＝板/盘，一板 30 个。: 계란 (鶏卵) is Sino-Korean, a transliteration of 'chicken egg'. 판 means tray/plate, with 30 eggs per tray.
계란是汉字词，超市标牌常用；달걀是固有词，日常口语常用。意思一样。: 계란 is Sino-Korean, common on supermarket signs; 달걀 is native, common in everyday speech. They mean the same.
来自日语ラーメン，但韩语里默认指「方便面」而不是日式拉面。日式的叫「일본 라멘」: It comes from Japanese ラーメン, but in Korean it defaults to 'instant noodles' rather than Japanese ramen. Japanese-style is called '일본 라멘'.
배추＝固有词，量词用「통」（一颗一颗数）。배추김치＝白菜泡菜，最常见的泡菜种类。: 배추 is a native word, counted with '통' (by the head). 배추김치 is napa cabbage kimchi, the most common type.
배추＝长条形韩式白菜（做泡菜）；양배추＝西方圆卷心菜（洋+배추）。完全不同。: 배추 is the long Korean napa cabbage (for kimchi); 양배추 is the Western round cabbage (洋+배추). They're completely different.
汤/泡菜都用。: Used in both soups and kimchi.
무＝一个音节的固有词，韩国最短的蔬菜名。깍두기(萝卜块泡菜)/무국(萝卜汤)的主: 무 is a one-syllable native word, the shortest vegetable name in Korean. It's the star of 깍두기 (radish cube kimchi) and 무국 (radish soup).
파＝一个音节的固有词。파김치(葱泡菜)/대파(大葱)。: 파 is a one-syllable native word. 파김치 (scallion kimchi) / 대파 (large green onion).
파＝葱（细长绿色）；양파＝洋葱（洋+파，圆球状）。多一个「양」就变洋葱。: 파 means green onion (long and green); 양파 means onion (洋+파, round). Adding '양' turns it into an onion.
마늘＝固有词。韩料几乎每道都要，是「五辛」之首。다진 마늘＝蒜末，超市有袋装。: 마늘 is a native word. Almost every Korean dish uses it; it's the top of the 'five pungent vegetables.' 다진 마늘 means minced garlic, sold in bags at supermarkets.
고추＝固有词。고추장(辣椒酱)/고춧가루(辣椒粉)都从고추来，是韩料辣味的源头。: 고추 is a native word. 고추장 (chili paste) and 고춧가루 (chili powder) both come from 고추, the source of Korean cuisine's spiciness.
싸다＝形容词基本形，修饰名词时变싼（싼 거＝便宜的东西）。: 싸다 is the basic adjective form; when modifying a noun it becomes 싼 (싼 거 = cheap thing).
싸다(便宜)配对记：加个비就翻面成비싸다(贵)。词源不清，直接当固定搭配背下来最: Remember 싸다 (cheap) as a pair: add 비 and it flips to 비싸다 (expensive). The etymology is unclear, so just memorize it as a set phrase.
正在打折吗？: Is there a sale going on?
할인(割引)＝汉字词，日语也用同一个词。「30% 할인」＝七折（韩国说法是「打掉: 할인 (discount) is a Sino-Korean word, also used in Japanese. '30% 할인' means 30% off (Korean says how much is taken off, not how much is kept).
할인＝具体折扣率（30% 할인）；세일＝限时促销活动（여름 세일＝夏季促销）。: 할인 refers to a specific discount rate (30% 할인); 세일 is a limited-time promotion event (여름 세일 = summer sale).
这是买一送一。: This is buy one, get one free.
1+1念「원 플러스 원」（英语式），不念「일 더하기 일」（数学式）。促销标签: 1+1 is read as '원 플러스 원' (English style), not '일 더하기 일' (math style). It's the industry standard for promo labels.
sale 音译，2 音节：세-일。「세일 중」＝促销中，商场大字招牌常见。: Transliteration of 'sale,' 2 syllables: 세-일. '세일 중' means 'on sale,' commonly seen on big store signs.
cart 音译，2 音节：카-트。大超市入口都有「카트 100 원」的投币栏，还: Transliteration of 'cart,' 2 syllables: 카-트. Large supermarkets have '카트 100 원' coin slots at the entrance; you get your money back when you return the cart.
카트＝带轮子的推车（大量购物）；바구니＝手提篮（少量购物）。: 카트 means a wheeled cart (for bulk shopping); 바구니 means a hand basket (for light shopping).
계산(计算)+대(台)＝计算台＝结账柜台，两个汉字词拼一起。「셀프 계산대」＝自: 계산 (calculation) + 대 (counter) = checkout counter, combining two Sino-Korean words. '셀프 계산대' means self-checkout.
봉투(封套)＝汉字词，本义信封，现在也指购物袋。超市塑料袋 100 원/个。: 봉투 (envelope) is a Sino-Korean word, originally meaning envelope, now also used for shopping bags. Plastic bags at supermarkets cost 100 won each.
봉투＝袋子（泛称）；비닐봉투＝塑料袋（비닐＝vinyl 塑料）。超市说봉투默认指: 봉투 means bag (general); 비닐봉투 means plastic bag (비닐 = vinyl/plastic). In supermarkets, 봉투 usually refers to plastic bags.
영수증(领收证)＝汉字词。收银机默认打印，不要就说「영수증 필요 없어요」。: 영수증 (receipt) is a Sino-Korean word. The register prints one by default; if you don't want it, say '영수증 필요 없어요.'
point 音译，3 音节：포-인-트。이마트/홈플러스 都有会员积分，用手机号: Transliteration of 'point,' 3 syllables: 포-인-트. Stores like E-Mart and Homeplus have membership points you can register with your phone number.
找货架用「어디에 있어요?」（在哪）；找出口/收银台通常用「어디로 가요?」（往: To find an item on a shelf, use '어디에 있어요?' (where is it); to find an exit or checkout, use '어디로 가요?' (which way to go) — use 에 for static locations and 로 for directions.
（更礼貌）能告诉我这个在哪吗？: (More polite) Could you tell me where this is?
有比这更便宜的吗？: Is there anything cheaper than this?
形容词修饰名词必须变修饰形——「싸다 거」错，「싼 거」对。无 收音加 -ㄴ：싸: Adjectives modifying nouns must take the modifier form—'싸다 거' is wrong, '싼 거' is right. If no batchim, add -ㄴ: 싸다→싼, 비싸다→비싼, 크다→큰; if batchim, add -은: 작다→작은, 좋다→좋은. Don't mix them up.
（更礼貌）不知道有比这更实惠的吗？: (More polite) I wonder if there's something more affordable than this?
看到促销标签时: When you see a promo tag
数字发音陷阱：1+1 读英语式「원 플러스 원」，不能读数学式「일 더하기 일」: Number pronunciation trap: 1+1 is read English-style as 'won peulleoseu won', not math-style 'il deohagi il'. Writing 1 but reading it as 'won' is the industry norm for Korean promos.
（更正式）这个商品是买一送一的活动吗？: (More formal) Is this item a buy-one-get-one-free deal?
买几个能打折？: How many do I need to buy to get a discount?
条件句「-(으)면」接在动词/形容词词干后。사다→사면（元音无收音直接加면）、먹: The conditional '-(으)면' attaches to verb/adjective stems. 사다→사면 (vowel ending, no batchim, add 면 directly), 먹다→먹으면 (batchim, add 으면). Don't forget to pick 면 vs. 으면 based on the batchim.
（更正式）买几个以上能享受折扣？: (More formal) How many or more do I need to buy to get a discount?
（更随意）买多点便宜吗？: (More casual) Is it cheaper if I buy more?
到收银台时: When you get to the checkout counter
「하다」类动词的-아/어 주세요 形是-해 주세요，不是「하아 주세요」。계산하: For '하다' verbs, the -아/어 주세요 form is -해 주세요, not '하아 주세요'. 계산하다→계산해, 결제하다→결제해, 포장하다→포장해 all follow the same rule.
店员问要不要袋子时: When the clerk asks if you need a bag
否定用「필요 없어요」。「필요없어요」也可写在一起（复合词），但分开写更常见。: Use 「필요 없어요」 for negation. It can also be written together as a compound word, but writing it separately is more common.
（更礼貌）能给我一个袋子吗？: (More polite) Could I get a bag?
结账时要积分: When checking out, ask for points
积分是「적립하다」（累积），存钱是「저축하다」（存款）——两个都能翻译成「攒/存: Points are 「적립하다」 (accumulate), saving money is 「저축하다」 (deposit)—both can translate to 'save up,' but saying 「저축해 주세요」 will confuse the clerk.
（更正式）请帮我积分。: (More formal) Please add points for me.
找不到问区域最快。: If you can't find it, asking for the section is fastest.
「(으)로요」是选择支付方式最简答法。: 「(으)로요」 is the simplest way to choose a payment method.
啊，那再拿一个。: Oh, then I'll take one more.
「그럼 + 行动」是响应促销信息的自然反应。: 「그럼 + action」 is a natural response to a promotion.
不好意思，白菜在哪？: Excuse me, where are the cabbages?
蔬菜区在那。2 号货架。: The vegetable section is over there. Aisle 2.
谢谢。这是买一送一吗？: Thanks. Is this buy one, get one free?
蒜在旁边。: Garlic is right next to it.
有比这个更便宜的吗？: Is there anything cheaper than this?
这边这个 6,000。10 个装。: This one here is 6,000. Pack of 10.
刚才那个呢？: What about the one from earlier?
那 8,000 的。每个更便宜。: I'll take the 8,000 one. Cheaper per item.
也方便面。这个打折吗？: Also ramen. Is this on sale?
2004 年通车的韩国高铁，从首尔到釜山 2.5 小时。但对初学者来说，最震撼的: Korea's high-speed rail, opened in 2004, takes you from Seoul to Busan in 2.5 hours. But for beginners, the most striking thing isn't the speed—it's Korea's 'ticket-grabbing culture.'
KTX 单程票价，约飞机的 60%: KTX one-way fare is about 60% of a flight
KORAIL 官方 App，韩国人都用它: KORAIL's official app, used by everyone in Korea
抢票比春运还难: Getting tickets is harder than Spring Festival rush
韩国人节假日（추석 秋夕、설날 春节）回乡，KTX 票 30 秒内抢光。코레일톡: During Korean holidays (Chuseok, Seollal), KTX tickets sell out within 30 seconds as people head home. The Korail Talk app routinely crashes the moment tickets go live. Foreigners can register accounts in advance, but Korean ID holders get priority—foreigner ticket quotas are limited.
KTX 分自由席（先到先得）和指定席（固定座位）。자유석便宜 10%，但旺季可能: KTX has free seating (first come, first served) and reserved seating. Free seats are 10% cheaper, but you might stand the whole way during peak season. Spend the extra 5,000 won on a reserved seat, especially for trips over 2 hours.
KTX 早期有食堂车（식당차），2018 年前后逐步取消，现在只剩自动售货机。上: KTX used to have dining cars, phased out around 2018. Now there are only vending machines. Grab coffee, triangle kimbap, or a lunchbox at GS25/CU on the platform before boarding.
迟到 5 分钟 = 走不了: 5 minutes late = you miss the train
KTX 发车前 5 分钟停止检票。不像中国高铁有 3 分钟缓冲，韩国人自己都说「: KTX stops boarding 5 minutes before departure. Unlike China's high-speed rail with its 3-minute buffer, Koreans themselves say 'KTX doesn't wait.' Arriving 20 minutes early is standard practice.
KTX / SRT / ITX / 무궁화 四种火车: Four train types: KTX / SRT / ITX / Mugunghwa
KTX 最快最贵；SRT 民营高铁走另一条路线，比 KTX 便宜 10%；ITX: KTX is fastest and priciest; SRT is a private high-speed rail on a different route, 10% cheaper than KTX; ITX-Saemaeul is semi-high-speed with great value; Mugunghwa stops at every station—cheapest but slow. Budget travelers take Mugunghwa, those in a hurry take KTX.
为什么 KTX 没有安全检查？: Why is there no security check on KTX?
韩国铁路信任乘客——买票=可乘车，跟中国的安检+身份验证完全不同。但票必须实名，: Korean rail trusts passengers—buying a ticket means you can board, totally different from China's security checks and ID verification. But tickets are tied to real names for traceability in emergencies. This system is built on low crime rates and high social trust.
KTX 和 SRT 有什么区别？: What's the difference between KTX and SRT?
KTX 是 KORAIL（国有）运营，从首尔站发车；SRT 是 SR（民营）运营: KTX is run by KORAIL (state-owned) and departs from Seoul Station; SRT is run by SR (private) and departs from Suseo Station. For the same destination, SRT is usually 5-10% cheaper but has fewer departures. Compare both before buying.
为什么车票要写「호차 X석」？: Why does the ticket say 'car X, seat Y'?
「호차」= 车厢号，「석」= 座位号。「3호차 12A석」= 3 号车厢 12A: 'Car' means carriage number, 'seat' means seat number. 'Car 3, seat 12A' means carriage 3, seat 12A. Board at the right carriage—Korean platforms mark positions to the centimeter, so there's no time to run if you're at the wrong one.
请给我去首尔的 KTX 票。: One KTX ticket to Seoul, please.
大件行李放车厢连接处: Large luggage goes at the carriage ends
KTX 座位上方行李架很小，大箱子放在车厢首尾的行李专区。别占过道，会被列车员提: Overhead racks on KTX are small—put big suitcases in the luggage areas at the ends of the carriage. Don't block the aisle or the attendant will call you out.
韩国人坐 KTX 会主动压低声音打电话，甚至走到车厢连接处。大声说话/外放视频会: Koreans lower their voices on KTX, even stepping into the carriage vestibule to take calls. Loud talking or playing videos out loud will get you dirty looks.
KTX 座椅前部有 2 孔插座，型号 C 型。手机/笔记本充满电再出站毫无问题。: KTX seats have a 2-pin Type C outlet up front. No problem charging your phone or laptop fully before you arrive.
请给我去首尔的火车票。: Please give me a train ticket to Seoul.
KTX 也可以说「KTX 표」。: KTX can also be called 'KTX pyo'.
기차(汽车)+표(票)＝汉字词，字面「汽车票」，两个字都跟中文同源。: 기차 (car) + 표 (ticket) = Sino-Korean word, literally 'car ticket'; both characters share roots with Chinese.
标准写作 KTX，按字母 케이-티-엑스 念。: Written as KTX, pronounced letter by letter as kei-ti-ek-seu.
英文字母缩写，Korea Train eXpress，念的时候按韩语字母 케이-: An English acronym for Korea Train eXpress, pronounced in Korean as kei-ti-ek-seu.
普速列车多少钱？: How much is the regular train?
「무궁화」= 木槿花，韩国国花，象征列车名。: 'Mugunghwa' = rose of Sharon, Korea's national flower, symbolizing the train's name.
무궁화(木槿花，韩国国花)+호(号)＝以国花命名的车次，是最便宜的绿皮车。: Mugunghwa (rose of Sharon, Korea's national flower) + ho (number) = a train named after the national flower, the cheapest and slowest.
무궁화호站站停最慢最便宜；ITX-새마을 半高速中间价；KTX 高铁最贵最快。三: Mugunghwa-ho stops at every station, slowest and cheapest; ITX-Saemaeul is semi-high-speed at a mid price; KTX is the most expensive and fastest. Three tiers in progression.
「예매하다」= 预约购票，App 或窗口都可。: 'Yemaehada' = to reserve and purchase a ticket, available via app or counter.
예매(豫买)＝汉字词，「豫」=事先，「买」=购买，即事先买票。: Yemae (豫买) = Sino-Korean word; '豫' means beforehand, '买' means to buy, so it's buying tickets in advance.
예매＝专门买票/买座位（票、演出、KTX）；예약＝预约位置/服务（餐厅、酒店、理: Yemae = specifically for buying tickets/seats (tickets, shows, KTX); yeyak = reserving a spot/service (restaurants, hotels, haircuts).
相反「지정석」= 指定席，票上有座号。: The opposite is 'jijeongseok' = reserved seat, with a seat number on the ticket.
자유(自由)+석(席)＝汉字词「自由席」，中文里也这么说，直接一对一。: Jayu (free) + seok (seat) = Sino-Korean word 'free seat', same as in Chinese, a direct one-to-one match.
자유석＝没编号，先到先坐，便宜 10%；지정석＝票上印座号，稳坐但贵。: 자유석 = no seat number, first come first served, 10% cheaper; 지정석 = seat number printed on ticket, guaranteed but pricier.
KTX 一般不查票机，直接进闸口。: KTX usually doesn't have ticket machines; you just go straight through the gate.
개찰(改札)+구(口)＝汉字词，源自日语「改札」，指剪票/验票，「口」是入口。: 개찰(改札)+구(口) = Sino-Korean word, from Japanese '改札', meaning ticket punching/inspection; '口' means entrance.
票上印「3번 승강장」，跟着指示牌走。: The ticket says '3번 승강장' (Platform 3); follow the signs.
승강(乘降)+장(场)＝上下车的地方，「乘」上车「降」下车，汉字直译。: 승강(乘降)+장(场) = place for getting on/off; '乘' means board, '降' means alight, direct Sino-Korean translation.
两者同义。승강장 正式（车站广播、指示牌）；플랫폼 外来语，年轻人偶尔说。: Both mean the same. 승강장 is formal (station announcements, signs); 플랫폼 is a loanword, occasionally used by younger people.
有充电口/免费 WiFi/自动贩卖机。: There are charging ports, free WiFi, and vending machines.
대합(待合)+실(室)＝汉字词「等候+室」，源自日语「待合室」，字面就是等待相见: 대합(待合)+실(室) = Sino-Korean 'waiting + room', from Japanese '待合室', literally a room for waiting to meet.
有中英文服务员，票务/失物/退款都可问。: Staff speak Chinese and English; you can ask about tickets, lost items, or refunds.
안내(案内，汉字词=引导)+데스크(desk 外来语)＝汉字+英文合成，「引导台: 안내(案内, Sino-Korean = guidance) + 데스크(desk, loanword) = Sino-Korean + English compound, meaning 'guidance desk'.
失物招领在哪？: Where is the lost and found?
丢东西越快去越好，员工会记录并联系。: The sooner you report a lost item, the better; staff will log it and contact you.
분실(纷失，遗失)+물(物)+센터(center)＝汉字词「遗失物」+ 英文 c: 분실(纷失, lost) + 물(物, item) + 센터(center) = Sino-Korean 'lost item' + English 'center', a hybrid word.
「좌석」是正式说法，日常用「자리」。: '좌석' is the formal term; in everyday speech, use '자리'.
자리＝纯韩语固有词，泛指「位置/座位/地方」，比汉字词좌석口语化。: 자리 is a pure Korean word meaning 'place/seat/spot' in general, and is more colloquial than the Sino-Korean word 좌석.
자리＝口语，任何位置都可；좌석(座席)＝汉字词，专指编号座位，正式场合/票上用。: 자리 is colloquial and can mean any spot; 좌석 (座席) is a Sino-Korean word specifically for numbered seats, used in formal settings or on tickets.
호(号)+차(车)＝汉字词「号+车」，即「几号车厢」的量词化说法。: 호 (号) + 차 (车) = Sino-Korean 'number + car', a way of saying 'which car' as a numbered unit.
广播会自动播报，也可看电子屏。: The announcement plays automatically, and you can also check the electronic display.
정차(停车)+역(驿)＝汉字词「停车+站」，停下来上下客的中间站。: 정차 (stop) + 역 (station) = Sino-Korean 'stop + station', an intermediate stop where passengers get on and off.
정차역＝路上停靠的中间站；종착역＝最终目的站。KTX 会经过多个정차역，只有一个: 정차역 is an intermediate stop along the way; 종착역 is the final destination. A KTX passes through several 정차역 but has only one 종착역.
终点站是釜山站。: The terminal station is Busan Station.
车头显示屏会滚动播报终点。: The display at the front of the train scrolls the final destination.
종착(终着)+역(驿)＝汉字词「终点到达+站」，「종」= 终，「착」= 到。: 종착 (终着) + 역 (驿) = Sino-Korean 'arrive at the end + station'; '종' means end, '착' means arrive.
现在 KTX 已经没餐车，进站前买好餐。: KTX no longer has a dining car, so buy food before boarding.
식당(食堂)+차(车)＝汉字词「食堂+车」，就是餐车。: 식당 (食堂) + 차 (车) = Sino-Korean 'dining hall + car', meaning dining car.
常口语说「몇 시에 출발해요?」。: In casual speech, people often say '몇 시에 출발해요?'.
출발(出发)+시간(时间)＝两个汉字词直接拼，「出发+时间」，中文一模一样。: 출발 (出发) + 시간 (时间) = two Sino-Korean words combined, 'departure + time', just like in Chinese.
延误时用「도착 예정 시간」= 预计到达。: When delayed, use '도착 예정 시간' = estimated arrival.
도착(到着)+시간(时间)＝汉字词「到达+时间」，「도」=到，「착」=达。: 도착(到着)+시간(时间) = Sino-Korean 'arrival+time', '도' = to arrive, '착' = to reach.
지연(迟延)＝汉字词「迟+延」，跟中文「延迟」同源，只是字序颠倒。: 지연(迟延) = Sino-Korean 'late+extend', same origin as Chinese '延迟' but with reversed order.
지연＝正在延误中（进行）；연착(延着)＝已经晚点到达（结果）。广播先지연再연착。: 지연 = currently delayed (ongoing); 연착(延着) = already arrived late (result). Broadcasts say 지연 first, then 연착.
票能退吗？: Can I get a refund for this ticket?
出发前 1 小时手续费低，之后高。: The fee is low up to 1 hour before departure, then high after.
환불(还拂)＝汉字词「还+付」，「还」=归还，「拂」=支付，即退款。: 환불(还拂) = Sino-Korean 'return+pay', '환' = return, '불' = pay, meaning refund.
「행(行)」是买票专用后缀，不能替换成方向助词「-으로」。「서울으로 표 주세요: '행(行)' is a ticket-specific suffix and can't be replaced with the direction particle '-으로'. '서울으로 표 주세요' sounds awkward and would confuse the ticket clerk.
（更正式）请给我一张去首尔的 KTX 票。: (More formal) Please give me a KTX ticket to Seoul.
请给自由席。: Please give me a non-reserved seat.
「자유석」以辅音结尾，助词用「으로」不用「로」。发音时 석 + 으로 会连读成: Since 자유석 ends in a consonant, the particle is 으로, not 로. When pronounced, 석 + 으로 blends into [서그로].
（更正式）请给我自由席。: (More formal) Please give me a free seat.
「번」前面必须用汉字数字（일/이/삼），不能用固有数字（하나/둘/셋）。「하나: Before 번, you must use Sino-Korean numbers (일/이/삼), not native numbers (하나/둘/셋). 하나 번 승강장 is incorrect.
（更委婉）能告诉我是几号月台吗？: (More polite) Could you tell me which platform?
车厢内借空位时: When asking for a seat in the car
可以坐吗（앉다 + -아도 되다 + 婉转疑问）: Can I sit? (앉다 + -아도 되다 + polite question)
「앉다」是不规则动词，+ -아/어도 变「앉아도」（不是「앉어도」）。ㅏ 元音后: 앉다 is an irregular verb; + -아/어도 becomes 앉아도 (not 앉어도). After the vowel ㅏ, -아 is a strict rule.
（更礼貌）不好意思，坐这里方便吗？: (More polite) Excuse me, is it okay to sit here?
问下一站时: When asking about the next stop
「어디예요」不是「어디이에요」——「어디」以元音结尾，直接连예요，不用이에요完整: 어디예요 is not 어디이에요 — 어디 ends in a vowel, so it directly takes 예요, not the full 이에요.
（更礼貌）能问下一站是哪里吗？: (More polite) May I ask where the next stop is?
「시」前必须用固有数字（한/두/세/네），「분」前必须用汉字数字（일/이/삼/사: Before 시, use native numbers (한/두/세/네); before 분, use Sino-Korean numbers (일/이/삼/사). 4시 20분 is read 네시 이십분, mixing both.
（更委婉）能告诉我几点到吗？: (More polite) Could you tell me what time it arrives?
（半语，对朋友）几点到？: (Casual, to a friend) What time do you arrive?
票可以退吗？: Can I get a refund on the ticket?
「환불하다」以元音结尾的语干「환불하-」，加 -ㄹ 수 있다 变「환불할 수」。: The stem of '환불하다' ends in a vowel, '환불하-', so adding -ㄹ 수 있다 makes '환불할 수'. Writing '환불을 수' is a part-of-speech error.
（更正式）票能退款吗？: (More formal) Can the ticket be refunded?
地名 + 이요/예요 是最短的回答，售票员会自动理解为目的地。: Place name + 이요/예요 is the shortest answer; the ticket clerk will automatically understand it as the destination.
「선택 + (으)로요」是选票车型的标准答法。: '선택 + (으)로요' is the standard way to choose a train type.
简短选一个 + 이요/예요 最快。: Picking one briefly + 이요/예요 is fastest.
「数字 + 명 + 이요」是人数标准回答。: 'Number + 명 + 이요' is the standard answer for the number of people.
「时间 + 이요/예요」是回答时间的直接说法。: 'Time + 이요/예요' is a direct way to state the time.
要用餐车吗？: Would you like the dining car?
「괜찮아요」是委婉拒绝的万能句。KTX 已无餐车，回答也可以「식당차 없죠?」。: '괜찮아요' is a versatile polite refusal. KTX no longer has a dining car, so you could also say '식당차 없죠?'
自由席便宜/指定席稳: Non-reserved is cheaper / reserved is reliable
哪天几点出发: What day and time to depart
票买好后问月台/车厢: After buying the ticket, ask about the platform/car
找座位/问站点/借空位: Finding seats / asking about stops / using empty seats
请给我一张去首尔的 KTX 票。: One KTX ticket to Seoul, please.
2:15 和 2:45 有。自由席还是指定席？: There's one at 2:15 and one at 2:45. Unreserved or reserved seat?
53,000 韩元。怎么结账？: That's 53,000 won. How would you like to pay?
在 2 号月台乘车。4:55 到首尔站。: Board at platform 2. Arrive at Seoul Station at 4:55.

地下商街 · 首尔的第二城市: Underground Shopping Streets · Seoul's Second City
首尔地下是另一个城市——地铁站下面藏着巨大的商业街，衣服、饰品、美食、手机壳，什: Underneath Seoul is another city—huge shopping streets hidden below the subway stations. Clothes, accessories, food, phone cases—they have everything, at only 1/3 of the price above ground.
地下商业街——藏在地铁站下面: Underground shopping streets—hidden beneath subway stations
T 恤起价，比地上便宜 60-80%: T-shirts start at prices 60-80% cheaper than above ground
连通地铁站——下雨天不用上地面: Connected to subway stations—no need to go above ground on rainy days
首尔三大地下商街: Seoul's Three Major Underground Shopping Streets
**고속터미널 지하상가 · 고투몰**（高速客运站，620+ 店铺最全）、**: **Gangnam Underground Shopping Street** (Gangnam Station, mainly clothes and accessories), **Yeongdeungpo Underground Shopping Street** (Yeongdeungpo). Goto Mall is the king of Seoul's underground shopping streets—it has everything from clothes to phone cases to nail art.
地下商街的衣服价格只有商场的 1/3——T 恤 5,000-10,000 원、连: Clothes in underground shopping streets cost only 1/3 of department store prices—T-shirts 5,000-10,000 won, dresses 15,000-25,000 won, phone cases 3,000 won. Quality is average but styles update fast, perfect for buying fast fashion you'll wear for one season and toss.
连通地铁 · 下雨天最佳: Connected to the subway · Best on rainy days
地下商街连通地铁站——下雨天不用上地面，从地铁直接进商街购物吃饭。地下恒温——夏: The underground shopping street connects to the subway station—on rainy days, you don't have to go above ground; you can go straight from the subway into the shopping street to shop and eat. It's temperature-controlled underground—cool in summer and warm in winter. When it's 35°C outside or freezing cold, Koreans commonly head to the underground shopping street to 'enjoy the AC / heating.'
第一次去一定迷路: You'll definitely get lost the first time
没有标志性建筑——所有通道看起来一样。记住出口编号（출구 번호），迷路时找出口定: There are no landmarks—all the corridors look the same. Remember the exit numbers (출구 번호) and use them to orient yourself if you get lost. **When arranging to meet, say '3번 출구 앞'** (in front of Exit 3), not 'in front of that one store'—you won't find it.
现金比刷卡多: Cash is more common than cards
大部分小店只收现金——摊位太小放不下 POS 机。深处的珠宝/饰品/袜子店都是。: Most small shops only accept cash—the stalls are too small for a POS machine. The jewelry/accessory/sock shops deeper inside are all like this. Withdraw 3-5 만원 in cash from an ATM beforehand; it's most satisfying to pull out small bills after successfully haggling.
为什么地下商街比地上便宜这么多？: Why is the underground shopping street so much cheaper than above ground?
地下商街的店租只有地面的 20-30%（首尔政府补贴 + 商街产权特殊）。加上没: Rent in the underground shopping street is only 20-30% of above-ground rates (Seoul government subsidies + special property rights for the shopping street). Plus, there's no fancy decor, and many shop owners have run family businesses for 40 years—all the saved costs are passed on to customers.
고투몰（고속터미널 지하상가）有多大？: How big is Goto Mall (고속터미널 지하상가)?
首尔最大地下商街——620+ 店铺，连通高速客运站 3/7/9 号线三条地铁。分: Seoul's largest underground shopping street—620+ stores, connected to subway lines 3, 7, and 9 at the Express Bus Terminal. It's divided into the East, Central, and West Halls, with clothing, accessories, wedding supplies, and flowers all here. Walking the whole place takes 30 minutes, and shopping takes at least 3 hours. First-timers should bring a map.
地下商街只收现金真的合法吗？: Is it really legal for the underground shopping street to only accept cash?
法律上韩国商家「不能拒绝刷卡」，但地下商街小摊位大多标明「현금가」（现金价）比刷: Legally, Korean businesses 'cannot refuse card payments,' but most small stalls in the underground shopping street mark '현금가' (cash price) as 5-10% cheaper than card, effectively encouraging cash. It's a gray area—few complaints, so it persists. Before buying, ask '카드 되나요?' (Can I pay by card?).
往这走就行吗？: Is it okay to just go this way?
地图先拍照: Take a photo of the map first
入口处商店街地图先拍下来。深处找方向靠它。手机没信号 App 地图也用不了。: Take a photo of the shopping street map at the entrance first. You'll rely on it to find your way deeper in. With no phone signal, app maps won't work either.
双肩包挂前面: Wear your backpack on your front
地下人多小偷多。双肩包挂胸前，钱包放包内里。少数游客易被盯上。: It's crowded and pickpocket-prone underground. Wear your backpack on your chest and keep your wallet in an inner pocket. A few tourists are easy targets.
很多小店只收现金。1,000/5,000 원面额准备好，砍价成功后掏零钱最爽快。: Many small shops only accept cash. Have 1,000/5,000 원 denominations ready; it's most satisfying to pull out small bills after successfully haggling.
지하(地下)＝汉字词，中文「地下」直接同源，两字都读得出来。: 지하(地下) is a Sino-Korean word, directly cognate with Chinese '地下'—you can read both characters.
출구(出口)＝汉字词，直接对应中文「出口」，地下商街必用词。: 출구(出口) is a Sino-Korean word, directly corresponding to Chinese '出口'—a must-know word for the underground shopping street.
입구(入口)＝汉字词「入口」，跟출구(出口)配对记，一进一出。: 입구 (入口) is a Hanja word for entrance. Pair it with 출구 (出口) for exit—one in, one out.
방향(方向)＝汉字词，两字与中文「方向」完全同源。: 방향 (direction) = Sino-Korean word, both characters share the exact same origin as Chinese '方向' (direction).
지도(地图)＝汉字词，中文「地图」直接同源，两字都读得出来。: 지도 (map) = Sino-Korean word, directly cognate with Chinese '地图' (map), both characters are readable.
길(路)+잃다(丢失)＝把路丢了，字面直译就是迷路。: 길 (road) + 잃다 (to lose) = lost the road, literally meaning 'to get lost'.
헤매다＝正在到处转找不到方向的过程；길을 잃다＝已经确认迷路的状态。: 헤매다 = the process of wandering around unable to find direction; 길을 잃다 = the state of having confirmed you're lost.
이(这)+쪽(边)＝这一边，跟저쪽(那边)配对记。: 이 (this) + 쪽 (side) = this side, memorize it paired with 저쪽 (that side).
이쪽＝这一侧/这个方向（含移动指向）；여기＝这个地点（静止点）。: 이쪽 = this side/this direction (implies movement); 여기 = this place (a stationary point).
저(那)+쪽(边)＝那一边，远指方向，跟이쪽成对。: 저 (that) + 쪽 (side) = that side, pointing to a far direction, paired with 이쪽.
沿原路返回。: Go back the way you came.
돌다(转)+가다(去)＝转回去＝返回，两个动作拼在一起。: 돌다 (to turn) + 가다 (to go) = turn back = to return, two actions combined.
오른쪽＝右；왼쪽＝左。共享 쪽(边)，前面词根不同，配对记最快。: 오른쪽=right; 왼쪽=left. They share 쪽 (side), but the roots differ—pair them up for fastest memorization.
앞＝前；뒤＝后。都是固有词单音节，一前一后配对记。: 앞=front; 뒤=back. Both are single-syllable native words—pair front and back to memorize.
건너(跨过)+편(侧)＝跨到另一侧＝对面。: 건너 (cross over) + 편 (side) = cross to the other side = opposite.
매장(卖场)＝汉字词，中文也说「卖场」，同源直接记。: 매장 (store) = Sino-Korean; Chinese also says '卖场'—same origin, just memorize it directly.
매장＝较正式/较大型的店铺（品牌店/专柜）；가게＝口语小店，两者都能指店。: 매장 = more formal/larger store (brand store/counter); 가게 = casual small shop; both can mean 'store'.
固有词。店员招呼时的万能回避句。: Native word. The go-to polite brush-off when a staff member greets you.
구경하다＝随便看看、逛。店员问「뭐 찾으세요?」时用「구경만 할게요」是万能回避: 구경하다 = to browse, look around. When staff ask '뭐 찾으세요?', saying '구경만 할게요' is the perfect dodge.
sale 音译，两音节：세-일，跟英文几乎一样。: Loanword from 'sale', two syllables: 세-일, almost identical to English.
진열(陈列)＝汉字词，与中文「陈列」完全同源。: 진열(陈列) is a Sino-Korean word, completely cognate with Chinese '陈列' (to display).
「길을 잃다」用过去时「잃었어요」——迷路是已完成状态，不能说「잃어요」。: '길을 잃다' uses the past tense '잃었어요' — being lost is a completed state, so you can't say '잃어요'.
（更礼貌）不好意思，我迷路了，请问 3 号出口在哪？: (More polite) Excuse me, I'm lost. Could you tell me where Exit 3 is?
「맞다」是「对/正确」，跟「맞추다」（对准/匹配）不同；确认方向对错用「맞아요」: '맞다' means 'correct/right', different from '맞추다' (to align/match); to confirm if a direction is right, use '맞아요', not '맞춰요'.
（更委婉）走这边对吗？: (More tentative) Is it right to go this way?
地铁站怎么走？: How do I get to the subway station?
往地铁站（+ 助词 으로）: toward the subway station (with particle 으로)
方向用「(으)로」不用「에」——「지하철역에 어떻게 가요?」也能说但语感偏「到: For direction, use '(으)로' not '에' — '지하철역에 어떻게 가요?' is also possible but feels like 'arriving at', while '으로' emphasizes 'in this direction'.
（更礼貌）到地铁站该怎么走呢？: (More polite) How should I get to the subway station?
往右走就行吗？: Is it enough to go right?
往右（+ 方向助词 으로）: to the right (with direction particle 으로)
方向用助词「(으)로」——「오른쪽에 가면 돼요?」会显得不地道，方向移动一律「: For direction, use the particle '(으)로' — '오른쪽에 가면 돼요?' sounds unnatural; for directional movement, always use '으로'.
（更委婉）往右走可以吗？: (More tentative) Is it okay to go right?
得返回。迷失方向了。: I need to go back. I'm lost.

得原路返回: I need to go back the way I came
「방향을 잃다」用过去时「잃었어요」——已经迷失了才说这句，不能用现在时「잃어요: Use the past tense '잃었어요' for '방향을 잃다' — you say this only after getting lost, not the present tense '잃어요'.
（更委婉）好像走错了，得回去。: (More polite) I think I went the wrong way; I need to go back.
（更口语）啊走错了，得回去。: (More casual) Oh, wrong way; I need to go back.
位置用「에」不用「에서」——「있다/없다」搭配的位置助词固定是「에」，「에서」用: Use '에' for location, not '에서' — '있다/없다' always takes '에'; '에서' is for where actions happen.
（更委婉）请问附近有便利店吗？: (More polite) Excuse me, is there a convenience store nearby?
「보여주세요」（给我看）≠「보세요」（你看）——请对方展示要用使动的「보이다」+: '보여주세요' (show me) ≠ '보세요' (you look) — to ask someone to show you, use the causative '보이다' + '주세요', not telling them to look themselves.
（极度礼貌）能给我看一下地图吗？: (Very polite) Could you show me the map?
（更随意）我看下地图。: (More casual) Let me see the map.
肯定 + 具体求助内容一步到位。: Be direct with a positive statement and specific request.
被指路后立刻道谢。: Thank them right after getting directions.

听一句话，选出最合适的回答。多为日常问候、疑问句的回应。: Listen to a sentence and choose the most appropriate response. These are mostly replies to everyday greetings or questions.
抓句尾语气与疑问词（뭐/누구/어디…）就能锁定应答方向。: Focus on the sentence-ending tone and question words (뭐/누구/어디…) to pinpoint the right response.
两句短对话之后，选出接下来最自然的一句。: After a short two-line dialogue, choose the most natural next line.
注意前一句是提议/请求/致谢，答句常见套路：감사→아니에요、괜찮으세요？→네…: Note that if the previous line is a suggestion, request, or thanks, common reply patterns include: 감사→아니에요, 괜찮으세요?→네…
听两人的短对话，判断对话发生的地点（药店、银行、餐厅等）。: Listen to a short dialogue and identify where it takes place (pharmacy, bank, restaurant, etc.).
关键词定位法：处方笺→약국、통장→은행、주문→식당，一个词就能锁场所。: Keyword spotting: prescription→pharmacy, bankbook→bank, order→restaurant—one word can lock in the location.
听对话，判断两人在谈论的话题（家人、天气、爱好等）。: Listen to the dialogue and identify the topic being discussed (family, weather, hobbies, etc.).
别被局部词汇干扰，抓两次以上重复出现的名词，通常就是主题。: Don't get distracted by isolated words—nouns that repeat more than twice are usually the main topic.
听对话，选出与情境一致的图片。: Listen to the dialogue and choose the picture that matches the situation.
先扫图片差异（人物动作/物品位置）再听，效率翻倍。: Scan the picture differences (people's actions/item positions) before listening—it doubles your efficiency.
听完对话或独白，选出与内容一致的选项。: After listening to the dialogue or monologue, choose the option that matches the content.
边听边划出选项关键词。听力常改数字/时间/人物关系来当干扰项。: Underline keywords in the options as you listen. Listening tests often change numbers/times/relationships as distractors.
判断话者想表达的核心观点或建议。: Identify the speaker's core opinion or suggestion.
注意 -는 게 좋다 / -아야 하다 / -고 싶다 这类表态度的句尾。: Pay attention to attitude-marking endings like -는 게 좋다 / -아야 하다 / -고 싶다.
一段较长的独白或对话，判断整体谈论的主题。: Listen to a longer monologue or dialogue and identify the overall topic.
开头一两句一般已点出主题。听不清就抓反复出现的名词。: The first sentence or two usually states the topic. If you can't hear clearly, catch the nouns that keep repeating.
长对话中的具体信息（时间、地点、原因、结果）判断。: Identify specific information in long dialogues (time, place, reason, result).
先看选项圈出数字与专有名词，再带着问题去听。: First scan the options and circle numbers and proper nouns, then listen with those questions in mind.
判断话者说这段话的目的（介绍、通知、请求、道歉等）。: Determine the speaker's purpose (introduce, notify, request, apologize, etc.).
句尾情态（-겠습니다 / -십시오 / -드리다）常是目的的直接信号。: Sentence-ending moods (-겠습니다 / -십시오 / -드리다) are often direct signals of purpose.
读两个短句，判断在说的是什么话题（天气、家人、时间等）。: Read two short sentences and identify the topic (weather, family, time, etc.).
两句都指向同一类事物，找它们的共通名词。: Both sentences point to the same category—find their common noun.
在空格处填入正确的助词（은/는、이/가、을/를、에、에서…）。: Fill in the correct particle (은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서…).
想清楚主语/宾语/场所，别被\"感觉像\"骗了，语法功能优先。: Think clearly about subject/object/place—don't be fooled by what "feels right"; grammatical function comes first.
在句子空格处填入合适的名词。: Fill in the blank with an appropriate noun.
看前后动词与助词，判断名词的语义范畴（物/人/地点）。: Look at the surrounding verbs and particles to determine the noun's semantic category (thing/person/place).
在空格处填入符合语境的动词。: Fill in the blank with a verb that fits the context.
注意时态（-았/었어요 vs -을 거예요）和主语能不能做这个动作。: Pay attention to tense (-았/었어요 vs -을 거예요) and whether the subject can perform the action.
在空格处填入符合语境的形容词。: Fill in the blank with an adjective that fits the context.
找语境里的情绪线索：긍정（좋다/즐겁다）还是 부정（피곤하다/힘들다）。: Look for emotional clues in the context: positive (좋다/즐겁다) or negative (피곤하다/힘들다).
在空格处填入符合语境的副词（시간/빈도/정도类）。: Fill in the blank with an adverb that fits the context (time/frequency/degree).
先判断副词类别（时间/频率/程度），再看句子里跟谁搭配。: First determine the adverb type (time/frequency/degree), then see what it pairs with in the sentence.
看广告、通知、日程等实用文，选出与其一致的说法。: Read practical texts like ads, notices, and schedules, and choose the statement that matches.
干扰项常把日期、价格、数量改一位数字，把选项每个数据都对回原文。: Distractors often change a digit in dates, prices, or quantities; check each option's numbers against the original text.
读短文，选出与原文不一致的一项。: Read the passage and choose the option that does not match the original.
把选项与原文逐句比对，最容易漏的是\"没有说过\"vs\"说过相反\"。: Compare each option sentence by sentence with the original; the easiest to miss is 'not mentioned' vs 'stated the opposite'.
读短文，选出作者想表达的主要观点。: Read the passage and choose the author's main point.
注意首尾句和 -는 게 좋다 / -아야 한다 这类主张句型。: Pay attention to the first and last sentences and opinion patterns like -는 게 좋다 / -아야 한다.
在短文的空格中填入合适的词汇或短语，多为词汇+文脉题。: Fill in the blanks with the right words or phrases—mostly vocabulary and context questions.
先看空格前后连词与句子逻辑，再回选项挑最能\"接得上\"的那个。: First check the connectors and sentence logic around the blank, then pick the option that fits best.
在两句之间填入合适的连接词（그래서/그런데/하지만/그리고…）。: Fill in the right connective between two sentences (그래서/그런데/하지만/그리고…).
判断两句关系：因果→그래서、转折→그런데/하지만、并列→그리고。: Determine the relationship: cause→그래서, contrast→그런데/하지만, addition→그리고.
判断作者写这段文字的目的（介绍、说明、通知、感谢等）。: Identify the author's purpose (introduce, explain, notify, thank, etc.).
看文末往往揭示目的：-려고、-기 위해、-으니까 等结尾表意图。: The ending often reveals the purpose: endings like -려고, -기 위해, -으니까 show intent.
四个句子打乱顺序，重新排成一段完整的短文。: Four sentences are scrambled; rearrange them into a coherent passage.
先找总起句（不含指示词）作首句，再靠 그런데/그래서/이/그 定位串接。: Find the topic sentence (no demonstratives) as the first, then use 그런데/그래서/이/그 to link the rest.
把给定的句子插入到短文最合适的位置。: Insert the given sentence into the best spot in the passage.
看给定句里的指示词/连接词，找上下文里能接住它的锚点。: Look at the demonstratives/connectives in the given sentence and find the anchor in the context.
听内容后选出对应的图片或图表（含数据比较）。: Listen and choose the matching picture or chart (including data comparisons).
图表题先扫两个轴的标签，边听边追增减/最多/最少这类词。: For chart questions, scan the axis labels first, then listen for words like increase/decrease, most/least.
两人对话之后，选出下一句最自然的回应。: After a two-person dialogue, choose the most natural next response.
把语域（尊敬 vs 半말）和话轮位置对上，再判断内容是否合理。: Match the speech level (formal vs. casual) with the turn position, then judge if the content makes sense.
听完对话，判断女方/男方接下来会做什么。: After listening, determine what the woman/man will do next.
注意\"我先去…你等一下\"这种任务分工，最后一次动作提示往往是答案。: Watch for task division like "I'll go first... you wait," the last action clue is often the answer.
听对话/独白，选出与内容一致的一项。: Listen to the dialogue/monologue and choose the option consistent with the content.
数字、时间、否定形（안/못）是最高频的陷阱点。: Numbers, times, and negative forms (안/못) are the most common traps.
判断话者的核心主张或立场。: Identify the speaker's core claim or stance.
中级听力主张句常包 -아/어야 한다、-는 것이 중요하다、-면 좋겠다。: Intermediate listening claim sentences often include -아/어야 한다, -는 것이 중요하다, -면 좋겠다.
长对话中特定一方的中心想法。: The central idea of a specific person in a long dialogue.
认准题干问的是남자还是여자，其它人的观点全部是干扰。: Note whether the question asks about the man (남자) or woman (여자); other people's views are all distractors.
长对话里具体信息判断（时间、原因、后果、参与者）。: Judging specific information in a long dialogue (time, reason, consequence, participants).
边听边在选项旁边打对号叉号，别等听完再判断。: Mark checkmarks or X's next to the options as you listen—don't wait until the end to decide.
专家访谈中受访者的核心主张。: The interviewee's core claim in an expert interview.
受访者的转折句（하지만/오히려）后面往往就是他真正的立场。: The interviewee's true stance often follows a contrastive phrase (하지만/오히려).
话者说这话是想干嘛（说服/警告/建议/共鸣）。: What the speaker is trying to do (persuade/warn/suggest/empathize).
别只看内容，要看\"为什么这么说\"——语气词和让步表达能暴露意图。: Don't just focus on the content—look at "why they said it." Tone particles and concessive expressions reveal intent.
判断话者的职业或身份（教授、记者、市民代表等）。: Identify the speaker's profession or role (professor, journalist, citizen representative, etc.).
专业词汇+对听者的称呼是身份指纹，如\"연구 결과\"提示学者。: Specialized vocabulary and how the speaker addresses the listener are identity fingerprints—e.g., "연구 결과" signals a scholar.
话者对某话题的具体看法（不同于中心思想的整体主张）。: The speaker's specific opinion on a topic (distinct from the overall main idea).
注意 -다고 생각하다/-는 편이 좋다 这类明说的观点句。: Watch for explicit opinion markers like -다고 생각하다/-는 편이 좋다.
整段讲话围绕的主题（讲座、演讲、专题）。: The topic the entire talk revolves around (lecture, speech, special feature).
第一段常抛主题句，后面全是论证，主题词至少出现三次。: The first paragraph often states the topic sentence, followed by supporting arguments—the key term appears at least three times.
判断谈话发生的场所或场合（研讨会、颁奖礼、发布会等）。: Identify the place or occasion where the conversation occurs (seminar, awards ceremony, press conference, etc.).
开头的问候语和结尾的礼节表达通常暴露正式度和场合。: Opening greetings and closing formalities often reveal the level of formality and the setting.
判断话者对话题的态度（肯定、批判、中立、担忧等）。: Determine the speaker's attitude toward the topic (positive, critical, neutral, concerned, etc.).
态度题看形容词和情态：긍정的态度形容 vs 否定的批判形容。: For attitude questions, look at adjectives and modality: positive attitude descriptors vs. negative critical descriptors.
判断当前段落在整段讲话中的作用（引入、举例、结论等）。: Identify the role of the current paragraph in the overall speech (introduction, example, conclusion, etc.).
按讲话结构模板：현상→원인→해결，就能定位每段。: Follow the speech structure template: phenomenon → cause → solution, to locate each paragraph.
大学讲座类长音频，判断内容或主讲主旨。: Long audio of a university lecture; identify the content or main point.
专业词汇不必全懂，抓概念定义句（-란 -이다）和例子标记词（예를 들어）。: You don't need to understand all technical terms; focus on definition sentences (-란 -이다) and example markers (예를 들어).
纪录片/新闻报道，选出与内容一致或核心观点。: For documentaries or news reports, choose the option consistent with the content or the core viewpoint.
注意采访片段和旁白的立场差异，题目常问旁白的态度。: Note the difference in stance between interview clips and narration; questions often ask about the narrator's attitude.
致辞、发布会、报告中话者的立场与态度。: The speaker's stance and attitude in addresses, press conferences, and reports.
尊敬体级越高、态度越正式，注意 -고자、-오니 等公文体线索。: The higher the honorific level, the more formal the attitude; watch for formal style markers like -고자, -오니.
判断整段演讲的目的（呼吁行动/介绍成果/表态支持等）。: Determine the purpose of the entire speech (calling for action/introducing results/expressing support, etc.).
演讲开头 + 结尾 + 最激动那句 = 意图三角，任一位置都能定答案。: Speech opening + ending + the most impassioned line = the intent triangle; any one of these can determine the answer.
对谈节目中受访者对争议话题的态度。: The interviewee's attitude toward a controversial topic in a talk show.
受访者不一定完全否或完全肯——注意\"우려된다\"\"공감한다\"这类程度词。: The interviewee may not fully agree or disagree—watch for degree words like "우려된다" (I'm concerned) and "공감한다" (I relate).
在句子空格处填入正确的语法或连接语尾。: Fill in the blank with the correct grammar or connective ending.
判断前后动作的时序、原因、条件关系，语法书里的功能标签直接对号入座。: Determine the sequence, cause, or condition between actions—match them to the function labels in your grammar book.
看广告或标语，选出它传达的核心信息。: Read the ad or slogan and choose the core message it conveys.
广告通常一句话，抓关键动词/名词就能锁定行业和目的。: Ads are usually one sentence—grab the key verb/noun to pinpoint the industry and purpose.
读文段（说明文/新闻/日程等），选出与内容一致的一项。: Read the passage (explanatory text, news, schedule, etc.) and choose the option consistent with the content.
选项中\"总是/所有/绝对\"这种绝对化措辞十有八九是干扰。: Absolute wording like "always/all/absolutely" in options is almost always a distractor.
四个句子重新排列成一段完整的短文。: Rearrange four sentences into a coherent short passage.
首句一般不含 이/그/이것; 后续句常带因果连接词或指示代词。: The first sentence usually lacks 이/그/이것; following sentences often have causal connectors or demonstratives.
在短文空格处填入符合上下文的词汇。: Fill in the blanks in the passage with words that fit the context.
带入四个选项各自读一遍，读起来最顺 + 语义最贴的通常就是答案。: Read each of the four options in the sentence—the one that flows most naturally and fits the meaning best is usually the answer.
连题里的细节判断（时间、人物、结果等）。: Identify details in the passage (time, people, outcomes, etc.).
先看题再回原文找定位词，比顺序读整段快得多。: Read the questions first, then scan the passage for keywords—much faster than reading the whole thing in order.
判断整篇文段谈论的核心主题。: Determine the core topic the entire passage discusses.
主题往往在首句或首段最后一句，末段做呼应。: The theme is often in the first sentence or the last sentence of the first paragraph, with the final paragraph echoing it.
连题空格里填入符合语义或语用功能的表达。: Fill in the blanks with expressions that serve the right semantic or pragmatic function.
注意前后句的因果、对比、举例关系，再判断空格承担哪种功能。: Pay attention to cause-effect, contrast, and example relationships between sentences, then decide what function the blank serves.
高级论述文中的空格补全（连接词或概念名词）。: Fill in the blanks in advanced argumentative passages (connectors or conceptual nouns).
论述文空格常测因果、让步、递进——记住 10 个高频关联词就够用。: Blanks in argumentative passages often test cause-effect, concession, and progression—memorizing 10 high-frequency connectors is enough.
看新闻标题，选出它传达的信息含义。: Read the news headline and choose what information it conveys.
韩语标题惯用缩略与比喻，把\"急涨/暴跌/破纪录\"式的词汇背下来。: Memorize Korean headline abbreviations and metaphors like "surge/plunge/record-breaking."
连题的具体信息判断题（对照选项与原文数据）。: Specific information true/false questions (compare options with the original text data).
把选项里的数字、日期、人物先圈出来，再回原文对照。: Circle numbers, dates, and people in the options first, then check against the passage.
连题里对作者中心主张的判断。: Judging the author's central argument in the passage.
作者立场句通常带 -아야 한다 / -이 필요하다 / -은 바람직하다。: Author's stance sentences often use -아야 한다 / -이 필요하다 / -은 바람직하다.
判断作者写这段文字的目的（说服、通知、反驳、呼吁）。: Determine the author's purpose (persuade, inform, refute, appeal).
结尾一句常直白点题：-기를 바라다 / -해야 할 것이다。: The final sentence often states the point directly: -기를 바라다 / -해야 할 것이다.
把给定句子插入到文段中最合适的位置。: Insert the given sentence into the most appropriate position in the passage.
看给定句里的指示词/连接词，反向找上文能接住它的锚点。: Look at the demonstratives/connectors in the given sentence and find the anchor in the preceding text that connects.
文学类短文中，判断主人公的心情（悔恨、怀念、期待等）。: In literary passages, determine the protagonist's feelings (regret, nostalgia, anticipation, etc.).
记住 15 个高频韩语情感词（섭섭하다、안타깝다、뿌듯하다…）就足以覆盖。: Memorizing 15 high-frequency Korean emotion words (섭섭하다, 안타깝다, 뿌듯하다…) is enough to cover them.
识别具体场景下人物微妙的情绪变化。: Identify subtle emotional shifts in specific scenes.
情境句里的动作细节（어깨를 떨구다、한숨을 쉬다）都是心情线索。: Action details in situational sentences (어깨를 떨구다, 한숨을 쉬다) are all clues to the mood.
判断作者写作背后的深层用意（唤起共鸣、警示、批评现状等）。: Determine the deeper intent behind the author's writing (evoking empathy, warning, criticizing the status quo, etc.).
看批判性表达（-어서는 안 된다、-이 우려된다）和呼吁句就能定基调。: Look at critical expressions (-어서는 안 된다, -이 우려된다) and imperative sentences to set the tone.
熟悉每个韩文字母对应的键盘位置: Get familiar with the keyboard position for each Korean letter.
练习最常见的韩文音节，建立肌肉记忆: Practice the most common Korean syllables to build muscle memory.
打你最常用的词汇，开始有意义的输入: Type your most-used vocabulary and start meaningful input.

中性，YouTube等平台常用: Neutral, common on platforms like YouTube
