叫店员别说\"죄송합니다\": Don't say "죄송합니다" to call a staff member
想让店员过来时用 저기요（\"那个\"）或 사장님（老板），是最自然的叫法。죄송: To get a staff member's attention, use 저기요 ("excuse me") or 사장님 (boss) — that's the most natural way. 죄송합니다 is only for when you're genuinely interrupting or apologizing for a mistake — saying it just to order will confuse the staff.
中文说\"要冰的\"直译成 차가운 거 주세요 韩国人能懂但不地道。饮品的冷热是: Saying "I want it iced" as 차가운 거 주세요 is understandable but unnatural. Hot or iced is indicated by adding 아이스 (iced) or 따뜻한 (hot) before the drink name — that's the standard phrasing at Korean cafés.
教材里学的 계산해 주세요 没错，但连锁店店员实际会说 결제 도와드릴게요（我帮: What textbooks teach, 계산해 주세요, isn't wrong, but chain store staff actually say 결제 도와드릴게요 (I'll help you pay). If you don't know 결제, you'll freeze up. Both words mean "payment," but in chain store contexts, 결제 is used almost exclusively.
\"한 잔이요\" 是首尔年轻人语感: "한 잔이요" has the feel of young Seoulites' speech
\"~이요\" 是简说式，比 \"~ 주세요\" 更符合年轻人和连锁店的语感。但: "~이요" is a shortened form that fits the vibe of young people and chain stores better than "~ 주세요." But with older staff or at traditional tea houses, sticking with 주세요 is more polite.
先付款再等叫号: Pay first, then wait for your number to be called
除麦当劳等快餐外，韩国咖啡厅流程是：点单 → 立刻付款 → 拿号码牌 → 离开柜: Except for fast food like McDonald's, the flow at Korean cafés is: order → pay immediately → get a number → step away from the counter and wait for your number → come back to pick up when called. Don't stand at the counter after paying; staff will ask you to move aside.
饮品名 + 한 잔 주세요，直接报品名即可: Drink name + 한 잔 주세요, just state the drink name directly
店员确认冷热，回答 네/아니요 即可: When the clerk confirms hot or cold, just answer 네/아니요
드리다（给·敬）+ 을까요（询问对方意向）: 드리다 (to give, polite) + 을까요 (asking the other's intention)
堂食说 여기서 마실게요，外带说 테이크아웃이요: For dine-in, say 여기서 마실게요; for takeout, say 테이크아웃이요
먹다/마시다 的敬语，冠形形: Polite form of 먹다/마시다, adnominal form
也可说 현금이요（现金）或 삼성페이요: You can also say 현금이요 (cash) or 삼성페이요
落座后询问时: When asking after taking a seat
有时密码贴在桌上或收据上，先找找: Sometimes the password is on the table or receipt—look for it first
向已坐着的人询问旁边是否有人: Ask someone seated if the seat next to them is taken
点单时直接说，也可说 설탕 빼 주세요（去糖）: Say it directly when ordering; you can also say 설탕 빼 주세요 (no sugar)
没有就说 없어요，想办就说 만들고 싶어요: Say 없어요 if you don't have one, or 만들고 싶어요 if you want to get one
韩国餐厅进门 → 点菜 → 加菜 → 结账/打包完整链路: Complete flow of a Korean restaurant: enter → order → add dishes → pay/pack
两人去 삼겹살 店（1인분 12,000원 左右）: Two people go to a samgyeopsal place (about 12,000 won per serving)
한 명（1位）/ 세 명（3位）以此类推: han myeong (1 person) / se myeong (3 people), and so on
追加小菜 + 要水: Add side dishes + ask for water
用餐中，小菜见底: During the meal, side dishes run out
\"이모\"是对餐厅阿姨的亲切叫法，比 아줌마 更常用: "Imo" is a friendly way to address restaurant aunties, more common than ajumma
\"셀프\"是自助，韩国餐厅水几乎全是自助: "Self" means self-service; water in Korean restaurants is almost always self-serve
吃完饭到柜台: Go to the counter after eating
不少店打包盒收 500-1000 원: Many places charge 500-1,000 won for takeout boxes
排队等号 · 用平板登记: Queue for a number · register on a tablet
弘大网红店门口，用店门口的平板取号: At popular Hongdae spots, take a number using the tablet at the entrance
\"태블릿\" = tablet 平板，弘大/성수 网红店必备: "Tablet" = tablet; a must-have at trendy spots in Hongdae/Seongsu
\"자동 취소\" 是等位系统固定规则: "Automatic cancellation" is a fixed rule in the waiting system
午饭时间到 김밥천국 一个人吃: At lunchtime, eat alone at Gimbap Heaven
\"혼자예요\" = 一个人（혼밥 场景最常听）；\"자리에 앉다\" 是标准搭: "Honjaye-yo" = alone (most heard in solo-dining scenes); "jari-e anda" is the standard collocation
\"~ 걸로요\" 是\"要~的\" 常用缩略: "~ geollo-yo" is a common abbreviation for "I'll have the ~"
\"오뎅 국물\" 免费自助是 김밥천국 传统: Free self-serve odeng broth is a Gimbap Heaven tradition
\"단무지\" = 黄萝卜，김밥 标配小菜: "Danmuji" = yellow pickled radish, the standard side for gimbap
教科书教 웨이터 但没人这么叫。韩国餐厅：阿姨用 이모（阿姨/姨母），中老年男性: Textbooks teach "weiteo" but nobody says that. In Korean restaurants: for ajummas use "imo" (aunt), for middle-aged/older men or the owner use "sajang-nim", and for young servers use "jeogiyo". Wrong terms are understood but clearly mark you as a foreigner.
반찬（小菜）无限续 —— 不用买: Banchan (side dishes) are unlimited refills — no need to buy
韩餐几乎所有小菜（泡菜、豆芽、海带等）都免费无限续。不够就说 반찬 더 주세요: Almost all Korean side dishes (kimchi, bean sprouts, seaweed, etc.) are free with unlimited refills. If you want more, just say "banchan deo juseyo". First-timers often mistakenly think they cost extra or feel shy about asking.
烤肉/火锅 通常 2인분 起点: Grilled meat / hotpot usually requires a minimum of 2 servings
삼겹살、갈비 等烤肉，还有 부대찌개 等锅类，多数店规定 2인분 起点。一个人去: Grilled meats like samgyeopsal and galbi, plus stews like budae jjigae, are mostly served with a 2-serving minimum. Ordering 1 serving alone may get you refused or charged more. Look for places that offer 1-person samgyeopsal or are solo-dining friendly.
韩国人说的\"不辣\"和中国南方人的\"不辣\"差好几个级别。真的怕辣要说 하나: What Koreans call "not spicy" is several levels above what southern Chinese call "not spicy". If you really fear heat, say "hanado an maepge hae juseyo" (make it not spicy at all) or just ask "eolmana maewoyo?" (how spicy is it?).
안 매워요? 네, 그거 주세요. ← 结果辣哭: "An maewoyo? Ne, geugeo juseyo." ← Ends up crying from the spice
开饭前说 잘 먹겠습니다（我要好好吃了），吃完说 잘 먹었습니다（我吃好了）。学: Before eating say "jal meokgesseumnida" (I will eat well), after eating say "jal meogeosseumnida" (I ate well). Learners often mix these up — if you say "jal meogeosseumnida" when the owner brings your food, it means "I'm done eating", which is awkward.
进门时店员询问: When you enter, staff will ask
如果没人来，可以叫 저기요（喂/不好意思）: If no one comes, you can call out "jeogiyo" (excuse me)
不知道点什么时: When you don't know what to order
店员推荐后可说 그걸로 주세요（就要那个）: After staff recommend, you can say "geugeollo juseyo" (I'll take that one)
인분是份量单位，1인분/2인분 按人数点: "inbun" is a serving unit — order 1 inbun / 2 inbun based on headcount
也可说 조금 맵게（稍微辣一点）: You can also say 조금 맵게 (a little spicy)
韩国餐厅水一般免费，可随时要求添加: Water is usually free at Korean restaurants, and you can ask for more anytime
吃不完时: When you can't finish your food
也可以在点单时直接说포장이요（打包带走）: You can also just say 포장이요 (to go) when ordering
用餐结束结账时: When finishing your meal and paying
也可直接说 계산해 주세요（请结账）: You can also just say 계산해 주세요 (please bill)
韩国礼仪，吃完说 잘 먹었습니다: Korean etiquette: say 잘 먹었습니다 after eating
超市 · 服装店 · 传统市场购物全流程，含试穿、砍价、退换货: Full shopping flow at supermarkets, clothing stores, and traditional markets, including trying on, haggling, and returns
GS25 或 이마트结账台，买了零食和水: At the GS25 or E-Mart checkout, bought snacks and water
韩国便利店/超市袋子收费 100-500 韩元，不问不给: Korean convenience stores/supermarkets charge 100-500 won for bags; they won't give one unless you ask
멤버십 是英语 membership，比 회원카드 更常用: 멤버십 is the English 'membership,' more common than 회원카드
现金说 현금이요，手机 pay 说 카카오페이/삼성페이요: For cash, say 현금이요; for mobile pay, say 카카오페이/삼성페이요
弘大 / 明洞街边小店，看中一件卫衣: At a street shop in Hongdae/Myeongdong, spotted a hoodie I like
叫店员用 저기요，不要说 죄송합니다: Use 저기요 to get a staff member's attention, not 죄송합니다
不要说 큰 사이즈, 说 L 사이즈/한 치수 더 큰 것 更自然: Don't say 큰 사이즈; say L 사이즈 or 한 치수 더 큰 것 — it's more natural
동대문/남대문 传统市场买围巾: Buying scarves at Dongdaemun/Namdaemun traditional markets
传统市场叫老板 사장님 最自然，年纪大的女店主可叫 이모: Call the owner 사장님 at traditional markets — it's most natural; for older female owners, 이모 works
大型商场/连锁店绝对不能砍价，只在传统市场和小摊有用: Never bargain at large malls or chain stores — it only works at traditional markets and street stalls
传统市场很多摊位只收现金，随身带一些: Many traditional market stalls only take cash, so carry some with you
다이소 结账 · 卡最低金额: Checking out at Daiso · card minimums
在 다이소 买了 3000 韩元的小物，想刷卡: Bought a small item for 3,000 won at Daiso and want to pay by card
\"최소 금액\" 是不少小店的隐藏规则，法律层面其实要接受但很多店会说: '최소 금액' is a hidden rule at many small shops — legally they must accept cards, but many still mention it
\"수수료가 부담이 있다\" = 手续费负担，店主常见解释: '수수료가 부담이 있다' = the fee is a burden — a common explanation from shop owners
올리브영 · 手机 App 现金券: Olive Young · mobile app cash vouchers
结账时用 올리브영 App 里的会员券: Use the member coupons in the Olive Young app at checkout
\"쿠폰\" = coupon 券，올리브영/CJ 系常给会员送: '쿠폰' = coupon; Olive Young and CJ affiliates often send them to members
\"1+1\" 韩国促销标配写法: '1+1' is the standard way to write promotions in Korea
砍价只用于传统市场: Bargaining is only for traditional markets
在 이마트、롯데마트、올리브영 或百货商场砍价会让店员非常尴尬 —— 这些都是明: Bargaining at E-Mart, Lotte Mart, Olive Young, or department stores will make staff very uncomfortable — these are all fixed-price chain stores. 깎아 주세요 only works at traditional markets (Dongdaemun/Namdaemun/재래시장) and street stalls; if the price tag is in the seller's hand, that's your cue to bargain.
\"试穿\" 动词要看是穿什么: The verb for 'try on' depends on what you're wearing
中文一个\"试\"字，韩语要按身体部位分动词：衣服用 입어보다，鞋子用 신어보다: Chinese has one word for 'try,' but Korean splits it by body part: 입어보다 for clothes, 신어보다 for shoes, 써보다 for hats/glasses, 껴보다 for rings/watches. Using the wrong verb is understandable but marks you as a foreigner.
袋子要主动要，超市不免费: Ask for a bag — supermarkets don't give them free
2019 年起韩国大型超市/便利店禁止免费提供塑料袋，环保袋（봉투）100-50: Since 2019, large supermarkets and convenience stores in Korea can't give out free plastic bags; eco-bags (봉투) cost 100-500 won each. Staff won't offer one unless asked, so say 봉투 하나 주세요 before paying or bring your own. Plastic bags are 비닐봉투, paper bags are 종이봉투.
교환 是换（换颜色/尺码/款式），환불 是退（退回现金）。韩国大部分店铺：교환: 교환 means exchange (color/size/style), 환불 means return (cash refund). In most Korean stores, 교환 policies are lenient (within 7 days with receipt), but 환불 is strict — many stores don't allow it, especially for underwear, cosmetics, or sale items. Always confirm before buying, and 영수증은 꼭 챙기세요.
询问价格三种说法：얼마예요（口语敬语，最常用）、얼마입니까（书面/正式敬语，百货: Three ways to ask the price: 얼마예요 (polite spoken, most common), 얼마입니까 (formal/written, used by department store staff), 얼마야 (casual, only for friends/close relationships). In daily shopping, 얼마예요 is safest with any staff—don't use 얼마야, it comes off as rude.
看中商品没标价时: When you like an item without a price tag
指着商品说最直接，얼마 前面加 이거/저거 明确指代: Pointing at the item is most direct; add 이거/저거 before 얼마 to specify clearly
传统市场/小摊砍价时: When haggling at traditional markets or street stalls
\"~면 안 돼요\" 比直接 \"깎아 주세요\" 更委婉: "~면 안 돼요" is more polite than directly saying "깎아 주세요"
깎다 (减/砍价) 的 아/어 形: The 아/어 form of 깎다 (to reduce/bargain)
주다 + 시(敬) + 면(条件)，\"如果为我~\": 주다 + 시 (honorific) + 면 (conditional), "if you do for me"
\"不行吗\"，反问加强请求: "Isn't it okay?"—a rhetorical question to strengthen the request
款式满意但颜色不合心时: When you like the style but not the color
也可换成 다른 사이즈（尺码）/ 다른 디자인（款式）: Can also swap in 다른 사이즈 (size) / 다른 디자인 (design)
拿起衣服想去试衣间时: When picking up clothes to head to the fitting room
鞋子说 신어봐도 돼요，帽子说 써봐도 돼요: For shoes, say 신어봐도 돼요; for hats, say 써봐도 돼요
입다 (穿衣服) 的 아/어 形: The 아/어 form of 입다 (to wear clothes)
试穿后觉得小时: After trying it on, it feels small
小一码说 한 치수 더 작은 것，치수 是\"号数\"的固有词: One size smaller is 한 치수 더 작은 것; 치수 is the native word for "size"
超市/便利店结账时: When checking out at a supermarket/convenience store
塑料袋 비닐봉투、纸袋 종이봉투、大袋 큰 봉투: Plastic bag 비닐봉투, paper bag 종이봉투, large bag 큰 봉투
现金说 현금이요/현금으로 할게요，手机说 삼성페이로 할게요: For cash, say 현금이요/현금으로 할게요; for phone, say 삼성페이로 할게요
带着商品和小票回店时: When returning to the store with the item and receipt
退款说 환불할 수 있어요，一般需 7 天内 + 保留小票: For a refund, say 환불할 수 있어요; usually within 7 days + keep the receipt
首尔地铁 · 从买 T-money 卡 → 换乘 → 出站问路完整链路: Seoul subway: from buying a T-money card → transferring → asking for directions after exiting, the full chain
在便利店买 T-money 卡 + 充值: Buy a T-money card + top up at the convenience store
首尔仁川机场到达后，先在 GS25 买交通卡: After arriving at Seoul Incheon Airport, first buy a transit card at GS25
T-money 是韩国通用交通卡，几乎每家便利店都卖: T-money is Korea's universal transit card, sold at almost every convenience store
充值说 충전해 주세요，\"충전\" 是\"充电/充值\" 两用词: To top up, say 충전해 주세요 — "충전" means both "charge" and "top up"
\"대다\" 是\"贴/接触\"，进站/结账\"贴卡\"都用这个词: "대다" means "to touch/contact" — used for tapping your card at the gate or checkout
在乙支路 3 街站，要从 3 号线换到 2 号线: At Euljiro 3-ga Station, transfer from Line 3 to Line 2
\"갈아타다\" 是\"换乘\" 的固定动词: "갈아타다" is the standard verb for "to transfer"
\"반대 방향\" 是站台常见指示: "반대 방향" is a common sign on platforms meaning "opposite direction"
找出口 + 问步行时间: Find the exit + ask walking time
在江南站，要去朋友说的咖啡店: At Gangnam Station, heading to the café your friend mentioned
\"~려는데요\" 是委婉说明目的: "~려는데요" is a polite way to state your intention
出站前记得上厕所，站外可能要走很远: Use the restroom before exiting — outside the station you might have to walk far
在홍대 玩到很晚，站台前问工作人员: After a late night out in Hongdae, ask staff at the platform
\"심야 버스\"（N 打头）= 首尔夜间巴士，凌晨到 4 点运营: "심야 버스" (starting with N) = Seoul night bus, running from late night until 4 AM
故障延误 · 广播听不懂: Breakdowns & delays · can't understand the announcements
车厢里广播说延误，问旁边乘客: When the onboard announcement says there's a delay, ask a fellow passenger
\"알아듣다\" = 听懂，问广播必用: "알아듣다" = to understand (what's said) — essential for asking about announcements
\"~는대요\" 是\"据说~\" 缩略，间接引述: "~는대요" is a shortened form of "they say that~" — used for indirect quotes
韩国路人常推 카카오맵/네이버 지도: Koreans often recommend KakaoMap or Naver Map
\"타다\" 助词是 을/를 不是 에: The particle for "타다" is 을/를, not 에
中文说\"上地铁/坐公交\"，容易套上\"~에 타다\"（坐到...里），但韩语: In Chinese, you say "get on the subway/take the bus," so it's easy to use "~에 타다" (ride into...), but Korean "타다" is a transitive verb, so it takes 을/를. 지하철에 타요 is the most common beginner mistake — the correct form is 지하철을 타요. Conversely, "내리다" (get off) uses 에서: 지하철에서 내려요.
中文\"换乘\"直译成 바꾸다（换）会让韩国人愣一下 —— 바꾸다 是换东西（换: Translating "transfer" literally as 바꾸다 (to change) will make Koreans pause — 바꾸다 is for exchanging things (money, clothes). Switching subway/bus lines is the fixed verb 갈아타다 (to transfer). In-station transfers are called 환승 (Sino-Korean), which is what you'll see on signs.
\"1号线/2号线\" 说 1호선/2호선，前面数字读汉字数（일/이/삼/사）不: Say 1호선/2호선 for "Line 1/Line 2," reading the number in Sino-Korean (일/이/삼/사), not native Korean (하나/둘). Don't say 원 라인/투 라인 — it's understandable but sounds foreign. Named lines like 신분당선 (Shinbundang Line) and 공항철도 (Airport Railroad) are read by name without 호선.
T-money 卡贴上就走，别插卡: Tap your T-money card and go — don't insert it.
韩国地铁闸机是感应式（NFC），把卡\"贴\"在圆形感应区（단말기）上\"嘀\": Korean subway gates are contactless (NFC): tap your card on the circular sensor (단말기) and you'll hear a beep to pass. Don't look for a card slot like in Beijing's subway — there isn't one. Mobile pay (Samsung Pay/Apple Pay transit card) works the same way by tapping your phone. Tap again when exiting; forgetting will charge the maximum fare for the whole trip.
\"几站\" 是 몇 정거장，不是 몇 역: For "how many stops," use 몇 정거장, not 몇 역.

和同伴说要下车了: Telling a companion you're getting off

博爱座（노약자석/임산부석）即使空也别坐: Priority seats (노약자석/임산부석) should not be used even if empty

感冒发烧去 내과（内科）: Go to 내과 (Internal Medicine) for colds and fevers

中文\"我肚子疼\"，主语容易带错成 저를 배 아파요。韩语正确结构是\"部位: In Chinese, 'my stomach hurts' — people often mistakenly say 저를 배 아파요. The correct Korean structure is 'body part + 가 아파요' — the body part is the subject. 배가 아파요, 머리가 아파요, 목이 아파요. Don't use 를/을.

比 어디가 아파요 更委婉，医生固定问句: More polite than 어디가 아파요; the standard question doctors use.
~부터 表起点，部位 + 가 아파요 万能句型: ~부터 marks starting point; body part + 가 아파요 is a versatile pattern
也可说 열이 나요，量了体温说 삼십팔 도예요: You can also say 열이 나요; after taking your temperature, say 삼십팔 도예요
问医生要处方: ask the doctor for a prescription
拿到 처방전 后到 약국 取药: after getting the 처방전, pick up medicine at the 약국
받다 (领取) 未来冠形: future adnominal form of 받다 (to receive)
药剂师交代用法: the pharmacist explains how to take it
一天几次 = 하루에 X 번，X 天 = X일 동안: how many times a day = 하루에 X 번; X days = X일 동안
식전 = 饭前, 공복 = 空腹, 자기 전 = 睡前: 식전 = before meals, 공복 = on an empty stomach, 자기 전 = before bed
常见回复 졸릴 수 있어요（可能犯困）: Common response 졸릴 수 있어요 (may cause drowsiness)
需要请病假/交学校时: When needing sick leave / submitting to school

떼다 = 开(证明)/摘下: 떼다 = to issue (a certificate) / to take off

明洞地区商务酒店，晚上 8 点到达: Business hotel in Myeongdong, arriving at 8 PM
\"체크인\" 就用英语外来语，很少用 입실: "Check-in" is used as a loanword from English; 입실 is rarely used.
\"금연실\" 禁烟房，\"흡연실\" 吸烟房，全酒店禁烟叫 완전 금연: "금연실" is a non-smoking room, "흡연실" is a smoking room; a fully non-smoking hotel is called 완전 금연.
\"호실\" = 房号，\"조식\" = 早餐（汉字词）: "호실" means room number, "조식" means breakfast (Sino-Korean word).
打前台电话 · 客房请求: Calling the front desk · room requests

\"여보세요\" 是电话开场，\"갖다주다\" = 送来: "여보세요" is a phone greeting, "갖다주다" means to bring over.
\"~ 것 같다\" 委婉抱怨: "~ 것 같다" is used for polite complaints.
\"곧\" = 马上，酒店回应固定用语: "곧" means soon, a fixed phrase in hotel responses.
\"모닝콜\" = morning call，\"7시에 깨워 주세요\" 也行: "모닝콜" means morning call; "7시에 깨워 주세요" also works.

\"미니바\" 冰箱里的酒水，用了会额外收费: "미니바" refers to drinks in the minibar; using them incurs extra charges.

\"얼리 체크인\" = early check-in，越来越常用: "얼리 체크인" means early check-in, increasingly common.
홍대 게스트하우스（青旅）多人间第一晚: First night in a dorm at a Hongdae guesthouse (hostel)

中文说\"订房\"直译容易讲成 방을 예약하다 或 예약하다 방 —— 前者正确: In Chinese, "订房" (book a room) literally translated can become 방을 예약하다 or 예약하다 방 — the former is correct, the latter has wrong word order. In Seoul, common Airbnb-style backpacker hostels are called 게스트하우스, and family-run inns are 펜션. It's common to ask for 민박 and get directed to a rural route by mistake.

穷游/临时过夜韩国人常去 찜질방（汗蒸幕过夜，1-2 万韩元），提供公共大厅睡地: Budget travelers and those needing a quick overnight stay often go to a 찜질방 (jjimjilbang, overnight sauna, 10,000-20,000 KRW), which offers a common hall with floor sleeping. Saying "체크인" at the front desk will get you laughed at — at a 찜질방, you just walk in, pay, and change clothes; there's no room key. For a private room, you'd need a 모텔 (motel) or 호텔.
\"방\" 不加号数用 \"몇 인실\": For "방" without a room number, use "몇 인실"
问几人间用 \"몇 인실\"（几人房），不是 \"몇 방\"。单人间 1인실、双: To ask how many people a room fits, use "몇 인실" (how many-person room), not "몇 방". Single room is 1인실, double is 2인실, family room is 가족실. Don't literally translate Chinese "几个房间" (how many rooms) into 몇 방 이에요 — count rooms with 개: 방 몇 개 있어요? (How many rooms are there?)
\"체크인\" 时间没到只能寄行李: If it's not yet "체크인" time, you can only store your luggage
韩国酒店标准 체크인 时间是下午 3 点，早到只能寄存行李（짐 보관）—— 不能: Standard check-in time at Korean hotels is 3 PM; arriving early means you can only store luggage (짐 보관) — no "early check-in". To check in early, you'd say 얼리 체크인 가능해요? and it's likely to be refused or charged. Conversely, check-out is usually 11 AM; if you want to sleep in, mention 레이트 체크아웃 in advance.

\"~이름으로 예약했어요\" 是固定报名字方式: "~이름으로 예약했어요" is the standard way to state your name for a reservation

取行李说 짐 찾으러 왔어요，凭 태그（牌子）: Say 짐 찾으러 왔어요 to pick up luggage, with the 태그 (tag)
见面 · 自我介绍 · 寒暄 · 告别 · 韩国社交 60% 场景的礼节话术: Meeting, self-introduction, small talk, farewells — polite phrases for 60% of Korean social situations
入职第一天，被介绍给部门同事: First day at work, being introduced to department colleagues
\"~라고 합니다\" 比 \"~예요\" 更正式，工作/正式场合专用: "~라고 합니다" is more formal than "~예요", used in work/formal settings
\"잘 부탁드립니다\" 是入职/入学万能收尾: "잘 부탁드립니다" is the go-to closing for starting a new job/school

朋友间用 반말（半语），加 야 或直接叫名字: Between friends, use 반말 (casual speech), add 야 or just call their name
\"어머\" 是女性感叹词，男性用 어/야: "어머" is a feminine exclamation; men use 어/야
\"정신없다\" 直译\"没精神\"实际是\"忙昏\": "정신없다" literally means "no spirit" but actually means "swamped/busy"

离职最后一天向部长告别: Saying goodbye to the department head on your last day

\"~구나\" 是长辈对晚辈的感叹语气: "~구나" is an exclamatory tone used by elders to younger people
\"안녕히 계세요\" 对留下方说；对方对你说 \"안녕히 가세요\": "안녕히 계세요" is said to the one staying; they say "안녕히 가세요" to you
설날 前一天给上司发카톡拜年: Sending a New Year's greeting via KakaoTalk to your boss the day before Seollal
发消息必须自报姓名，即使是熟人: Always state your name when messaging, even with acquaintances
\"지도해 주다\" = 指导，比 \"가르쳐 주다\" 更敬: "지도해 주다" = to guide, more respectful than "가르쳐 주다"
\"~시길 바랍니다\" 是节日祝福最正式的收尾: "~시길 바랍니다" is the most formal closing for holiday greetings
搬家第二天，隔壁开门自我介绍: The day after moving, the neighbor opens the door and introduces themselves
搬家后主动打招呼是韩国传统，尤其在老房区: Greeting neighbors after moving is a Korean tradition, especially in older neighborhoods
\"~구나\" 长辈对晚辈发现式感叹: "~구나" is an exclamation of discovery from elders to younger people
\"별거 아닌데\" 是送礼时惯用的谦语: "별거 아닌데" is a common humble phrase when giving gifts
首尔层间噪音是敏感话题，先说这句可以缓冲: Noise between floors in Seoul is a sensitive topic; saying this first can ease tension
两个都是告别，但方向完全相反：安녕히 \"가세요\"（请慢走）说给离开的人 ——: Both are farewells, but in opposite directions: 안녕히 "가세요" (go safely) is said to the one leaving — you stay, they go. 안녕히 "계세요" (stay well) is said to the one staying — you go, they stay. If you mix them up, the other person might pause, but it's not a politeness mistake. If both are leaving, use 다음에 봐요/또 만나요.
\"오빠/언니\" 别对不熟的人乱叫: Don't casually use "오빠/언니" with people you don't know well
这些是\"哥/姐\"称呼，只用于比自己大的亲密朋友/恋人/亲哥姐。初次见面直接叫: These are "older brother/sister" terms, used only for close friends, lovers, or biological older siblings who are older than you. Calling someone 오빠 on first meeting is seen as overly intimate (especially a woman to a man), even with romantic undertones. Safe options: name + 씨 (○○씨), or title (팀장님/선배님). K-pop fans calling idols 오빠 is fine, since it's a fan context.

Just answer 네, 먹었어요/아직요; no need to actually meet up. Conversely, "밥 한번 먹자" (let's eat sometime) is often just politeness — 80% of the time it won't happen.
第一次见面别问年龄/婚否: Don't ask about age or marital status on first meeting
虽然韩国人自己见面确认年龄很常见（因为敬语系统需要），但外国人第一次见韩国人别直: While Koreans often confirm age when meeting (due to the honorific system), foreigners shouldn't directly ask 몇 살이에요? on first meeting — it makes the other person uncomfortable, especially women or elders. Wait for them to offer, or ask 실례지만 나이가 어떻게 되세요? (excuse me, may I ask your age?) with polite hedging. Never ask about marital status.
入职、入学、认识新朋友、房东见面、加入群聊 —— 韩国所有关系开始都用 \"잘: Starting a job, school, meeting new friends, seeing a landlord, joining a group chat — in Korea, every new relationship ends with "잘 부탁드립니다" (please take care of me). It's not just politeness; it's a social pact of "I'm entrusting our future relationship to you." Not saying it seems cold; saying it shows you know etiquette. You can add it as the last line of a self-intro message too.
뵙겠습니다 是 보다 的敬语最高级，比 만나겠습니다 更礼貌: 뵙겠습니다 is the highest honorific of 보다, more polite than 만나겠습니다

韩剧里女主叫男主 오빠 是\"亲密/暧昧\"信号，不是家人称呼。中文语境说\"哥: In K-dramas, the female lead calling the male lead 오빠 signals intimacy/ambiguity, not family. In Chinese, "哥哥" only means biological brother, but Korean 오빠 covers: older brother, older male friends (for women), boyfriends, and male idol members. Context and tone tell them apart. Don't copy the female lead calling strangers 오빠—that's a flirty tone.

When the female lead says 됐어, 90% of the time it's cutting off or sulking: 됐어, 이제 그만해 (enough, stop talking). Don't literally translate it as "completed."

街头拦人问路用 저기요（\"那个\"），不用 죄송합니다（\"对不起\"）。죄송: When stopping someone on the street to ask directions, use 저기요 ("excuse me"), not 죄송합니다 ("sorry"). Koreans only use 죄송합니다 when genuinely apologizing, making a mistake, or asking someone to move aside. Using it to start a question might make the other person think you bumped into them. For calling staff at a restaurant or asking about something at a convenience store, always use 저기요. For older people, 사장님/이모 also works.
两个都是\"问\"，但对象不同：물어보다 是普通问（对朋友/平辈），여쭤보다 是: Both mean "ask," but they differ by target: 물어보다 is a regular ask (to friends/peers), while 여쭤보다 is humble speech (to elders/strangers/formal settings). Using 여쭤보다 when asking directions on the street shows politeness: 길 좀 여쭤봐도 될까요? Asking a friend 물어봐도 돼? is fine too. Using them the other way around sounds odd.
两个都能问位置但语感不同：어디예요? 侧重\"是哪儿\"（本质属性）—— 화장실: Both can ask for location but differ in nuance: 어디예요? focuses on "what place is it" (essential nature) — 화장실 어디예요?; 어디에 있어요? focuses on "where is it right now" (current location) — 사장님 어디에 있어요? They're interchangeable in most situations, but for people, 어디에 있어요? is more polite, and for objects, 어디예요? is more concise.
两个都译\"旅游\"，语感有别：여행 = 广义旅行（含商务/探亲），관광 = 观: Both translate to "travel," but differ in nuance: 여행 = broad travel (including business/visiting family), 관광 = sightseeing (pure leisure, often used in official/customs contexts). When customs asks 방문 목적, answering 관광 (sightseeing) is most standard. Telling a friend "I'm traveling to Korea" sounds more natural with 여행 가요: 다음 달에 서울 여행 가요. Don't always translate it as 관광.
请对方帮拍：사진 찍어 주세요（请给我拍照，\"주다\" 是给我）。你帮对方拍：: Asking someone to take a photo: 사진 찍어 주세요 (please take a photo for me, "주다" means give to me). When offering to take a photo for someone while traveling, say 사진 찍어 드릴까요? (Would you like me to take one for you?)

Saying 수고하세요 to a manager/superior when leaving work makes them uncomfortable. To superiors, say 수고하셨습니다 (past tense, you've worked hard) or 먼저 들어가 보겠습니다 (I'll head off first). 韩国邮件开头几乎必写：안녕하세요, [부서]/[회사] [이름]입니다. 例如: Korean emails almost always start with: 안녕하세요, [부서]/[회사] [이름]입니다. E.g., 안녕하세요, 마케팅팀 김민지입니다. Don't follow English email style and jump straight to the point — that seems rude. End with 감사합니다 / [Name] 드림 (respectfully) / Name 올림 (more humble, for superiors).
\"부탁드립니다\" 不加 요，也不省略: "부탁드립니다" doesn't take 요 and isn't shortened
邮件/正式沟通标准套话是 부탁드립니다（合니다体，最正式），不是 부탁드려요（아: The standard phrase in emails/formal communication is 부탁드립니다 (합니다 form, most formal), not 부탁드려요 (아/어요 form is too casual) nor 부탁해요 (only for friends). This is a "courtesy label" in Korean workplaces; using it wrong makes you seem undisciplined. Similar: 감사드립니다, 죄송합니다, 알겠습니다 all use the 합니다 form.
韩国职场请假单位：연차 = 全天年假、반차 = 半天假（오전 반차/오후 반차）: Korean workplace leave units: 연차 = full-day annual leave, 반차 = half-day leave (오전 반차/오후 반차), 월차 = monthly leave (old term, now mostly merged into 연차). To request leave, say 연차 쓸게요 (use annual leave), 반차 신청할게요 (apply for half-day). Don't use Chinese-style thinking and say 하루 쉬어요 (take a day off) — too casual.
카톡（KakaoTalk）已成韩国职场标配，但公司内一般用 카카오워크（Kaka: 카톡 (KakaoTalk) is standard in Korean workplaces, but companies usually use 카카오워크 (KakaoWork) or dedicated groups, not personal 카톡. Even messaging colleagues requires honorifics and the 님 title: 김민지 님, 확인 부탁드립니다. (Not 민지야 확인해줘). For peers/close colleagues, you can use ~님 with half-polite speech, but for superiors, full honorifics are mandatory.

两个都译\"知道/明白\" 但完全不同：알아요 = \"我知道/我认识\"（陈述: Both translate to "know/understand" but differ completely: 알아요 = "I know/I recognize" (stating existing knowledge); 알겠어요 = "I understand/I got it" (reaction to new info). When the teacher asks 알겠어요? the student replies 네, 알겠어요/알겠습니다 (got it), not 네, 알아요 (I know—sounds arrogant). In daily life: 이 사람 알아요? 알아요! (Do you know this person? Yes, I do!)
\"선생님\" 不能省，也不用中式称呼: "선생님" can't be omitted, and don't use Chinese-style titles
韩国课堂对老师必称 선생님（老师 + 님，敬称一体），不能只说 선생 或直呼姓名: In Korean classrooms, you must call teachers 선생님 (teacher + 님, an integrated honorific). You can't just say 선생 or use their name. When raising your hand to ask, always start with 선생님, 질문 있어요. Some Chinese students say 교수님 (professor) — but that's only for university professors; for middle/high school and language institute teachers, it's always 선생님. Teachers don't mind students repeating 선생님 — in fact, they see it as polite.
两个都译\"难\"但不通用：어렵다 = 难懂/难度大（客观），指知识内容：이 문: Both translate to "hard" but aren't interchangeable: 어렵다 = difficult to understand/objectively hard, for content: 이 문법 어려워요 (this grammar is hard). 힘들다 = tiring/tough (subjective feeling), for body/mind: 요즘 공부하기 힘들어요 (studying is tiring these days). 韩国大学里学长学姐叫 선배（前辈），学弟学妹叫 후배（后辈），同期叫 동기。선배: In Korean universities, seniors are called 선배 (sunbae), juniors 후배 (hubae), and same-year peers 동기. 선배 holds clear seniority/relationship advantages — treating juniors to meals and giving advice first is the culture. Course registration, job hunting, and contacting professors all rely on the 선배 network. Don't assume it's as casual as China's "学长" — especially in CC/liberal arts majors, the sunbae-hubae bond is tight. Adding 님 (선배님) sounds more polite.

A professor saying 이 과목 3학점이에요 means "This course is 3 credits." Students ask each other 이번 학기 학점 얼마 나왔어? meaning "What's your GPA this semester?" — distinguish by context. Scholarships (장학금) usually require 3.5 학점 이상 (GPA 3.5+).

麻烦陌生人拍照要用客气的 찍어 주시겠어요 或 찍어 주세요，别用生硬的 찍어（: When asking a stranger to take a photo, use polite forms like 찍어 주시겠어요 or 찍어 주세요, not blunt 찍어 (take) or 찍어라. Being too direct sounds rude — always add 주시겠어요/주세요 when making a request.

辞职别只说 “그만둘래요”: Don't just say 그만둘래요 when quitting
对店长或老板正式提辞职时，해요体的 그만둘래요（我想不干了）听起来太随意、甚至任: When formally resigning to a manager or boss, the 해요-form 그만둘래요 ('I want to quit') sounds too casual, even willful. In formal settings, use 그만두겠습니다 or 그만두려고 합니다, and soften it with 죄송하지만. This conveys your decision while staying polite.
주휴수당 是法定权利，别放弃: 주휴수당 is a legal right—don't give it up

Similarly, use 보고드리다 for 'report' and 답변드리다 for 'reply'—this 드리다 is essential in the workplace.

答不上来别硬编，用缓冲句: Don't make up answers when you're stuck—use a buffer phrase

The natural approach is to say 확인 후에 답변드리겠습니다 (I'll get back to you after confirming) to hold the question, then add 자료는 메일로 전달드리겠습니다. This is encouraged as a rigorous attitude in Korean workplaces, not something to be ashamed of.

The casual 늘었어요, 줄었어요 mean the same but are too informal and reduce professionalism in formal reports. Use 증가/감소 consistently for numerical changes, paired with framework terms like 전년 대비 (year-over-year).
想对听众说“我要强调”，正式场合用 강조드리다（把强调这个动作谦让地呈现给对方）: To tell the audience 'I want to emphasize' in formal settings, use 강조드리다 (humbly presenting the act of emphasizing to the other person). 강조해요 is too flat; 강조하겠습니다 works but lacks respect for the audience. 你更愿意住在城市还是农村?请从生活便利、环境、人际关系三方面对比。: Would you rather live in a city or the countryside? Compare them in terms of convenience, environment, and relationships.

主语\"저\"后面用主题助词\"는\"(收音有无:은/는)。这里 저 无收音选: The subject "저" takes the topic particle "는" (with/without final consonant: 은/는). Here, 저 has no final consonant, so choose 는.
\"책\"是宾语,用宾格助词\"을/를\"。책 有收音 ㄱ 选 을。: "책" is the object, so use the object particle "을/를". 책 has the final consonant ㄱ, so choose 을.
\"에\"表示动作的目的地。区分:에(去/在静态)vs 에서(在...做事)。: "에" indicates the destination of an action. Distinguish: 에 (going to/being at a static place) vs. 에서 (doing something at a place).
在某地做动态动作用\"에서\"。공부하다 是动作,选 에서。: Use "에서" for dynamic actions done at a place. 공부하다 is an action, so choose 에서.
\"和...一起\"用\"와/과\"。有收音+과,无收音+와。친구 无收音选 와: Use "와/과" for "together with". With final consonant + 과, without + 와. 친구 has no final consonant, so choose 와.
\"보다\"用于比较。N보다 (더) A · \"比 N 更 A\"。: "보다" is used for comparison. N보다 (더) A · "more A than N".
(她)比姐姐漂亮。: (She) is prettier than her older sister.
过去时:보다 → 봤어요(缩略自 보+았어요)。어제 提示过去。: Past tense: 보다 → 봤어요 (contracted from 보+았어요). 어제 indicates the past.
\"V-고 있다\"表示正在进行。지금(现在)明确提示进行时。: "V-고 있다" indicates an ongoing action. 지금 (now) clearly signals the progressive tense.
将来时\"V-(으)ㄹ 거예요\":动词词干+ㄹ 거예요。가+ㄹ = 갈。: Future tense "V-(으)ㄹ 거예요": verb stem + ㄹ 거예요. 가+ㄹ = 갈.
\"V-(으)ㄴ 적이 있다\"表示经历过。가+ㄴ = 간。: "V-(으)ㄴ 적이 있다" indicates having experienced something. 가+ㄴ = 간.
\"N + 중이다\"表示进行中。会议中 = 회의 중이에요。空格填 중이,连上: "N + 중이다" indicates something is in progress. In a meeting = 회의 중이에요. Fill in the blank with 중이, and with -에요 attached it becomes 중이에요.
现在正在开会。: We're in a meeting right now.
\"V-았/었던\"表示回忆中已完成的动作。10년 전(10年前)提示过去回忆。: "V-았/었던" indicates an action completed in the past that you're recalling. 10년 전 (10 years ago) signals a past memory. 간 (V-(으)ㄴ) is grammatically correct but sounds more objective; 갔던 fits better with "a place from memory."
这是10年前去过的地方。: This is a place I went to 10 years ago.
\"V-아/어서\"表示原因。오+아서 → 와서。前后主语可不同,但结果句不能是: "V-아/어서" expresses cause. 오+아서 → 와서. The subjects can differ, but the result clause can't be a command.
\"A/V-지만\"表示转折\"虽然但是\"。前后语义相反选 지만。: "A/V-지만" expresses contrast, "although/but." Choose 지만 when the clauses are semantically opposite.
虽然累但还在继续工作。: I'm tired, but I'm still working.
\"V-(으)면\"表示条件/假设\"如果...就...\"。: "V-(으)면" expresses a condition or hypothesis, "if... then..."
\"V-(으)면서\"表示同时进行。듣다 是 ㄷ 不规则,ㄷ → ㄹ + 으면서: "V-(으)면서" indicates simultaneous actions. 듣다 is a ㄷ-irregular verb: ㄷ → ㄹ + 으면서 = 들으면서.
\"아무리 V-아/어도\" · 无论怎么...也...。让步语气,搭配 아무리: "아무리 V-아/어도" means "no matter how..." It's concessive and pairs with 아무리.
再怎么做也不成功。: No matter how I try, it doesn't work.
\"V-고 나서\"表示一个动作结束后再做另一个。오다 → 오고 나서。: "V-고 나서" means doing one action after another finishes. 오다 → 오고 나서.
来韩国以后经常吃泡菜锅。: Since coming to Korea, I often eat kimchi stew.
尊敬语 -(으)시- + 过去 -었- = -(으)셨-。오다 无收音直接接 -: Honorific -(으)시- + past -었- = -(으)셨-. 오다 has no final consonant, so it directly takes -셨- (no 으).
\"V-아/어 주세요\"请对方为自己做某事。찍다 + 어 주세요 = 찍어 주: "V-아/어 주세요" asks someone to do something for you. 찍다 + 어 주세요 = 찍어 주세요.
请帮我拍张照。: Please take a picture for me.
\"V-(으)시겠어요?\"是很礼貌的建议/意愿询问。먹다→드시다(尊敬替换词): "V-(으)시겠어요?" is a very polite suggestion or inquiry about intention. 먹다→드시다 (honorific substitute).
(您)要来一杯咖啡吗？: Would you like a cup of coffee?
\"V-(으)면 안 되다\"表示禁止\"不可以做\"。나가 + 면 안 돼요。: "V-(으)면 안 되다" expresses prohibition, "can't do." 나가 + 면 안 돼요.
现在不能出去。: I can't go out right now.
\"V-아/어야 하다/되다\"表示必须/应当。끝내 + 야 해요。: "V-아/어야 하다/되다" expresses obligation or necessity. 끝내 + 야 해요.
明天之前得完成。: I have to finish it by tomorrow.
\"V-았/었거든요\"回答式解释\"因为(过去)...嘛\"。终结词尾 -거든: "V-았/었거든요" is a response-style explanation, "because (in the past)..." It's a sentence-ending ending -거든요, with past tense -았/었거든요.
因为昨天睡得晚嘛。: Because I went to bed late yesterday.
\"께\"是\"에게/한테\"的敬语形式,给尊长时用。这里对象是老师,且谓语用谦: "께" is the honorific form of "에게/한테," used when giving to someone of higher status. Here, the recipient is a teacher, and the verb is the humble form 드리다, so 께 is used.
送给了老师礼物。: Gave a gift to the teacher.
\"(으)로\"表示手段/方式(乘什么、用什么)。버스 无收音选 로。干扰项 에: "(으)로" indicates means/method (by what, with what). 버스 has no final consonant, so 로 is used. The distractor 에 is a location particle, not for tools.
\"만\"表示\"只、仅\"。물만 마셔요 = 只喝水。: "만" means "only." 물만 마셔요 = only drink water.
\"부터\"表示时间/顺序的起点\"从...开始\"。干扰项 까지 是终点\"到: "부터" marks the starting point of time/order, "from..." The distractor 까지 is the endpoint "until," which is the opposite.
给\"人\"某物用\"에게/한테\"。写信给朋友 → 친구에게。干扰项 에서 用: To give something to a "person," use "에게/한테." Writing a letter to a friend → 친구에게. The distractor 에서 is for places (at/from), not for people as recipients.
给朋友写信。: Write a letter to a friend.
\"처럼\"表示\"像...一样\"。가수처럼 = 像歌手一样。干扰项 보다 是: "처럼" means "like..." 가수처럼 = like a singer. The distractor 보다 is for comparison "than a singer," which is different.
唱歌像歌手一样好。: Sings as well as a singer.
\"밖에\"必须搭配否定谓语(없어요/안...),意为\"只有\"。천 원밖에: "밖에" must be used with a negative predicate (없어요/안...), meaning "only." 천 원밖에 없어요 = only 1,000 won.
\"매일\"提示现在时/习惯。마시다 现在时 아/어요 缩略为 마셔요。마시어요: "매일" indicates present tense/habit. 마시다 in present tense 아/어요 contracts to 마셔요. 마시어요 is an uncontracted error, and 마셨어요 is past tense.
\"어제\"提示过去时。만나다 → 만났어요(만나+았어요,同元音省略)。: "어제" indicates past tense. 만나다 → 만났어요 (만나 + 았어요, same vowel omitted).
形容词也有过去时。\"어제\"提示过去 → 좋다 + 았어요 = 좋았어요。: Adjectives also have past tense. "어제" indicates past → 좋다 + 았어요 = 좋았어요.
\"-겠-\"表示根据眼前依据的推测\"看样子快要...\"。\"하늘을 보니(: "-겠-" expresses a guess based on visible evidence, "looks like it's about to..." "하늘을 보니 (looking at the sky)" is the basis for the guess → 오겠어요. 왔어요 is past tense, which doesn't fit.
看天空,快要下雨了。: Looking at the sky, it's about to rain.
\"V-(으)ㄹ게요\"表示说话人(第一人称)的意志/承诺。\"이따가(等会儿): "V-(으)ㄹ게요" expresses the speaker's (first person) intention/promise. "이따가 (later) + 제가 (I)" → 전화할게요.
\"아까(刚才)\"是过去,进行时要用过去形 \"-고 있었어요\"。있어요 是: "아까 (earlier)" is past, so the progressive must be in past form "-고 있었어요." 있어요 is present progressive, which conflicts with 아까.
\"V-(으)ㄴ 지 + 时间 + 됐다\"表示做某事以来过了多久。오다 → 온: "V-(으)ㄴ 지 + time + 됐다" indicates how long it's been since doing something. 오다 → 온 지.
来韩国已经3年了。: It's been 3 years since I came to Korea.
\"-아/어 있다\"表示动作完成后的状态持续。门开着(状态)用自动词 열리다: "-아/어 있다" indicates a state that continues after an action is completed. For the door being open (state), use the intransitive verb 열리다 → 열려 있어요. The distractor 열고 있어요 means "opening the door" (action in progress, and requires the object 문을).
\"V-(으)러 가다/오다\"表示移动的目的。먹다 + 으러 = 먹으러(去做: "V-(으)러 가다/오다" expresses the purpose of movement. 먹다 + 으러 = 먹으러 (to go do something).
\"-(으)니까\"表原因,且后句可接命令/劝诱。而 \"-아/어서\" 后不能: "-(으)니까" indicates a reason, and the following clause can be a command or suggestion. But "-아/어서" cannot be followed by a command, so 없어서 + 서두르세요 is wrong.
因为没时间,请快点。: Since there's no time, please hurry.
\"-는데\"引出后续话语的背景\"我正要出门(那么)...\"。나가다 → 나: "-는데" sets the background for what follows, "I'm about to go out (so)..." 나가다 → 나가는데. 나가서 (then) and 나가려고 (in order to go out) don't fit this question context.
我现在要出门,你需要什么吗?: I'm about to go out now, do you need anything?
\"-거나\"表示并列选择\"或者\"。读书或者看电影 → 읽거나。干扰项 읽고: "-거나" indicates a choice between alternatives, "or." Reading or watching a movie → 읽거나. The distractor 읽고 means "read and watch a movie" (doing both), which is different.
周末读书或者看电影。: On weekends, I read or watch movies.
\"-(으)려고\"表示意图/目的\"为了...\"。배우다 无收音 + 려고: "-(으)려고" expresses intention/purpose, "in order to." 배우다 (no batchim) + 려고 = 배우려고.
为了学韩语去上补习班。: I go to a cram school to learn Korean.
\"-느라고\"表示因忙于做前项(消耗时间精力)而导致后项消极结果(常配 못/안: "-느라고" indicates that being busy with the first action (consuming time/energy) leads to a negative result in the second (often with 못/안). 하다 → 하느라고. The subject must be the same for both clauses.
因为忙着打游戏没做作业。: I was busy playing games, so I didn't do my homework.
\"-도록\"表示目的/程度\"以便、为了(使)...\"。为了不迟到 → 늦지: "-도록" indicates purpose/degree, "so that, in order to (make)..." To not be late → 늦지 않도록.
为了不迟到早点出发。: Leave early so you won't be late.
\"-자마자\"表示\"一...就...(紧接着)\"。오다 → 오자마자,配: "-자마자" means "as soon as... (immediately after)." 오다 → 오자마자, and it's more natural with 바로. The distractor 와서 just indicates sequence, which is weaker.
一到家就马上睡了。: As soon as I got home, I went straight to sleep.
表\"存在\"的 있다 的尊敬形是特殊词 계시다,不是 있으세요。主语 아버지께: The honorific form of 있다 (to exist) is the special word 계시다, not 있으세요. With the subject 아버지께서 → 계세요.
\"V-(으)ㄹ까요?\"用于向对方提议/征求意见。먹다 + 을까요 = 먹을까: "V-(으)ㄹ까요?" is used to make a suggestion or ask for the other's opinion. 먹다 + 을까요 = 먹을까요.
为尊长做事用谦让语 드리다。도와주다 → 도와드리다,承诺时 도와드릴게요。干扰: Use the humble form 드리다 when doing something for an elder. 도와주다 → 도와드리다, and when promising, 도와드릴게요. The distractor 줄게요 is only used with peers or those younger.
看起来很重,我来帮您。: That looks heavy. Let me help you.
\"V-(으)세요\"是尊敬的请求/命令。앉다 有收音 + 으세요 = 앉으세요: "V-(으)세요" is a polite request/command. 앉다 has a final consonant + 으세요 = 앉으세요 (Please sit).
\"V-지 마세요\"表示禁止/劝阻\"请不要...\"。\"위험하니까(因为危: "V-지 마세요" indicates prohibition/discouragement, "Please don't...". "위험하니까 (because it's dangerous)" signals prohibition → 찍지 마세요. The distractor 찍으세요 means "please take (a photo)", which is the opposite.
危险,请不要在这里拍照。: It's dangerous, please don't take photos here.
\"V-(으)ㄹ 수 있다\"表示能力\"会/能\"。\"조금(一点)\"提示能: "V-(으)ㄹ 수 있다" indicates ability, "can/be able to". "조금 (a little)" hints at the degree of ability → 할 수 있어요. The distractors are future intention/progressive/past.
我会说一点韩语。: I can speak a little Korean.

意思是不管什么事，一旦开始就已经完成了一半。: It means that no matter what you do, once you start, you've already done half of it.
很多国家都流传着这样意思的话。: Many countries have sayings with this meaning.
森林村庄里住着一只慢吞吞的乌龟。: In a forest village lived a slow turtle.

\"又要搬石头，又要砌墙……唉，太累了。\": "I have to carry stones, build walls... ugh, it's too tiring."

\"乌龟啊，你怎么还不盖房子？\": "Turtle, why haven't you built your house yet?"

第二天放两块，再第二天放三块。: The next day he put two, and the day after, three.
一点一点堆着，墙就出来了。: Stacking bit by bit, the wall took shape.

请穿暖和些出门。: Please dress warmly when going out.

可是芽儿一直不冒出来。: But the sprout just wouldn't come out.
也不下雨，土都干了。: It didn't rain either, and the soil dried up.

\"有点累，不过我要等下去。\": "A little tired, but I'll keep waiting."

叫\"열 번 찍어 안 넘어가는 나무 없다（砍十次没有不倒的树）\"。: It's called '열 번 찍어 안 넘어가는 나무 없다' (No tree falls without ten chops).
意思是只要坚持，没有做不成的事。: It means if you persist, nothing is impossible.

可是壳太硬了。: But the shell was too hard.
用门牙咚咚地敲了敲。: It tapped it with its front teeth, knock knock.

松鼠又咚咚地敲起来。: The squirrel knocked again, knock knock.
敲了一次、两次、三次。: It knocked once, twice, three times.
壳上出现了一道小小的裂纹。: A small crack appeared on the shell.
松鼠来了劲，又敲起来。: The squirrel got motivated and started knocking again.
敲了四次、五次、六次。: It knocked four, five, six times.
额头上冒出了细细的汗珠。: Fine beads of sweat appeared on its forehead.
第十次使劲敲了下去。: On the tenth try, it knocked hard.
\"咔\"的一声，核桃裂开了。: With a "crack," the walnut split open.
里面满是香香的果仁。: Inside was full of fragrant nutmeat.
它和刺猬分着吃了果仁。: It shared the nutmeat with the hedgehog.
再硬的核桃也一样。: No matter how hard the walnut is.
只要坚持敲，就一定能打开。: As long as you keep knocking, you'll definitely open it.
所以才说\"砍十次没有不倒的树\"。: That's why they say, "Strike ten times, and no tree will stand."
小朋友们不放弃的心，真可爱。: The children's never-give-up hearts are truly adorable.
现在把手轻轻松开，休息吧。: Now gently let go and rest.
核桃壳很硬。: The walnut shell is very hard.
玻璃上有了裂纹。: There's a crack in the glass.
枕着软软的枕头躺下吧。: Lie down on a soft pillow.
悄悄告诉你们今天的老话。: Let me quietly tell you today's proverb.

意思是一句好话有很大的力量。: It means a kind word has great power.

兔子急急忙忙地跑在路上。: The rabbit was running hurriedly down the road.
一不小心撞到了鼹鼠的篮子。: It accidentally bumped into a mole's basket.
橡子骨碌碌地撒了一地。: Acorns rolled all over the ground.
鼹鼠吓了一跳，生气了。: The mole was startled and got angry.
\"真对不起，我太着急了。\": "I'm so sorry, I was in too much of a hurry."
\"我全都帮您捡起来。\": "I'll pick them all up for you."
兔子蹲下身把橡子捡起来。: The rabbit crouched down and picked up the acorns.
听到温柔的声音，鼹鼠的气消了。: Hearing the gentle voice, the mole's anger faded.
两个一起捡起了橡子。: The two picked up the acorns together.
篮子很快又装满了。: The basket was soon full again.
\"你帮忙，反倒该我谢谢。\": "You helped, but I should be the one thanking you."
兔子笑盈盈地打招呼。: The rabbit greeted with a bright smile.
\"下次我会看好路再走。\": "Next time, I'll watch where I'm going."
生气的心像春雪一样融化了。: The angry heart melted like spring snow.
两个手拉着手一起走。: The two walked hand in hand.
一句好话化解了争执。: A kind word resolved the quarrel.
那天傍晚两个分着吃了橡子。: That evening, they shared acorns together.
只用一句温暖的\"对不起\"。: Just one warm "I'm sorry" is enough.
再大的争执也会慢慢化开。: Even the biggest arguments slowly melt away.
所以才说\"一句话能还清千两债务\"。: That's why they say "one word can repay a thousand taels of debt."
小朋友们说的话也又美又暖。: What the little ones say is also beautiful and warm.
现在安心地放下心来吧。: Now, rest easy and let your worries go.
夜风在窗外轻轻吹着。: The night breeze blows softly outside the window.
今天也准备了一句老话。: Today, we have another old saying ready.

意思是再温顺的人，被随便对待也会生气。: It means even the gentlest person gets angry when treated carelessly.

别的朋友常常取笑蚯蚓。: The other friends often tease the earthworm.

更用力地蹦蹦踩着泥土。: It stomps on the ground even harder.
蚯蚓把身子用力扭了一下。: The earthworm gives a strong wriggle.
这是第一次听到蚯蚓这么大的声音。: It's the first time they hear the earthworm speak so loudly.
蚱蜢吓了一跳，停了下来。: The grasshopper is startled and stops.
\"对不起，我不知道你会疼。\": "I'm sorry, I didn't know you could feel pain."
\"温顺也不能被随便对待呀。\": "Even the gentle shouldn't be treated carelessly."
蚱蜢深深地低下了头。: The grasshopper lowers its head deeply.
别的朋友也在旁边看着。: Other friends were watching from the side too.

蚯蚓的心稍稍舒展了。: The earthworm's heart relaxed a little.
从那以后，没人再取笑蚯蚓。: From then on, no one teased the earthworm anymore.
再温顺再安静的朋友。: No matter how gentle and quiet a friend is.
被随便对待，心也会扭动起来。: If treated carelessly, their heart will squirm too.
所以才说\"蚯蚓被踩也会扭一扭\"。: That's why they say, "Even an earthworm wriggles when stepped on."
小朋友们也要好好珍惜朋友哦。: Kids, make sure to cherish your friends too.
现在慢慢地呼出一口气吧。: Now, slowly let out a breath.
泥土里有蚯蚓。: There are earthworms in the soil.
星光轻轻落在窗边。: Starlight softly falls by the window.
抱着被子舒服地躺下吧。: Lie down comfortably hugging your blanket.
叫\"바늘 도둑이 소도둑 된다（偷针的贼会变成偷牛的贼）\"。: It's called "바늘 도둑이 소도둑 된다 (A needle thief becomes a cow thief)."
意思是小的坏习惯会变成大错。: It means small bad habits can turn into big mistakes.

松鼠悄悄拿走了一颗橡子。: The squirrel quietly took one acorn.
到了晚上也睡不着。: It couldn't sleep even at night.

忽然想起了熊大叔的话。: Suddenly, it remembered Uncle Bear's words.
\"再小的东西，别人的也是别人的呀。\": "No matter how small, what's others' is still others'."

用两只手把橡子还了回去。: It returned the acorn with both hands.
松鼠的心一下子轻松了许多。: The squirrel's heart felt much lighter.
\"还好在错还小的时候就还了。\": "Good thing I returned it while the mistake was still small."
两个又和好如初了。: The two made up as before.
那天晚上松鼠睡得很香。: That night, the squirrel slept soundly.
小的坏习惯要是放着不管。: If small bad habits are left unattended.
所以才说\"偷针的贼会变成偷牛的贼\"。: That's why they say, "A thief who steals needles becomes a thief who steals cows."
在小的时候马上改正，真了不起。: Correcting it early is truly admirable.
小朋友们诚实的心真可爱。: Children's honest hearts are truly adorable.
现在把肩膀的力气慢慢放松吧。: Now slowly relax the tension in your shoulders.
做错了很惭愧。: Feeling ashamed after doing something wrong.
叫\"하나를 보면 열을 안다（看到一件就知道十件）\"。: It's called "하나를 보면 열을 안다 (see one, know ten)".
意思是从一个小举动就能了解一个人。: It means you can understand a person from a small action.

把掉在路上的树枝清理干净。: It cleared away branches that had fallen on the path.
就算没人看，它也悄悄地做。: Even when no one was watching, it did it quietly.

猫头鹰只看到它清理一根树枝。: The owl only saw it clear one branch.
但仅凭这一点就明白了它的心。: But that alone was enough to understand its heart.

\"我想把重要的事交给你。\": "I want to entrust something important to you."

\"连小事你都用心呢。\": "You put care into even the smallest things."
宴席上刺猬招待着客人。: At the feast, the hedgehog hosted the guests.
\"果然见一就知十呀。\": "Indeed, seeing one thing tells you ten."
所以才说\"看到一件就知道十件\"。: That's why they say, "See one, know ten."
小朋友们的小小善意也闪闪发光。: Children's small acts of kindness also shine.

把事情交给别人。: Entrust a task to someone else.
窗外的星星一颗颗冒出来。: Stars pop out one by one outside the window.
钻进暖暖的被子里吧。: Let's snuggle into the warm blanket.
叫\"아니 땐 굴뚝에 연기 날까（没生火的烟囱哪会冒烟呢）\"。: It's called "아니 땐 굴뚝에 연기 날까 (How can smoke rise from a chimney without a fire?)".
意思是任何事情都一定有个缘由。: It means everything has a reason.

因为兔子会大大方方地来敲门啦。: Because the rabbit would come knocking openly now.

所以才说\"没生火的烟囱哪会冒烟呢\"。: That's why they say, "A chimney without a fire won't smoke."

温柔的夜空静静铺展开来。: The gentle night sky quietly spreads out.

意思是再好的东西，也得吃饱了才觉得开心。: It means even the best things are more enjoyable on a full stomach.
森林里聚了一群小动物。: A group of little animals gathered in the forest.
今天它们打算去看红叶。: Today they plan to go see the autumn leaves.
松鼠和兔子都很兴奋。: The squirrel and the rabbit are both excited.
\"快走吧！听说红叶很美呢。\": "Let's hurry! I heard the autumn leaves are beautiful."
可是它们没吃早饭就出来了。: But they left without eating breakfast.
走着山路，肚子就饿了。: Walking up the mountain path, they got hungry.
松鼠的腿一直发软。: The squirrel's legs kept feeling weak.
兔子无缘无故就烦躁起来。: The rabbit got irritable for no reason.
\"什么红叶不红叶的，我没力气啦。\": "Forget the leaves, I have no energy."
这时鼹鼠奶奶走了过来。: Just then, Grandma Mole came over.
还给每个倒了一杯热茶。: She also poured a cup of hot tea for each of them.
小动物们吃得饱饱的。: The little animals ate until they were full.
烦躁也不知不觉消失了。: The irritability also faded away without them noticing.
\"现在去看红叶吧！\": "Now let's go see the autumn leaves!"
爬上山顶，红叶漫山铺开。: Climbing to the top, the autumn leaves spread across the mountain.
整座山染成了红红黄黄。: The whole mountain was dyed in reds and yellows.
肚子饱了，风景看起来更美了。: With full stomachs, the scenery looked even more beautiful.
小动物们拍着手，高兴极了。: The little animals clapped their hands, overjoyed.
再好看的风景。: No matter how beautiful the scenery.
也得肚子实实的才玩得尽兴。: You can only enjoy it fully with a full stomach.
所以才说\"就算是金刚山，也要吃饱了再观赏\"。: That's why they say, "Even at Geumgangsan, eat first before sightseeing."
小朋友们也要好好吃饭、加油哦。: Kids, eat well and keep up the good work!
现在让肚子和心都踏踏实实地休息吧。: Now let both your stomach and heart rest peacefully.
吃了饭，肚子饱了。: After eating, your stomach is full.
今晚星星也密密地亮起来了。: Tonight the stars are shining densely too.
叫\"가는 날이 장날（去的那天正好是集市日）\"。: It's called "가는 날이 장날" (the day you go happens to be market day).
意思是特意去的那天，偏偏赶上了不平常的日子。: It means the day you specifically went turned out to be an unusual one.
森林里住着一只小獾。: A little badger lived in the forest.
小獾喜欢安静的池塘。: The little badger liked the quiet pond.
\"今天要一个人玩水啦。\": "Today I'm going to play in the water all by myself."
它带上便当去了池塘。: It brought a lunchbox and headed to the pond.
可是池塘边聚满了小动物。: But the pond was crowded with little animals.
偏偏赶上了打扫池塘的日子。: It just happened to be the day for cleaning the pond.
\"唉呀，我本想安安静静地玩呢。\": "Oh no, I wanted to play quietly."
小獾有点失望。: Little Badger felt a bit disappointed.
这时松鼠向它招手。: Just then, Squirrel waved at it.
大家一起把落叶捞了上来。: Together, they scooped up the fallen leaves.
挖出淤泥，捡走石头。: They dug out the mud and picked up the stones.
虽然累，可笑声不断。: It was tiring, but laughter never stopped.
水清得像镜子一样。: The water was as clear as a mirror.
大家拿出便当分着吃。: Everyone took out their lunchboxes and shared.
小獾的便当也一起分了。: Little Badger's lunchbox was shared too.
本想一个人吃的饭，更香了。: The meal meant to be eaten alone tasted even better.
本来盼着安静的一天。: It had hoped for a quiet day.
却成了意外开心的一天。: But it turned into an unexpectedly happy day.
打定主意的那天，也会变成特别的日子。: Even a day planned out can become something special.
所以才说\"去的那天正好是集市日\"。: That's why they say, "The day you go just happens to be market day."
小朋友们也试着享受意外的一天吧。: Kids, try to enjoy an unexpected day too.
池塘里有鱼。: There are fish in the pond.
偏偏今天下雨。: It just had to rain today.
从水里捞落叶。: Scoop fallen leaves out of the water.
夜晚像毯子一样温柔地盖下来。: The night fell gently like a blanket.
枕好枕头躺下吧。: Fluff your pillow and lie down.
叫\"티끌 모아 태산（积攒尘埃也能堆成大山）\"。: It's called "티끌 모아 태산 (even dust piled up becomes a mountain)."
意思是再小的东西，攒起来也会变大。: It means even the smallest things grow when you save them up.
森林里住着一只小蚂蚁。: A little ant lives in the forest.
蚂蚁正在准备过冬。: The ant is preparing for winter.
每天搬一粒小麦粒。: It carries one grain of wheat each day.
蚱蜢看到这情景笑了。: The grasshopper saw this and laughed.
\"那样一点点，什么时候才攒得完？\": "At that rate, when will you ever finish?"
一天一粒，又一粒。: One grain a day, and another.
麦粒一点点堆了起来。: The grains piled up little by little.
过了十天，攒了一把。: After ten days, it had gathered a handful.
过了一个月，堆成了小丘。: After a month, it piled up into a small mound.
蚂蚁擦着汗笑了。: The ant wiped its sweat and smiled.
\"尘埃攒起来也能这么大呢。\": "Even dust, when saved up, can get this big."
终于，白雪纷纷飘落。: Finally, white snow fell in flurries.
森林全被雪盖住了。: The whole forest was covered in snow.
蚱蜢一点吃的都没有。: The grasshopper had nothing to eat at all.
它饿着肚子来找蚂蚁。: It came to the ant, starving.
蚂蚁把仓库门大大打开。: The ant opened the warehouse door wide.
麦粒像大山一样堆得满满的。: Wheat grains were piled up like a big mountain.
\"这是一直攒的，一起吃吧。\": "This is what I've been saving. Let's eat together."
蚱蜢眼里含着泪。: Tears welled up in the grasshopper's eyes.
两个一起暖暖地过了冬。: The two spent the winter warmly together.
再小的东西，攒了又攒。: No matter how small, save and save again.
也会变得像山一样大、一样踏实。: It can become as big and solid as a mountain.
所以才说\"积攒尘埃也能堆成大山\"。: That's why they say, 'Saving dust can build a mountain.'
小朋友们也一点点积累起来吧。: Kids, let's also build up little by little.
蚂蚁排成队走。: The ants walk in a line.
捡起一粒麦子。: Pick up a grain of wheat.
仓库里有很多米。: The warehouse is full of rice.
石头堆得像大山。: Rocks piled up like a big mountain.
肚子饱饱的很踏实。: A full belly feels steady and grounded.
夜风轻轻叩着窗子。: The night breeze gently taps on the window.
把被子盖到肩膀。: Pull the blanket up to your shoulders.
意思是只知道狭小的地方，不懂外面广阔的世界。: It means knowing only a small place, unaware of the vast world outside.
深深的井里住着一只小青蛙。: A little frog lives in a deep well.
青蛙以为井就是整个世界。: The frog thinks the well is the whole world.
\"这口井最宽最棒啦。\": "This well is the widest and best!"
每天只仰望那圆圆的天。: Every day, it only looks up at the round sky.
有一天一只小鸟落在井边。: One day, a little bird lands by the well.
小鸟让青蛙趴在背上。: The bird lets the frog cling to its back.
扑棱棱飞出了井外。: With a flutter, it flies out of the well.
青蛙的眼睛瞪得圆圆的。: The frog's eyes go wide and round.
看见了辽阔的原野和高高的山。: It sees vast fields and tall mountains.
小鸟微微一笑说道。: The little bird smiled and said.
\"世界越了解就越宽广呢。\": "The more you learn about the world, the wider it becomes."
青蛙回到了井里。: The frog returned to the well.
但心却宽广了许多。: But its heart had grown much wider.
\"我要多看多学。\": "I want to see and learn more."
只看狭小的地方，就误以为懂了全世界。: Looking only at a narrow place, one mistakenly thinks they understand the whole world.
所以才说\"井里的青蛙\"。: That's why they say "a frog in a well."
小朋友们会遇见广阔的世界。: Children will encounter a vast world.
今天这一天也过得很好。: Today was a good day too.
把头靠在软软的枕头上。: Rest your head on a soft pillow.
叫\"호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다（提到老虎，老虎就来了）\"。: It's called "호랑이도 제 말 하면 온다 (speak of the tiger, and it appears)."
意思是正说着某人，那人恰好就来了。: It means when you're talking about someone, they happen to show up.
森林里住着一只小鹿。: A little deer lives in the forest.
好朋友松鼠去远方旅行了。: Its good friend, the squirrel, went on a trip far away.
小鹿非常想念松鼠。: The deer misses the squirrel very much.
它和朋友们聊起松鼠。: It talks about the squirrel with its friends.
\"就是那个爱吃橡子的小家伙吧？\": "That little one who loves acorns, right?"
大家想起松鼠都笑了。: Everyone smiles thinking about the squirrel.
\"什么时候回来呢？好想它。\": "When will it come back? I miss it so much."
\"真的？真神奇，正好赶上了。\": "Really? How amazing, I arrived just in time."
小鹿蹦过去抱住了松鼠。: The deer hopped over and hugged the squirrel.
\"好想你，一路顺利吗？\": "I missed you so much. Did the trip go well?"
松鼠讲起了旅行的故事。: The squirrel told stories of its travels.
朋友们聊到很晚，笑语不断。: The friends talked late into the night, full of laughter.
也许是思念传到了天上吧。: Maybe the longing reached the heavens.
正念叨的朋友恰好出现了。: The friend you're thinking of happens to appear.
想起某人时，常常就神奇地遇见了。: When you think of someone, you often magically run into them.
所以才说\"提到老虎，老虎就来了\"。: That's why they say, "Speak of the tiger, and it appears."
小朋友们也想想思念的人吧。: Kids, let's also think of someone you miss.
现在把心暖暖地裹起来。: Now wrap your heart up warmly.
星光轻轻洒在被子上。: Starlight gently falls on the blanket.
叫\"될성부른 나무는 떡잎부터 알아본다（会成材的树，从嫩芽就看得出来）\"。: It's called "될성부른 나무는 떡잎부터 알아본다 (A tree that will grow tall is known from its sprout)."
意思是有出息的孩子，从小就与众不同。: It means a child who will succeed stands out from a young age.
森林里住着一只小灰松鼠。: A little gray squirrel lives in the forest.
小灰松鼠身子很小。: The little gray squirrel is small.
每天早上清理掉在路上的树枝。: Every morning it clears fallen branches from the path.
没人吩咐，它也自己做。: It does this on its own, without being asked.
\"那孩子从小就与众不同呢。\": "That one has been special since it was young."
有一天森林里起了大火。: One day, a big fire broke out in the forest.
动物们慌慌张张乱作一团。: The animals panicked and ran around in chaos.
这时小灰松鼠沉着地喊道。: Then the little gray squirrel calmly called out.
它用小小的身子领着大家带路。: With its small body, it led the way for everyone.
动物们跟着小灰松鼠跑。: The animals followed the little gray squirrel.
多亏了它，大家都平安到了小溪。: Thanks to it, everyone safely reached the stream.
火势在水边停住了。: The fire stopped at the water's edge.
大家都松了口气。: Everyone breathed a sigh of relief.
猫头鹰走过来点了点头。: The owl came over and nodded.
\"你从小心就大呢。\": "You've had a big heart since you were little."
小灰松鼠害羞地低下了头。: The little gray squirrel shyly lowered its head.
\"我只是做了该做的事呀。\": "I just did what needed to be done."
那谦逊的心显得更可爱了。: That humble heart made it even more endearing.
心地善良的孩子。: A child with a kind heart.
从小那份光就闪闪发亮。: That light has been shining brightly since childhood.
所以才说\"会成材的树，从嫩芽就看得出来\"。: That's why they say, "A tree that will grow tall is visible from its sprout."
小朋友们美好的心也早就在发光啦。: The beautiful hearts of children are already shining bright.
灰松鼠爬树。: The gray squirrel climbs a tree.
窗外的月亮笑盈盈的。: The moon outside the window is smiling.
叫\"남의 떡이 더 커 보인다（别人的糕看起来更大）\"。: It's called "남의 떡이 더 커 보인다 (Other people's rice cakes look bigger)."
意思是别人的东西看起来比自己的好。: It means other people's things seem better than your own.
森林里住着一只小老鼠。: A little mouse lives in the forest.
小老鼠分到了一块黄奶酪。: The little mouse got a piece of yellow cheese.
邻居小老鼠也分到一块奶酪。: The neighbor mouse also got a piece of cheese.
可是邻居的奶酪看起来更大。: But the neighbor's cheese looked bigger.
自己的奶酪看着都不好吃了。: Even their own cheese didn't look appetizing anymore.
邻居小老鼠恰好也这么想。: The neighbor mouse happened to think the same.
两个决定换一换奶酪。: The two decided to swap cheese.
\"来，我们互相换着吃吧。\": "Here, let's trade and eat each other's."
可换过之后却觉得奇怪。: But after swapping, they felt something was off.
两块奶酪一样大。: The two pieces of cheese were the same size.
并排一放，真的一模一样。: Side by side, they were truly identical.
\"咦？本来就一样大嘛！\": "Huh? They were the same size all along!"
两个对望着哈哈大笑。: The two looked at each other and burst out laughing.
\"大概是隔着看才显得更大吧。\": "Maybe it looks bigger because we're seeing it from a distance."
小老鼠又把奶酪换了回来。: The little mouse swapped the cheese back again.
珍惜地捧起自己的奶酪。: Carefully held up its own cheese.
两个并排坐着香香地吃。: The two sat side by side, eating happily.
其实我自己的也一样珍贵。: But my own is just as precious.
所以才说\"别人的糕看起来更大\"。: That's why they say, "The other person's cake looks bigger."
小朋友们也珍惜自己拥有的吧。: Kids, cherish what you have too.
现在把两只手轻轻放在肚子上。: Now gently place both hands on your belly.
奶酪又黄又香。: The cheese is yellow and fragrant.
咬一口苹果。: Take a bite of an apple.
窗外的星星密密地升起来了。: The stars outside the window rose densely in the sky.
窝进暖暖的被子里吧。: Curl up in a warm blanket.
叫\"백 번 듣는 것이 한 번 보는 것만 못하다（听一百次不如亲眼看一次）\: It's called "백 번 듣는 것이 한 번 보는 것만 못하다 (Hearing it a hundred times is not as good as seeing it once)."
意思是听再多次，也不如亲眼看一次。: It means no matter how many times you hear it, it's not as good as seeing it once with your own eyes.
小鼹鼠一次也没见过大海。: The little mole has never seen the sea.
朋友们给它讲大海的故事。: His friends tell him stories about the sea.
\"大海无边无际地蓝，好宽呢。\": "The sea is endlessly blue and so wide."
\"海浪哗啦哗啦地涌过来呢。\": "The waves come rushing in with a splash."
小鼹鼠听了再多也想不出来。: No matter how much the little mole hears, he can't picture it.
最后它决定亲自去看。: Finally, he decides to see it for himself.
小鼹鼠踏上了地面上的长途旅行。: The little mole sets off on a long journey above ground.
终于，远处出现了大海。: Finally, the sea appears in the distance.
小鼹鼠愣在了原地。: The little mole stands frozen in place.
大海一直蓝到天边。: The sea stretches blue to the horizon.
咸咸的风拂过鼻尖。: The salty wind brushes past his nose.
小鼹鼠眼里泛起了泪。: Tears well up in the little mole's eyes.
\"听一百次都不知道是这样。\": "Hearing it a hundred times couldn't tell me this."
亲眼看到，心里满满的。: Seeing it with his own eyes fills his heart.
和海浪玩了好一会儿才回来。: He plays with the waves for a while before heading back.
它兴奋地讲给朋友们听。: He excitedly tells his friends all about it.
\"你们也一定要亲眼去看！\": "You must go see it with your own eyes too!"
光用话听再多。: No matter how much you hear it said.
也比不上亲眼看一次。: It's nothing compared to seeing it once with your own eyes.
所以才说\"听一百次不如亲眼看一次\"。: That's why they say, 'Hearing it a hundred times is not as good as seeing it once.'
小朋友们有一天也会遇见大海。: One day, you kids will also meet the sea.
现在闭上眼睛，想象海浪的声音吧。: Now close your eyes and imagine the sound of the waves.
鼹鼠挖土。: The mole digs in the earth.
大海又宽又蓝。: The sea is wide and blue.
风带着咸味。: The wind carries a salty taste.
心里满是激动。: My heart is filled with excitement.
把软软的被子盖到下巴。: Pull the soft blanket up to your chin.
今天也给你们讲最后一句老话。: Today, I'll tell you one last proverb.
叫\"웃는 낯에 침 못 뱉는다（对着笑脸吐不出唾沫）\"。: It's called '웃는 낯에 침 못 뱉는다 (You can't spit on a smiling face).'
意思是有人笑着走来，就没法对他发火。: It means if someone comes to you with a smile, you can't stay angry at them.
森林里住着一只小狐狸。: A little fox lives in the forest.
小狐狸总是笑盈盈的。: The little fox is always smiling.
森林里还住着一头暴躁的野猪。: A grumpy wild boar also lives in the forest.
野猪总是皱着脸。: The wild boar always had a frown on its face.
动物们都悄悄躲着野猪。: All the animals quietly avoided the wild boar.
可只有小狐狸每天都打招呼。: But only the little fox greeted it every day.
小狐狸总是笑得灿烂，挥着手。: The little fox always smiled brightly and waved.
野猪起初装作没听见。: At first, the wild boar pretended not to hear.
可小狐狸每天都对它笑。: But the little fox smiled at it every day.
过了几天，野猪也动摇了。: After a few days, the wild boar began to waver.
皱着的脸稍稍舒展了。: Its frowning face relaxed a little.
\"那狐狸为什么冲我笑呢？\": "Why does that fox smile at me?"
有一天小狐狸分给它糕点。: One day, the little fox shared its pastries with it.
野猪懵懵地接过了糕。: The wild boar took the pastry, dazed.
本想发火，却忍不住笑了。: It wanted to get angry but couldn't help smiling.
\"谢谢你对我这么好。\": "Thank you for being so kind to me."
野猪的声音变得很温柔。: The wild boar's voice became very gentle.
小狐狸紧紧握住野猪的手。: The little fox held the wild boar's hand tightly.
在温暖的笑脸面前。: In the face of a warm smile.
再暴躁的心也会慢慢融化。: Even the grumpiest heart slowly melts.
所以才说\"对着笑脸吐不出唾沫\"。: That's why they say, "You can't spit at a smiling face."
现在带着微笑闭上眼睛吧。: Now close your eyes with a smile.
野猪住在森林里。: Wild boars live in the forest.
皱（眉/脸）: to frown / to scrunch up (one's face)

欢迎来到深夜思辨咖啡馆，我是狐狸。: Welcome to the Late Night Thinking Café, I'm Fox.
今天我没准备咖啡，而是备了一杯甜米露。: Today I didn't prepare coffee, but a glass of sweet rice punch instead.
因为今天的主题正是汗蒸房。: Because today's theme is the jjimjilbang.
这是初到韩国的外国人觉得最新奇的场所之一。: It's one of the places foreigners new to Korea find most fascinating.
因为它把澡堂、桑拿和休息室全揉在了一处。: Because it combines a bathhouse, sauna, and lounge all in one.
有意思的是，汗蒸房绝不只是个洗澡的地方。: Interestingly, a jjimjilbang is far more than just a place to wash up.
它更接近一家人一起过夜的歇脚处。: It's more like a resting spot where families can stay overnight together.
把毛巾叠成羊角头的样子戴着，也是一种文化。: Wearing a towel folded into horn shapes is also part of the culture.
其实那本是用一条毛巾固定头发的实用智慧。: Actually, it started as the practical wisdom of using a towel to keep hair in place.
可不知不觉，它竟成了汗蒸房的标志性形象。: But before anyone knew it, it became the iconic image of the jjimjilbang.
还有麦饭石烤蛋配甜米露那种组合呢。: And there's the combo of elvan-roasted eggs with sweet rice punch.
