-을/ㄹ 뿐 表示\"只是/仅仅\"，后面通常接否定或说明。\\n-을/ㄹ 뿐이: -을/ㄹ 뿐 means "just/only," usually followed by a negation or explanation. \n-을/ㄹ 뿐이다 as a predicate expresses "it's just...that's all," often carrying a humble, resigned, or limiting tone. \nCommon in both speech and writing—used in K-drama lines and formal settings alike.
表达愿望和期望的两种核心句型: Two core patterns for expressing wishes and hopes
-(으)면 좋겠다 表示\"要是……就好了\"，用于表达个人希望或遗憾。\\n-: -(으)면 좋겠다 means "I wish..." and is used to express personal hopes or regrets. \n-기(를) 바라다 means "hope/expect..." and is more formal than 좋겠다, often used in letters, well-wishes, or formal settings. \nBoth express hope, but they differ clearly in tone and usage.
表达\"在考虑是否……\"和\"打算/有意……\"的两种意向句型: Two patterns for expressing "considering whether..." and "planning/intending to..."
-을/ㄹ까 생각하다 表示正在考虑要不要做某事，尚未决定，语气较犹豫。\\n-을: -을/ㄹ까 생각하다 means considering whether to do something, not yet decided, with a hesitant tone. \n-을/ㄹ 생각이다 means having a plan or intention, more certain than 생각하다. \nBoth are more colloquial and everyday than -겠다 or -(으)려고 하다.
表达\"同时进行\"和\"为了……目的\"的两类句型: Two types of patterns for "doing simultaneously" and "for the purpose of..."
-(으)면서 表示两个动作同时发生，主语相同。\\n-기 위해서 表示为了做某事:
-(으)면서 means two actions happen simultaneously with the same subject. 
-기 위해서 means "in order to do something" (purpose), attached to verbs. 
을/를 위해서 means "for someone/something" (object), attached to nouns. 
All three are core grammar for expressing purpose and parallel actions.
精确表达\"从……中\"选择、\"在……时候\"发生的场所与时间助词: Precisely expressing "selecting from..." and the place/time particles for "when..."
에서 在此课中重点学习\"在……范围内\"的用法（选择范围）。\\n중에서 表示:
에서 in this lesson focuses on the usage of "within..." (selection range). 
중에서 means "among..." and is used to select from a group. 
때 means "when..." and marks a specific point or period of time. 
All three are deeper uses of previously learned particles, requiring attention to detail.
表达\"尽管如此\"和\"然而\"的两种转折连接词: Two contrastive connectives for "even so" and "however"
그래도 表示\"即使这样/尽管如此\"，前后形成让步转折，口语和书面都常用。\\: 그래도 means "even so/despite that," forming a concessive contrast, common in both speech and writing. \n그러나 means "however/but," a more formal written connective, more formal than 그런데/하지만. \nBoth connect two sentences, but they differ in tone and usage.
区分\"持续状态\"和\"持续动作\"的两种进行体: Two progressive aspects distinguishing "continuing state" vs. "continuing action"
-고 있다 表示动作正在持续进行（动作进行中）。\\n-아/어/여 있다 表示动: -고 있다 means an action is ongoing (in progress). \n-아/어/여 있다 means a state continues after an action is completed (result state). \nBoth can be translated as "-ing" in Chinese, but Korean distinguishes them clearly—one of the most confusing grammar points for intermediate learners.
表达\"提前做好并保持\"的两种结果保持句型: Two patterns for "doing in advance and keeping" the result
-아/어/여 두다 表示做某事后保持那个状态，强调\"留着备用/留着以后用\"。: -아/어/여 두다 means doing something and keeping that state, emphasizing "keep it for later use." \n-아/어/여 놓다 means finishing and leaving the result there, emphasizing "done and left there," similar to 두다 but with a slightly different focus. \nThey're often interchangeable in daily conversation, with 놓다 more common in speech.
表示\"地方/处所\"的三种依存名词，各有细微差别: Three dependent nouns for "place/location," each with subtle differences
곳 是表示具体地点的依存名词，较正式。\\n데 是口语化的\"地方/处\"，也可:
곳 is a dependent noun for a specific place, more formal. 
데 is the colloquial "place/spot," also used for situations or aspects. 
군데 means "several places/points," often used with numbers. 
All three are similar in meaning, but differ in usage and collocations.
区分\"这/那/那\"三种指示代词的精确用法: Learn the precise usage of the three demonstrative pronouns: 'this/that/that'
이 指离说话人近的事物或刚提到的内容。\\n저 指离说话人和听话人都远的事物。\:
이 refers to something close to the speaker or just mentioned.
저 refers to something far from both speaker and listener.
그 refers to something close to the listener, or known to both, and also refers back to previously mentioned content.
These three are the core of the Korean demonstrative system, essential in everyday conversation.
P10 全部语法点综合复习: P10 Comprehensive Review of All Grammar Points
本课汇总 P10（第1–10课）所有语法点，通过情景对话和替换练习巩固掌握。: This lesson summarizes all grammar points from P10 (Lessons 1–10), reinforcing them through situational dialogues and substitution drills.
间接引语是把别人的话或自己之前说的话转述出来的语法结构。陈述句间接引语根据谓词类: Indirect speech is a grammatical structure used to report what someone else said or what you said earlier. Declarative indirect speech has four forms based on the predicate type, all ending with -고 하다.\nIn spoken Korean, -고 하다 often shortens to -고 해요, and even more colloquially to -대요.
动词：词干 + -는다고/ㄴ다고 하다\\n形容词：词干 + -다고 하다\\n:
Verbs: stem + -는다고/ㄴ다고 하다
Adjectives: stem + -다고 하다
Noun predicates: noun + -(이)라고 하다
Past tense (all): -았/었다고 하다
时态由被引语句本身决定：现在/过去/将来 均可出现。\\n口语缩略：-는다고 해: Tense is determined by the quoted clause itself: present/past/future all possible.\nSpoken contractions: -는다고 해요 → -는대요, -다고 해요 → -대요, -(이)라고 해요 → -(이)래요.
陈述句间接引语形式总览: Overview of Declarative Indirect Speech Forms
疑问句间接引语把别人提问的内容转述出来，根据谓词类型有不同接续形式，统一用 -냐: Interrogative indirect speech reports the content of someone's question, with different endings based on predicate type, all ending with -냐고 하다.\nIn spoken Korean, -는지/은지/인지 is often used instead of -냐고, pairing more naturally with 알다/모르다.\nWhen the question contains a question word (뭐/어디/왜/언제/어떻게), it stays in the quoted clause.
动词：词干 + -느냐고/-냐고 하다\\n形容词：词干 + -(으)냐고 하다:
Verbs: stem + -느냐고/-냐고 하다
Adjectives: stem + -(으)냐고 하다
Noun predicates: noun + -(이)냐고 하다
Past tense: -았/었냐고 하다
口语 -냐고 比 -느냐고 更常用。\\n与 알다/모르다 搭配时用 -는지/-: In speech, -냐고 is more common than -느냐고.\nWith 알다/모르다, use -는지/-은지/-인지 instead of -냐고.
疑问句间接引语形式总览: Overview of Interrogative Indirect Speech Forms
转述\"叫人做某事\"或\"叫人一起做某事\": Reporting "telling someone to do something" or "suggesting doing something together"
命令句间接引语用 -(으)라고 하다 转述别人的命令或请求。\\n共动句间接引语: Imperative indirect speech uses -(으)라고 하다 to report someone's command or request.\nPropositive indirect speech uses -자고 하다 to report someone's invitation or suggestion to do something together.\nBoth forms are fixed and do not distinguish whether the verb stem ends in a consonant.
命令句：动词词干 + -(으)라고 하다\\n共动句：动词词干 + -자고 하다: Imperative: verb stem + -(으)라고 하다\nPropositive: verb stem + -자고 하다\nNegative imperative: -지 말라고 하다
-(으)라고 的으 在有收音词干后加，无收音词干直接 -라고。\\n-자고 형태: For -(으)라고, add 으 after stems ending in a consonant; stems without a consonant take -라고 directly.\n-자고 is fixed and does not change.\n하다 itself: 해라체 → 하라고, 하자체 → 하자고.
表示\"因为……所以……\"和\"一……就发现……\": Expressing "because... so..." and "as soon as... I found..."
-(으)니까 表示原因或理由，比 -아/어서 更强调说话人的主观判断，后句可以接: -(으)니까 expresses cause or reason, emphasizing the speaker's subjective judgment more than -아/어서, and can be followed by commands, suggestions, or invitations.\n-(으)니 is a shortened form of -(으)니까, often used in speech or to connect a following statement.\n-아/어/여 보니까 means "after doing something, I found/realized," emphasizing a discovery from firsthand experience.
-(으)니까：有收音+으니까，无收音+니까\\n-(으)니：有收音+으니，无收音: -(으)니까: with final consonant + 으니까, without + 니까\n-(으)니: with final consonant + 으니, without + 니\n-아/어/여 보니까: verb + 아/어/여 보니까
-(으)니까 后面可以接命令（-세요）、提议（-ㅂ시다）等，-아/어서 不可以。: -(으)니까 can be followed by commands (-세요), suggestions (-ㅂ시다), etc., but -아/어서 cannot.\n-아/어/여 보니까 emphasizes a new discovery after doing something firsthand, and the subject is usually the same before and after.
(으)로 유명하다 表示某人或某地\"以某事物著名\"，로 后接名词。\\n-기: (으)로 유명하다 means someone or somewhere is "famous for something," with 로 attached to a noun. \n-기로 유명하다 means someone or somewhere is "famous for doing something," with 기로 attached to the nominalized verb form. \n이/가 되다 means "to become..." and is the core expression for describing changes in identity or state.
(으)로 유명하다：名词 + (으)로 유명하다\\n-기로 유명하다：动词词干: (으)로 유명하다: noun + (으)로 유명하다\n-기로 유명하다: verb stem + 기로 유명하다\n이/가 되다: noun + 이/가 되다
(으)로：名词有收音 + 으로，无收音/ㄹ结尾 + 로。\\n이/가 되다 中: (으)로: noun with final consonant + 으로, without final consonant or ending in ㄹ + 로. \nIn 이/가 되다, 되다 itself can change tense: 돼요/됐어요/될 거예요. \nThe noun before 이/가 되다 takes 이 (with final consonant) or 가 (without).
表示\"值得做某事\"和\"最好做某事\": Expressing "worth doing" and "it's best to do"
-을/ㄹ 만하다 表示某事值得做、有意义，相当于\"值得……\"。\\n-는 게: -을/ㄹ 만하다 means something is worth doing or meaningful, equivalent to "worth..." \n-는 게 좋겠다 expresses the speaker's suggestion or gentle advice, equivalent to "it's best to..." or "it might be better to...", and is more polite than -(으)세요.
-을/ㄹ 만하다：动词 词干 + -을/ㄹ 만하다\\n-는 게 좋겠다：动词: -을/ㄹ 만하다: verb stem + -을/ㄹ 만하다\n-는 게 좋겠다: verb stem + -는 게 좋겠다
-을/ㄹ 만하다 中 만 是依存名词\"价值\"，前用冠词形 -을/ㄹ。\\n-: In -을/ㄹ 만하다, 만 is a dependent noun meaning "value," preceded by the adnominal form -을/ㄹ. \n-는 게 좋겠다 is more polite and suggestive than -는 게 좋아요. 겠 expresses the speaker's subjective judgment.
-을/ㄹ 만하다 可与 -아/어 보다 结合：-아/어 볼 만하다: -을/ㄹ 만하다 can combine with -아/어 보다: -아/어 볼 만하다
与 보다 结合时形式是 -아/어 볼 만하다，보다 不能省略。: When combined with 보다, the form is -아/어 볼 만하다, and 보다 cannot be omitted.
아니면 是连接两个句子或词组的\"或者\"，用于提供另一个选项。\\n(이)나: 아니면 is "or" that connects two sentences or phrases, used to offer another option. \n(이)나 attaches to nouns, meaning "...or...", and can also convey a sense of "at least." \n-거나 attaches to verbs/adjectives, connecting two equal options, meaning "either one is fine."
아니면：独立连接词，接在句子或名词组后\\n(이)나：名词 + (이)나（有收音: 아니면: independent connector, follows sentences or noun phrases\n(이)나: noun + (이)나 (with final consonant + 이나, without + 나)\n-거나: verb/adjective stem + -거나
아니면 用于句子之间，(이)나 接名词，-거나 接用言（动词/形容词）。\\n(: 아니면 is used between sentences, (이)나 attaches to nouns, and -거나 attaches to predicates (verbs/adjectives). \n(이)나 also means "approximately/at least" besides "or": 시간이 한 시간이나 걸려요 (it takes a whole hour).
-아/어/여 보이다 表示根据外表或视觉印象判断\"看起来……\"，主要接形容词: -아/어/여 보이다 means "looks..." based on appearance or visual impression, mainly used with adjectives. \n-나 보다 means "seems like.../appears..." based on some evidence, used for conclusions the speaker infers. \n-는/은/ㄴ 가 보다 is similar in meaning to -나 보다 but slightly different in form.
-아/어/여 보이다：形容词 词干 + -아/어/여 보이다\\n-나 보다：动: -아/어/여 보이다: adjective stem + -아/어/여 보이다\n-나 보다: verb stem + -나 보다, adjective stem + -(으)나 보다\n-는/은/ㄴ 가 보다: verb -는 가 보다, adjective -은/ㄴ 가 보다
-아/어/여 보이다 主要与形容词结合，与动词结合较少见。\\n-나 보다 与: -아/어/여 보이다 mainly combines with adjectives, rarely with verbs. \n-나 보다 and -(으)ㄴ가 보다 are almost identical in meaning and interchangeable, with the latter being slightly more formal. \nBoth expressions indicate speculation that hasn't been directly confirmed.
综合练习 P11——间接引语与进阶表达: Comprehensive Practice P11 — Indirect Speech and Advanced Expressions
本章围绕间接引语展开：陈述句（-는다고/-다고/-(이)라고 하다）、疑问句（-: This chapter focuses on indirect speech: declarative (-는다고/-다고/-(이)라고 하다), interrogative (-(느)냐고 하다), imperative (-(으)라고 하다), and propositive (-자고 하다) forms, along with advanced expressions -(으)니까, -아/어 보니까, (으)로 유명하다, 이/가 되다, -을/ㄹ 만하다, -는 게 좋겠다, 아니면/(이)나/-거나, -아/어 보이다/-나 보다.
表示\"我会……所以你……\"和\"不管……都……\": Expressing "I'll... so you..." and "no matter... it's all..."
-을/ㄹ 테니까 表示说话人自己的意图或推测作为前提，让对方据此采取行动，相当于: -을/ㄹ 테니까 expresses the speaker's intention or guess as a premise for the other person to act on, equivalent to "I'll..., so you..." \n-(이)든지 means "either one is fine," similar to -거나 but emphasizing that any case is acceptable, often followed by 괜찮다/좋다/상관없다.
-을/ㄹ 테니까：动词 词干 + -을/ㄹ 테니까（有收音+을，无收音/ㄹ+ㄹ）: -을/ㄹ 테니까: verb stem + -을/ㄹ 테니까 (with final consonant + 을, without/ㄹ + ㄹ)\n-(이)든지: noun + (이)든지, verb + -든지
-을/ㄹ 테니까 的 테 来源于表意志/推测的依存名词 터 的冠词形，表意志时主: -을/ㄹ 테니까 comes from the adnominal form of the dependent noun 터, which indicates intention or conjecture. When expressing intention, the subject must be first person (나/우리). When expressing conjecture, there is no such restriction.\n-(이)든지 when listing two or more: A든지 B든지 form.
表示\"打算做某事\"和\"去/来做某事\": Expressing "intending to do something" and "going/coming to do something"
-(으)려고 하다 表示打算或意图，相当于\"打算……/想要……\"，强调说话人: -(으)려고 하다 expresses intention or plan, equivalent to "intend to.../want to...", emphasizing the speaker's subjective intention.\n-(으)려고 가다/오다 expresses going/coming for a purpose, equivalent to "go/come to do...".\nBoth use -(으)려고 as the first part, but differ in the following verb.
-(으)려고：有收音词干 + -으려고，无收音/ㄹ词干 + -려고\\n-(으): -(으)려고: stem with final consonant + -으려고, stem without final consonant or with ㄹ + -려고\n-(으)려고 하다: intend to...\n-(으)려고 가다/오다: go/come to do...
-(으)려고 하다 的主语通常是有意志的人（나/우리/그 사람 등）。\\n-(: The subject of -(으)려고 하다 is usually a person with intention (나/우리/그 사람 etc.).\n-(으)려고 가다/오다 expresses purpose, paired with movement verbs 가다/오다.\n-러 가다/오다 has the same meaning, but -(으)려고 가다/오다 is more intentional.
表示\"原本打算……\"和\"你当时为何不……\": Expressing "originally intended to..." and "why didn't you... then"
-(으)려고 했다 表示原本有某个意图但最终未实现，相当于\"本来打算……的\": -(으)려고 했다 expresses that there was an intention but it was not ultimately realized, equivalent to "had intended to...", implying it wasn't done.\n-지 그랬어(요)? expresses the speaker suggesting that the listener should have done something at that time, with a slight tone of regret or reproach, equivalent to "Why didn't you... then?"\nThey often appear together: stating the original plan → the other gives advice or regret.
-(으)려고 했다：动词 词干 + -(으)려고 했다（有收音+으려고，无收音/: -(으)려고 했다: verb stem + -(으)려고 했다 (with final consonant + 으려고, without final consonant or with ㄹ + 려고)\n-지 그랬어(요)?: verb stem + -지 그랬어요? (all stems directly + 지, fixed form)
-(으)려고 했다 过去形表示意图未实现，若接 -는데 更自然：가려고 했는데: The past form -(으)려고 했다 indicates an unrealized intention; it's more natural with -는데: 가려고 했는데 못 갔어요.\nIn -지 그랬어(요)?, 그랬어요 is the past form of 그러다, literally "why didn't you do that?"\nBoth forms carry a tone of regret/remorse.
表示\"一举两得\"和\"趁着……顺便……\": Expressing "killing two birds with one stone" and "while at it, ..."
겸 连接两个名词，表示同时兼顾两个目的或功能，相当于\"既……又……／兼……\": 겸 connects two nouns, indicating simultaneously serving two purposes or functions, equivalent to "both... and.../兼...".\n-은/ㄴ 김에 attaches to the past adnominal form, meaning to take the opportunity of something already done or ongoing to do another thing, equivalent to "while at it, ...".\nBoth convey a "two birds with one stone" nuance; 겸 emphasizes parallel purposes, -은/ㄴ 김에 emphasizes seizing the opportunity.
겸：名词 + 겸 + 名词（两个名词之间）\\n-은/ㄴ 김에：动词 过去冠词形: 겸: noun + 겸 + noun (between two nouns)\n-은/ㄴ 김에: verb past adnominal form + 김에 (stem with final consonant + -은 김에, stem without final consonant + -ㄴ 김에)
겸 只与名词结合，不能直接附加在动词上。\\n-은/ㄴ 김에 的 김 是表示\": 겸 only combines with nouns, cannot directly attach to verbs.\nIn -은/ㄴ 김에, 김 is a dependent noun meaning "opportunity/timing". Mainly used to suggest an additional action based on an already occurring action.\n-는 김에 (present progressive) is also possible: 청소하는 김에 정리도 해요.
表示金额量词：价值分量、面值规格和单价: Expressing amount quantifiers: value/quantity, denomination/specification, and unit price
(어)치 接在金额后面，表示\"该金额相应的价值/分量\"，相当于\"……价值的: (어)치 attaches after an amount, meaning "the value/quantity corresponding to that amount", equivalent to "...worth of / ...won worth of".\n짜리 attaches after a quantity or amount, meaning "a thing of that unit or specification", mainly used for currency units or sizes.\n에 for price uses the form "...에 팔다/사다", expressing unit price or total.
(어)치：金额（数字+单位）+ 어치（标准形，不论收音有无均用 어치）\\n짜리: (어)치: amount (number+unit) + 어치 (standard form, always 어치 regardless of final consonant)\n짜리: number+unit + 짜리 (expressing size, denomination, specification)\n에: amount + 에 (～에 사다/팔다, indicating price)
(어)치 通常写作 어치，不论收音有无均用 어치 较自然：만 원어치，오천 원어: (어)치 is usually written as 어치, and it's natural to use 어치 regardless of final consonant: 만 원어치, 오천 원어치.\n짜리 can also be used for size or capacity besides currency units: 100ml 짜리, 3인분짜리.\n에 as a particle is also used to ask price: "얼마에 샀어요?" (How much did you buy it for?).
ㄹ词干动词/形容词在特定词尾前ㄹ脱落的规则: Rule of ㄹ deletion for ㄹ-stem verbs/adjectives before certain endings
以 ㄹ 收音结尾的动词/形容词（ㄹ词干）在某些词尾前 ㄹ 会脱落。\\nㄹ 脱落: Verbs/adjectives ending in ㄹ (ㄹ-stems) drop the ㄹ before certain endings.\nㄹ deletion condition: when the ending starts with ㄴ, ㅂ, 시, 오 (mnemonic: 나비시오).\nㄹ retention condition: when the ending starts with 아/어, 고, 지, 면, 도, etc.
ㄹ脱落：ㄹ词干 + -(으)ㄴ/-(으)ㄹ（除将来冠词形）/ -ㅂ니다/-습니다: ㄹ deletion: ㄹ-stem + -(으)ㄴ/-(으)ㄹ (except future adnominal) / -ㅂ니다/-습니다 / -(으)세요 / -(으)오\nㄹ retention: ㄹ-stem + -아/어요 / -고 / -지 / -(으)면 / -아/어도 etc.\nNote: ㄹ drops in past adnominal -(으)ㄴ; but retained in future adnominal -(으)ㄹ
记忆法（나비시오）：以 ㄴ 开头的词尾、以 ㅂ 开头的词尾、以 시 开头的词尾、:
Mnemonic (나비시오): ㄹ drops before endings starting with ㄴ, ㅂ, 시, or 오.
알다 (to know): 알아요 (know) / 아세요 (do you know/please know) / 압니다 (know) / 아는 (knowing)
살다 (to live): 살아요 (live) / 사세요 (please live) / 삽니다 (live) / 사는 (living)
만들다 (to make): 만들어요 (make) / 만드세요 (please make) / 만듭니다 (make) / 만드는 (making)
ㅎ词干形容词在元音词尾前 ㅎ 脱落并发生元音缩约: ㅎ-stem adjectives drop ㅎ before vowel endings and undergo vowel contraction
以 ㅎ 收音结尾的形容词（ㅎ词干）在以元音开头的词尾前 ㅎ 脱落，并发生元音缩约: Adjectives ending in ㅎ (ㅎ-stems) drop ㅎ before vowel-initial endings and undergo vowel contraction.\nTypical ㅎ-irregular adjectives: 빨갛다 (red), 파랗다 (blue), 노랗다 (yellow), 하얗다 (white), 까맣다 (black), 어떻다 (how), 이렇다 (like this), 그렇다 (like that), 저렇다 (like that/over there).\nBefore consonant-initial endings (-고, -지, -면), ㅎ is retained.
ㅎ脱落：ㅎ词干 + -아/어요 → ㅎ脱落后与前元音缩约（ㅏ/ㅓ→ㅐ）\\n冠词: ㅎ drop: ㅎ-stem + -아/어요 → ㅎ drops and contracts with the preceding vowel (ㅏ/ㅓ→ㅐ)\nAdnominal form: ㅎ-stem + -(으)ㄴ → ㅎ drops (빨간, 파란, 어떤, 그런, 이런)\nㅎ retained: ㅎ-stem + -고/-지/-면/-다 → unchanged (빨갛고, 어떻지, 그렇다면)
元音缩约规则：ㅎ脱落后 前元音 ㅏ/ㅓ + 词尾 아/어 → 缩约为 ㅐ。\\n:
Vowel contraction rule: after ㅎ drops, preceding vowel ㅏ/ㅓ + ending 아/어 → contracts to ㅐ.
빨갛다 (ㅏ) + 아요 → 빨가+아요 → 빨개요
파랗다 (ㅏ) + 아요 → 파라+아요 → 파래요
어떻다 (ㅓ) + 어요 → 어떠+어요 → 어때요
그렇다 (ㅓ) + 어요 → 그러+어요 → 그래요
하얗다 exception: 하얗다 + 아요 → 하얘요 (ㅑ+아→ㅒ contraction)
复习 P12 所有语法点：-을/ㄹ 테니까，-(이)든지，-(으)려고 하다/가: Review all P12 grammar points: -을/ㄹ 테니까, -(이)든지, -(으)려고 하다/가다/오다, -(으)려고 했다, -지 그랬어요?, 겸, -은/ㄴ 김에, (어)치, 짜리, 에, ㄹ irregular, ㅎ irregular.
韩语被动的核心方式之一：在动词词干后加入被动接尾 -이-/-히-/-리-/-기-: One of the core ways to form the passive in Korean: add the passive suffix -이-/-히-/-리-/-기- to the verb stem. This lesson covers the -이- and -히- groups first: 보다→보이다, 잡다→잡히다. Learn high-frequency short-form passive verbs like "be seen / be caught / be heard."
动词词干 + -이/히- + 语尾｜特定动词各自属于哪个接尾需记忆: Verb stem + -이/히- + ending｜Which suffix a verb takes must be memorized
-이- 类：보다→보이다、쓰다→쓰이다、바꾸다→바뀌다｜-히- 类：잡다→잡히다: -이- group: 보다→보이다, 쓰다→쓰이다, 바꾸다→바뀌다｜-히- group: 잡다→잡히다, 먹다→먹히다, 읽다→읽히다
短形被动的另外两组：-리- 和 -기-。-리- 类：듣다→들리다、팔다→팔리다、: The other two groups of short-form passive: -리- and -기-. -리- group: 듣다→들리다, 팔다→팔리다, 열다→열리다; -기- group: 안다→안기다, 쫓다→쫓기다, 빼앗다→빼앗기다. Which group a verb belongs to must be learned from the memorization table.
词干 + -리/기- + 语尾｜属于哪个接尾按动词固定: Stem + -리/기- + ending｜Which suffix is used is fixed per verb
-리-类：듣→들리다、팔→팔리다、열→열리다、풀→풀리다｜-기-类：안→안기다、: -리- group: 듣→들리다, 팔→팔리다, 열→열리다, 풀→풀리다｜-기- group: 안→안기다, 쫓→쫓기다, 빼앗→빼앗기다, 씻→씻기다
「-아/어지다」是另一种韩语被动化方式：贴在任意及物动词或形容词后。相比 -이/: '-아/어지다' is another way to form the passive in Korean: attach it to any transitive verb or adjective. Compared to -이/히/리/기 (one verb takes one fixed suffix), -아/어지다 is grammatically more general. It emphasizes "the result of a change" or "happening involuntarily."
动词/形容词词干 + -아/어지다｜阳性 -아지다, 阴性 -어지다, 하다 →: Verb/adjective stem + -아/어지다｜Positive vowel -아지다, negative vowel -어지다, 하다 → 해지다
-이/히/리/기 是被动接尾（固定动词），-아/어지다 是被动化后缀（任意动词/: -이/히/리/기 are passive suffixes (fixed verbs), -아/어지다 is a passive-forming suffix (any verb/adjective)
「-게 되다」表示\"因某种外因/自然发展变成了……的状态\"\"不是自愿地……: '-게 되다' means 'came to be in a state due to some external cause or natural development' or 'not voluntarily...'. Though covered under the passive voice section, its actual meaning leans toward 'naturally/forcedly entering a state' and is a key way Korean softly expresses 'decisions/changes.'
不看받침；表述\"外因导致\"\"不由自主\"的变化；常与 决定/邂逅/结局 类: No batchim check; expresses changes caused by external factors or beyond one's control; often pairs with contexts of decisions, encounters, or outcomes
「하다」结尾的动词无法直接加 -이/히/리/기 变被动。它们靠 하다 → 되다: Verbs ending in '하다' cannot directly take -이/히/리/기 to become passive. Instead, they change 하다 → 되다: 공부하다 → 공부되다, 결정하다 → 결정되다, 발견하다 → 발견되다. This is the largest passive group in Korean.
汉字词/N + 하다 → 汉字词/N + 되다: Sino-Korean word/N + 하다 → Sino-Korean word/N + 되다
하다 类动词 → 直接把 하다 换成 되다｜其他动词需用 -이/히- 或 -아/: 하다-type verbs → simply replace 하다 with 되다 | Other verbs need -이/히- or -아/어지다
「당하다」表示\"遭受（不好的事）\"，「받다」表示\"接受（中性或好的事）\": '당하다' means 'to suffer (something bad),' and '받다' means 'to receive (something neutral or good).' These are emotionally colored passive forms in Korean: semantically passive, but grammatically active structures. They emphasize the impact on the person.
汉字词 + 당하다（负面）/ 汉字词 + 받다（中性/正面）: Sino-Korean word + 당하다 (negative) / Sino-Korean word + 받다 (neutral/positive)
당하다=遭受（受害）；받다=接受（中性/受益）；两者语法都是主动动词形式: 당하다 = to suffer (victimized); 받다 = to receive (neutral/beneficial); both are grammatically active verb forms
被动句助词 이/가 · 에게 · 에 의해: Passive Sentence Particles 이/가 · 에게 · 에 의해
被动句的核心不在动词，而在助词。受动者做主语用 이/가；施动者根据身份用 에게（: The core of a passive sentence isn't the verb—it's the particles. The patient as subject takes 이/가; the agent takes 에게 (people/animals), 에 (things/natural forces), or 에 의해 (formal writing) depending on what it is. This lesson systematically organizes particle choice in passive sentences.
受动者 + 이/가 + 施动者 + 에게/에/에 의해 + 被动动词: Recipient + 이/가 + Agent + 에게/에/에 의해 + Passive Verb
人/动物施动 → 에게；物/自然力 → 에；正式书面 → 에 의해: People/animals as agent → 에게; objects/natural forces → 에; formal writing → 에 의해
\"双重被动\"是韩语学习者常犯的错误：把已经含被动语义的词再叠加 -아/어지다: "Double passive" is a common mistake among Korean learners: adding -아/어지다 to words that already have passive meaning, like 되어지다, 보여지다, 잊혀지다. Standard written Korean requires a single passive layer; however, 잊혀지다 is accepted as a fixed exception.
되다 + 어지다 = 되어지다 → 避免；보이다 + 어지다 = 보여지다 →: 되다 + 어지다 = 되어지다 → avoid; 보이다 + 어지다 = 보여지다 → avoid; 잊히다 + 어지다 = 잊혀지다 → acceptable as idiom
本课综合 P13 全部 8 个被动语法点：短形被动（-이/히/리/기）、-아/어: This lesson covers all 8 passive grammar points from P13: short-form passive (-이/히/리/기), -아/어지다, -게 되다, 되다, 당하다/받다/맞다, particle selection, and double passive distinction. Tests overall passive sensitivity.
韩语使动的核心方式之一：动词词干加使动接尾 -이-/-히-/-리-/-기-。使动: One of the core ways to form causatives in Korean: adding the causative suffix -이-/-히-/-리-/-기- to the verb stem. Causative means "make A do B." This lesson covers the common rules for the four groups -이-/-히-/-리-/-기-. Which verb belongs to which group must be memorized.
动词词干 + -이/히/리/기- + 语尾｜句式：S가 O를 V-이/히-（S: Verb stem + -이/히/리/기- + ending | Pattern: S가 O를 V-이/히- (S makes O do V)
-이-：보다→보이다（给看）｜-히-：읽다→읽히다（让读）｜-리-：울다→울리다: -이-: 보다→보이다 (show) | -히-: 읽다→읽히다 (make read) | -리-: 울다→울리다 (make cry) | -기-: 웃다→웃기다 (make laugh)
短形使动的另外三组接尾：-우-/-구-/-추-。-우- 是最常见的，如 자다→재: The other three causative suffixes: -우-/-구-/-추-. -우- is the most common, e.g., 자다→재우다 (put to sleep), 타다→태우다 (give a ride); -구- is rare, e.g., 솟다→솟구다; -추- includes 낮다→낮추다 (lower), 늦다→늦추다 (delay).
-우-：자다→재우다、타다→태우다、깨다→깨우다、서다→세우다｜-추-：낮다→낮: -우-: 자다→재우다, 타다→태우다, 깨다→깨우다, 서다→세우다 | -추-: 낮다→낮추다, 늦다→늦추다, 맞다→맞추다 | -구-: 솟다→솟구다 (rare)
「-게 하다」是韩语最通用的使动表达：\"让 A 做 B\"\"使 A 变得……: '-게 하다' is Korean's most versatile causative expression: 'make A do B' or 'make A become...'. It can attach to any verb/adjective, regardless of 받침. Compared to short-form causatives (which require memorizing words), -게 하다 is a universal formula.
动词/形容词词干 + -게 하다｜句式：S가 O를 V-게 하다: Verb/Adjective stem + -게 하다 | Pattern: S가 O를 V-게 하다
不看받침；可接任意动词/形容词；比短形使动更委婉、更客观: Ignores 받침; works with any verb/adjective; more euphemistic and objective than short-form causatives
「-도록 하다」和 -게 하다 类似，都表\"让/使\"，但语气更书面、更正式，: '-도록 하다' is similar to -게 하다, both meaning 'make/let', but it's more written and formal, carrying a sense of 'arrangement/suggestion/regulation'. Commonly used in workplaces, rules, and advice from superiors to subordinates.
动词词干 + -도록 하다｜句式：S가 O를 V-도록 하다: Verb stem + -도록 하다 | Pattern: S가 O를 V-도록 하다
正式/书面/含安排感；不接形容词；也常用于自我规劝 -도록 하다: Formal/written/with a sense of arrangement; doesn't attach to adjectives; also used for self-admonition with -도록 하다
「하다」结尾的动词无法直接加 -이/히/리/기，要变使动就用 -시키다：공부하다: Verbs ending in '하다' can't directly take -이/히/리/기; use -시키다 instead: 공부하다 → 공부시키다 (make someone study), 청소하다 → 청소시키다 (make someone clean), 운동하다 → 운동시키다. The meaning often carries 'command/order/make do', and the tone can be strong.
汉字词/N + 하다 → N + 시키다｜句式：S가 O에게 N을 시키다: Sino-Korean word/N + 하다 → N + 시키다 | Pattern: S가 O에게 N을 시키다
하다 类专用；日常口语常用；有时带\"使唤/命令\"的语气感: Exclusive to 하다 verbs; common in everyday speech; sometimes carries a 'bossing/ordering' tone
被动和使动共用 -이/히/리/기 接尾，学习者最容易混。分辨的钥匙是\"句子结构: Passive and causative share the suffixes -이/히/리/기, which learners find most confusing. The key to distinguishing them is sentence structure and particles: in passive, the subject is the 'person/thing being acted upon' (이/가 + V-히-); in causative, the subject is the 'person making someone do something' (이/가 + O를 + V-히-).
被动：受动者이/가 + 施动者에게 + V-이/히-｜使动：施动者이/가 + 受: Passive: receiver이/가 + doer에게 + V-이/히- | Causative: doer이/가 + receiver를 + V-이/히-
结构里有没有\"目的宾语 을/를\"是关键：有 → 使动；没有 → 被动: The presence of an object particle 을/를 is key: if there is one → causative; if not → passive
使动句里\"被使动者（被让做的人）\"到底该用 을/를 还是 에게？规则：不及物: In causative sentences, should the passive causee (the person being made to do something) take 을/를 or 에게? Rule: causative of intransitive verbs → use 을/를; causative of transitive verbs → use 에게, because the object position is already taken by the 'purpose object.' This 'occupancy' logic is the core of causative particles.
不及物 → S가 O를 V-使动｜及物 → S가 O에게 N을 V-使动: Intransitive → S가 O를 V-causative | Transitive → S가 O에게 N을 V-causative
判断动词原型是否及物 → 决定被使动者用 을/를 还是 에게: Check if the base verb is transitive → determines whether the passive causee takes 을/를 or 에게
同样是\"让\"，语气差异巨大：短形使动多为\"照顾/亲密\"、-게 하다 多为: All meaning 'make/let,' but tones differ greatly: short-form causatives are often 'caring/intimate,' -게 하다 is usually 'permissive/neutral,' -도록 하다 is typically 'arrangement/regulation,' and -시키다 often carries a 'bossing around' feel. Choosing the wrong tone can come off as forceful or disrespectful.
短形使动 → 亲密照顾｜-게 하다 → 中性允许｜-도록 하다 → 正式安排｜-: Short-form causative → intimate care | -게 하다 → neutral permission | -도록 하다 → formal arrangement | -시키다 → commanding
本课综合 P14 全部 8 个使动语法点：短形使动（-이/히/리/기/우/추）、: This lesson covers all 8 causative grammar points from P14: short-form causatives (-이/히/리/기/우/추), -게 하다, -도록 하다, -시키다, passive vs causative distinction, particles 을/를·에게, and tone levels.
주체높임 是韩语敬语体系的核心：在动词/形容词词干加 -(으)시-，抬高句子主语: 주체높임 is the core of Korean honorifics: add -(으)시- to verb/adjective stems to elevate the sentence subject (elders/superiors/clients). With 받침 → -으시-, without 받침 → -시-. Endings fuse with -시-: present -세요/-십니다, past -셨어요/-셨습니다.
动词/形容词词干 + -(으)시- + 语尾｜有받침 -으시- / 无받침 -시: Verb/adjective stem + -(으)시- + ending | With 받침 -으시- / without 받침 -시-
一些高频动词/形容词的敬语形式不是加 -(으)시-，而是换成另一个词：있다→계시: Some high-frequency verbs/adjectives don't take -(으)시- but instead change to a different word: 있다→계시다 (to be), 먹다/마시다→드시다·잡수시다 (to eat/drink), 자다→주무시다 (to sleep), 죽다→돌아가시다 (to pass away), 말하다→말씀하시다 (to speak), 아프다→편찮으시다 (to be unwell). These are must-memorize items.
不加 -시-，直接换特殊词｜多为身体活动/生命状态相关动词: No -시- added; use a special word instead | Mostly verbs related to physical actions or life states
주체높임 特殊词汇速查: Subject Honorific Special Vocabulary Quick Reference
객체높임 抬高动作\"接受者\"（宾语/间接宾语）。这类动词多是\"给/见/问/: Object honorifics elevate the "recipient" of the action (object/indirect object). These verbs are mostly ones involving the other person, like "give/see/ask/bring": 주다→드리다 (to give to elder), 보다→뵙다 (to meet respectfully), 묻다→여쭙다 (to ask respectfully), 데리다→모시다 (to accompany).
换成特殊动词｜受动者用 -께 助词｜多与 주체높임 -시- 一起用: Change to a special verb | Recipient takes -께 particle | Often used with subject honorific -시-
敬语系统的助词升级：主语的 -이/가 → -께서；给的对象 -에게 → -께；名: Particle upgrades in the honorific system: subject -이/가 → -께서; recipient -에게 → -께; nouns take -님 for respect. These combine with verb -시- or special words to form complete honorific sentences.
-께서 与 -이/가 语法功能同（主语标记）｜-께 与 -에게 同（间接宾语）｜: -께서 has the same grammatical function as -이/가 (subject marker) | -께 same as -에게 (indirect object) | -님 attaches to person nouns
청자높임 靠句尾语体表达对\"听者\"的尊敬程度，是韩语敬语的第三个维度。四大语: Listener honorifics express respect toward the "listener" through sentence endings — the third dimension of Korean honorifics. Four speech levels: 하십시오체 (most formal, -습니다), 해요체 (formal-friendly, -어요), 해체 (banmal, -어), 해라체 (written/imperative). Choosing the wrong level means choosing the wrong relationship.

韩语敬语系统的另一半是\"自谦（낮춤）\"：把自己/自己群体压低，也是尊敬对方的: The other half of Korean honorifics is "self-lowering (낮춤)": lowering yourself/your group is also a way to show respect. First person 나→저, 우리→저희, 주다→드리다 (to give to elder), 말하다→말씀하다 (also used when speaking about oneself) are all self-lowering forms.

Changing the vowel in the same root creates a completely different feel: 깡충깡충 (little bunny hops) vs. 껑충껑충 (big leaps); 졸졸 (small stream) vs. 줄줄 (large flow).

In written style, (으)로 인하여 is used; in spoken style, -로 인해 sounds more natural.\n-길래 is used when the speaker directly observes or hears the situation in the preceding clause and then writes the corresponding reaction in the following clause. The subject is mostly first person.

-듯하다 除推测外，也用于\"마치 ~인 것처럼\"的比喻表达（눈이 녹듯 사라: -듯하다 is also used for metaphorical expressions like "마치 ~인 것처럼" (e.g., 눈이 녹듯 사라졌어요), in addition to guessing.\n-모양이다 is a guess based on the current situation or indirect evidence, with more emphasis on external signs than 듯하다.

(so...)".\n-더러/보고 both indicate the object of an action, equivalent to "tell.../say to...", mainly used in commands, requests, or relaying messages. 더러 is slightly more formal than 보고.

-을/ㄹ 텐데 前句主语可以是说话人自己或第三人称。后面接请求、担忧、建议等。\: -을/ㄹ 텐데: the subject of the preceding clause can be the speaker or a third person. It is followed by requests, worries, suggestions, etc.\n더러/보고: the preceding noun must be a person, not a thing or abstract noun.
-을/ㄹ 텐데 常用于体谅对方，如 \"피곤할 텐데 쉬세요\"。\\n더러/보: -을/ㄹ 텐데 is often used to show consideration, e.g., "피곤할 텐데 쉬세요".\n더러/보고 is often used with verbs of relaying (말하다/시키다/부탁하다), e.g., "누구보고 가라고 했어?".

-잖아요 用于确认说话双方都知道的事实，带有\"你不是知道吗/你看……不是……嘛: -잖아요 is used to confirm a fact both the speaker and listener know, with a tone of "you know, right?/see, isn't it...", implying the listener should already know.\n-거든요 is used to add background information or a reason the speaker thinks the listener doesn't know, equivalent to "because... (you might not know)/actually...", softer than -니까, with a slight explanatory feel.

-잖아요 用于说话人和听话人共享的信息。用于听话人完全不知道的信息时不自然。\\: -잖아요 is used for information shared between speaker and listener. -잖아요 用在 \"그 사람 알잖아요！（你认识那个人的嘛！）\" 这样的句子中: -잖아요 is used in sentences like "그 사람 알잖아요!" (You know that person, right!), also for mild protest or drawing attention.\n-거든요 is used in sentences like "사실 저 한국 사람이거든요" (Actually, I'm Korean), often to naturally introduce new background information.
表示把某动作的结果转移或提供给他人: Indicates transferring or providing the result of an action to someone
-아/어/여다 주다 表示做完某动作后把结果给对方，相当于\"……给……/帮……: -아/어/여다 주다 indicates doing an action and then giving the result to someone, equivalent to "...for.../do... for...", adding a sense of movement (bringing/taking the result) compared to -아/어/여 주다.\n-아/어/여다 드리다 is the honorific form, used for elders or superiors.\nOften used with verbs of movement like "사다 주다 (buy and give)", "가져다 주다 (bring and give)", "데려다 주다 (take someone)".
-아/어/여다 주다：动词词干 + 아/어/여다 주다\\n词干元音为 ㅏ/ㅗ: -아/어/여다 주다: verb stem + 아/어/여다 주다\nIf stem vowel is ㅏ/ㅗ → 아다, otherwise → 어다, 하다 verbs → 여다 (해다)\n-아/어/여다 드리다: replace 주다 with 드리다 (honorific)
-아/어/여다 주다 vs -아/어 주다：前者带有把结果送过去的移动语气，后者: -아/어/여다 주다 vs -아/어 주다: the former has a nuance of sending the result over, the latter is just helping/serving.\nFor elders, replace 주다 with honorific 드리다: 가져다 드리다, 사다 드리다.
-아/어/여다 주다 常与\"사다 주다（买来给）\"\"가져다 주다（拿来给）: -아/어/여다 주다 is often used with verbs of movement like "사다 주다 (buy and give)", "가져다 주다 (bring and give)", "데려다 주다 (take someone)".
가져다 주다（拿来给），데려다 주다（带〔人〕过去），만들어다 주다（做好给）: 가져다 주다 (bring and give), 데려다 주다 (take someone there), 만들어다 주다 (make and give)
데려다 주다：把人送到某处（移动性动词的常见搭配）: 데려다 주다: take someone to a place (common collocation with verbs of movement)
친구를 데려다 줬어요（送朋友，人✓）vs 책을 가져다 줬어요（拿书来给，物✓: Took a friend (person ✓) vs brought a book (thing ✓); 가져다 주다 with a person ✗, 데려다 주다 with a thing ✗
데려다 줬어요：平辈关系用 데려다 주다（✓）。할머니께 要用 드렸어요，사줬드: 데려다 줬어요: Use 데려다 주다 for peers (✓). For 할머니, use 드렸어요; 사줬드려요 is double honorific, 가져어다 is a non-existent form.
表示做完某动作后来/回来，或连续动作: Indicates coming/returning after doing an action, or a continuous action
-아/어다 오다 表示做完某事后来（到说话现场），相当于\"做了……来了/带来了: -아/어다 오다 means coming (to the speaker's location) after doing something, like "did... and came/brought," emphasizing the result is here. \n-아/어다 주다 in this lesson focuses on the direction difference in "bring to give": 오다 emphasizes movement toward the speaker, 가다 emphasizes movement away from the speaker. \nThe core variable in both is direction: 사다 오다 (buy and come), 사다 가다 (buy and go).
动词 词干 + 아/어다 오다/가다\\n词干 元音 ㅏ/ㅗ → 아다，그 외: Verb stem + 아/어다 오다/가다\nStem vowel ㅏ/ㅗ → 아다, otherwise → 어다\nDirection: 오다 (toward speaker) vs 가다 (away from speaker)
-아/어다 오다 与 -아/어다 가다 的区别在于移动方向。以说话人位置为基准，: The difference between -아/어다 오다 and -아/어다 가다 is the direction of movement. Based on the speaker's position, determine whether the result comes or goes. \nWhen combined with 주다/드리다, it's the 오다 series: bringing the result to the speaker's side.
像\"밥을 해다 오다（做了饭来）\"\"빨래를 해다 가다（洗了衣服去）\"这: Like "밥을 해다 오다 (cook and come)" or "빨래를 해다 가다 (do laundry and go)," these often appear in household actions.
表示惊讶/反问，或强调\"当然是/那还用说\": Indicates surprise/rhetorical question, or emphasizes "of course/needless to say"
-다니요 用于对听到的内容表示惊讶、意外或质疑，相当于\"竟然……？/……这是什: -다니요 is used to express surprise, shock, or doubt about what you heard, like "really...?/what do you mean...?", a reactive follow-up to previous info. \n-고 말고요 strongly affirms the other's suggestion or question, like "of course.../needless to say...", firm and positive.
-다니요：动词/形容词基本形（终止形）+ 다니요，이다 → 이라니요，있다/없다: -다니요: verb/adjective base form (final) + 다니요, 이다 → 이라니요, 있다/없다 → 있다니요/없다니요\n-고 말고요: verb/adjective stem + 고 말고요 (unconditional affirmation)
-다니요 原样重复或引用对方的话语来表示惊讶，接近直接引用。\\n-고 말고요: -다니요 repeats or quotes the other's words as-is to show surprise, close to direct quotation. \n-고 말고요 is a strong affirmation to a question, more emotional than "물론이죠". It can stand alone or follow a sentence.
-다니요 如\"그게 사실이라니요！（那竟是真的？！）\"，常用于震惊或难以置信: -다니요 like "그게 사실이라니요! (That's really true?!)", often used in shocking or unbelievable situations. \n-고 말고요 like "같이 가고 말고요! (Of course I'll go!)", used to enthusiastically agree.
表示状态/动作从过去持续到现在，或向未来延续: Indicates a state/action continuing from the past to now, or extending into the future
-아/어 오다 表示某状态或动作从过去持续到现在，相当于\"一直……到现在/……: -아/어 오다 means a state or action has continued from the past to now, like "have been... until now/...has come about," emphasizing the arrival point is the present. \n-아/어 가다 means a state or action continues from now into the future, like "increasingly.../gradually... on," emphasizing the direction is the future. \nThe core of both is time direction: 오다 (past→present), 가다 (present→future).
动词/形容词词干 + 아/어 오다（过去→现在）\\n动词/形容词词干 + 아/: Verb/adjective stem + 아/어 오다 (past→present)\nVerb/adjective stem + 아/어 가다 (present→future)\nStem vowel ㅏ/ㅗ → 아, otherwise → 어, 하다 → 해
-아/어 오다 主要与\"지금까지\"搭配，表示过去的持续。\\n-아/어 가다: -아/어 오다 mainly pairs with "지금까지," indicating past continuation. \n-아/어 가다 pairs with "점점" or "서서히," indicating change toward the future.
像\"한국어를 배워 오다（一直在学韩语）\" vs \"한국어 실력이 늘어: Like "한국어를 배워 오다 (have been learning Korean)" vs "한국어 실력이 늘어 가다 (Korean skills are improving)," even with the same topic, the time direction differs.
表示假装做某动作或处于某状态: Indicates pretending to do an action or be in a state
-는/은/ㄴ 체하다 和 -는/은/ㄴ 척하다 意思完全相同，均表示\"假装……: -는/은/ㄴ 체하다 and -는/은/ㄴ 척하다 have exactly the same meaning, both meaning "pretend to.../act as if...", indicating it's not actually so, just putting on that appearance. \n척하다 is more common in speech, 체하다 is slightly more formal. They can be freely swapped.
动词现在冠词形（-는）+ 체하다/척하다\\n形容词/动词过去冠词形（-은/ㄴ）: Verb present adnominal (-는) + 체하다/척하다\nAdjective/verb past adnominal (-은/ㄴ) + 체하다/척하다\nVerb/adjective future adnominal (-을/ㄹ) + 체하다/척하다
冠词形词尾选择：动词现在用 -는，动词/形容词过去用 -은/ㄴ，形容词现在用 -: Adnominal ending choice: verbs present use -는, verbs/adjectives past use -은/ㄴ, adjectives present use -은/ㄴ\nDon't confuse 체하다/척하다 with 체하다 meaning "indigestion" (체하다 = food stagnation, 척하다 = pretend).
像\"자는 척하다（假装睡觉）\"\"모르는 체하다（假装不知道）\"，是日常中: Like "자는 척하다 (pretend to sleep)" or "모르는 체하다 (pretend not to know)," these are common daily expressions.
说去哪里、和谁一起: Saying where you're going and who with
两个核心：\\n说目的地用 에 가요，说\"和……一起\"用 와/과 或 하고。: Two key points:\nUse 에 가요 to say the destination, and 와/과 or 하고 to say "with...".\nIn Chinese, "go" and "with" are separate words, but Korean attaches particles directly to nouns—no separate verb needed.
这节课有两个句型：\\n去哪里（에 가요）、和谁一起（와/과/하고）。\\n先看: This lesson has two patterns:\nWhere you're going (에 가요) and who with (와/과/하고).\nFirst, see where each one sits in the sentence.
와/과 的选择只看一件事：\\n前面名词最后有没有收音。\\n口语直接用하고，不: Choosing between 와/과 depends on one thing:\nwhether the preceding noun ends in a final consonant (받침).\nIn speech, just use 하고—no need to worry about 받침, it's easier.
约朋友、出行、购物是用这套语法最频繁的场景约朋友去哪里、买东西\"和\"什么都用: Making plans with friends, going out, and shopping are the most common situations for this grammar—asking where to go, what to buy, and who with.
说有没有、人在不在: Saying if something exists or someone is there
있어요 表示\"有\"或\"在\"，없어요 表示\"没有\"或\"不在\"，主语: 있어요 means "have" or "is there," and 없어요 means "don't have" or "isn't there," with the subject marked by 이/가.\nUnlike Chinese, Korean uses the same pattern for "I have a book" and "The book is here"—the only difference is whether a location is mentioned.
这节课有三种句型：\\n说\"有/没有\"、说\"在哪里\"、说\"某地有什么\: This lesson has three patterns:\nsaying "have/don't have," saying "where something is," and saying "what's in a place."\nAll three revolve around 있어요/없어요, so first check if a location word is in the sentence.
이/가 的选择只看主语名词最后一个字有没有收音。\\n有收音接 이，没有收音接: Choosing between 이/가 depends on whether the subject noun's last syllable has a final consonant.\nWith 받침, use 이; without, use 가.\nIt's the same logic as 은/는 from P1, just a different particle function.
있어요/없어요 在日常对话里出现频率极高找东西、约时间、描述房间、拒绝邀请，全都: 있어요/없어요 come up constantly in daily conversation—finding things, setting times, describing rooms, declining invitations.\nMaster this lesson and you'll cover 80% of "have/have not" situations in everyday Korean.
邀请别人一起做，或礼貌请求: Inviting someone to do something together, or making a polite request
-ㅂ시다/읍시다 是\"我们一起……吧\"，-(으)세요 是礼貌地请对方做某事。: -ㅂ시다/읍시다 means "let's... together," and -(으)세요 is a polite way to ask someone to do something.\nIn Chinese terms:\nㅂ시다 ≈ "let's..." (speaker joins in), 세요 ≈ "please..." (only asking the other person).
这节课有两套词尾：\\nㅂ시다/읍시다 用来发出邀请，(으)세요 用来礼貌请求。: This lesson has two sets of endings:\nㅂ시다/읍시다 for invitations, and (으)세요 for polite requests.\nBoth need conjugation, so first figure out which situation calls for which.
变形规则和之前一样，只看词干最后有没有收音：\\n无收音接 -ㅂ시다/-세요，有: The conjugation rule is the same as before—just check if the stem ends in a final consonant:\nNo 받침: add -ㅂ시다/-세요; with 받침: add -읍시다/-으세요.\nException: ㄹ stems drop the ㄹ before adding -ㅂ시다 (알다→압시다).
세요 在餐厅、课堂、服务业随处可见\"请坐\"\"请看\"；\\nㅂ시다 则是约: 세요 is everywhere in restaurants, classrooms, and service settings—"please sit," "please look."\nㅂ시다 is for inviting friends—"let's go," "let's study."\nThese two endings will instantly make your Korean sound more polite.
数东西、点餐、报人数: Counting things, ordering food, and stating numbers of people
韩语数字有两套：\\n固有数词（하나/둘…）配个/人/杯，汉字数词（일/이/삼…: Korean has two number systems:\nNative numbers (하나/둘…) go with items/people/cups, and Sino-Korean numbers (일/이/삼…) go with money/dates/phone numbers.\nChinese has just one set; Korean has two because it borrowed Sino-Korean numbers historically but kept native words for counting physical things.
这节课核心是\"数字 + 量词\"的搭配。\\n先认识两套数字各自负责什么，再看: The core of this lesson is "number + counter" combinations.\nFirst learn what each number system handles, then see how counters follow the number.
搞清楚两件事：①固有数词 vs 汉字数词数实物用固有（개/명/잔），数钱/时间分: Get two things straight: ① Native vs. Sino-Korean numbers—count physical things with native (개/명/잔), and money/minutes/dates with Sino-Korean.\n② Native numbers shorten before counters:\n하나→한, 둘→두, 셋→세, 넷→네; the rest stay the same.
点餐、购物、订位是用数词最集中的场景。\\n掌握\"커피 한 잔 주세요\"这一: Ordering food, shopping, and making reservations are where numbers come up most.\nMaster the pattern "커피 한 잔 주세요" and you'll get by smoothly in cafés, restaurants, and convenience stores.
三个小助词各有一招：\\n의 标所属，도 加\"也\"，만 限制\"只有\"。\: Each of the three particles has its own trick: \n의 marks possession, 도 adds 'also,' and 만 limits to 'only.' \nAll three attach to nouns, but their functions are totally different—similar to Chinese '的/也/只.' Once you know the function, usage becomes clear.
这节课三个助词各自独立，不需要接续变形。\\n重点是搞清楚每个助词替换掉的是哪个: In this lesson, the three particles are independent and need no conjugation. \nThe key is figuring out which slot each particle replaces: \n도 and 만 replace 은/는/이/가/을/를.

This lesson is the conjugation challenge of Chapter 2—not about "how to use" but "why it changes this way."

结构：动词过去词干（-았/었-）+ 어야 했는데。\\n可看作 -아/어야 하다: Structure: verb past stem (-았/었-) + 어야 했는데. Can be seen as the past + retrospective form of -아/어야 하다 (must). The subject can be oneself or others, making it more flexible than -을 걸 그랬다.
判断口诀：既有\"没做\"的懊悔，又有\"本该是义务\"的意味。\\n-을 걸: Quick tip: it combines regret for not doing something with a sense of obligation. -을 걸 그랬다 leans toward personal wish, while -았어야 했는데 leans toward duty. It's also used to judge others: 너 그때 갔어야 했는데 (You should have gone then).
对过去情况的遗憾感叹，比 -았더라면 更口语化。\\n\"要是……就好了\" —: A colloquial expression of regret about the past, more casual than -았더라면. "If only..." — it didn't happen, so you just lament. Structurally similar to -았더라면, but more common in everyday speech; -았더라면 is more formal.
结构：动词/形容词过去词干 + 으면 좋았을 텐데。\\n可看作 -았/었으면: Structure: verb/adjective past stem + 으면 좋았을 텐데. Can be seen as the past retrospective form of -았/었으면 좋겠다 (wish). Often stands alone or omits the second half.
Choosing between -았더라면: 1. Everyday speech: -았으면 좋았을 텐데 2. Written/formal: -았더라면 -았을 텐데. The meanings are nearly identical and interchangeable.
表达\"差一点就发生了但幸好没发生\"。\\n主要功能是庆幸没发生某件（通常不好: Expresses that something almost happened but fortunately didn't. Its main function is relief that something (usually bad) didn't occur. The structure is simple, but note: the verb in -을/ㄹ 뻔했다 always takes the future adnominal form.
结构：动词词干（无收音 + ㄹ；有收音 + 을）+ 뻔했다。\\n뻔하다 是\": Structure: verb stem (no batchim + ㄹ; with batchim + 을) + 뻔했다. 뻔하다 is the fixed verb for "almost" and always takes the past form 뻔했다. Even though it didn't happen, the future adnominal form is used because it "was about to" happen.
这个语法看似简单，但学习者容易混淆两点：\\n1. 结尾必须是过去形 뻔했다，不: This grammar looks simple, but learners often confuse two points: 1. The ending must be past tense 뻔했다, not 뻔한다 or 뻔해요. 2. The preceding form uses the future adnominal (-을/ㄹ), not the past adnominal (-은/ㄴ).
对别人过去没做的事表达\"当时怎么不这样呢\"的责备+建议。\\n可以看作 -을: Expresses reproach and advice about something someone didn't do in the past: "Why didn't you do it then?" It's the "other-directed" version of -을 걸 그랬다: one is self-blame, the other addresses others. The ending must be past tense 그랬어요, referring to the other person's past choice.
结构：动词词干 + 지 그랬어요。\\n注意：-지 마세요（禁止）和 -지 그랬: Structure: verb stem + 지 그랬어요. Note: -지 마세요 (prohibition) and -지 그랬어요 (reproach) look similar but mean completely different things. Only attaches to verbs, not adjectives.
和 -을 걸 그랬다 配对：\\n1. 自责：-을 걸 그랬다（我该……的）\\: Paired with -을 걸 그랬다: 1. Self-blame: -을 걸 그랬다 (I should have...) 2. Blaming others: -지 그랬어요 (Why didn't you...). Completely different from -지 마세요: -지 마세요 = please don't do; -지 그랬어요 = why didn't you do it then.

表达\"即使过去做了/是了，结果也不会变\"的让步语气。\\n和 -아/어도（即: Expresses a concessive tone that "even if it had been done or been the case in the past, the result wouldn't change." It's the past counterfactual version of -아/어도 (even if...). Often paired with -았을 것이다 / -았을 텐데 to emphasize that "changing the past wouldn't help."
结构：动词/形容词过去词干（-았/었-）+ 어도。\\n跟第一课 -았더라면 结:
Structure: verb/adjective past stem (-았/었-) + 어도.
Similar to Lesson 1's -았더라면, but opposite in meaning:
· -았더라면 = "If only I had..." (hypothetical change)
· -았어도 = "Even if I had..." (change wouldn't have helped)
判断口诀：\\n· 假设改变过去，好结果会发生 → -았더라면\\n· 假设改变:
Quick rule:
· If changing the past would lead to a good outcome → -았더라면
· If changing the past wouldn't improve things → -았어도
The second clause usually has a negative or unfavorable meaning.

表达对某种（不希望发生的）情况的担心。\\n后半句通常是为避免这个担心而采取的行: Expresses worry about an (undesired) situation.\nThe second clause usually describes an action taken to avoid that worry.\nExtremely common in both speech and writing—it's Korean's most important expression for worry.
结构：动词/形容词词干（无收音+ㄹ；有收音+을）+ 까 봐。\\n可看作 -을까: Structure: verb/adjective stem (no batchim + ㄹ; with batchim + 을) + 까 봐.\nCan be seen as a blend of -을까? (whether) + 봐 (worry), literally "watching whether..."\nThe second clause often has actions like 걱정하다, 안 하다, 챙기다, 준비하다 to avoid the worry.

Common patterns:
1. -을까 봐 걱정이에요 (worried that...)
2. -을까 봐 [action] (did... because afraid that...)
3. -을까 봐서 (connective form, adding 서 to emphasize the reason)
Past tense uses -았/었을까 봐 (afraid that... at the time).
表达低概率的推测，\"说不定会……\"、\"没准儿……\"。\\n比 -을 것: Expresses a low-probability guess: "might..." or "could be..."\nWeaker and more uncertain than -을 것 같다 (seems like); just offers a possibility.\nCarries a "I'm not sure, but maybe" tone—a high-frequency expression in intermediate Korean.
结构：动词/形容词词干（无收音+ㄹ；有收音+을）+ 지도 모르다。\\n直译\": Structure: verb/adjective stem (no batchim + ㄹ; with batchim + 을) + 지도 모르다.\nLiterally "don't even know (whether)..." extended to mean "might."\nOften ends with 몰라요 / 모르겠어요 for a softer tone.
推测的确定性梯度（从低到高）：\\n1. -을지도 모르다（说不定）— 最不确定:
Certainty gradient for speculation (low to high):
1. -을지도 모르다 (might) — least certain
2. -을 수도 있다 (could) — objective possibility
3. -을 것 같다 (seems like) — a hunch
4. -을 것이다 (probably will) — fairly sure
5. -을 게 틀림없다 (definitely) — most certain
强烈否定某种可能性：\"那怎么可能\"、\"不可能\"。\\n和 -을 리가 있: Strongly denies a possibility: "how could that be" / "impossible."\nPairs with -을 리가 있어요? (rhetorical question); both convey total disbelief.\nOften used in conversation to respond to someone's assumption, meaning "no way / absolutely not."
结构：动词/形容词词干（无收音+ㄹ；有收音+을）+ 리가 없다。\\n리 = 道: Structure: verb/adjective stem (no batchim + ㄹ; with batchim + 을) + 리가 없다.\n리 = reason/logic (dependent noun), "no such logic" → "impossible."\nPast speculation uses -았/었을 리가 없다.
和 -지 않을 것이다（不会）差别：\\n· -을 리가 없다：语气强烈，几乎断:
Difference from -지 않을 것이다 (won't):
· -을 리가 없다: strong, almost asserting "absolutely impossible"
· -지 않을 것이다: ordinary negative speculation, "probably won't"

In speech, -을 리가 있어요? (rhetorical: how could it?) is common and means the same as -을 리가 없다.

表达\"某种情况自然而然会发生\"的规律性判断。\\n带有\"这是天经地义\"的: Expresses a judgment that something happens naturally and inevitably.\nCarries the nuance of "it's only natural," often used for universal truths and life patterns.\n-기 마련이다 and -게 마련이다 are identical in meaning; either can be used.
结构：动词/形容词词干 + 기 마련이다（或 -게 마련이다）。\\n마련이다: Structure: Verb/Adjective stem + 기 마련이다 (or -게 마련이다).\n마련이다 literally means "is prepared" → extended to "it's naturally so."\nAttach directly to the stem regardless of the final consonant.
两个变体：\\n1. -기 마련이다：TOPIK 高频，日常也用\\n2. -게:
Two variants:
1. -기 마련이다: High-frequency in TOPIK, also used daily
2. -게 마련이다: Slightly more colloquial, with a stronger nuance
Meaning is identical; either is correct.

Common usage: Often paired with 누구나 (anyone), 다들 (everyone) to emphasize universality.
十有八九会……（多为负面）: Nine times out of ten... (usually negative)
表达\"某种情况很容易发生\"，通常指不好的结果。\\n和 -기 마련이다 结构: Expresses that something is very likely to happen, usually a bad outcome.\nSimilar in structure to -기 마련이다, but stronger and more negative.\nOften appears in warnings, advice, and worry contexts.
结构：动词词干 + 기 십상이다。\\n십상 是汉字词\"十上\"，\"十次里有: Structure: Verb stem + 기 십상이다.\n십상 is a Sino-Korean word meaning "ten out of ten" → "nine times out of ten."\nMostly attaches to verbs, used for high-probability negative outcomes.
语感差别：\\n· -기 마련이다：中性，指普遍规律\\n· -기 십상이다：偏:
Nuance difference:
· -기 마련이다: Neutral, refers to universal patterns
· -기 십상이다: Negative, refers to easy mistakes

Examples:
· 늙기 마련이다 (one gets old) — objective law
· 넘어지기 십상이다 (easy to trip) — warning
本来就……（道理规律）/ 从不……: It's the way things are (principle/rule) / Never...
-는 법이다 表达\"按道理/情理就是这样\"的规律。\\n-는 법이 없다 相: -는 법이다 expresses a rule that things are so by logic or common sense.\n-는 법이 없다 is the opposite, expressing a fixed negation of "never like this."\nFocuses on "how it should be" or convention, more moral/social than -기 마련이다.
结构：\\n· 动词词干 + 는 법이다（现在规律）\\n· 形容词词干（无收音:
Structure:
· Verb stem + 는 법이다 (present rule)
· Adjective stem (no final consonant + ㄴ; with final consonant + 은) + 법이다
· Noun + 인 법이다
Negative: -는 법이 없다 (never)
和 -기 마련이다 的选择：\\n· -기 마련이다：偏自然/生理规律\\n·:
Choosing between -기 마련이다 and -는 법이다:
· -기 마련이다: Natural/physiological patterns
· -는 법이다: Social/logical rules
· They're often interchangeable; the subtle difference is "physiological" vs. "logical" emphasis.

表达\"根据情况判断，事情显然会是这样\"的强推测。\\n뻔하다 就是\"明摆着: Expresses a strong guess that something is obviously the case based on the situation.\n뻔하다 means "plain to see, obvious."\nCarries subjective judgment; the speaker is very confident in the conclusion.
结构：\\n· 动词 + 는 게 뻔하다（现在/将来）\\n· 动词 + 은/ㄴ:
Structure:

Opposite of -을 리가 없다:
· -을 리가 없다 = asserts "impossible"
· -는 게 뻔하다 = asserts "obviously will"

· -는 게 뻔하다 = inferred from the immediate situation

表达\"根据证据/规律，一定会……\"的最高确定性推测。\\n틀림없다 直译\": Expresses the highest certainty of speculation, "based on evidence/rules, it must be..." \n틀림없다 literally means "no mistake" → "without a doubt." \nIt and -을 리가 없다 are two ends of the same spectrum: one asserts "certainly," the other "impossible."
结构：\\n· 动词/形容词 + 을/ㄹ 게 틀림없다（未来推测）\\n· 动词:
Structure:

· Noun + 인 게 틀림없다

Highest level of speculative certainty: 
· -을지도 모르다 (20%) 
· -을 것 같다 (60%) 
· -을 것이다 (80%)

和 -는 데다가 意思相似的书面表达。\\n\"不仅 A，而且 B\"，A 和: A formal expression similar to -는 데다가. \n"Not only A, but also B," where A and B are additive traits of the same kind. \nMore common in written language, formal speeches, and TOPIK writing.

Difference from -는 데다가:

· -을뿐더러: More written/formal, solemn tone

They are interchangeable; choose based on context. Prefer -을뿐더러 in TOPIK writing and company reports.
书面累加连接词，\"不仅 A 也 B\"、\"既是 A 也是 B\"。\\n后半: A formal additive connector: "not only A but also B," "both A and B." \nThe second clause often pairs with -도 to emphasize "also." \nLiterary in tone, common in TOPIK reading and news reports.
结构：\\n· 动词/形容词词干 + 거니와\\n· 过去 + -았/었거니와\:
Structure:

· Past + -았/었거니와
· Noun + 이거니와 / 거니와

Attach directly to the stem regardless of final consonant. For nouns, choose 이거니와 / 거니와 based on presence of final consonant.

Difference from -을뿐더러:

「-더라도」表示强让步，\"就算……也……\"\"即使……也……\"。用于假设的: -더라도 indicates strong concession, "even if..." "even though...". Used for hypothetical situations, emphasizing that regardless of the premise, the following action/state remains unchanged. It's stronger and more formal than -아/어도.
直接连接词干，不看받침；过去 -았/었더라도；名词用 -(이)라 하더라도: Connect directly to the stem, regardless of 받침; past -았/었더라도; nouns use -(이)라 하더라도

좋다 词干 좋 有받침，用 -을지라도 → 좋을지라도。: The stem 좋 has a batchim, so use -을지라도 → 좋을지라도.
「-을/ㄹ지언정」表达强烈的\"宁可A也不B\"\"哪怕A也不做B\"，前句是宁: '-을/ㄹ지언정' expresses a strong 'would rather A than B' or 'even if A, never B.' The first clause is a negative situation you'd rather accept, and the second is something you absolutely won't do. The tone is firm and formal, often found in writing.

죽다 有받침，用 -을지언정 → 죽을지언정。: 죽다 has a batchim, so use -을지언정 → 죽을지언정.
늦다 有받침，用 -을지언정 → 늦을지언정。: 늦다 has a batchim, so use -을지언정 → 늦을지언정.
「-을/ㄹ망정」表达\"就算……也……\"\"哪怕……也……\"，含有\"退一步: '-을/ㄹ망정' expresses 'even if... still...' or 'even though... still...', carrying a tone of 'conceding a little, but the bottom line stays.' The first clause is a minimal concession, and the second emphasizes a line that cannot be crossed.
词干：有받침 -을망정 / 无받침 -ㄹ망정 · 名词 -(이)ㄹ망정: Stem: with batchim -을망정 / without batchim -ㄹ망정 · Nouns: -(이)ㄹ망정

가난하다 词干 가난하 无받침，加 -ㄹ망정 → 가난할망정。: The stem of 가난하다 is 가난하, no batchim, add -ㄹ망정 → 가난할망정.
「-는 한이 있어도 / -는 한이 있더라도」表示\"即便到了……的地步也……: '-는 한이 있어도 / -는 한이 있더라도' means 'even if it comes to...', where the first clause is the most extreme/worst outcome and the second expresses firm resolve. The tone is strong, used mainly in writing and firm statements.

「-고자 / -고자 하다」表示意图、目的、打算，\"想……\"\"打算……\": '-고자 / -고자 하다' expresses intention, purpose, or plan, meaning 'want to...', 'plan to...', 'in order to...'. It's formal, used in writing, speeches, news, and official documents—the formal equivalent of colloquial -(으)려고 / -(으)려고 하다.

「N + 치고」有两种用法：① 全称\"说到……没有例外/都是……\"，② 例外: 'N + 치고' has two uses: ① Generalization: 'when it comes to..., no exception/all...', ② Exception/concession: 'as for..., (surprisingly)...'. The meaning depends on context.
名词 + 치고 · 常见搭配 \"N 치고 -지 않은/없는 것이 없다\"（全: Noun + 치고 · Common patterns: 'N 치고 -지 않은/없는 것이 없다' (generalization) or 'N 치고 unexpected result' (exception)

名词 + 치고（不看받침，直接接）: Noun + 치고 (attach directly, regardless of batchim)
本练习综合复习 P26 让步与意图强化章节的 8 个语法点：-더라도、-을/ㄹ지: This exercise reviews the 8 grammar points from the P26 concession and intention chapter: -더라도, -을/ㄹ지라도, -을/ㄹ지언정, -을/ㄹ망정, -는 한이 있어도, -고자, -도록, -치고.

「-기 마련이다」表示\"本来就……\"\"必然会……\"\"理所当然……\"。: '-기 마련이다' means 'it's only natural that...', 'it's bound to...', 'of course...'. Used to state universal rules, common sense, or inevitable results. The tone is objective, often used in lessons or summarizing experiences.

直接接词干，不看받침；名词加系词 이 后再接；等同 -는 법이다: Attach directly to the stem, regardless of batchim; for nouns, add the copula 이 before it; equivalent to -는 법이다
动词/形容词词干 + -기 마련이다，不看받침: Verb/Adjective stem + -기 마련이다, regardless of batchim
「-는 법이다 / -은/ㄴ 법이다」表示\"本来就……\"\"按道理讲……\": '-는 법이다 / -은/ㄴ 법이다' means 'it's only natural that...', 'by all logic...', 'naturally...'. Used to state universal rules or principles, with a more formal tone and a hint of lesson/warning. Also commonly used as -는 법이 없다 to mean 'will never...'.

动词冠形 -는，形容词冠形 -은/ㄴ；否定用 -는 법이 없다 表强烈否认: Verb adnominal -는, adjective adnominal -은/ㄴ; negative uses -는 법이 없다 for strong denial
形容词：有받침 -은 법이다 / 无받침 -ㄴ 법이다: Adjectives: with batchim -은 법이다 / without batchim -ㄴ 법이다

「-을/ㄹ 법하다」表示\"看起来会……\"\"有可能……\"\"大概会……\": '-eul/ril beophada' means 'seems like it will...', 'it's possible that...', 'probably will...'. It's used to speculate about a possibility, with a literary, written feel. Similar to -eul/ril geot gatda, but more euphemistic and classical.

「-기 나름이다」表示\"取决于……的方式/程度\"\"看你怎么……\"。前接动: '-gi nareumida' means 'depends on the way/degree of...' or 'it's up to how you...'. It follows a verb to express that the result depends on that action/manner. The noun version is 'N nareumida' (depends on N).

「-기에 달려 있다」表示\"取决于……\"\"在于……\"\"看……\"。用于: '-gie dallyeo itda' means 'depends on...', 'lies in...', 'hinges on...'. It's used to emphasize the key determining factor. The noun version is 'N-e dallyeo itda'. It's more formal and written than -gi nareumida.

固定搭配\"-기에 달려 있다\"；主语常为决定的对象（성공/실패/미래 等）: Fixed expression '-gie dallyeo itda'; the subject is often the thing being determined (success/failure/future, etc.).
正确形是 달려 있다（不是 달렸다）: The correct form is dallyeo itda (not dallyeotda).
「-는/은/ㄴ 셈이다」表示\"算是……\"\"相当于……\"\"可以说是……\: '-는/은/ㄴ 셈이다' means 'can be considered as...', 'amounts to...', 'one could say...'. It's used for estimates/evaluations made after considering various aspects, often in conclusions after summarizing, assessing, or comparing.
动词现在 -는 셈이다 · 形容词 -은/ㄴ 셈이다 · 名词 -인 셈이다 ·: Verb present -는 셈이다 · Adjective -은/ㄴ 셈이다 · Noun -인 셈이다 · Past -은/ㄴ 셈이다
关注冠形选择：动词现在 -는，动词过去 -은/ㄴ，形容词 -은/ㄴ，名词 -인: Note the adnominal form: verb present -는, verb past -은/ㄴ, adjective -은/ㄴ, noun -인

싸다 形容词无받침，冠形 -ㄴ → 싼 셈이에요。: 싸다 is an adjective without batchim, adnominal -ㄴ → 싼 셈이에요.
「-는/은/ㄴ 셈치다」表示\"就当作……\"\"假设……\"\"视为……\"。: '-는/은/ㄴ 셈치다' means 'to consider as...', 'to assume...', 'to regard as...'. Used for hypotheticals, mental concessions, or comforting oneself to accept a situation. The tone is similar to 'just pretend it didn't happen'.
动词现在 -는 셈치다 · 动词过去 -은/ㄴ 셈치다 · 形容词 -은/ㄴ 셈: Verb present -는 셈치다 · Verb past -은/ㄴ 셈치다 · Adjective -은/ㄴ 셈치다 · Noun -인 셈치다
常搭配 -고 用作连接：\"-는 셈치고\" = 就当作……，然后……: Often used with -고 as a connector: '-는 셈치고' = consider it as..., then...
「-는/은/ㄴ 척하다 / -는/은/ㄴ 체하다」表示\"假装……\"\"装作…: '-는/은/ㄴ 척하다 / -는/은/ㄴ 체하다' means 'to pretend...', 'to act as if...'. The two are nearly identical in meaning; 척하다 is more colloquial, 체하다 more formal. The adnominal form changes by part of speech, same as -셈이다.
动词现在 -는 척하다 · 动词过去 -은/ㄴ 척하다 · 形容词 -은/ㄴ 척: Verb present -는 척하다 · Verb past -은/ㄴ 척하다 · Adjective -은/ㄴ 척하다 · Noun -인 척하다

重点辨析：-는 법이다 vs -을 법하다；-셈이다 vs -셈치다: Key distinctions: -는 법이다 vs -을 법하다; -셈이다 vs -셈치다
「-기(가) + 形容词/名词하다」表示\"做……是……的\"\"……起来……\: '-기(가) + adjective/noun하다' means 'doing... is...', '...to do'. It turns a verb into a subject, followed by an adjective evaluating difficulty or feeling. Core expressions: 어렵다/쉽다/힘들다/편하다/좋다, etc.
常用搭配：-기 어렵다/쉽다/힘들다/편하다/좋다/싫다；助词 -가 可省略: Common collocations: -기 어렵다/쉽다/힘들다/편하다/좋다/싫다; particle -가 can be omitted

「얼마나 + -는지/은지 + 모르다」表示\"不知有多……\"\"……得不得了: 「얼마나 + -는지/은지 + 모르다」means "you have no idea how..." or "...to an extreme degree." It's used to strongly exclaim about the depth of a degree; although literally it says "don't know," it actually emphasizes "very/extremely."
얼마나 + 动词现在 -는지 / 形容词有받침 -은지 / 无받침 -ㄴ지 +: 얼마나 + verb present -는지 / adjective with 받침 -은지 / without 받침 -ㄴ지 + 모르다
어렵다 形容词有받침，用 -은지 → 어려운지。: 어렵다 is an adjective with 받침, so use -은지 → 어려운지.
「-다 못해」表示\"……到甚至……的地步\"\"……以致于……\"。前项达到某: 「-다 못해」means "to the point of even..." or "so much that..." The first clause reaches a certain degree, leading to a more extreme second clause. The core is an emphasis on "progression of degree + going beyond the norm."
直接接词干，不看받침；后接更极端的状态/结果: Attach directly to the stem, regardless of 받침; followed by a more extreme state/result
形容词/动词词干 + -다 못해，不看받침: Adjective/verb stem + -다 못해, regardless of 받침
「-을/ㄹ수록」表示\"越……越……\"，随着前项程度增加，后项程度也相应变化。: 「-을/ㄹ수록」means "the more..., the more..." As the degree of the first clause increases, the degree of the second clause changes accordingly. It's often paired with "-으면 -을수록" for emphasis.
词干：有받침 -을수록 / 无받침 -ㄹ수록 · 名词 -(이)ㄹ수록: Stem: with 받침 -을수록 / without 받침 -ㄹ수록 · noun -(이)ㄹ수록
常见强调形：\"-으면 -을수록\"（越……越……）；前后主语通常一致: Common emphatic form: "-으면 -을수록" (the more..., the more...); subject is usually the same before and after
공부하다 词干 공부하 无받침，用 -ㄹ수록 → 공부할수록。: 공부하다 stem 공부하 has no batchim, use -ㄹ수록 → 공부할수록.
「오죽 -으면」是一种感叹反问：\"该多……啊\"\"得多么……才……\"。常与: 「오죽 -으면」 is an exclamatory rhetorical: "How..." "Just how... to...". Often paired with the following clause "-겠어요/-겠니" to express deep speculation/empathy about a degree.
\"오죽\" 本身是\"多么/该多\"的意思；结构 \"오죽 -으면 -겠어요\: "오죽" itself means "how/just how"; the structure "오죽 -으면 -겠어요" is a fixed exclamatory expression
词干 힘들 有받침，加 -으면 → 힘들면（ㄹ 已在词干中）: Stem 힘들 has batchim, add -으면 → 힘들면 (ㄹ already in stem)
「-기(는) 하다」表示\"虽然……但\"\"……倒是……\"。前项承认某事实，: 「-기(는) 하다」 means "although... but" "...is... though". The first part acknowledges a fact, followed by a contrast or addition. It's a concessive tone, often paired with -지만/-는데.
动词/形容词词干 + -기(는) 하다 · 名词 + 이기(는) 하다: Verb/adjective stem + -기(는) 하다 · Noun + 이기(는) 하다
常用形式：-기는 하다 / -기는 하지만 / -기는 한데；作让步转折: Common forms: -기는 하다 / -기는 하지만 / -기는 한데; used for concession/contrast
「-고말고요 / -고말고」表示\"当然……了\"\"那还用说\"\"……不用说: 「-고말고요 / -고말고」 means "of course..." "that goes without saying" "needless to say". Used to strongly affirm/agree with the other person, with a warm, direct, colloquial tone. Equivalent to "of course" "absolutely".
直接接词干，不看받침；只用于口语回应；名词用 -이고말고요: Attach directly to the stem, regardless of batchim; only used in spoken responses; for nouns use -이고말고요
「-을/ㄹ 따름이다」表示\"只是……而已\"\"不过是……\"。用于强调\"没: The pattern '-을/ㄹ 따름이다' means 'just... that's all' or 'merely...'. It emphasizes the feeling of 'nothing else, just this'. It has a formal, written tone and is often used in expressions of humility, regret, helplessness, or gratitude.
动词/形容词词干：有받침 -을 따름이다 / 无받침 -ㄹ 따름이다: Verb/Adjective stem: with batchim -을 따름이다 / without batchim -ㄹ 따름이다
\"따름\" 意为\"仅仅/只是\"；-을/ㄹ 따름이다 是固定搭配；名词 -(: '따름' means 'merely/just'; -을/ㄹ 따름이다 is a fixed expression; for nouns, use -(이)ㄹ 따름이다
가다 无받침，用 -ㄹ 따름이다: 가다 has no batchim, so use -ㄹ 따름이다
감사하다 词干 감사하 无받침，用 -ㄹ 따름이다 → 감사할 따름이에요。: 감사하다 stem is 감사하, no batchim, so use -ㄹ 따름이다 → 감사할 따름이에요.
本练习综合复习 P28 强调与感叹深化章节的 8 个语法点：-기(가) N하다: This exercise comprehensively reviews the 8 grammar points from the P28 Emphasis and Exclamation Deepening chapter: -기(가) N하다 / 얼마나 -는지 모르다 / -다 못해 / -을수록 / 오죽 -으면 / -기(는) 하다 / -고말고요 / -을 따름이다.
重点辨析：感叹强度阶梯 및 让步转折与限定表达: Key Distinctions: Intensity Scale of Exclamations and Concessive/Contrastive & Limiting Expressions
「-(으)ㄴ/는 것으로 알려지다/전해지다」是新闻报道最常用的引述句式，表示\: The pattern '-(으)ㄴ/는 것으로 알려지다/전해지다' is the most common quotative structure in news reports, meaning 'it is known', 'according to reports', or 'it is said'. It conveys information as a 'known fact' without specifying the source. 알려지다 emphasizes 'widely known', while 전해지다 emphasizes 'the news coming in'.
动词现在 -는 + 것으로 + 알려지다/전해지다｜形容词/过去 -(으)ㄴ +: Verb present: -는 + 것으로 + 알려지다/전해지다 | Adjective/Past: -(으)ㄴ + 것으로
알려지다=被知晓；전해지다=被传告；名词 -인 것으로；否定 -지 않은 것으로: 알려지다 = to be known; 전해지다 = to be reported; Noun: -인 것으로; Negative: -지 않은 것으로
「-(으)ㄴ/는 것으로 나타나다/드러나다」表示\"（据调查/数据）显示\"\: The pattern '-(으)ㄴ/는 것으로 나타나다/드러나다' means '(according to surveys/data) shows' or 'results indicate'. 나타나다 focuses on 'showing/presenting' (neutral data), while 드러나다 focuses on 'exposing/revealing' (hidden facts being uncovered). It's a high-frequency structure in newspapers, government reports, and white papers.
나타나다=（结果）显示｜드러나다=（隐藏的）被揭露｜句尾用过去 -았/었다: 나타나다 = (results) show | 드러나다 = (hidden) is revealed | End with past tense -았/었다
「-(으)ㄹ 전망이다」和「-(으)ㄹ 것으로 보이다/예상되다」都是新闻体\": Both '-(으)ㄹ 전망이다' and '-(으)ㄹ 것으로 보이다/예상되다' are fixed expressions in news style for 'expected/forecast'. The former is more definitive ('there is a prospect of...'), while the latter is more tentative ('it looks like...'). They indicate objective predictions about future trends, economic movements, and policy directions.
动词/形容词词干 + -(으)ㄹ + 전망이다｜-(으)ㄹ + 것으로 + 보이: Verb/Adjective stem + -(으)ㄹ + 전망이다｜-(으)ㄹ + 것으로 + 보이다 / 예상되다
有받침 -을，无받침 -ㄹ；名词 -일 전망이다；否定 -지 않을 전망이다: With 받침 -을, without 받침 -ㄹ; noun -일 전망이다; negative -지 않을 전망이다
머무르다 → 머무를 전망이다（받침×，但 르→ㄹ）: 머무르다 → 머무를 전망이다 (no 받침, but 르→ㄹ)
「-기에 앞서 / -에 앞서」是\"在……之前\"的书面表达，比口语的 -기: 「-기에 앞서 / -에 앞서」 is a written expression meaning "before...", more formal than the colloquial -기 전에. Often used in news, speeches, and report openings to indicate what must be done before a formal action or ceremony. Verbs take -기에 앞서, nouns take -에 앞서.
书面正式；后文常接告知/说明/致谢；不用于日常口语: Formal written style; often followed by announcements, explanations, or thanks; not used in everyday speech
「-기(를) 요구하다/촉구하다/당부하다」是新闻/公文报道公众诉求或官员发言的: 「-기(를) 요구하다/촉구하다/당부하다」 is a formal pattern used in news and official documents to report public demands or officials' statements. 요구하다 = to demand (strong); 촉구하다 = to urge, press (formal/media); 당부하다 = to earnestly ask, appeal (polite/superior to subordinate).
助词 -를 常可省；主语多为 团体/官方；否定用 -지 않기(를): Particle -를 often omitted; subject is usually a group/official body; negative uses -지 않기(를)
「-는 데 그치다 / -에 그치다」表示\"仅仅停留在……\"\"只做到……为: 「-는 데 그치다 / -에 그치다」 means "to stop at just..." or "to only go as far as...", implying criticism or regret that something didn't go further or meet expectations. It's the most common evaluative pattern in news analysis and commentary. Verbs take -는 데 그치다, nouns take -에 그치다.
句尾常用 -았/었다 表示结果；含消极评价（\"未达预期\"）: Endings often use -았/었다 to indicate result; carries negative evaluation ("below expectations")
「-자」是\"一……就……\"的书面语连接词尾，语义与 -자마자 相近但更简洁、: 「-자」 is a written connective ending meaning "as soon as...", similar to -자마자 but more concise and formal, used in writing, news, and literature. The actions happen in immediate succession, often in objective statements about past events. Cannot be used with imperative or request endings.
仅接动词；主语可不同也可相同；不能与命令/请求/劝诱形式搭配；不含\"预期外\": Only attaches to verbs; subjects may differ or be the same; cannot be used with commands/requests/suggestions; does not carry an "unexpected" nuance
「이래(로) / -(으)ㄴ 이래」表示\"自从……以来（一直……）\"，比 -: 이래(로) / -(으)ㄴ 이래 means "since... (continuously)" and is more formal and literary than -(으)ㄴ 후로 / -고 나서. Attach 이래(로) to nouns and -(으)ㄴ 이래 to past verb stems. Commonly used in news retrospectives and historical statements.
이래(로) 中的 -로 可省；后文常接\"最……\"\"持续……\"\"从未……: The -로 in 이래(로) is optional; the following clause often uses "most...", "continuously...", or "never..." to describe a long-term state
本课综合 P29 全部 8 个书面/新闻体语法点：것으로 알려지다/전해지다、것: This lesson covers all 8 written/news style grammar points from P29: 것으로 알려지다/전해지다, 것으로 나타나다/드러나다, -(으)ㄹ 전망이다, -기에 앞서, -기를 촉구/당부하다, -에 그치다, -자, 이래(로). Tests sensitivity to written language.
说正在做、之前一直在做: Saying what's happening now and what was happening before
-고 있어요 把动作拉成正在进行的状态；\\n-고 있었어요 表达过去某个时候正: -고 있어요 stretches an action into an ongoing state; -고 있었어요 expresses something that was ongoing at a past time. Similar to "currently doing..." in Chinese, but Korean also uses it for continuous states like "wearing/holding/carrying."
这节课只有一个核心结构：\\n动词词干 + -고 있어요。\\n现在进行用 있어: This lesson has one core structure: verb stem + -고 있어요. Use 있어요 for present progressive and 있었어요 for past progressive. Note this structure only attaches to verbs, not adjectives.
-고 接续时不触发不规则变化（듣다→듣고 있어요，不变形）。\\n特殊用法：\\: -고 does not trigger irregular conjugations (듣다→듣고 있어요, no change). Special usage: wearing verbs like 입다/쓰다/들다 + -고 있어요 indicates a continuous state of "wearing/holding/carrying," not an action in progress.
-고 있어요 是 SNS 和聊天里最自然的表达\"在听歌\"\"在看剧\"\"在: -고 있어요 is the most natural way on SNS and in chats to say "listening to music," "watching a show," or "waiting for someone." The wearing usage (입고 있어요/쓰고 있어요) is also very common when describing someone's appearance.
说以前曾经……现在不一样了: Saying what used to be... but is different now
-았었/었었/였었어요 表达过去曾经有过的经历或状态，常带有\"现在可能已经不同: -았었/었었/였었어요 expresses past experiences or states, often implying "things may be different now," adding a layer of nostalgia compared to the simple past. There's no exact Chinese equivalent; think of it as "used to... (but not necessarily now)."
这节课在P1过去时基础上加一层：\\n-았어요 是普通过去，-았었어요 是\"回: This lesson builds on the P1 past tense: -았어요 is simple past, while -았었어요 is "recollective past" emphasizing that the present differs from the past. The structure adds another -었어요 to the past tense ending.
变形逻辑和普通过去时完全一样（看词干末尾元音选 았/었/였），只是再叠一层 었어: The conjugation logic is identical to the simple past (choose 았/었/였 based on the final vowel of the stem), just with an extra 었어요 added. Note: use -았어요 for ordinary events that happened yesterday, not -았었어요 (어제 밥을 먹었어요 ✓, 먹었었어요 ✗).
\"以前喜欢过这个歌手\"\"小时候住过首尔\"\"以前经常听这首歌\"这类带着: Expressions like "used to like this singer," "lived in Seoul as a kid," or "used to listen to this song a lot"—full of nostalgia and change—are exactly where -았었어요 shines. It's used for fandom, sharing experiences, and reminiscing.
-았었어요 强调过去经历、现在已不同。살았어요 是普通过去陈述。题目问\"回忆感: -았었어요 emphasizes a past experience that is now different. 살았어요 is a simple past statement. The question asks for the "nostalgic" expression.
名词+이었었어요 表示\"以前是学生（现在不是了）\"，带回忆感。: Noun + 이었었어요 means "used to be a student (but not anymore)," with a nostalgic feel.
说想做什么，以及\"那样的话\": Say what you want to do, and "in that case"
-고 싶어요 表达说话人自己的愿望；\\n그러면 连接条件和结果，表示\"那么/:
-고 싶어요 expresses the speaker's own wish; 
그러면 connects condition and result, meaning "then/in that case." 
-고 싶어요 is mainly used for first-person wishes; for third-person "wants to do," switch to -고 싶어하다. 
Unlike Chinese: 
Chinese "wants to do" doesn't distinguish person, but Korean uses 싶어요 for first person and 싶어하다 for third person.
两块内容：①-고 싶어요（想做）动词词干直接加，非常规律；\\n②그러면（那么）: Two parts: ① -고 싶어요 (want to do) attaches directly to the verb stem, very regular; \n② 그러면 (then) goes at the start of a sentence to connect two clauses, often shortened to 그럼 in speech.
-고 싶어요 只接动词词干，不能直接接名词（커피고 싶어요 ✗）。\\n说第三人: -고 싶어요 only attaches to verb stems, not nouns (커피고 싶어요 ✗). \nFor third-person wishes, use -고 싶어하다 (친구는 가고 싶어해요). \n그러면 marks a conditional sequence, unlike 그렇지만 which is contrastive.
-고 싶어요 是表达愿望最自然的方式说学习目标、旅行计划、购物心愿都用它。\\n: -고 싶어요 is the most natural way to express wishes—use it for study goals, travel plans, and shopping desires. \nAdd 그러면/그럼 to make "if... then..." suggestions, and your conversations flow instantly.
认识ㄹ收音词的特殊变形规律: Learn the special conjugation rules for words ending in ㄹ
ㄹ 不规则不是永远变化，而是遇到 ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ 开头的语尾时 ㄹ 脱落。\\n接:
The ㄹ irregular isn't always changing—ㄹ drops only before endings starting with ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ. 
It's kept before -아요/어요 and -고. 
Common words: 
살다, 알다, 만들다, 놀다. 
Chinese has no similar rule, so just remember "drops before ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ."
这节课不是新句型，而是变形规则：\\nㄹ 词干在接哪些语尾时会脱落 ㄹ，在哪些语: This lesson isn't a new pattern but a conjugation rule: \nwhich endings make ㄹ stems drop the ㄹ, and which keep it. \nComparing forms of common words (살다/알다/만들다) is faster than memorizing rules.
ㄹ 脱落触发条件：\\n后接语尾首字母是 ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ（如 -(으)세요、正式体:
ㄹ drop triggers: 
when the following ending starts with ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ (e.g., -(으)세요, formal -ㅂ니다/습니다, adnominal -는). 
Before vowel endings (-아요/어요) or -고, ㄹ stays. 
Mnemonic: 
살아요 (keep) / 사세요 (drop) / 삽니다 (drop) / 사는 (drop).
살다/알다/만들다 是极高频词问住哪、问认不认识、说自己做的。\\n掌握 ㄹ 脱: 살다/알다/만들다 are super high-frequency—asking where someone lives, if they know something, or what they made. \nMastering ㄹ drop means you won't misspell these forms and can recognize them more easily in listening.
判断对错：ㄹ不规则音变: True or false: the ㄹ irregular sound change
说\"好的我知道了\"和做选择: Saying "okay, got it" and making choices
-을/ㄹ래요 表达\"我要……/要不要……\"，比 -고 싶어요 更直接；\\n: -을/ㄹ래요 expresses "I'll... / shall we...?", more direct than -고 싶어요; \n-겠- marks intention, conjecture, or politeness, with the most common fixed phrase being 알겠어요 (got it). \n-을/ㄹ래요 is like casual "I'll..." in Chinese, and -겠- is like "I will / let me..."
两块内容：①-을/ㄹ래요（要做/要不要）看词干有无收音选 을래요/ㄹ래요；\\n: Two parts: ① -을/ㄹ래요 (will do / shall we) choose 을래요 or ㄹ래요 based on whether the stem ends in a consonant; \n② -겠- (intention/politeness) at this stage, just master the fixed phrase 알겠어요.
-을/ㄹ래요 收音规则和之前完全一样：\\n有收音接 을래요，无收音接 ㄹ래요。:
-을/ㄹ래요 follows the same final-consonant rule as before: 
with a final consonant use 을래요, without use ㄹ래요. 
-겠- attaches directly to the stem, no consonant check. 
Note the difference: 
-고 싶어요 is an inner wish (softer), -을/ㄹ래요 is a direct statement (more colloquial).
갈래요/먹을래요/볼래요 是朋友间最自然的邀约用语\"要去吗？\"\"要吃什么？: 갈래요/먹을래요/볼래요 are the most natural ways to invite friends—"wanna go?" "what'll you eat?" \n알겠어요 is a daily response in class and service settings. \nAfter this lesson, your everyday conversations will flow much better.
选择正确的意志表达: Choose the correct expression of intention
问什么、哪个、什么样的: Asking what, which, and what kind
三个疑问词都可译成\"什么/哪\"，但用法不同：\\n무슨 问名称内容，어느 从: All three question words can translate to "what/which," but they differ: \n무슨 asks for name or content, 어느 picks one from options, 어떤 asks about nature or characteristics. \nChinese "what song," "which song," and "what kind of song" map to these three.
这节课三个疑问词都放在名词前面，结构一样，区别只在\"问的是什么\"。\\n记住: This lesson puts all three question words before nouns—same structure, differing only in what they ask. \nRemember three model sentences: \n무슨 뜻이에요? / 어느 나라 사람이에요? / 어떤 음식을 좋아해요?
어느 只用于疑问句，肯定句里不用（不说\"어느 노래가 좋아요\"来表达喜欢）。: 어느 is only used in questions, not in statements (you don't say "어느 노래가 좋아요" to express liking). \nThe difference between 무슨 and 어떤: \nuse 무슨 to ask "what's it called/what is it," and 어떤 to ask "what kind/what characteristics."
这三个词是开启话题的万能钥匙\"这是什么歌\"\"你是哪国人\"\"喜欢什么样的: These three words are the master key to starting topics—"what song is this," "which country are you from," "what food do you like." \nMaster this lesson and you can ask sharper questions, no longer relying only on "뭐예요?"
그렇지만 是明确转折\"但是\"；\\n그런데 语气更口语，可以是轻转折\"不过:
그렇지만 is a clear contrast "but"; 
그런데 is more colloquial, a soft "though," and can also advance the topic or introduce new info. 
This lesson overlaps with P2's 그렇지만, but the focus is the new 그런데—clarify the difference. 
It's like Chinese "但是" vs "不过": 
그렇지만 ≈ 但是 (formal contrast), 그런데 ≈ 不过 (colloquial, also shifts topics).
两个连词都放在第二句句首，结构完全一样。\\n区别在语气和功能：\\n그렇지만: Both conjunctions go at the start of the second sentence, with identical structure. \nThe difference is tone and function: \n그렇지만 only contrasts, while 그런데 can also shift topics ("By the way, what does this word mean?").
判断用哪个很简单：\\n前后有明确对比关系用 그렇지만；\\n想轻松转换话题或信:
Choosing is simple: 
Use 그렇지만 for a clear contrast; 
use 그런데 to casually shift topics or info. 
In speech, 그런데 is far more common than 그렇지만 and covers most situations.

连接两个动作，说原因和顺序: Connecting two actions: expressing reasons and sequence
-고 把两个动作并列或按顺序连起来；\\n-아/어/여서 表示原因、理由，或前后: -고 connects two actions in parallel or sequence; -아/어/여서 indicates cause, reason, or a natural flow between actions. This lesson is the starting point for complex sentences—master these two connectors to expand simple sentences into coherent expressions. In Chinese, "eating and drinking" uses "and" directly, but Korean uses -고 attached to the verb stem; in Chinese, "because...so" are separate words, but Korean's -아/어서 attaches directly to the verb with no standalone "because."
两个连接形式功能不同：\\n-고 是中性连接（做A然后做B），-아/어/여서 是: The two connectors serve different functions: -고 is a neutral connector (do A, then do B), while -아/어/여서 is causal (because A, so B). Structurally, both attach to the preceding verb stem, and the following clause is stated normally.
-고 接续最简单直接去掉 다 加 고，-고 以辅音开头，不触发任何不规则变化（ㄷ: -고 is the simplest connector: just drop 다 and add 고. Since -고 starts with a consonant, it doesn't trigger any irregular changes (ㄷ, ㅂ, ㅅ, 르, ㅡ, ㄹ are all unaffected). When attaching -고 to an already-conjugated past tense, keep the changed form (e.g., 들었고). For -아/어/여서, the conjugation is the same as -아요/어요: if the stem's final vowel is ㅏ/ㅗ → 아서, otherwise → 어서, and 하다 → 해서. Note: a cause clause with -아/어/여서 shouldn't be followed by a command.
这两个连接形式是韩语表达的骨架\"喝完咖啡再学\"\"因为发音快所以难\"\"因: These two connectors are the backbone of Korean expression—"study after finishing coffee," "it's hard because the pronunciation is fast," "I'll rest because I have a headache." Almost every complex sentence uses them. Master this lesson, and your Korean will shift from choppy fragments to smooth, connected sentences.
说必须做，或请别人别做: Saying what must be done, or asking someone not to do something
-아/어/여야 해요 / 돼요 表达\"必须、应该、得……\"；\\n-지 마세: -아/어/여야 해요 / 돼요 expresses "must, should, have to"; -지 마세요 expresses "please don't." -아/어/여야 해요 corresponds to Chinese "得……/必须……" (have to/must), and -지 마세요 to "请不要……" (please don't). Both are extremely common in daily speech.

说花了多长时间、多少钱: Saying how much time or money something took
걸려요 表示花费时间；\\n-는 데 돈이 들어요 表示做某事花钱。\\n和中文: 걸려요 indicates time spent; -는 데 돈이 들어요 indicates money spent on something. Unlike Chinese, where "spent 30 minutes" and "costs a lot" use the same verb, Korean requires distinct verbs: 걸리다 (for time) and 들다 (for money). Don't mix them up.
两块内容：①걸려요（花时间）时间词做主语，结构是\"时间 + 걸려요\"；\\n: Two parts: ① 걸려요 (takes time) — the time word is the subject, structure is "time + 걸려요"; \n② 돈이 들어요 (costs money) — paired with -는 데 to say "doing something costs money".\nThe subjects differ: for 걸려요, the subject is time; for 들어요, the subject is 돈.

\"从家到学校要多久\"\"去演唱会很花钱\"这类描述日常花费的表达，出行、购物: Expressions like "how long does it take from home to school" or "going to a concert costs a lot" are essential for travel, shopping, and planning. Master this lesson to accurately describe time and money costs.
说话时加自然的铺垫语气: Adding a natural, softening tone when speaking
-은/ㄴ/는데요 是口语常用的铺垫表达，带有\"是这样，不过……\"的语气，用于: -은/ㄴ/는데요 is a common conversational filler that carries a tone of "well, you see..." It's used for contrast, explanation, or leading into what comes next. Chinese has no exact equivalent—it's more like a discourse marker that makes sentences sound softer, more natural, and less blunt.
变形规则按词性分三类：\\n动词→-는데요，形容词→-은/ㄴ데요（按收音），名词: The conjugation rules fall into three categories by part of speech: verbs → -는데요, adjectives → -은/ㄴ데요 (depending on the final consonant), nouns → 인데요. 形容词的变形：\\n有收音→은데요（좋은데요），无收音→ㄴ데요（예쁜데요）。\\: Adjective conjugation: with a final consonant → 은데요 (좋은데요), without → ㄴ데요 (예쁜데요). The ㅂ irregular applies here: 어렵다 → 어려운데요. 있다/없다 use -는데요 (like verbs). For past tense, uniformly use 았/었는데요.

把动作变名词，把形容词变副词: Turn Actions into Nouns, Adjectives into Adverbs
-는 것 直接接动词词干，形容词名词化是 -ㄴ/은 것（后续课程）。\\n-게: -는 것 attaches directly to verb stems; adjective nominalization uses -ㄴ/은 것 (covered later).\n-게 attaches directly to adjective stems, but note:\n빠르다, 많다, 높다, etc. have dedicated adverbs (빨리/많이/높이)—use those instead of -게.
