N보다 表示\"比……\"；\\n에 비해서 表示\"和……相比\"（更书面）。: N보다 means "than...";\n에 비해서 means "compared to..." (more formal).\nLike Chinese, Korean comparatives follow "A is more... than B"—보다 works like Chinese 比, attaching directly after the comparison base.
这节课两个比较结构：①보다（口语比较）直接接在名词后，配合 더 加强；\\n②에: Two comparative structures this lesson: ① 보다 (spoken) attaches directly to nouns, and pairs with 더 for emphasis;\n② 에 비해서 (written) suits analysis and explanation.\nBoth mean "than..."—the difference is register.
보다 直接贴名词后，无需考虑收音。\\n더 可加可不加，加了更强调\"更\"。\:
보다 attaches directly to nouns with no batchim rules.
더 is optional—add it to emphasize "more."
Watch out for 보다's double identity:
The verb 보다 means "to see," while the particle 보다 means "than"—distinguish by position in the sentence.
에 비해서/비하면/비하여 are three forms of the same expression.
比较两首歌、两个语言的难度、两个地方的特点보다 是日常表达里用频率最高的比较词。: Comparing two songs, the difficulty of two languages, the traits of two places—보다 is the most frequently used comparison word in everyday speech.\nAfter this lesson, you can accurately say "sounds better than..." and "harder than yesterday."
(으)로 是多义助词：\\n表示工具/语言、方向、身份结果。\\n有收音用 으로:
(으)로 is a multi-purpose particle:
It marks tools/languages, direction, identity, and results.
Use 으로 after a batchim, 로 after no batchim or ㄹ.
Chinese phrases like "say it in Korean," "go right," and "pay by card" all rely on (으)로.
(으)로 有四种用法：\\n方向（往哪走）、工具/语言（用什么说/做）、变化结果: (으)로 has four uses:\ndirection (where to go), tool/language (what to use), result of change (what it becomes), and identity (as what).\nThe structure is the same—attach to a noun—and context tells you the meaning.
收音规则有个例外：\\nㄹ 收音不接 으로，直接接 로（지하철로 / 서울로）。:
There's an exception to the batchim rule:
ㄹ batchim doesn't take 으로—just 로 (지하철로 / 서울로).
Distinguish 에 from (으)로:
에 marks "arriving at a destination," while (으)로 marks "moving in a direction"—학교에 가요 (go to school) vs 오른쪽으로 가요 (go right).
\"用韩语说\"\"往右转\"\"用相机拍\"\"换大号\"(으)로 是你在韩国: "Say it in Korean," "turn right," "take a photo with the camera," "get a bigger size"—(으)로 is the particle you can't avoid when asking directions, shopping, or communicating in Korea.\nMaster this lesson and you'll naturally produce "with/ toward/ as" expressions.
(이)나 连接名词表示\"或者\"；\\n-거나 连接动作表示\"或者做……\": (이)나 links nouns to mean "or";\n-거나 links actions to mean "or do...".\nIn Chinese, "coffee or tea" and "listen to music or watch a show"—the first uses (이)나, the second -거나. Just sort by noun vs. verb and you've got it.
两块内容：①(이)나（名词之间的或者）按收音选 이나/나；\\n②-거나（动作之: Two parts: ① (이)나 ("or" between nouns)—choose 이나/나 by batchim;\n② -거나 ("or" between actions)—attach directly to verb stems, no batchim rules.\nExpressing choices is one of the most basic needs in daily conversation.
(이)나 的收音规则和 이/가 完全一样：\\n有收音→이나（책이나），无收音→:
(이)나 follows the exact same batchim rule as 이/가:
With batchim → 이나 (책이나), without → 나 (커피나).
-거나 just attaches to the stem—simple and consistent.
Note (이)나 has another use:
It can mean "at least/just" (밥이나 먹어요 = just have a meal), softening the tone.
\"休息日听歌或者看剧\"\"喝咖啡还是茶\"\"无聊就刷刷手机\"(이)나/-: "Listening to music or watching shows on days off," "coffee or tea," "scrolling through your phone when bored" — (이)나/-거나 is super common for describing everyday choices and habits.\nMaster this lesson to describe your daily life more naturally.
说从谁那里得到，礼貌称呼人: Say who something came from, and address people politely
三块内容：①에게서/한테서（从谁那里收到/听说）和 에게/한테 方向相反；\\n: Three parts: ①에게서/한테서 (received/heard from someone) is the opposite direction of 에게/한테; \n②씨 (title) goes after the full name, not the surname; \n③짜리 (attribute modifier) attaches to prices/quantities to modify nouns.
에게서/한테서 的方向逻辑：\\n에게/한테=给出去，에게서/한테서=从那里收进:
The direction logic of 에게서/한테서: 
에게/한테 = giving out, 에게서/한테서 = receiving in from there. 
씨 usage: 
김민준 씨 (full name + 씨) or 민준 씨 (given name + 씨), never just 김 씨 (surname only). 
짜리 attaches directly after numbers.
\"从朋友那里收到礼物\"\"从老师那里学到的\"\"买了一万韩元的票\"这三个: "Got a gift from a friend," "learned it from a teacher," "bought a 10,000-won ticket" — these three expressions are common in shopping, chatting, and introducing people. \n씨 is also the most polite way Koreans address someone in daily life.
学会基本敬语，说话更有礼貌: Learn basic honorifics to speak more politely
-(으)세요 是最基础敬语请求形式；\\n部分特殊敬语词（드세요/계세요/말씀하:
-(으)세요 is the most basic polite request form; 
some special honorifics (드세요/계세요/말씀하세요/주무세요) need to be memorized as whole words. 
Honorifics are a cultural must in Korean — with elders, servers, and strangers, skipping them comes off as rude. 
Unlike Chinese: 
Chinese uses "please" for politeness, but Korean changes the verb ending itself — honorifics are a grammatical requirement, not an optional polite word.
两块内容：①-(으)세요（敬语请求）已在P2学过，这节课补充更多用法和场景；\\: Two parts: ①-(으)세요 (polite request) was covered in P2; this lesson adds more uses and contexts; \n②special honorifics like 먹다→드세요, 있다→계세요, 자다→주무세요 need to be memorized whole — you can't derive them from regular verbs.
-(으)세요 变形和P2完全一样（有받침→으세요，无받침→세요）。\\n特殊敬语:
-(으)세요 conjugates exactly like in P2 (with 받침→으세요, without→세요). 
There are only a few special honorifics — memorize them all: 
먹다/마시다→드세요, 자다→주무세요, 말하다→말씀하세요. 
있다 splits into two: "to be/exist" (person as subject)→계세요 (아버지가 계세요); "to have"→있으세요 (질문이 있으세요?). 
These have no pattern — just memorize them.
在韩国咖啡店、地铁、见朋友父母随处都需要用到敬语。\\n드세요（请吃/请喝）和: You need honorifics everywhere in Korea — coffee shops, subways, meeting a friend's parents. \n드세요 (please eat/drink) and 계세요 (to be) are the most frequent special honorifics. \nMaster this lesson to speak naturally in polite settings without sounding out of place.
综合运用第四章 L01-L10 所学语法：\\n动作连接与原因（-고/-아서）、: Put together everything from Chapter 4, L01-L10: \nconnecting actions and reasons (-고/-아서), must and prohibition (-아야 해요/-지 마세요), spending time/money (걸리다/들다), softening tone (-는데요), nominalization and adverbialization (-는 것/-게), comparison (보다/에 비해서), tool/direction/identity ((으)로), choice ((이)나/-거나), source and titles (에게서/씨), and basic honorifics (-(으)세요).
这是第四章的总复习。\\n第四章的主线是\"表达更精细\"怎么连句、怎么说义务、: This is the final review for Chapter 4. \nThe chapter's theme is "expressing yourself more precisely" — how to connect sentences, talk about obligations, compare, and speak politely. \nAs you work through it, think about the "communicative function" behind each grammar point, not just the form.
-(으)면 表示\"如果……\"的条件；\\n-(으)려면 表示\"想要做……的: -(으)면 means "if..."; \n-(으)려면 means "if you want to do..." and is often followed by a suggestion or request. \n-(으)면 matches Chinese "if...then...", and -(으)려면 matches "if you want to...you should..." — these are the core conditional structures of Chapter 5.
两个条件结构共用一套收音规则：\\n有收音→으면/으려면，无收音/ㄹ收音→면/려:
Both conditionals share the same batchim rules: 
with batchim→으면/으려면, without batchim or with ㄹ→면/려면. 
The difference is in meaning: 
-(으)면 is a general condition, while -(으)려면 is a condition based on a goal, often paired with -야 해요 or -세요.
ㄹ 收音直接接 -면（살면/알면），不脱落 ㄹ。\\n不规则在此正常触发：\\n:
ㄹ batchim attaches directly to -면 (살면/알면) without dropping the ㄹ. 
Irregulars trigger normally here: 
듣다→들으면, 춥다→추우면, 어렵다→어려우면. 
-(으)려면 is a contraction of -(으)려고 하면, and the following clause suits commands or obligations.
\"如果有时间就去\"\"想把韩语学好就要每天练习\"条件句是日常对话里最常用的: "If I have time, I'll go" and "if you want to get good at Korean, you need to practice daily" — conditionals are among the most common sentence patterns in everyday conversation. \nMaster this lesson to give advice, express plans, and describe "if..." situations.
안/-지 않다 表示主观\"不做\"；\\n못/-지 못하다 表示客观\"不能/: 안/-지 않다 means a subjective "don't do"; \n못/-지 못하다 means an objective "can't do" — often due to ability or circumstances. \nThis distinction isn't obvious in Chinese, but in Korean, "I don't drink coffee" and "I can't drink coffee" are completely different expressions.
两套否定各有短形和长形：\\n안/못（短形，口语常用）和 -지 않다/-지 못하:
There are two sets of negation, each with a short and long form: 
안/못 (short, common in speech) and -지 않다/-지 못하다 (long, more complete). 
The short form goes directly before the verb; the long form attaches to the stem with 지. 
Note: 못 cannot be used with adjectives.
하다 动词的否定要把 안/못 插在 하다 前面：\\n공부 안 해요，不是 안:
To negate 하다 verbs, insert 안/못 before 하다: 
공부 안 해요, not 안 공부해요. 
못 cannot be used with adjectives (날씨가 못 좋아요 ✗→안 좋아요 ✓). 
Key distinction: 
Use 안 when you choose not to do something; use 못 when circumstances or ability prevent it.
\"我不吃辣\"\"因为过敏所以不能喝\"\"发音太快跟不上\"\\n안 和 못: "I don't eat spicy food," "I can't drink it because of allergies," "The pronunciation is too fast to follow." \nKnowing the difference between 안 and 못 is a very practical skill in everyday conversation—it makes your expressions more precise and helps avoid misunderstandings.
说打算做什么，大概会怎样: Say what you plan to do and what will probably happen
-(으)려고 해요 表示\"打算/准备做某事\"；\\n아마 -을/ㄹ 거예요:
-(으)려고 해요 means "plan/intend to do something"; 
아마 -을/ㄹ 거예요 expresses a guess of "will probably...". 
The former extends the future tense -을/ㄹ 거예요 from P1 to say "will do," while this lesson's -(으)려고 해요 emphasizes "having a plan/intention." 
In Chinese, "plan to go" and "will go" are distinguished by separate words, but Korean uses different endings attached directly to the verb.
两块内容：①-(으)려고 해요（计划/意图）有收音接 으려고，无收音接 려고；\: Two parts: ① -(으)려고 해요 (plan/intention) — attach 으려고 after a final consonant, 려고 without; \n② 아마 -을/ㄹ 거예요 (guess) — you've learned -을/ㄹ 거예요; adding 아마 means "probably/possibly."
-(으)려고 해요 的主语必须是有意志的人/动物，天气等无意志主语不能用（날씨가:
The subject of -(으)려고 해요 must be a person or animal with intention; non-volitional subjects like weather can't be used (날씨가 따뜻하려고 해요 ✗). 
Strength of guess: 
갈 거예요 (will go) → 아마 갈 거예요 (will probably go). 
ㅂ irregular: 
어렵다→어려울 거예요.
\"今天打算复习单词\"\"打算去演唱会\"\"票大概会很贵\"计划和推测是学习: "I plan to review vocabulary today," "I'm planning to go to the concert," "The tickets will probably be expensive." Plans and guesses are the most common expressions in study diaries, chats, and discussions about the future. \nMaster this lesson and you can state your own plans and guess others' situations.
说\"不是……\"和\"不是A而是B\": Say "it's not..." and "it's not A but B"
이/가 的收音规则和主格助词相同：\\n有收音→이 아니에요，无收音→가 아니에:
The final consonant rule for 이/가 is the same as the subject particle: 
with a final consonant → 이 아니에요, without → 가 아니에요. 
In -는 게 아니라, 게 is the colloquial contraction of 것이. 
Note: 
아니에요 can end a sentence alone, but 아니라 must be followed by B예요 to give the correct answer.
\"这不是咖啡而是茶\"\"不是背单词而是要理解\"\"我不是老师，我是学生\": "This isn't coffee but tea," "It's not memorizing words but understanding," "I'm not a teacher, I'm a student." Correcting misunderstandings, clarifying identity, and stating the truth—these situations are very common in daily conversation. \nLearn this lesson and you can confidently say "that's not how it is."
选择正确的否定判断表达: Choose the correct negative judgment expression
用动作和状态来修饰名词: Modify nouns with actions and states
动词/形容词加冠词形后置于名词前：\\n现在动作用 -는，形容词用 -은/ㄴ，未: Verbs/adjectives take an adnominal form and go before the noun: \npresent action uses -는, adjectives use -은/ㄴ, future/incomplete uses -을/ㄹ. \nIn Chinese, adjectives can directly modify nouns ("difficult grammar," "a person studying"), but Korean requires a specific ending through conjugation to place them before a noun.
动词 -는 不看收音，统一接 는。\\n形容词 -은/ㄴ 看收音：\\n有收音→:
For verbs, -는 doesn't depend on the final consonant—always attach 는. 
For adjectives, -은/ㄴ depends on the final consonant: 
with a final consonant → 은, without → ㄴ. 
For -을/ㄹ: 
with a final consonant → 을, without → ㄹ. 
Note: 있다/없다 use -는 (있는/없는), like verbs. 
ㅂ irregular: 
어렵다→어려운.
\"现在听的歌\"\"学习韩语的人\"\"明天要去的地方\"冠词形是韩语里使用频: "The song I'm listening to now," "a person studying Korean," "the place I'll go tomorrow." Adnominal forms are extremely frequent in Korean—almost every complex sentence uses them. \nMaster this lesson and you can describe things, modify nouns, and greatly enrich your expressions.
请别人帮忙，或用\"对吧\"确认: Ask for help, or confirm with "right?"
-아/어/여 주세요 表示\"请帮我……\"；\\n-지요? 表示确认语气\"…: -아/어/여 주세요 means "please do... for me"; -지요? is a confirming tone meaning "...right? isn't it?", often shortened to -죠? in speech. -아/어/여 주세요 is the most common and polite way Koreans make requests in restaurants, classrooms, and service settings. In Chinese, "please help me do" uses separate words like "help/please," but Korean embeds "help" into the ending 주세요, which cannot be used alone.
两块内容：①-아/어/여 주세요（请帮我做）变形和 -아요/어요 一样，加 주세: Two parts: ① -아/어/여 주세요 (please do for me) conjugates like -아요/어요, then add 주세요; ② -지요?/-죠? (confirming tone) attaches directly to the stem regardless of the final consonant, used to seek agreement or confirmation.
-아/어/여 주세요 变形：\\n词干末元音 ㅏ/ㅗ→아 주세요，其他→어 주세: -아/어/여 주세요 conjugation: if the stem's last vowel is ㅏ/ㅗ → 아 주세요, otherwise → 어 주세요, 하다 → 해 주세요. -지요? is almost always shortened to -죠? in speech. Note: 주세요 is a request to the listener, while 주다 is used for a third party (e.g., 친구한테 선물을 줘요).
\"请慢点说\"\"请再说一遍\"\"这首歌很好听吧？\"-아/어/여 주세요: "Please speak slowly," "Please say it again," "This song is nice, right?" -아/어/여 주세요 is used whenever you need help, and -죠? is the most natural tone for sharing feelings or confirming information. After this lesson, your conversations will immediately become smoother and more natural.
读电话号码，说具体时间: Read phone numbers and say specific times
电话号码用汉字数词逐个读；\\n时间点用 에，时间范围用 부터…까지。\\n这节: Phone numbers are read digit by digit using Sino-Korean numbers; time points use 에, and time ranges use 부터…까지. This lesson integrates the time knowledge from P2, combining number reading and the time particles 에/부터/까지. Unlike Chinese, where "at three" and "from three to five" use different prepositions, Korean uses 에 for time points and 부터…까지 for ranges, with clear division.
三块内容：①电话号码读法（汉字数词逐位读，0读 공）；\\n②시간+에（在某个时: Three parts: ① phone number reading (Sino-Korean numbers digit by digit, 0 as 공); ② 시간+에 (at a specific time); ③ 부터…까지 (from one time to another). Time points and time ranges are different expressions and cannot be mixed.
时间点用 에（세 시에 만나요），时间范围用 부터/까지（세 시부터 다섯 시까: Time points use 에 (e.g., 세 시에 만나요), time ranges use 부터/까지 (e.g., 세 시부터 다섯 시까지). In phone numbers, 0 is read as 공, not 영. For hours (시), use native Korean numbers; for minutes (분), use Sino-Korean numbers as learned in P2—this lesson reinforces that.
\"下午三点见\"\"课程从十点到十一点\"\"我的电话是010-xxxx-xx: "See you at 3 PM," "The class runs from 10 to 11," "My number is 010-xxxx-xxxx"—making plans, talking about schedules, and sharing contact info are daily scenarios. Master this lesson to handle time-related conversations smoothly in Korea.
说坐什么交通工具去/来: Say what transportation you take to go/come
을/를 타다 表示乘坐；\\n타고 가다/오다 表示坐着去/来；\\n(으)로: 을/를 타다 means to ride; 타고 가다/오다 means to go/come by riding; (으)로 가다/오다 means to go/come using a certain mode of transport. The three are similar but differ in emphasis: 타고 stresses the action of getting on and going, while (으)로 stresses the method. In Chinese, "go by subway" is three separate words, but Korean requires choosing between 타고 or (으)로, and you must check for a final consonant to pick 으로 or 로.
三个表达方式：①타요（单独说乘坐）；\\n②타고 가요/와요（坐上后去/来，强调: Three expressions: ① 타요 (just riding); ② 타고 가요/와요 (go/come after riding, emphasizing the sequence); ③ (으)로 가요/와요 (go/come by a method, more concise). In everyday speech, 타고 and (으)로 are both common and interchangeable.
타고 가다 中的 타고 是 타다+-고 的连接形（已学）。\\n(으)로 的收音: In 타고 가다, 타고 is the connective form of 타다 + -고 (already learned). The rule for (으)로: if there's a final consonant → 으로, if no final consonant or ends in ㄹ → 로 (e.g., 버스로/지하철로). 걸어서 가요 (go on foot) is an exception—walking doesn't use 타다, but 걸어서.
\"坐地铁去公司\"\"坐飞机去韩国\"\"坐公交去学校\"说出行方式是日常对话: "Take the subway to work," "fly to Korea," "take the bus to school"—describing transportation is one of the most basic daily conversation topics. Master this lesson to describe travel smoothly and handle directions in Korea.
갈아타다 表示换乘；\\n을/를 갈아타다 强调换乘对象；\\n(으)로 갈아타: 갈아타다 means to transfer; 을/를 갈아타다 emphasizes what you're transferring from; (으)로 갈아타다 emphasizes what you transfer to; A에서 B로 갈아타다 means transferring from A to B. 갈아타다 is an extension of 타다 (to ride), with 갈아 meaning "change," so together it means "change rides/transfer." Unlike Chinese, where "transfer to the subway" is a direct combination, Korean uses particles to distinguish "which line you transfer from" (을/를) and "what you transfer to" ((으)로), making it more precise.
这节课是上节课 타다/(으)로 가다 的延伸，核心动词换成 갈아타다。\\n三种: This lesson extends the previous one on 타다/(으)로 가다, with the core verb changed to 갈아타다. Three expressions: ① 을/를 갈아타요 (transfer from a vehicle); ② (으)로 갈아타요 (transfer to a direction); ③ A에서 B로 갈아타요 (transfer from A to B, the most complete).
갈아타다 的助词选择和 타다 一样：\\n宾语位置用 을/를，方向/工具位置用: The particle choice for 갈아타다 is the same as for 타다: use 을/를 for the object, and (으)로 for direction/tool. The starting point uses 에서 (e.g., 버스에서), and the destination uses (으)로 (e.g., 지하철로). To express the number of transfers: 두 번 갈아타야 해요 (I need to transfer twice).
\"在这里换乘2号线\"\"从公交换地铁\"\"要换几次\"问路和乘车时这类表达: "Transfer to Line 2 here," "switch from bus to subway," "how many transfers?"—these expressions are essential for asking directions and riding transit. You'll use them when traveling in Korea and transferring on the subway. Combined with the previous lesson, your travel conversations will be complete.
说做着做着发生了变化: Say that something changed while doing an action
-다가 表示在做某动作的过程中发生变化、中断或切换，相当于\"做着做着……\"。: -다가 indicates a change, interruption, or switch that happens during an action, equivalent to "while doing..." in Chinese. For expressions like "fell asleep while studying" or "cried while watching," Korean uses -다가.
结构非常简单：\\n动词词干直接加 -다가，不看收音，后句说发生的变化或结果。\:
The structure is very simple: 
Add -다가 directly to the verb stem, regardless of the final consonant. The second clause states the change or result.

变形规则取决于词性和时态。\\n动词现在时 + 는 것 같다 / 形容词 + 은: The conjugation rules depend on the part of speech and tense.\nVerb present + 는 것 같다 / Adjective + 은/ㄴ 것 같다 / Future + 을/ㄹ 것 같다.

以后、回头（时间上稍后）: later, in a bit (slightly later in time)
回头再联系你。: I'll get back to you later.
突然（临时改约、有事时常用）: suddenly (often used when plans change at the last minute)
突然有事，可能去不了了。: Something came up suddenly, I might not be able to make it.
怎么这么突然就取消了？: Why did you cancel so suddenly?
有事、出了状况（改约最常用的理由）: something came up (the most common reason for rescheduling)
家里有事，出不了门。: Something came up at home, I can't leave.
有急事，我先走了。: I have something urgent, so I'll head out first.
不是急事的话待会儿再说。: If it's not urgent, let's talk about it later.
我确认一下行程再告诉你。: Let me check my schedule and get back to you.
周末完全没安排。: I have no plans at all this weekend.
我在咖啡厅等你。: I'll wait for you at the café.
我去地铁站接你。: I'll pick you up at the subway station.
几点去接你好？: What time should I pick you up?
这周有同学聚会。: There's a class reunion this week.
聚会一定要来哦。: Make sure you come to the gathering.
聚餐一般几点结束？: What time does the company dinner usually end?
玩、一起玩耍（朋友间约出去玩）: hang out, play together (making plans with friends)
好久没聚了，出来玩吧。: It's been a while—let's get together.
下周时间可以吗？: Does next week work for you?
那就推到下周吧。: Let's push it to next week then.
待会儿再联系你。: I'll get back to you in a bit.
守约、遵守约定: keep a promise, stick to plans
这次一定守约。: I'll definitely keep my promise this time.
我喜欢守约的人。: I like people who keep their word.
先约、已经有约在先（婉拒时的高级理由）: prior commitment, already have plans (polite excuse to decline)
那天已经有约了。: I already have plans that day.
抱歉，已经有约在先，去不了。: Sorry, I already have plans, so I can't make it.
一会儿、片刻（约“见一下”时常用）: a moment, a bit (often used when meeting briefly)
就见一面就走。: Just a quick meet-up, then I'll go.
待会儿有一小会儿时间吗？: Do you have a few minutes later?
谢谢（最标准的正式道谢，对长辈、店员、陌生人都能用）: thank you (standard formal, for elders, staff, strangers)
今天真的很感谢。: Thank you so much for today.
谢谢（해요体，对平辈、熟人温和又礼貌）: thanks (해요 style, polite and friendly to peers)
谢谢你照顾我。: Thank you for taking care of me.
谢啦（半语，对亲近的朋友、晚辈）: Thanks (casual, to close friends or younger people)
致谢、深表感谢（谦语，最郑重的道谢）: To express gratitude, deep thanks (humble, most formal)
感谢大家的关注。: Thank you all for your attention.
借此机会向您致谢。: I'd like to take this opportunity to thank you.
多亏了、托……的福（把功劳归给对方，很地道的感谢表达）: Thanks to, owing to (crediting the other person, a very natural way to say thanks)
多亏了你才顺利结束。: Thanks to you, it went smoothly.
多亏老师我才考上了。: Thanks to my teacher, I passed the exam.
这次多承蒙您关照了。: Thank you for all your help this time.
总是麻烦您，很不好意思。: I'm sorry for always troubling you.
抱歉、对不起（比 죄송하다 轻，对平辈、熟人）: Sorry, I apologize (lighter than 죄송하다, to peers or acquaintances)
抱歉、非常抱歉（比 미안하다 郑重，对长辈、上司、客人）: I apologize, very sorry (more formal than 미안하다, to elders, superiors, or guests)
给您添麻烦了，抱歉。: Sorry for the trouble I've caused you.
对不起（最标准的正式道歉，职场、服务业万能）: I'm sorry (the most standard formal apology, versatile in work and service)
都是我的错，对不起。: It's all my fault, I'm sorry.
道歉、赔礼（正式表达“道歉”这一行为）: Apology, apology (formal expression of the act of apologizing)
我先向你道歉。: Let me apologize to you first.
故意地（辩解“不是故意的”时常用）: Deliberately (often used when denying it was intentional)
没关系、不要紧（回应道歉/道谢的万能词）: It's okay, no problem (all-purpose response to apologies/thanks)
没关系，别在意。: It's okay, don't worry about it.
不客气、哪里的话（回应感谢，略书面）: You're welcome, don't mention it (responding to thanks, slightly formal)
不客气，能帮上忙就好。: You're welcome, glad I could help.
哪里的话、您太客气了（谦逊地回应感谢或称赞）: Don't mention it, you're too kind (humbly responding to thanks or praise)
哪里的话，该我谢您才对。: Don't mention it, I should be the one thanking you.
您太客气了，请随意。: You're too kind, please make yourself at home.
不是啦、不用（口语里回应感谢，最自然常用）: No, no need (colloquial response to thanks, most natural and common)
不用啦，该我谢你才对。: No need, I should be the one thanking you.
送礼、赠送: to give a gift, to present
给、呈上（주다 的谦语，对长辈递东西）: to give, to present (humble form of 주다, used when giving to elders)
这个作为礼物送给您。: I'd like to give this to you as a gift.
照顾、张罗、（特意）准备好: to take care of, to arrange, (specially) prepare
谢谢您一直照顾我。: Thank you for always taking care of me.
心意（送礼收礼时说“这是我的心意”）: thoughtfulness, gesture (said when giving/receiving gifts, meaning 'this is my token of appreciation')
虽然不贵，是我的一点心意。: It's not expensive, but it's a small token of my appreciation.
费心、在意（“您太费心了/别在意”）: to go to trouble, to care (as in 'you went to too much trouble' / 'don't worry about it')
谢谢您这么费心。: Thank you for going to all this trouble.
您不用费心。: You don't need to go to any trouble.
辛苦、受累（慰劳对方的付出）: hard work, trouble (to acknowledge someone's effort)
因为我，让您费心了吧。: I've caused you trouble, haven't I?
报答、回报: to repay, to return a favor
这份恩情我一定报答。: I will definitely repay this kindness.
下次一定回报你。: I'll definitely return the favor next time.
请客（为了道谢或庆祝而请对方吃喝）: to treat someone (to a meal or drinks, as thanks or celebration)
为了谢你，今天我请客。: To thank you, today's on me.
找到工作了，得请客啊。: You got a job, you have to treat us.
难得朋友帮了我。: Thanks to a friend who helped me.
真心地、由衷地（加重感谢或道歉的诚意）: Sincerely, from the heart (to emphasize gratitude or apology)
福气、多亏（常与에一起用，把好结果归功于对方）: Fortune, thanks to (often used with 에, attributing good results to the other person)
这全靠各位。: This is all thanks to everyone.
添麻烦、打扰（郑重致歉时说“给您添麻烦了”）: To cause trouble, to disturb (used in formal apologies like 'Sorry for the trouble')
不想再打扰您了。: I don't want to bother you anymore.
反省、检讨（深刻道歉时表态）: To reflect, to self-examine (used when making a deep apology)
是我错了，我在反省。: I was wrong, I'm reflecting on it.
我不知道自己错在哪。: I don't know where I went wrong.
低头（鞠躬致歉或致谢的肢体动作）: bowing (a physical gesture of apology or gratitude)
我低头行礼道谢。: I bow to express my thanks.
受宠若惊、不知如何是好（收到过分的好意或称赞时的谦辞）: overwhelmed and at a loss (a humble expression when receiving excessive kindness or praise)
您这么照顾我，真让我受宠若惊。: Your care for me is overwhelming.
过奖了，真让我不知如何是好。: You flatter me; I'm at a loss.
虽然像是辩解，但确实有原因。: It may sound like an excuse, but there's a real reason.
今后、以后（道歉后表态“今后会注意”）: from now on, in the future (used after apologizing to promise to be careful)
今后我会小心的。: I'll be careful from now on.
道谢、致谢的问候: a greeting of thanks, an expression of gratitude
我想先向您道谢。: I'd like to thank you first.
感谢您施予的恩惠。: Thank you for the favor you've shown me.
拒绝的时候有点不好意思。: I felt a bit awkward when refusing.
我是不太会拒绝人的性格。: I'm the type who finds it hard to say no.
为难、不方便（委婉表示做不到的经典词）: difficult, inconvenient (a classic euphemism for being unable to do something)
难、困难（委婉说“恐怕不行”时用“좀 어려울 것 같아요”）: difficult, hard (used to politely say 'I'm afraid it won't work' with '좀 어려울 것 같아요')
这次恐怕有点难。: I'm afraid this time might be a bit difficult.
忙（婉拒最常见的理由）: busy (the most common reason for politely declining)
最近有点忙。: I've been a bit busy lately.
那天工作忙，恐怕不行。: I'm busy with work that day, so I'm afraid I can't.
得找个合适的借口。: I need to find a suitable excuse.
找借口、拿……当托辞: to make excuses, to use... as a pretext
别老是找借口。: Stop making excuses all the time.
借口说累就没去。: He used tiredness as an excuse not to go.
谢绝、推辞（客气地拒绝好意）: to decline, to refuse (politely turning down kindness)
心意我领了，就不收了。: I appreciate the thought, but I'll have to decline.
不用了、够了（婉拒好意，语气随场合，稍不注意会显冷）: no thanks, that's enough (politely declining kindness; tone varies by situation, can seem cold if not careful)
不用了、没关系（婉拒时的高频“软拒绝”，比 됐어요 更客气）: no thanks, it's fine (a common soft refusal, more polite than 됐어요)
可惜、遗憾（拒绝时先说“真可惜”来缓冲）: a pity, regrettable (used to soften a refusal by saying 'what a pity' first)
很可惜，这次可能去不了。: It's a pity, but I probably can't make it this time.
真的很可惜，下次吧。: It's really a pity, maybe next time.
下次机会（婉拒的经典收尾“다음 기회에요”）: next opportunity (a classic way to end a polite refusal with '다음 기회에요')
这次先留到下次吧。: Let's save it for next time.
有约在先（婉拒最体面的理由，对方无法追问）: Already have plans (the most polite excuse to decline; the other person can't press further)
那天有约在先。: I already have plans that day.
身体状态（“컨디션이 안 좋다”是委婉推掉约的常用理由）: Physical condition (“컨디션이 안 좋다” is a common excuse to politely decline plans)
状态不好，得休息一下。: I'm not in good shape; I need to rest.
今天太累了，我要休息。: I'm too tired today; I need to rest.
太累了，得早点回去。: I'm too tired; I need to head back early.
勉强、超出能力（“무리예요”＝做不到、太勉强了）: Too much, beyond one's ability (“무리예요” = can't do it, too much)
今天之内恐怕做不到。: I'm afraid I can't do it by today.
负担、压力（婉拒好意时“부담스러워요”很常用）: Burden, pressure (“부담스러워요” is common when politely declining kindness)
您这么客气我会有负担的。: I'd feel burdened if you're so kind.
感到有负担、觉得为难（好意过重时的委婉回绝）: Feel burdened, find it difficult (a polite refusal when kindness is too much)
太贵重的礼物我会有负担。: I'd feel burdened by such a valuable gift.
让我收下有点为难。: It's a bit hard for me to accept.
我再想想（软性婉拒，往往意味着倾向于不做）: I'll think about it (a soft decline, often implying leaning toward not doing it)
我再考虑一下，回头联系您。: I'll think it over and get back to you.
下次见吧（婉拒当下邀约、留有余地的常用语）: See you next time (a common phrase to decline an invitation while leaving room)
今天不行，下次见吧。: Not today; see you next time.
下次见，我一定联系你。: See you next time; I'll definitely contact you.
不太、不怎么（委婉表达不喜欢、不想去）: not really, not so much (a gentle way to express dislike or reluctance)
我不太想去啊。: I don't really want to go.
那里我不太想去。: I don't really want to go there.
有心情、乐意（多用否定“안 내켜요”＝不太想）: in the mood, willing (often used in the negative '안 내켜요' = not really feeling it)
今天不太想。: I'm not really feeling it today.
不想去的话不去也行。: If you don't want to go, you don't have to.
眼力见儿、察言观色（韩国社交核心概念，拒绝时靠察觉气氛）: reading the room, social awareness (a core concept in Korean socializing; used to sense the mood when declining)
我看气氛悄悄避开了。: I read the mood and quietly slipped away.
他很会看眼色，会先察觉。: He's good at reading the room and picks up on things first.
我用了委婉的说法。: I used a euphemistic way of putting it.
拒绝、抵制（比 거절 更强硬、正式，多用于制度性场合）: refuse, reject (stronger and more formal than 거절, often used in institutional contexts)
有权拒绝这个要求。: He has the right to refuse this request.
讨厌、不愿意（直接拒绝，语气强，慎用于长辈）: dislike, unwilling (a direct refusal with strong tone; use cautiously with elders)
那个我不太愿意。: I'm not too keen on that.
我不喜欢勉强去做。: I don't like being forced to do things.
请求、拜托（拒绝的对象常是对方的 부탁）: request, favor (what you decline is often the other person's 부탁)
能帮我一个忙吗？: Can you do me a favor?
这个忙恐怕帮不了。: I'm afraid I can't help with this one.
这次的请求恐怕答应不了。: I'm afraid I can't grant this request.
我也想答应，但条件不允许。: I'd like to say yes, but the circumstances don't allow it.
缘由、情况（“사정이 있어서”是不便明说时的挡箭牌）: reason, circumstances ('사정이 있어서' is a shield when you can't say the real reason)
有些原因去不了。: I can't go for some reasons.
不好意思、抱歉（拒绝开头的缓冲垫，几乎必备）: Sorry, excuse me (a buffer phrase to start a refusal, almost essential)
不好意思，今天恐怕不行。: Sorry, I'm afraid today won't work.
抱歉，那个我帮不了您。: Sorry, I can't help you with that.
不好意思（拒绝平辈、熟人时的缓冲开头）: Sorry (a buffer phrase when refusing peers or acquaintances)
抱歉，这次帮不了你。: Sorry, I can't help you this time.
这可怎么办呢（面露难色的婉拒语气词）: What should I do (a hesitant tone for politely refusing)
这可怎么办，那天好像不行。: What should I do, that day doesn't seem to work.
啊，怎么办，我已经有约了。: Oh, what to do, I already have plans.
谅解、体谅（正式拒绝后请求对方谅解）: Understanding, consideration (asking for understanding after a formal refusal)
感谢您的宽容谅解。: Thank you for your understanding and patience.
保持距离（婉拒进一步来往的行为表达）: Keeping distance (an act of politely declining further interaction)
我想保持一点距离。: I'd like to keep some distance.
最近我倾向于保持距离。: Lately, I've been leaning toward keeping my distance.
略过、揭过（把话题岔开以回避）: Skimming over, glossing over (changing the subject to avoid)
不会拒绝人的性格（韩国人常自嘲的社交困扰）: A personality that can't say no (a social struggle Koreans often joke about)
我就是不会拒绝人的性格。: I'm just the type who can't say no.
因为不会拒绝，总是吃亏。: I always lose out because I can't say no.
心情受伤、不高兴（拒绝时最怕让对方 기분 상하다）: Feeling hurt, upset (the fear of making someone 기분 상하다 when refusing)
我说得很小心，怕伤到他。: I said it carefully, afraid of hurting him.
谨慎、小心翼翼（说难以启齿的拒绝前铺垫）: cautious, careful (paving the way before a difficult refusal)
虽然难以启齿，但我还是拒绝。: It's hard to say, but I have to decline.
这话说出来有点为难。: It's a bit awkward to say this.
推脱、扭捏推辞（口语里“몸을 빼다”式的躲避）: dodge, hem and haw (avoiding like '몸을 빼다' in colloquial speech)
怕显得矫情，就去了。: I went anyway, afraid of seeming fussy.
拒绝的意向（正式场合表达“拒绝的意思”）: intention to decline (formal way to express refusal)
我委婉地表明了拒绝的意向。: I politely indicated my intention to decline.
为难、难堪（比 곤란하다 更强调进退两难）: awkward, embarrassing (more about being stuck than 곤란하다)
您突然这么问，我有点为难。: You asking so suddenly puts me in a tough spot.
果断、坚决（该硬起来拒绝时的态度）: decisive, firm (the attitude when you need to refuse firmly)
给人压力、让人为难（拒绝时避免“부담 주는” 说法）: pressuring, burdensome (avoid saying '부담 주는' when refusing)
我不是想给你压力。: I don't mean to pressure you.
怕给你添压力，就没说。: I didn't say it, afraid of burdening you.
最近这档综艺真好看。: This variety show is really good lately.
周末刷了一堆综艺。: I binge-watched a bunch of variety shows over the weekend.
字幕（综艺里花字，制作组的吐槽神器）: subtitles (the witty captions in shows, the producers' roast tool)
这节目的字幕真的搞笑。: The subtitles on this show are hilarious.
字幕的梗玩得太绝了。: The subtitles' jokes are absolutely brilliant.
超有趣、贼好玩（꿀＝蜂蜜＋재미，网络缩语）: Super fun, really entertaining (꿀 = honey + 재미, internet slang)
这一集简直太有意思了。: This episode is just so entertaining.
超好看，一定要看。: It's amazing, you must watch it.
本来挺期待，结果超无聊。: I was looking forward to it, but it turned out super boring.
这一期有点无聊啊。: This episode is a bit boring.
抖包袱、玩梗（来自 ad-lib，指临场搞笑的话）: To drop a punchline, play with memes (from ad-lib, meaning improvised funny remarks)
抖包袱、开玩笑（临场说搞笑的话）: To drop a punchline, joke around (saying funny things on the spot)
正经着呢，别开玩笑。: I'm being serious, stop joking around.
传说级、名场面（legend，指经典到载入史册的片段）: Legendary, iconic scene (legend, referring to a classic moment that goes down in history)
经典的那期看多少遍都好笑。: The classic episode is funny no matter how many times you watch it.
截图、表情包图（网络上流传的搞笑图片）: Screenshot, meme image (funny pictures shared online)
这张图哪来的？: Where did this image come from?
做成表情包肯定火。: It would definitely go viral as a meme.
看动图更好笑。: It's funnier as an animated image.
整段被剪掉（통＝整个＋편집，戏份全没了）: Entirely cut out (통 = whole + 편집, all scenes removed)
戏份被整段剪掉了，好可惜。: The scenes were entirely cut out, what a shame.
戏份、镜头量（综艺里出镜时长）: screen time (amount of appearance in a variety show)
这期戏份给得挺多。: They gave him a lot of screen time this episode.
为了多点镜头拼命表现呢。: He's working hard to get more screen time.
反应（reaction，综艺里夸张的即时反应）: reaction (exaggerated immediate response in variety shows)
反应真的很浮夸。: The reaction is really over the top.
突然冷场（갑자기 분위기 싸해짐 的缩语）: sudden awkward silence (abbreviation of 갑자기 분위기 싸해짐)
那话一出口就冷场了。: The moment he said that, it got awkward.
很会把气氛搞冷。: He's really good at killing the mood.
大家默认的惯例、约定俗成（국민 룰 的缩语）: unspoken rule, common practice (abbreviation of 국민 룰)
炸鸡配可乐是标配啊。: Fried chicken with cola is a must.
这基本是公认的惯例了。: This is basically a well-known rule.
认同、同意（弹幕里刷“ㅇㅈ”表示赞同）: agree (typing 'ㅇㅈ' in comments to show agreement)
真的、确实（real 的音译，弹幕缩写“ㄹㅇ”）: really, for real (transliteration of 'real', abbreviated as 'ㄹㅇ' in comments)
带劲、绝了（强调程度很高，弹幕高频）: awesome, insane (emphasizing high degree, frequent in comments)
最近常看这个主播的直播。: I've been watching this streamer's broadcasts a lot lately.
这主播游戏打得真好。: This streamer plays games really well.
看直播才有意思。: Watching live is way more fun.
实时聊天刷得飞快。: The live chat is flying by.
喜欢实时互动的感觉。: I love the feel of real-time interaction.
聊天框、弹幕框（直播里观众打字的地方）: Chat box (where viewers type during a stream)
弹幕刷慢一点吧。: Slow down the chat a bit.
打赏留言会被念出来。: Donation messages get read out loud.
星星气球（아프리카TV 的打赏道具，简称별풍）: Star balloon (AfreecaTV donation item, aka Byeolpung)
